body:
## What Problem This Solves

Advances the shared CI and app Bun runtime from 667c to fc53bf8c0f after qualification of the published prerelease.

## User Impact

Worker heap-cap termination and idle-worker collection benefit from the runtime and engine fixes below. The release contains the four Darwin/Linux targets. Windows publication remains gated on signing (openclaw/bun#132).

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected [Bun prerelease](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/tag/openclaw-v1.4.3-20261007-fc53bf8c0f-webkit-cb8d6f202b) is a superset of 670b and uses [OpenClaw WebKit autobuild-cb8d6f202b5a396caa204ee1bb75d78175aa841a](https://github.com/openclaw/WebKit/releases/tag/autobuild-cb8d6f202b5a396caa204ee1bb75d78175aa841a). The shared JSON is regenerated from its checksum-verified manifest; CI and app staging continue to use one pin.

Changes since 667c:

- WebKit worker heap-cap termination fix: the 512 MiB OOM benchmark improved from 19.45 s to 1.06 s on Linux and 5.05 s to 258 ms on macOS in the earlier engine qualification.
- Detached `import.meta.resolve` origin handling (openclaw/bun#116) and external URLs through package validation (openclaw/bun#119).
- Unlimited-child `bun test` deadline handling and progress-based compile-cache test (openclaw/bun#133), plus retained-memory coverage for `vm.Script` (openclaw/bun#131).
- GC cadence changes (openclaw/WebKit#14 and openclaw/WebKit#15), passive-collector wakeup fixes (openclaw/WebKit#21 and openclaw/WebKit#22), and immediate GC timer wakeups for idle worker event loops (openclaw/bun#129).
- The engine release also contains the mimalloc exit TLS race fix; mimalloc is not linked into Bun. Windows-only changes openclaw/bun#130, openclaw/bun#126 and openclaw/bun#127 do not add Windows publication.

The test source includes the managed process-group cleanup owner fix in #166435; the admitted tooling pair passed. Original failed outcomes and source-bound accounting records remain preserved.

## Evidence

Exact tag: `openclaw-v1.4.3-20261007-fc53bf8c0f-webkit-cb8d6f202b`; fork commit: `fc53bf8c0fccd0dcbcccfcf75e2c306ab8953cae`; Gate evidence preserves three source revisions: 22 unchanged selections at `0d06bc0fec0129608ed04ed286e7e1e2c28021e3`, six at `68ea9948d186ff39f9d982e967183f3ba9b411d4` after #166533, and seven at `986a594e3da344c7127a68d1fcbc170abc65a3c9` after the #166572 admissions change. Planner comparisons established retained selection equality; the retained agents-support scope includes earlier bytes of `src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-recovery.test.ts`, and unit-fast-isolated includes earlier bytes of `src/system-agent/{assistant.configured,system-agent,tui-backend}.test.ts`. These remain explicitly attributed to their original source under the selection-equality retention policy, with final-head checks handled separately.

Checksum sources: [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/download/openclaw-v1.4.3-20261007-fc53bf8c0f-webkit-cb8d6f202b/SHA256SUMS) and [release manifest](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/download/openclaw-v1.4.3-20261007-fc53bf8c0f-webkit-cb8d6f202b/manifest.json). All four archive and executable hashes were independently verified. The canonical stager verified all four targets and executed both Darwin architectures. Linux arm64 received archive/executable/ELF validation; Linux x64 also ran the gate.

**Gate A: PASS**, with the recorded full-UI known intermittent below. The complete repaired-prerequisite CLI candidate passed all 6,178 assertions; its baseline-only database teardown failure is pre-existing and already fixed on main by `02e2078de7f634af018906abd7a43c3e275d5e25`, included in this PR’s base. author: carolinitsi
body:
## Objetivo

Entrega do teste técnico: a tela de cotação de fretes do FretePro, a partir do PNG do designer. O usuário informa os CEPs, as medidas, o peso e o seguro e recebe as opções de frete das transportadoras, com dados reais do Sandbox do Melhor Envio.

**Versão publicada:** https://sistema-cotacao-fretes.vercel.app/calcular-frete

## Como a solução evoluiu

Cada etapa entrou em um PR próprio, com o CI passando:

1. #1 Design tokens e tema do Nuxt UI, a partir do PNG
2. #2 Application shell (sidebar, topbar e breadcrumb)
3. #3 Schemas zod, máscaras e formatadores
4. #4 Integração com o Melhor Envio (rota interna, mock de desenvolvimento e composable)
5. #5 Formulário de cotação com o request na URL
6. #6 Tela de resultados
7. #7 Versão mínima do Node exigida na instalação
8. #8 README
9. #9 Estados vazios nas páginas não implementadas

Este PR fecha os itens que tinham ficado adiados na revisão de validação: testes de borda (`NaN`, `Infinity`, texto no lugar de número, prazo 0, preço inválido vindo da API) e atualização do [registro da revisão](.claude/specs/quote-validation/review-issues.md).

Também alinha o `docs/DECISIONS.md` ao código: a decisão 027 passa a registrar que a cotação só no cliente (`onMounted`) vive no `FreightQuoteResults`, e não mais no formulário.

## Principais decisões

Registro completo, com alternativas, em [`docs/DECISIONS.md`](docs/DECISIONS.md).

- **Nuxt UI como design system** (001, 009): o PNG virou tokens em três camadas; correções de contraste ficam em variantes `-a11y`, sem alterar os valores do design.
- **Um schema zod para tudo** (003, 017): o mesmo schema valida o formulário, a URL e o server.
- **Estado na URL, sem Pinia** (004, 028): reload, voltar do navegador e link compartilhado reproduzem a cotação.
- **Vue Query** (002, 025): cache por parâmetros; repetir uma cotação recente não chama a API.
- **API externa só no server** (021, 023): o token não chega ao navegador, e a resposta é validada e normalizada num contrato próprio.
- **Mock nunca é fallback** (022): só existe em `pnpm dev` e não esconde falha da API real.

## Como testar

Pela versão publicada ou localmente (`pnpm install` e `pnpm dev`, sem `.env`; ver README).

- [ ] Cotação válida: origem `01310-100`, destino `20040-020`, 10 × 15 × 20 cm, 1 kg.
- [ ] Erros: CEP `123` e altura `0`. Os erros aparecem no campo, e o foco vai para o primeiro inválido.
- [ ] Recarregar a página e abrir a URL dos resultados em outra aba: a cotação é refeita.
- [ ] "Editar dados" e o botão voltar do navegador.
- [ ] Largura de celular (375px): a tabela vira lista.

Automatizados (o CI roda todos):

- [ ] `pnpm lint`
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm test`
- [ ] `pnpm test:e2e`

## Limitações conhecidas

- Token do Melhor Envio gerado à mão, válido por 30 dias. Não há fluxo OAuth.
- O Sandbox tem preços de teste.
- "Selecionar" só mostra um toast. Histórico, Configurações e as demais páginas mostram um estado "Em breve".
- A busca e as notificações da barra superior seguem o layout, mas ainda não têm função.
- Nas máscaras, o cursor vai para o fim do campo quando o texto é reformatado.

## O que melhoraria com mais tempo

- Contratação do frete e cotações salvas no Histórico.
- OAuth com o Melhor Envio, com renovação automática do token.
- Motivo da indisponibilidade visível na tabela.
- Testes de acessibilidade automatizados (axe) e E2E em Firefox e WebKit.

When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP server internally uses the header values to populate the Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory overhead. author: sungjunlee
body:
Remediates the 2026-10-07 engineering audit (Epics #581, #582, #583, #584; baseline `a34ae5b`). Each sub-issue was implemented on its own branch, independently reviewed, and merged into this branch with a `Merge #N` commit, so every issue stays a separate review and rollback unit. **Please merge with a merge commit, not a squash**, to keep those units.

## Changes

| Issue | Change | Implementation | Independent review | Rounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #585 | Cached orphaned worktrees are re-derived from current Git evidence (owner, members, markers, gitdir) at the mutation boundary, including drift during confirmation; `--force` still rechecks | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Opus high: approve | 1 |
| #586 | Claude cwd parser honours JSON key escapes; duplicate top-level `cwd` makes the record unverifiable → undetermined/keep | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Opus medium: approve | 1 |
| #587 | Cleanup recipes are re-derived from the live catalog (cached argv is inventory only); Homebrew removes only the verified cache path instead of `brew cleanup --prune=all` | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Opus high: approve | 1 |
| #588 | perfharness owns only its `MkdirTemp` child; `-workdir` parent is never removed | gpt-6.1-sol medium | Claude Opus medium: approve | 1 |
| #589 | Incomplete activity evidence refuses age-based deletion; size measurement moved before the final barrier; context/identity/activity rechecked right before mutation; bounded residual measurement | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Opus high: approve after 2 change requests | 3 |
| #590 | One domain plan per invocation for review, JSON projection and execution; typed prepared execution; missing prepared target → invariant error before mutation | gpt-6.1-sol xhigh | Claude Opus high: approve | 1 |
| #591 | Local indexes remove the component × rows × targets lookup (2,000 targets: 23.8 s → 3.3 s, median of 5 on a shared M2) | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Sonnet high: approve | 1 |
| #592 | Codex activity uses the same resolved homes as discovery, per-home coverage, cache source identity + schema revision, bounded `codexsession` reader | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Sonnet high: approve | 1 |
| #593 | Release publish/tap depend on same-SHA verification; perfharness in `make check`/`make test` and Linux/macOS CI; `internal/safedelete` on Windows CI; actions and tools pinned | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Sonnet high: approve | 1 |
| #594 | Every clean confirmation (final, per-item, guided, unified, APFS) observes cancellation via `internal/confirminput` | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Sonnet high: approve | 1 |
| #595 | Installer tests call the production `install.sh` / `install.ps1` paths; failure paths preserve the existing binary | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Sonnet high: approve | 1 |
| #596 | `activity_source_not_registered` survives to final JSON; one supported reason-code catalog. Follow-up commit adds the new execution codes `cleanup_recipe_changed` and `worktree_evidence_changed` to that catalog and the docs | gpt-6.1-sol medium | Claude Sonnet medium: approve | 1 + 1 |
| #597 | Retention honours explicit roots; an odd regular file no longer hides its normal siblings | gpt-6.1-sol medium | Claude Sonnet medium: approve | 1 |
| #598 | `Size` is apparent bytes from one walker (`du` fast path removed); scan-cache revision 11 → 12 | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Sonnet high: approve after 1 change request | 2 |
| #599 | Current safety/release/installer contracts versus dated history; perfharness commands use `go -C`; prose-pinning doc tests replaced by structural checks | gpt-6.1-sol high | Claude Sonnet medium: approve | 1 |
| #600 | Keep the unregistered Codex tmp implementation; document why it is not supported and what reintroduction needs; public CLI test proves tmp content is never a candidate | gpt-6.1-sol medium | Claude Sonnet medium: approve | 1 |

Conflicts between #585/#587 and between #589 and the integrated tree were resolved by gpt-6.1-sol high in merge commits, then reviewed by Claude Sonnet (`--remerge-diff`). Codex workers also ran their own Grok 4.7 reviews in most lanes; the Claude reviews above are the independent gate.

## Behavior changes reviewers should know

- **Size meaning (#598):** apparent bytes, sparse files at logical length, symlinks not followed, and each hardlinked file counted once per (device, inode) within a target on Unix (per path on Windows, where identity is unavailable). Numbers differ somewhat from the old `du -sk` allocated figures. Old scan caches are rejected and rebuilt.
- **Homebrew (#587):** cleanup removes only the previewed cache directory through `safedelete`; old kegs are no longer touched.
- **Orphaned worktrees (#585):** a `.git` marker that is a symlink is now always refused (fail-closed).
- **New receipt reason codes:** `cleanup_recipe_changed` and `worktree_evidence_changed` (additive; documented in `docs/JSON_SCHEMA.md`).

## Verification

On the final head (macOS, darwin/arm64, Go 1.26.3): `make check`, `make test` (root and perfharness modules), `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./...`, `go -C tools/perfharness test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C tools/perfharness vet ./...`, `make build` plus `aibris --help` and `aibris clean --help`, and `go -C tools/perfharness run . --help` all exited 0. The same root race and perfharness suites passed after every per-issue merge.

Pre-merge end-to-end checks with the built binary:
- **Hermetic E2E (temporary HOME, real deletions only there):** 13/13 pass. It removes an orphaned worktree, old `node_modules`, and an orphaned Claude store. It keeps fresh `node_modules`, a sentinel, and a live project. Dry-run changes nothing, and SIGINT at the prompt exits promptly with the target kept. The same script against `a34ae5b` fails exactly the fixed defects: a restored-parent dirty worktree deleted (#585), an escaped-key live-owner store deleted (#586), and a process still alive after SIGINT (#594).
- **Maintainer's real HOME, read-only `scan` + `clean --dry-run` only:** same decisions as `a34ae5b` (522 selected / 488 protected / 130 skipped). This run also found that per-path hardlink counting overstated `node_modules` by 5.6 GB (one target 10.77 GB vs 5.36 GB unique), all within single targets. That is fixed in 39d1290: the reported `node_modules` total now equals an independent unique-inode measurement (10.09 GB). Scan wall time was too noisy on a busy machine to compare (64–123 s for both binaries).
- **First CI run** caught two real defects, now fixed: the installer leaked its temp dir on Linux when a staged install failed (a bare `return` inside the EXIT trap, bash ≥ 4.4), and perfharness built Windows binaries without `.exe`. Native Windows now passes `TestNativeInstallPowerShell`, `internal/safedelete` and perfharness.

**Not verified:** a real tag-triggered release (reusable-workflow gate, OIDC attestation, publish and tap) only runs on the next release. No real HOME cleanup, package-manager cleanup, tag or release was run.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- #587 makes `writeExecutable` skip on Windows, so some command tests no longer run on Windows CI.
- perfharness `go.mod` now `replace`s the root module only to use `testutil.SetHome`.
- `NewGuidedExecutionReceipt` still builds its own target ID map without duplicate/missing checks; `cleanjson` now imports `internal/executor`.
- Pre-existing: npm cleanup can write `<parent>/_logs`; `go clean -cache` can trigger a GOTOOLCHAIN download; piped multi-prompt input can be lost between scanners; root `--help` omits Grok from the agent-state list.

Closes #585, closes #586, closes #587, closes #588, closes #589, closes #590, closes #591, closes #592, closes #593, closes #594, closes #595, closes #596, closes #597, closes #598, closes #599, closes #600.

author: ebro912
body:
## Summary

PR B2 of the chat-watches milestone (P-WDY-258 M3). In `wendy chat`, you can say "tell me when someone comes to the door", and Wendy tells you when it happens without being asked. It is stacked on B1 (#2207, the MCP watch tools), which is stacked on PR A (#2206, leased campaigns).

- **Inbox:** the top-level chat session receives `notifications/wendy/watch_event` and `notifications/wendy/watch_status` into a 64-item inbox. The handler runs on mcp-go's stdio reader goroutine, so it never blocks. Dropped notices are counted and shown.
- **Transcript lines:** each notice shows as one dim line, for example `· 14:02:11  front door  person 0.91 entered`. The status bar shows `watching: N` while watches run. A line arriving mid-reply no longer splits the reply or makes a running tool look finished.
- **Event turns:** these events start a reply by themselves:
  - an arrival;
  - a watch ending for any reason other than `stopped`;
  - a watch's first error, unless `watch_start` already returned it;
  - READY after a `watch_start` that returned PREPARING.

  Other notices are shown and folded into the next event turn. Event turns start only when chat is idle, typed queued prompts go first, and turns are spaced at least 10 s apart, with reports that arrive in between merged into one turn. Esc and Ctrl+C leave the event queue alone; `/clear` empties it.
- **Event turns are not the user speaking:**
  - They skip memory recall and learning, hide the memory write tools, and give delegated children no memory.
  - They never show an approval prompt, with or without `--yes`. A tool that needs approval is refused with "Not run: a watch report started this turn, not the user…", and the model tells the user what it would do.
  - The event JSON reaches the model only inside an escaped `untrusted_sensor_event_json` block. That helper is now shared with `agentservice`, whose output is byte-identical. The label and camera name are JSON-quoted in the header.
- **Commands:** `/watches` and `/watches stop all` call the MCP server directly, never through the model.
- **Scope:** delegated children and unattended services, including `wendy agent serve`, never see `watch_*` tools.
- **Headless `--prompt`:** gets instructions to start a watch only to wait for it now with `watch_events`, because no reports arrive after the turn.
- **Restarts:** the TUI's watch state survives a `/voice` setup or a cancelled `/setup` on the same session. A completed `/setup` shows "Watches ended" with the number that ended.
- **Guidance:** the system prompt, the `sensors` profile group, the device-sensors skill and `guides/chat.mdx` cover watches.

Design: `specs/2026-10-05-chat-watches-design.md` §7. Plan: `specs/2026-10-07-chat-watches-plan-b2-chat-watches.md`.

## Changes from the plan, made during review and testing

- **Alert wording:** the event prompt asks for the alert directly. The planned "Tell the user if this is what they asked to be alerted about." made Haiku start every alert with "Yes, this is what you asked for". In a headless A/B with Haiku, the old line did that 3 out of 3 times. The new line gave direct alerts 6 out of 6 times, across arrivals, ended watches and errors. The spec §7.3 example is updated to match.
- **No approvals in event turns:** decided to keep, on review with Ethan. The trade-off is that a snapshot or `watch_stop` after an alert takes one more message from the user. Without it, a stray `y` or `n` while the user is typing could answer a prompt they never read, and `--yes` would auto-approve turns started by device data. The per-watch opt-in follow-up below covers a snapshot on alert, with consent given when the watch starts.
- **Reply merging:** event replies no longer merge into the previous reply. The plan's "append to the last assistant entry" fallback was removed. Speech is cancelled only for user turns, so an alert doesn't cut off a spoken answer.
- **Compact view:** a tool group stays whole across watch lines, so `watch_start` no longer shows as "1 unfinished".
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - At most 20 non-trigger notices are queued, and the rest are counted as omitted.
  - `noteWatchStart` drops statuses that `watch_start` already reported.
  - An ENDED that `watch_start` returned doesn't trigger a turn.
  - `/watches stop all` clears queued triggers.
  - Event turns don't scroll a reader who has scrolled up.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Speak alerts when voice is on; today they are shown, not spoken.
- Condense answered event turns, since long watches grow the conversation.
- Per-watch opt-in for actions on alert, such as "include a snapshot".
- Mention running watches in the `/clear` notice.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -race ./internal/cli/chat/ ./internal/cli/mcp/ ./internal/cli/agentservice/` passes. In chat, only the five `TestBackgroundProcess*` tests fail, and they fail on macOS at the base commit too, before any B2 change.
- [x] `go vet` is clean for chat, mcp, agentservice and commands; `gofmt -l .` is clean; `go build ./...` succeeds.
- [x] Per-task spec and quality reviews, plus a whole-branch review. Its findings are fixed or listed above.
- [x] On a Jetson Orin Nano with a Logitech Brio 101 and PR A's agent, using claude-haiku-5-5:
  - **Headless:** `wendy chat --yes --prompt "Watch the Brio camera and tell me if someone is at the door."` finished in 29 s. It ran `watch_sources`, then `watch_start` (label "front door", READY), then `watch_events` (`entered person 0.67`), then `watch_stop`, and replied "Yes, the Brio 101 detected a person at the door…". No campaign was left on the device.
  - **Interactive (Ethan):** "tell me when someone comes to the door", then two arrivals more than 30 s apart. Each one produced an event line and a reply Wendy gave without being asked. `watching: 1` showed, and `/watches` and `/watches stop all` worked. The only issue was the "Yes, this is what you asked for" opening, fixed above. No campaign was left on the device.
  - Cleanup when chat exits goes through B1's server shutdown, which was verified on the device in #2207: campaign removed within about 1 s on client close, and by the lease 51 s after `kill -9`.
  - The device was restored to agent 2026.10.05-134249 afterwards.

author: tunaycel
body:
OpenAPI 3.0 entity fields declared with `nullable: true` currently become non-nullable model types. Read the existing nullable-type conversion when building fields in both TypeScript and Go, so request and response fields carry the same `$ONE` representation as an OpenAPI 3.1 type list.

The conversion leaves untyped schemas open and adds null only once. The shared fixture covers primitive, object, array and composed fields through load, list, create and update; it also checks requiredness and that shared schema properties remain unchanged. Include rebuilt package/test output.

For simple scalar allOf collapse, nullable is determined from the original typed nodes before their facts are combined. An untyped nullable annotation cannot add null to another member's type, and a typed member that excludes null still excludes it. This follows the [OpenAPI 3.0.3 nullable rule](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.0.3.html#schema-object). The two existing annotation-only allOf expectations remain unchanged from upstream. This patch is not a complete schema-constraint validator.

Closes #153.

Validation:
- Negative control on unchanged upstream `96f0a99`: 44 of the 88 shared operation cases fail; the revised fix passes all 88 plus the fixture-presence check (89).
- Independent parser/guide/transformer builds reproduce a plain required nullable string becoming `$STRING` before the fix and `[$ONE, [$STRING, $NULL]]` after it. Controls cover plain strings, untyped nullable wrappers, typed nullable members and a parent type that excludes null.
- After the allOf refinement, `npm test`: 2,057 passed, 1 skipped, no failures; dependency-gate tests also passed (25).
- Go nullable and allOf tests passed.
- Current combined check with #171 after the allOf refinement: 2,070 TypeScript tests pass, one is skipped, and the targeted Go nullable/allOf/validator suites pass.
- Source-comment tests passed (10); dependency gate, model mirror check, Python prose gate and Vale (20 pages) passed.
- `make all` reaches the Go suite and fails on `TestGuideOverlayTypeErrorFails` on Windows. The identical failure reproduces in a separate, unchanged upstream-main worktree: an Aontu diagnostic retains an `apidef-model-` temporary path. This PR does not change that diagnostic path. External apidef-validate corpus tests skip because that sibling checkout is absent; no corpus-wide golden validation is claimed.

author: markhpc
body:
<!--  Thanks for your contribution to LMCache!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'Fixes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'Refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Each resident `NixlStoreObj` carries its own `threading.Lock`. In the measured CPython 3.12.3 environment, `threading.Lock` instances are GC-tracked, so each resident entry adds a long-lived tracked object.

The per-object lock was redundant: `pin_count` is only touched by the adapter, and every access can run under the adapter's existing `_lock`. This PR removes `NixlStoreObj._lock`, relies on the adapter lock for `pin_count`, and documents that invariant. It reduces one long-lived GC-tracked object per resident entry.

- `nixl_store_l2_adapter.py`, `nixl_store_dynamic_l2_adapter.py`: drop the `_lock` field and the `field` import; `increase_pin_count` / `decrease_pin_count` become plain methods (caller holds the adapter lock); the queued `_unlock_keys` now runs under `with self._lock:`.
- `docs/design/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/nixl_store.md`: state the locking invariant.
- Tests: replace the `time.sleep(0.1)` unlock wait with `_drain_scheduled_unlocks`, an event-loop barrier, in both adapter test files; extend the dynamic-adapter test; remove the structure test that only asserted the removed field.

Two commits: the lock removal, then the test change.

Measured by counting Python objects in the adapter process while storing entries (local test, fresh processes, fixed 128-object store batches). The counts are of the adapter's own objects, so they don't depend on the storage backend. Deltas are taken in the same process before and after the stores, so startup differences cancel:

| Resident entries | GC-tracked Δ (before → after) | `threading.Lock` Δ (before → after) |
|---|---|---|
| 256 | 2,691 → 2,435 | 384 → 128 |
| 1,024 | 8,835 → 7,811 | 1,152 → 128 |
| 2,048 | 17,027 → 14,979 | 2,176 → 128 |

In this harness the deltas fit exactly: tracked objects 643 + 8N before and 643 + 7N after; locks 128 + N before and 128 after (N = resident entries). The per-entry cost drops by one tracked object (−12.5% of the 8), and the per-entry lock is gone. The 128 locks that remain don't grow with N.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- **What is and isn't claimed.** This reduces the number of long-lived GC-tracked objects per resident entry. I have not yet measured a GC pause-time, RSS, or throughput change; the pause and RSS measurements were too noisy at these sizes to report.
- **Locking change.** `pin_count` is now protected only by the adapter `_lock`. `_unlock_keys` newly takes `_lock`, and it is only queued onto the event loop and never re-enters `_lock`. Deferred unlock now takes one batch-level adapter-lock acquisition where it previously took per-object acquisitions; I have no throughput measurement for that.
- **Test change.** The barrier avoids wall-clock timing by using FIFO event-loop ordering.
- **AI usage.** Developed with AI assistance (Opencode, Claude).

**If applicable**:

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests

author: alek07
body:
## Summary

Implements the imported Bandeja design in the Bandeja page, using the project's design tokens and the existing hand-rolled UI library.

The page (`frontend/pages/index.vue`) now renders:
- A summary card: a priority band bar plus four clickable stat tiles (Alto / Medio / Bajo / Evidencia insuficiente) that toggle the matching filter.
- A filter bar: mono search, a TVN/Banca modalidad segmented control, band and evidence selects, a sort select, and the `reglas` version chip.
- A dense row list: rank, mono id token, modalidad chip, serif title, dedup meta, the P score with its band chip, an explainable R·I·U·N·E breakdown, the evidence state, and the `Investigar, no publicar` flag shown when a high-band topic has insufficient evidence.
- No-results and empty states.

## Components

New primitives follow the repo convention of building on Reka UI — there is no shadcn-vue CLI wired into this hand-rolled design system, as documented in `Select.vue`:

- `components/ScoreBreakdown.vue` — the score-breakdown signature component (mini bars as the trigger, popover with the `P = 30R + 25I + 20U + 15N + 10E` decomposition).
- `components/ui/StateChip.vue` — the state-system pill, tokenized tones with soft and outline variants.
- `components/ui/Popover.vue` — a Reka UI popover wrapper matching `Select.vue`'s style.

`RankingTable.vue` is removed — it was dead after the replacement.

## Data mapping

Wired to the real `/ranking` response shape (P, components 0–1, weights, band, evidence_state, dedup, group_size). Two honest deviations from the static mock:
- Modalidad is the server scoring lens (the endpoint re-scores groups under it), so the segmented control triggers a refetch rather than a client-side "Todas" filter.
- Fields the backend does not provide (tema category, detection timestamp) are omitted rather than fabricated.

## Verification

- `bun run build` passes (exit 0); all new components type-check.
- Browser check with representative data: populated rows, the breakdown popover, amber replica dedup, the red investigate flag, full light/dark parity, and mobile stacking — no console errors, no horizontal overflow.

author: overblaze
body:
## What this does
Two buttons at the top of the **Features** tab.

**Add your own feature** — for a DM boon, a house rule, or anything from a book the app doesn't hold. You give it:
- a name, what it does in your own words, and where it comes from;
- whether it takes an action, bonus action or reaction;
- limited uses (how many, back on a short or long rest);
- dice buttons (label, dice, and whether it is damage, healing, temporary hit points or something else);
- flat bonuses to AC, speed, initiative, hit point maximum, attack rolls or damage rolls;
- a standing line for "In effect", and optionally a switch so the bonuses only count while it is on.

It then behaves like a book feature: a card on the Combat tab with Use and its dice, a counter that rests refill, and its bonuses named in each number's breakdown. It is labelled "your own" instead of a book page. Edit or delete it from its entry on the Features tab.

**Borrow a feature** — pick any class, then its features, a subclass, or an option list, and take one feature onto this character. It brings its own use counter, and the pool it spends if you don't have one (borrowing Stunning Strike brings a ki pool). Numbers that grow by level read your whole character level. "Give it back" removes it.

## What to click to test
1. Any character → Features → **Add your own feature**: name "Lucky Coin", 3 uses, a roll "Bonus" of 1d4, Armor Class 1 → Add. AC goes up by one (tap AC to see "Lucky Coin +1"); Combat shows the card with Use and the 1d4 button.
2. Edit it and type "lots" as dice: a notice says it can't be rolled, and it is left out when you save.
3. **Borrow a feature** → Martial Artist → Stunning Strike → Borrow it: it is listed as "Martial Artist (borrowed)" and a Ki pool appears on Combat.
4. Open it → **Give it back**; open Lucky Coin → Edit or delete → Delete. AC returns to what it was.

## Limits
- Bonuses are flat numbers; a custom bonus that scales with level or an ability is not offered yet.
- A borrowed feature's tracker (Hybrid Points, chords) is not brought along, only use counters and spent pools.
- Swapping a class's own features for others ("override") and a fully custom class are not built.

## Checks
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (835 passing, 14 new), `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, and a headless phone-width browser run of all four steps with no console errors.

body:
<!-- planwright:flight-record id=registry-test-leak-4c02052f home=pr -->
## Summary

The fleet test suites were writing into the operator's real fleet registry. A fleet worker exports its fleet home (`PLANWRIGHT_FLEET_STATE_DIR`), and `tests/test-fleet-dispatch-headless.sh` launched real headless workers without pinning a home of its own, so every run from a worker added about a dozen `headless-oneshot` records for `execution-backends:3`, pointing into test temp directories, that nothing ever retired. `tests/test-offload-dispatch.sh` had the same leak in two cases that skipped the suite's own sandbox. Those two cases left `@7 offload` records plus allocation-ledger and audit rows in the real home.

Each headless case now runs against its own fixture fleet home, set up by a new shared helper, `tests/lib/fleet-home.sh`. The suite also fails if the inherited registry names its temp root, and the offload cases now go through the sandbox. On top of that, `scripts/run-tests.sh` hands every test file a sentinel fleet home (the override always; plugin data and `CLAUDE_DIR` only when they are set), and fails any file that has created anything there by the time it exits. Under `mise run test`, a suite that forgets to pin a home therefore fails by name and never reaches a real home. `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` explains the rule and the helper.

The operator's real registry was not edited or cleaned. The leaked headless records, the two `@7 offload` records, and the offload allocation and audit rows are still there for the operator to remove. Two observations ride along: `tests/test-tower-loop-relay.sh` spins forever on main in this environment, and six suites fail identically on main and on this branch when run from a fleet worker. Both look environmental, not caused by this change.

## Verification

Reproduced first: with the fleet home pointed at a stand-in directory, the unfixed headless suite wrote 13 `headless-oneshot` records into it, the count the operator saw. A variant with the pin disabled fails the new leak assertion. With the fix, the stand-in stays empty and the suite passes.

Runner guard, test-first in `tests/test-run-tests.sh`: separate fixtures write a registry record through the override arm, the plugin-data arm and the writer arm, plus a dispatch marker, a ledger-only row, and a dangling link. Each failed to fail the run before its fix and fails it after. The inherited stand-in homes are never touched, a file that pins its own home passes, and unset arms stay unset. `tests/test-fleet-home.sh` covers the helper: pinning, the inherited registry surviving later pins, leak and non-leak records, refused pins, and the no-home case. A deliberately broken helper fails it.

Run through the branch's runner against the operator's real environment, about 70 fleet-touching suites created nothing in their sentinels except the offload suite, which is how its leak was found. The real registry gained no test records over the whole session; the two records it did gain were real tower dispatches.

Following the fleet's test-economy rule, only the suites covering the touched files ran locally (test-run-tests, test-run-tests-pool, test-fleet-home, test-fleet-dispatch-headless, test-offload-dispatch, test-obs-record), plus shellcheck, shfmt, markdownlint, the secret scan, and the cdpath, echo-safety, script-mode, link and observation checks, all clean. GitHub CI on this PR is the one full-suite run. The post-PR fixes (PS-8 to PS-10) were each written test-first and verified the same way, through the runner, on the suites they touch. One risk to watch there: the runner now gives CI a resolvable fleet home where it had none, so a suite that silently relied on registration failing in CI would now fail by name.

- **Flight:** `registry-test-leak-4c02052f` on `planwright/flight/registry-test-leak-4c02052f` · **Worker:** `tmux-flight-registry-test-leak-4c02052f`
- **Pending sign-off:** PS-1, PS-2, PS-3, PS-4, PS-5, PS-6, PS-7, PS-8, PS-9, PS-10 (see the collapsed checklist)

<details>
<summary>Flight record</summary>

### The ask

Quoted as the operator gave it, fenced so its markup stays inert.

```text
  Stop the fleet test suites writing the operator's real fleet registry.

  The operator's real fleet registry (the `registry` file under the planwright plugin data fleet home) gained about a dozen `headless-oneshot` records for `execution-backends:3`, each with a worktree path under a test temp directory (`/private/var/folders/.../T/tmp.*/state-h<N>/3` and `.../repo-h18/specs/execution-backends/.orchestrate/headless/3`). They were written within minutes of a worker running the fleet test suites on 2026-10-07 (first batch 2026-10-05). Most have no dispatch marker, so `scripts/fleet-registry-reconcile.sh` never retires them.

  Find the suite(s) whose cases register a headless worker without pointing the fleet home (and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA or whatever the registry path derives from) at a fixture directory, and fix them to use an isolated per-test fleet home. Add a guard so the suites fail if any case would write outside its own fixture home, for example a shared test helper that pins the home and an assertion over the real path's mtime or record count. Do not edit or clean the operator's real registry; leave that to the operator. The source observation rides the unmerged draft chore PR #600 (not on main), so do not look for it on your base (part 2).
```

### Route and grounds

author: darrenhuai
body:
#3376 made `UpdateLog.from_app_data` drop an embed update log that holds JSON of the wrong shape. Three other readers in `periodic_update.py` still parse the file with the raw `UpdateLog.from_dict(embed_update_log.read())`, and one of them runs first on the default path, so the guard only helps runs with `--no-periodic-update`.

With periodic update on (the default), `handle_auto_update` hits the bad log before `from_app_data` ever sees it. The app-data seeder logs the TypeError as `fail` with a traceback, then retries with `download=True` and pulls pip from PyPI even though nobody asked for a download. Offline it fails outright:

```console
$ echo '{"completed": null, "periodic": null, "started": null, "versions": {}}' > <app-data>/wheel/3.14/embed/3/pip.json
$ PIP_NO_INDEX=1 virtualenv venv
RuntimeError: seed failed due to failing to download wheels pip
```

`#3376`'s own test passed `do_periodic_update=False`, which is why it never reached this.

`add_wheel_to_update_log` and the background `_run_do_update` have the same unguarded read. All three now go through `from_app_data`, so a malformed log gets dropped with one warning wherever it's first read, and the reset log schedules a fresh periodic update the way a never-run log does.

The malformed-log cases are shared across the four entry points as `_MALFORMED_LOGS`. Each new test fails when its own call site is put back to `from_dict`. The full suite, ruff, and ty (3.9 and 3.14) pass.

Something I noticed but left alone: `test_periodic_update_skip` and `test_periodic_update_trigger` pass `os.environ, True` positionally into `(do_periodic_update, env)`, so the arguments are swapped. They only pass because `os.environ` is truthy. Happy to send that as a separate fix if you want it.

author: jungdaesuh
body:
This adds the JAX pieces for single-stage boozerQA optimization, on top of `BoozerSurfaceJAX` (#12).

- `NonQuasiSymmetricRatioJAX` takes `NonQuasiSymmetricRatio`'s arguments (`boozer_surface`, `bs`, `sDIM=20`, `quasi_poloidal=False`), with `bs` a `BiotSavartJAX`. It computes the ratio and its partial derivatives in one compiled program and uses the `BoozerSurfaceJAX` adjoint for the coil gradient. With native `Iotas` and `MajorRadius`, upstream's boozerQA composition runs on a JAX surface.
- `ExactSingleStageJAX` is an opt-in evaluator for the four-term boozerQA objective on an exact surface (unit weights, `G` as an explicit unknown). Each outer evaluation runs the Newton solve, the four terms and the adjoint as one compiled program, with the warm start passed in and returned. It uses the dense exact Newton from #12 (defaults: tolerance 1e-13, cap 40). If Newton doesn't converge, it returns native's failed-iterate gradient and the 1e3 value and keeps the incoming warm start. Singular systems still raise. Infinite iota or major-radius targets give native's inf values; a +inf length target stays inactive, as with native's max penalty.
- `examples/2_Intermediate/boozerQA_jax.py` runs upstream's NCSX boozerQA example with the drop-ins, or with `--fused`. CI runs both.

The tests compare both routes with native composition: values, coil gradients against native and against finite differences through re-solves, and failed solves. The fused evaluator is also checked with infinite iota and major-radius targets, against native at the same coil points along a BFGS run, and over a 3-iteration L-BFGS-B run. The drop-in BFGS test matches native for 3 iterations. Both check that new values don't recompile and that nothing transfers implicitly.

Feedback welcome.

author: paulwoitaschek
body:
## Summary

`Migration32to34` runs `db.query("SELECT * FROM BOOKMARK_TABLE_NAME")`. The constant isn't interpolated, so SQLite looks for a table literally named `BOOKMARK_TABLE_NAME` instead of `tableBookmarks` and the migration fails with `no such table`. Room has no destructive fallback configured, so anyone still on database version 32 can't open the database after upgrading.

The bug came in with 356d7e436 (April 2018), when the migration moved to `SupportSQLiteDatabase` and `db.query(BOOKMARK_TABLE_NAME, null, …)` became a raw SQL string. No other migration has the same pattern.

- Interpolate the table name: `"SELECT * FROM $BOOKMARK_TABLE_NAME"`.
- Add `Migration32to34Test`, following the existing `Migration39to40Test`/`Migration40to41Test` setup. It creates a version 32 bookmark table, runs the migration and checks that the bookmarks survive. It fails with `no such table: BOOKMARK_TABLE_NAME` without the fix.

Stacked on #4 (`bridge-handshake-and-animation-tools`), which is stacked on #2 and #1. The base branch is `bridge-handshake-and-animation-tools`, so this diff is only this batch. Merge #1, #2 and #4 first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

## Summary

**Expression controls and links**
- `addExpressionControl`: adds a slider, checkbox, colour, angle, point, 3D point, layer or dropdown control and returns the expression text that reads it. A control that fails partway is removed again.
- `getPropertyReference`: the expression text that reads any property (match names for transform and other fixed groups, names for effects, masks and shape groups).
- `linkProperty`: makes one property follow another with an expression, like the pick whip. Optional `factor` and `offset` (single-number properties only). Refuses different kinds of property or different comps, and restores the previous expression if After Effects rejects the new one.

**Camera and lights**
- `setCameraProperties`: one or two node, zoom, depth of field, focus distance, aperture, blur level, position, point of interest (`createCamera` already existed)
- `createLight` / `setLightProperties`: point, spot, parallel and ambient lights with intensity, colour, cone and shadow settings
- `getLayerInfo` now reports each layer's `type` (camera, light, text, shape, null, solid, precomp, footage)

**Backup**
- `backupProject`: copies the project file to a timestamped backup (default `~/Documents/ae-mcp-bridge/backups/`). It backs up the last *saved* state, since After Effects can't copy unsaved changes without a dialog. `saveFirst: true` saves the open project in place first, only on request. Refuses a project that was never saved.

## Testing

`npm run test:bridge -- --run-in-open-project` now has 158 checks. **The last run before the final commit was 153/158.** The camera, light and backup checks passed. The five failures were all in the expression-control code and are fixed in the last commit, but **that fix has not been re-run against After Effects yet**:
- An effect parameter's reference text wrongly included the "ADBE Effect Parade" group (`layer("X")("ADBE Effect Parade").effect("n")("Slider")`), which After Effects rejects. The group is now skipped, giving `layer("X").effect("n")("Slider")`. This caused three of the failures (the slider's reference text, and two `linkProperty` checks).
- A dropdown's handles went invalid after its menu items were set, because setting them rebuilds the effect. They are now re-fetched. This was the dropdown failure.

The remaining failure ("...and the linked opacity follows it") followed from the rejected link.

author: mehdehemmanuel-maker
body:
## What it does

"Take me to a go-kart track" (or "let's go karting", "I want to race karts") puts you in a kart at the back of a grid on a 546 m club circuit:
- 7 m wide (the CIK-FIA asks 6–8 m by circuit grade);
- 9 corners, the tightest an 8 m hairpin;
- red-and-white kerbs, grass, tyre walls;
- a start gantry with five lights and a timing board.

**The kart** (`src/nexus/karting.ts`)
- **Engine and drive:** a Honda GX270 (6.3 kW at 3,600 rpm, 19.1 N·m at 2,500 rpm: Honda's SAE J1349 figures) through a 3.2:1 chain, governed to about 59 km/h.
- **Handling:** a bicycle model, with front and rear tyres each slipping at their own angle and side forces that saturate at about 1.1 g.
- **Grip limits:** the rear shares its grip between drive and cornering (a friction circle). The brake is on the rear axle only, so it stops at about 0.5 g.
- **Spins:** past about 35° of slip every tyre slides against its own motion, so a spun kart slides to rest.

**The other drivers** follow the line at the speed each corner allows, √(μ g R), and brake in time for the next corner. The quickest laps in about 42 s, against about 40 s for a perfect lap at the grip's limit.

**Driving it**
- In a headset: the right trigger is the throttle, the left trigger the brake, and a stick steers. Your head is carried in the seat.
- On a keyboard: W/S and A/D, or the arrow keys.
- By voice: go, restart, practice, race N karts, lap times, get out or in, behind view, and "why did I spin" for the physics.

**Drawing** (`src/nexus/view/kart3d.ts`): the kart is drawn at rental-kart size, its bodywork rounded by the edge rules in `finish.ts`. Its wheel carries a dash showing speed, lap, position, last lap and best lap.

## Found by testing, fixed by cause

- **5 g in the slow-speed branch:** a test bounding the kart's true acceleration by μ g caught it at 49 m/s². Below 1.5 m/s the branch cut sideways speed by 20 % on every 2 ms step. Friction now removes it, at most μ g.
- **"let's go karting" was not read as a place:** the lead "let's" is stripped before the place check runs.
- **Tyre walls too heavy for a headset:** about 760k triangles, now about 250k.

## Tests

19 new tests in `tests/nexus/karting.test.ts`:
- track geometry, including clearance between parts of the track;
- engine torque and the governor;
- braking distance against v²/2a;
- true acceleration never past μ g, at three steering amounts;
- a spin comes to rest;
- grass;
- AI laps against the ideal lap, and the slower driver's margin;
- lap counting, bumps and race order;
- the place, and the ways people ask for it.

Gate: 131 files, 1,404 tests passing. Also run in the browser: the lights start the race, the AI karts lap with no wall hits, and the answers and camera views work.

## Not yet

Engine sound, weight shifting onto the outer tyres, and kerbs as bumps.

- Ship peak: 87.7M over the 14 days to 2026-10-07 (90M at the 2026-08-21 first deploy), so the margin is ~1.46x.
- Weekly check peak: 78-83M (BACKUP-063).
- OOM kills in the rpi3 journal over the same window: 0.

**Decision: option 3**
- Keep the cap, and treat an OOM kill as a reported backup failure.
- The ship unit has `OnFailure=kubelab-notify@%n.service` and `MemorySwapMax=0`, both read live on the rpi3. A kill therefore pages instead of thrashing the monitoring of record.
- Raising the cap (option 1) trades that clean failure for the swapping the cap exists to stop.
- Tuning restic's footprint (option 2) has no measured need yet.
- The comment names the trigger to revisit: a page naming an OOM kill, or a ship `MemoryPeak` past ~110M.

Comment-only change: no rendered unit changes and no deploy is needed.

## Knowledge
- Lesson: none: the finding was already recorded in BACKUP-044's verification.md. This PR only makes the comment match it.
- ADR: none: an operating parameter inside BACKUP-044's existing decision, not a new architectural one.
- Runbook: none: no procedure changes.

author: humble-little-bear
body:
## Summary

Stop `ckb miner` (and the CKB node) when offckb exits, whatever the exit path, and stop miners orphaned by an earlier run before a new devnet starts.

Fixes #512

## Root cause

`offckb node` spawns `ckb run` and `ckb miner` as ordinary children (not detached, no exit hooks). Child processes are not stopped when their parent dies. Only these exit paths stopped them:

- **Ctrl+C in a terminal:** works because the terminal sends SIGINT to the whole foreground process group.
- **`offckb node stop` in daemon mode:** works because it signals the daemon's process group.
- **A component exiting while offckb is alive:** works because the supervisor stops the rest.

Every other way offckb can die, the children keep running:

- `SIGTERM` or `SIGHUP` sent to the offckb PID only (`kill <pid>`, tool or IDE timeouts, wrappers), using Node's default action and so no cleanup
- a crash (uncaught exception, unhandled rejection), e.g. the RPC proxy failing to bind its port after the miner was already started
- `process.exit(0)` from the broken-pipe handler when stdout goes away
- with `--fiber`, the Fiber startup signal handler's `process.exit()` (it stopped FNNs but not CKB or the miner)
- `SIGKILL`, OOM kill or similar

In those cases the miner is re-parented to init/launchd (or a subreaper) and polls a dead RPC every second indefinitely. Nothing ever reaped such a miner. On the next start it would even resume mining against the new node as an extra miner.

## Fix

- **`src/util/child-lifetime.ts` (new):** `bindChildrenToProcessLifetime()` tracks the node and miner and sends them `SIGTERM` from a `process.on('exit')` hook. That hook fires on `process.exit`, a normal end, uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections. It also turns `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`/`SIGHUP` into `process.exit(128+n)` so the hook runs. When another handler owns the signal (the Fiber shutdown handlers), it defers to that handler, whose own `process.exit` still triggers the hook.
- **`src/devnet/stale-miner.ts` (new):** before launching the devnet, `reapStaleMiners()` lists processes (`ps` on POSIX, CIM via PowerShell on Windows). It stops only processes whose command line is exactly `<…/ckb|ckb.exe> miner -C <this devnet dir>` **and** whose parent is gone or no longer a Node process. The miner of a live offckb session is a direct child of its Node process, so it is never touched. It sends `SIGTERM` first and `SIGKILL` only if the process is still alive after 5s. Everything is best effort: a listing failure only logs at debug level and never blocks the start.
- **`src/cmd/node.ts`:**
  - Reaps stale miners and sets up the lifetime guard before spawning CKB. The spawn/supervise part moves into `superviseDevnet()` so the guard is removed if startup throws; the body itself is unchanged.
  - Stops the service if CKB or the miner already exited before the supervisor attached its `exit` listeners (possible during the Fiber startup await).
  - Adds `SIGHUP` to the Fiber shutdown handlers.
- **Tests:** `tests/stale-miner.test.ts` (command matching incl. paths with spaces and Windows quoting, parent rules), `tests/child-lifetime.test.ts` (exit hook, signal→exit codes, deferring, dispose), and three new cases in `tests/node-supervisor.test.ts` (reap before spawn, exit hook kills node and miner, component exited before the supervisor attached).
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/fix-orphan-miner.md` (patch).

## Before / after (reproduced on Linux)

Before (`develop`), `kill -TERM <offckb pid>`:
```
after SIGTERM to offckb pid:
 174798      52  …/bins/0.208.0/ckb run -C …/offckb-nodejs/devnet
 175250      52  …/bins/0.208.0/ckb miner -C …/offckb-nodejs/devnet
```
After stopping that orphan `ckb run`, the miner stayed and kept polling (as in the issue).

After (this branch):
```
# next start with the orphan miner from develop still running
Stopping stale CKB miner (PID 175250) left over from a previous offckb run.
Launching CKB devnet Node...
CKB devnet is ready at http://127.0.0.1:8114.

# kill -TERM <offckb pid>  → no ckb run / ckb miner left
# kill -HUP  <offckb pid>  → no ckb run / ckb miner left
# kill -INT  <offckb pid>  → no ckb run / ckb miner left
# node --daemon + node stop → no ckb run / ckb miner left

# kill -KILL <offckb pid> (uncatchable) → ckb run + ckb miner orphaned, PPID 52;
# once the orphan node is gone, the next start prints:
Stopping stale CKB miner (PID 191536) left over from a previous offckb run.
```

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`: pass. `pnpm fmt` leaves no diff.
- `pnpm lint`: 0 errors (1 pre-existing warning in `src/node/install.ts`).
- `pnpm test:ci`: 51/52 test files pass, 485 tests pass. The only failures are the 2 `isStoreLockHeld › with lsof` cases in `tests/fiber-lifecycle.test.ts`, which fail the same way on unmodified `develop` in my environment (no usable `lsof`); unrelated.
- Manual runs above on Linux x86_64 with CKB 0.208.0. macOS and Windows were not run: macOS uses the same `ps` path (BSD `ps` supports `-A -ww -o pid=,ppid=,args=` / `comm=`); the Windows listing is best effort and is skipped on any error.

## Notes / limitations

- `SIGKILL` cannot be handled. The miner left behind is reaped on the next start. An orphaned `ckb run` is deliberately **not** reaped: stopping a node process (and its DB) automatically is a bigger step, and the next start fails loudly in that case anyway.
- A `ckb miner -C <offckb devnet dir>` started by hand from a shell (parent not Node) counts as stale and is stopped when `offckb node` starts.

author: daniel-sarosi-gwc
body:
Closes #95

## Summary

Two operator-facing shell scripts under `scripts/` for routine cleanup of blitzlog-owned cloud artifacts:

- **`scripts/clean_ghcr.sh`** — delete `blitzlog-agent` package versions older than N days (default 2), scoped to one or more `--org` namespaces and a required `--image` filter. Direct fetch path for exact-match `--image` values bypasses the GitHub REST `GET /orgs/{org}/packages` list endpoint (which silently returns `[]` for some orgs even when specific packages exist).
- **`scripts/clean_amis.sh`** — deregister self-owned AMIs older than N days, then delete the EBS snapshots they own.

Both default to dry-run; `--yes` to apply. Both fail closed on missing auth, missing `--image` (GHCR only), or non-positive `--days`.

## What's new

- `scripts/clean_ghcr.sh` (executable, ~330 lines)
- `scripts/clean_amis.sh` (executable, ~175 lines)
- `tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py` (25 cases, all pass)

## Behavior details

### GHCR script

| `--image` value | Path |
|---|---|
| `blitzlog-agent` (exact) | Direct: `GET /packages/container/blitzlog-agent/versions` for each `--org` |
| `'blitzlog-*'` (glob) | List endpoint: `GET /packages?package_type=container` then filter by glob |

Both untagged intermediates **and** tagged versions older than N days are deleted (no special tag preservation). The `SEEN_VER` dedup key includes `api_root` so the same package in user and org namespaces don't collide.

### AMI script

- `--owners self` only. `--owners all` and `--owner-ids` are not accepted (foot-gun protection).
- Deregister AMI before deleting its snapshots.
- Region resolution: `--region` → `$AWS_REGION` → `aws configure get region`.

## Tests added

`tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py` covers:
- Scripts exist, are executable, parse cleanly under `bash -n`.
- Both default to dry-run; missing `--yes` never calls a destructive endpoint.
- Both validate `--days` as a positive integer.
- Both fail closed on missing auth (`gh auth status` / `aws sts get-caller-identity`).
- `clean_ghcr.sh` requires `--image`; refuses full-namespace wipes.
- `clean_ghcr.sh` routes exact `--image` to direct fetch and globs to the list endpoint.
- `clean_ghcr.sh` `SEEN_VER` dedup key includes `api_root`.
- `clean_ghcr.sh` `glob_to_regex` correctly produces anchored exact-match / glob / metachar-escaped regexes.
- `clean_amis.sh` deregisters before deleting snapshots.
- `clean_amis.sh` resolves region in the documented order.

## Local verification

```
ruff check .                              → All checks passed!
black --check .                           → All done! 26 files would be left unchanged
pytest tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py     → 25 passed
```

Live dry-run against `great-wall-connect/blitzlog-agent` (34 total versions):
```
$ ./scripts/clean_ghcr.sh --org great-wall-connect --image blitzlog-agent
==> summary
    packages scanned: 1
    versions flagged: 19    # 4 tagged + 15 untagged intermediates older than 2 days
    errors:           0
```

## Out of scope (intentional)

- Cross-region AMI cleanup loop (operator reruns with `--region` per env; safer than an automatic loop).
- Scheduled/cron wrapper. The list-endpoint quirk means a scheduled run would silently leave private packages untouched; better to keep these as one-shot operator tools.
- A `--keep-tagged` flag to preserve tagged versions regardless of age. The current behavior (delete anything older than N days, tagged or not) matches the issue's stated goal but is a one-line addition if we want it.

## Usage

```bash
# Dry-run
./scripts/clean_ghcr.sh --org great-wall-connect --image blitzlog-agent
./scripts/clean_amis.sh --region ap-east-1

# Apply
./scripts/clean_ghcr.sh --org great-wall-connect --image blitzlog-agent --yes
./scripts/clean_amis.sh --region ap-east-1 --yes
```

No deletions were performed against any real resource by this PR — only dry-runs.

author: sacredtrees
body:
opengpu.library now uses a driver when there is one, so OpenGPU batches reach the Cradle's command ring through ACRTG.gpu (amigachrome-guest) and are drawn by the runtime, not the 68k.

## What changes
- **Drivers.** The first time a DOS process asks opengpu.library anything, it looks in `LIBS:OpenGPU/` (ACRTG.gpu, PiStorm.gpu, AGA.gpu first, then any other `*.gpu`) and keeps the first driver whose `OGPU_DriverGet` (LVO -30, now written down in `include/opengpu/driver.h`) hands over a table. Every batch then goes to it. `OGPU_Query` answers for it (back end 1) and `OGPU_BackEndName(1)` names it. A plain task asking first gets the CPU until a process has asked.
- **Falling back.** A driver that returns `OGPU_ERR_DEVICE` is dropped: that batch and every later one run on the 68k. With no driver, nothing changes.
- **Golden scenes shared.** They move to `tests/golden_scenes.c`, so the host test and OpenGPUCheck draw the same ones. Checksums unchanged: de825f7b and 400d1333.
- **OpenGPUCheck** (`tools/ogpu_check.c`, built by `tools/build.sh`): on an Amiga it names the back ends, draws both golden scenes through the library and again on the 68k, checks all four, and times one batch both ways.

## Checked
- `tests/run.sh` on the host: 4873 checks pass, golden scene de825f7b, v1.1 scene 400d1333.
- On a scratch copy of the AmigaChrome Showcase instance (OS 3.2.3, AC090 68040, ACRTG with acrtg.card 2.3 and ACRTG.gpu), OpenGPUCheck reports back end 1 "ACRTG.gpu on the Cradle (PC's CPU)". Both scenes are right through the library and on the 68k. One batch (a 320 x 240 fill, a scaled composite and 20 lines) takes 2.12 ms through the ring and 2011 ms on the 68k.
- The same instance with the card 2.2 ROM and the deployed runtime: no driver, CPU back end, both scenes right.

Goes with amigachrome-guest (ACRTG.gpu) and amigachrome (acrtg.card 2.3 keeps the ring's place in video RAM).

author: deltawsierra
body:
Authority chain, follow-up gap 1: **`through_identity`, `performs` and reach are read as of dispatch, not live.** Follows #139 (part 5), which did the same for `under_policy` and `invokes`' approval, contract and route.

**The rule (owner's decision on this PR):** at dispatch, each hop reaches the verdict master's live rule would reach on the graph as it stood at dispatch.
- A contradiction then stays **broken** (`needs_remediation`), named as master named it.
- Only an edge simply not in force, with nothing contradicting it, reads unproven.
- No record reads `dispatch_state_unrecorded`. It is never read live instead.
- **Review round 1 (owner's decision):** a chain that records **no dispatch** is still broken by a contradiction in the graph as it stands, as on master. It is never proven by it. A component re-created or renamed since the dispatch reads unproven, never broken.

## What master does

Probed on `11366c8` with a scratch test (not committed) on the spine `_world`, for each of the three edges:

| Edge | Changed AFTER a proven effect | Removed BEFORE dispatch, restored after |
|---|---|---|
| identity (agent acts as svc-x → svc-admin) | `through_identity: broken ['acts_as_another']`, chain **broken** | chain **proven** (`declared_identity`) |
| reach (agent's tools → `[]`) | `invokes: broken ['unreachable']`, chain **broken** | chain **proven** (`declared_edge`) |
| action (server drops `customer:update`) | `performs: unproven ['permissions_undeclared']` | chain **proven** (`declared_permission`) |

An identity edit after a properly authorised effect held the deployment at `needs_remediation`. An effect made through an edge that was not there at dispatch read proven.

## Where the three hops read the graph, and what history existed

Mapped first. All of it is computed from the deployment's `Asset` rows as they stand (`load_graph`), and no history existed for any of it.
- **`_through_identity`:** the agent's declared `acts_as` edges, and its identity references discovery could not place (gaps). Gaps leave it unproven; another account breaks it.
- **`_reach`:** gaps about this tool, declared `invokes` edges, effective reach, inferred edges, and any tool gap. A graph fully resolved from the agent that does not reach the tool breaks it.
- **`_performs`:** which components declare their permissions and which permissions, over the identity, the chain's tool and the tools in the identity's effective reach. "All declare, none this one" breaks it. Plus the approval in force **now** for `within_approval`.

## The history

**`AuthorityEdgeVersion`** (migration `0059`), append-only: updates and deletes are refused, and an edge that returns is appended again. Each row is one piece of graph state appearing or disappearing (`in_force`), with the instant the platform noticed it (`noticed_at`), clamped so a stepped-back clock never reorders it. The rows record exactly the state the hops read, as defined by the pure function `authority_chain.graph_edges(graph)`: the state that contradicts a hop as well as the edge that proves it.

| kind | source → target | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `identity` | agent → account | a declared `acts_as` edge |
| `identity_gap` | agent → gap | an identity reference not placed cleanly (reference and reasons, as JSON) |
| `invokes` | agent → tool | a declared `invokes` edge |
| `reach` | principal → tool | effective access reaches the tool |
| `inferred` | component → tool | only an inferred edge joins them |
| `tool_gap` | agent → gap | a tool reference not placed cleanly |
| `declares` | component → "" | the component declares its permissions, possibly none |
| `action` | component → permission | a permission it declares |
| `component` | component → naming | the component exists, as named (kind, identifier and name, as JSON). Round 1: a contradiction is read only of components that are, as the chain names them now, the rows the history names |

- One `begun` row per deployment says from when the history covers it. A dispatch before that reads unrecorded, never "absent" and never live. Nothing is backfilled.
- The model is in `signals.DECISION_INPUTS`. The nine kinds are in the policy document, so they move the pin, and they are in the pin test's governing list.
- Append-only on instances **and on the queryset** (round 1): `update`, `bulk_update` and `delete` are refused, as in the `RepairContractQuerySet` pattern. Only the deployment's cascade, which runs through the base manager, removes rows.

**Write paths, each in the write's own transaction** (`assurance/edge_history.py`, `note_edges`):
- **`Asset` `post_save`**, when `update_fields` is absent or names a graph column (`kind`, `identifier`, `name`, `metadata`, `classification`, `deployment`, and since round 1 `provider`). A save that moves an asset to another deployment notes both.
- **`Asset` `post_delete`**, except on a deployment's own cascade.
- **`derive_assets` (scan ingest).** Its endpoint writes are bulk and no signal sees them, so per-save notes are suppressed inside it and the edges are noted once at its end (`edges_noted_once`). No half-reconciled graph is recorded.
  - **Ingest query budget:** the existing 12 still holds, unchanged. The 40-endpoint reconciliation takes 11 queries (8 on master): the note reads the assets once, with their providers, on a copy of the deployment.
- **Backstop:** `refresh_stored_decisions` calls `note_edges_quietly` beside `note_approvals_quietly`, for a write no signal saw. It never raises.
- **No other `Asset` writer** exists outside tests and migrations. Searched: `_get_or_refresh`, `_settle_legacy_rows`, `derive_assets`, the coverage stamp (writes only `assessed_at`, notes nothing), and the admin, which saves through the signals.

## The rule (`assurance/authority_chain.py`, still pure)

Each graph hop is read at the cited observed effect's signed `dispatch.dispatched_at`, against the last change at or before it.

| Hop | Proven | Broken (contradiction, master's code) | Unproven |
|---|---|---|---|
| `through_identity` | `identity_in_force_at_dispatch` (this account then) | `acts_as_another` (another account then, not this one) | `identity_unresolved` (an identity reference unplaced then); `identity_not_in_force_at_dispatch` (no identity then) |
| reach (in `invokes`) | `reach_in_force_at_dispatch` (a declared `invokes` edge or effective access then) | `unreachable` (none of that, over a graph fully resolved from the agent then) | `dangling_edge` (a reference to this tool unplaced then); `reach_not_in_force_at_dispatch` (only an inferred edge, or tool references unplaced then) |
| `performs` | `action_in_force_at_dispatch` (the identity, its tool, or a tool it reached then declared the permission then) | `permission_not_declared` (all of them declared their permissions then, none this one) | `action_not_in_force_at_dispatch` (not all declared then) |

- Every proving reading cites the history row and its instant.
- **Re-created or renamed components (round 1).** Before a hop returns `acts_as_another`, `unreachable` or `permission_not_declared`, every component the contradiction names must have existed at the dispatch as it is named now: the actor, the tool, the account, the identity and the chain's tool. If one did not, the hop reads unproven (`*_not_in_force_at_dispatch`), saying so. That covers a component re-created (a new row), renamed, swapped, or deleted and now dangling where its reference named it then.
- **No dispatch recorded (round 1).** The graph hops read `dispatch_state_unrecorded`, and the graph as it stands never proves them. Where the graph as it stands contradicts a hop as master's live rule did, the hop is broken with master's code: `acts_as_another`, `unreachable`, `permission_not_declared`, and `outside_approval` against the approval as it stands (its latest recorded version). The detail says it was read from the graph as it stands because no dispatch is recorded. A chain that records a dispatch the edge

## Summary

- This is task T2 of the approved spec `docs/specs/gh532-first-proof-evidence-rules.md` (decision: KEL-78 option (b)). A run without verified containment is now recorded as an explicit `unverified` authority profile. It is never dropped, and it is never read as strict or legacy evidence. This has to land before X01-T4 (#566), whose validator must parse `unverified` records.
- What is added: `AuthorityProfile::Unverified`, its `parse_authority` arm, `AuthorityProfile::as_str` as the one variant-to-string map, and `Scoreboard::authority_profile()`. The accessor is `Some` only when every contributing record shares one profile.
- How `score()` uses it: identity consistency now comes from the same profile-agreement fold. The gate and the accessor therefore share one rule, so a mixed board can neither publish a percentage nor be reported under one record's profile.
- Unchanged: the record `schema` stays `keld.compat.evidence/v1` (§4.4), the `claim` format is unchanged, and the existing harness records keep `legacy_sandbox_off`.
- Docs: the reporting rule is rule 7 in `docs/engineering/compat-scoreboard.md`, and `llms-full.txt` was regenerated.

## Spec refs

- `docs/specs/gh532-first-proof-evidence-rules.md` §3 AC13–AC15, §4.4, §5 (T2 boundary) and §6 T2.
- `docs/specs/kel74-compat-evidence-schema.md` §4.1 (the `authority_profile` row already lists `unverified`) and §4.3 rules 4, 6 and 7, all consumed unchanged.
- No boundary change. No handle ownership, crash ownership or principal minting moves.

## Review gates

- unsafe: none
- public API: yes, in `keld_compat::evidence`:
  - `AuthorityProfile::Unverified` is a new variant on an exhaustive public enum. A downstream exhaustive `match` would break, but the workspace has none.
  - `AuthorityProfile::as_str` is new.
  - `Scoreboard::authority_profile()` is new.
  - `Scoreboard` fields stay private (`scoreboard_struct_fields_are_not_public`).
- permission model: none
- dependency addition: none
- wire protocol: none, because kipc is unchanged. The spec §8 format review applies: the versioned JSON ledger's `authority_profile` vocabulary widens inside v1 without a `schema` bump. The rationale and falsifier are in §4.4. A pre-T2 parser fails closed with `KELD-COMPAT-005`.

## Tests

New colocated unit tests in `crates/keld-compat/src/evidence.rs`. Every oracle uses literal strings and variants, never `as_str` or `parse_authority` output.

- `unverified_is_never_merged_with_another_profile` (AC13): `unverified` is paired with each of the four other profiles, in both cell orders. Each pairing gives `complete == false` and `unweighted_percent == None`, and the unverified run is still counted (`passed == 2`, `missing == 0`). A same-profile control board is complete with `Some(100)`, which shows that only the profile difference withholds the result.
- `scoreboard_reports_unverified_only_for_an_all_unverified_board` (AC14):
  - An all-`unverified` board gives `Some(Unverified)`, which renders as `"unverified"`.
  - Each uniform other-profile board gives `Some(<that variant>)`.
  - Every mix, in both cell orders, gives `None`.
  - The claim is exactly `2/2 of showcase corpus phase2-hello@<digest> (primary_workflow)` and contains neither `strict_bun` nor `legacy_sandbox_off`.
- `contributing_identity_requires_one_profile_digest_and_engine`: added after the isolated review, and it pins the refactored identity gate. Each case differs in one dimension only. It covers all 20 ordered pairs of distinct profiles (`None`, not complete, no percentage), a digest-only mismatch, an engine-only mismatch, and foreign-kind and out-of-denominator records, which must contribute no profile.
- `authority_vocabulary_round_trips_and_unverified_is_distinct` (AC15): all five strings parse to their own variant inside a v1 record, `as_str` returns the same string, and `Unverified` is unequal to each of the other four. `EVIDENCE_SCHEMA` is the literal `keld.compat.evidence/v1`. Four unknown strings (`verified`, `Unverified`, `unverified_sandbox_off`, `""`) each fail with `KELD-COMPAT-005`.

Red first: before the implementation, the new tests failed to compile (9 `E0599` errors: no `Unverified`, `as_str` or `authority_profile`).

Negative controls: 26 mutations were applied one at a time with a script, and the source was restored byte-for-byte afterwards (sha256 checked). All 26 are caught on the tip.

| Mutation | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| `parse_authority` maps `"unverified"` to `LegacySandboxOff` | AC13, AC14, AC15 |
| `parse_authority` maps `"unverified"` to `StrictBun` | AC13, AC14, AC15 |

| `parse_authority` accepts a sixth string (`"Unverified"`) | AC15 |

| `"unverified"` arm deleted (pre-T2 parser) | AC13, AC14, AC15 |

author: blurbery
body:
## Problem

Related issue: #2092
Validation tasks: none

If a viewer picks a subtitle the version they're playing can't show, and the item's other version doesn't have that subtitle either, Silo moves them to the other version anyway and turns the subtitle off. They lose the better picture and still get no subtitle.

For example, a 4K HDR10 HEVC file with an English PGS track, and a 1080p SDR sibling without one. The client direct plays the 4K file but can't draw PGS, so the subtitle would need burning in, and the server can't re-encode the HDR picture (the same happens with 4K transcoding turned off). Starting with the subtitle on, or turning it on mid-playback, lands on a 1080p H.264 transcode with subtitles off. Playing the 4K file with subtitles off gives the same subtitle result with the original picture and no transcode.

## Approach

**Root cause.** When the requested file is refused, the start and replan paths try the item's other versions. A sibling that keeps the subtitle wins; otherwise the first sibling that plays with the subtitle dropped is used (#552). That fallback doesn't look at why the requested file was refused. `subtitle_conversion_unsupported` is the planner saying the subtitle was the problem, so the requested file would play without it, but the fallback still prefers a sibling.

**Fix.** When the requested (or, on a replan, the effective) file's refusal is `subtitle_conversion_unsupported` and the only siblings that play drop the subtitle, the server now plans that file again with the subtitle cleared and uses that plan if it succeeds. If it doesn't, the old fallback applies.

Some things stay the same:

- A sibling that keeps the subtitle still wins.
- A refusal for any other reason (4K policy, HDR decode, an unreadable file) still falls back to a version without the subtitle.
- A single-version item still gets the `subtitle_conversion_unsupported` refusal.
- In a replan that stayed on the active alternate only to keep its subtitle, playback still returns to the requested edition without it. That edition is the picture the viewer asked for.

The plan still carries a `subtitle_track_unavailable` warning. When the subtitle is on the file but can't be shown, the message now says so ("The selected subtitle cannot be shown on this file; playing without it.") instead of claiming the track isn't on the file. The code is unchanged, so clients don't need anything new.

This only changes which version the server picks. The response shape is the same, so neither silo-apple nor silo-android needs a change. jellycompat doesn't use this fallback, because Jellyfin clients choose the media source themselves.

## Validation

**Tests.** New handler tests cover the start path and a track-change replan, both with the 4K HDR file, the English PGS and a 1080p sibling without it. They fail on `main` (the effective file is the 1080p sibling) and pass with the fix. A third test covers an output change after the active alternate was kept for its subtitle: the server still returns to the requested edition. It fails without the requested-edition guard.

Run on `ea8c9f4b4` (macOS):

- `go test ./internal/api/handlers/ -count=1`: pass.
- `go test ./internal/playback/ -count=1`: everything passes except 34 hardware-encoder probe tests (VideoToolbox, NVENC, QSV, VAAPI) that fail the same way on `main` on this Mac.
- `make lint-changed`: 0 issues.
- CI on `ea8c9f4b4`: all required checks pass ([run](https://github.com/Silo-Server/silo-server/actions/runs/37725631944)): Go test, Go integration, Go lint, Go DB pins, Go DB external auth, repository checks.

**Benchmarks.** Not applicable. This changes which version is chosen, not how fast planning runs. The extra planner call only happens in this fallback, after the sibling search has already failed to keep the subtitle.

## Evidence

Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/pr-2081/

The excerpt below is the same data.

Trimmed `playback_plan` for the same two requests, from the new tests' fixture: file 42 is the 4K HDR10 HEVC file with the English PGS, file 84 is the 1080p SDR sibling without it. Before is `main` at `ca186fe3a`, after is this branch.

```
start with the English PGS selected
  before: effective_media_file_id 84, delivery server_transcode_hls, h264 1080p sdr,
          transformations video_to_h264 + audio_to_aac, subtitle off,
          warnings evidence_insufficient_for_direct,
                   subtitle_track_unavailable ("The selected subtitle track is not on this file; starting without it.")
  after:  effective_media_file_id 42, delivery original_http, hevc 2160p hdr10,
          no transformations, subtitle off,
          warning subtitle_track_unavailable ("The selected subtitle cannot be shown on this file; playing without it.")

track change turning the English PGS on (session started on file 42)
  before: effective_media_file_id 84, server_transcode_hls, h264 1080p sdr, subtitle off,
          same two warnings as above
  after:  effective_media_file_id 42, original_http, hevc 2160p hdr10, subtitle off,
          subtitle_track_unavailable ("The selected subtitle cannot be shown on this file; playing without it.")

output change after the 4K alternate was kept for its PGS (requested 1080p file 84 lacks it;
the new output can't draw PGS), unchanged by this PR
  before: effective_media_file_id 84, server_transcode_hls, subtitle off,
          subtitle_track_unavailable ("The selected subtitle track is not on this file; starting without it.")
  after:  identical
```

## Risks

The fallback plans the refused file one extra time, only in this case. Clients that show the warning message will see the new wording.

## Checklist

- [x] I read and can explain the complete diff.
- [x] This pull request addresses one concern.
- [x] The Evidence section shows every change a user can see, or says there is none.

## AI Disclosure

- Harness: Claude Code (Claude desktop app)
- Tool(s): Claude Code
- Model(s): claude-opus-5-5
- Involvement: AI-assisted. I directed the task and designed the work.
- Adversarial review: A separate Claude Code subagent (claude-opus-5-5) reviewed the diff read-only, checking:
  - whether both paths re-plan with the same file, request, audio index and settings as the base plan;
  - other sources of `subtitle_conversion_unsupported`;
  - warning handling;
  - whether the tests could pass for the wrong reason.

  It found three problems:
  - a replan that kept the active alternate for its subtitle would no longer return to the requested edition;
  - the helper's comment overstated what the refusal guarantees;
  - the warning claimed the track wasn't on the file.

  All three are fixed: the requested-edition guard has its own test, the comment is corrected, and the warning now says the subtitle can't be shown.
