author: mattdhill
body:
The SDK 3.0.3 migration, plus the primary-URL behavior it makes available.

- **start-sdk 3.0.3.** The lock is resolved against the live registry (`npm audit` 0). The toolchain the SDK now supplies is dropped, and `.prettierrc` names the SDK's shared config.
- **`config.json` is `z.looseObject`.** Under 3.0.1+ a `z.object` shape deletes undeclared keys on every write; `seedFiles` merges the file on every init.
- **Dependencies:** an empty `sdk.Dependencies.of()` builder, passed to `buildManifest` and `setupInit`.
- **Set Primary URL uses `sdk.setupPrimaryUrl`, and keeps its action id.**
  - The choice stays in `config.json`'s `primaryUrl`, so upgraders keep their value and are not prompted while it is still published.
  - n8n is given `bestUsable` for `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL` and `N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL`. A chosen address that disappears falls back to the preferred address (a public domain, HTTPS first, else `.local`) and comes back when the address does; before, init overwrote the choice with `.local` for good.
  - `bestUsable` only re-runs main when the resolved URL changes, so adding an unrelated address does not restart n8n — the concern that kept the old flow out of main.
  - An `important` task asks for a choice while none is valid, including on a fresh install, where n8n runs on the preferred address until it is answered.
  - The Web UI nominates the primary URL as `preferredLauncherAddress`, so Open UI opens it.
- **Reset Owner Password asks for confirmation.** It replaces the owner password on every run, so it now carries a warning naming that.
- **Release notes** cover only this revision's changes, since `2.35.3:0` is already on community-prod.
- Workflows synced to the package template (`ready_for_review`, `pr-retarget.yml`); `AGENTS.md`, README and instructions updated.

Review follow-ups on this branch:
- docs: describe SDK 3's primary-URL fallback order
- docs: Open UI prefers the primary URL only where the connection can reach it
- docs: release notes cover only this revision's changes

author: blurbery
body:
## Problem

Related issue: N/A
Validation tasks: changes #1143 C1 and C2; changes #1144 C1 and C3; changes Silo-Server/silo-apple#307 C1 and C3; changes Silo-Server/silo-apple#308 C1 and C3; changes Silo-Server/silo-android#317 C1 and C3; changes Silo-Server/silo-android#318 C1 and C3 (all passed on build 941)

Two different people with the same name can end up as one person in Silo. When a credit comes in and neither its TMDB ID nor its IMDb ID is stored yet, `FindOrCreate` and `BatchFindOrCreate` fall back to a case-insensitive name match and attach the credit to whoever already has that name, even when the two carry different provider IDs. One actor's films then appear on a namesake's person page, and the second person's provider IDs are thrown away.

This change lets the name fallback match only when the two share a provider ID, or when neither has any.

The person filmography and name search cases listed above passed with provider-identified fixture people. Those resolve by stored TMDB or IMDb ID before the name fallback runs, so their outcomes should still meet the criteria. Only namesakes with different provider IDs and name-only placeholders now resolve differently, which can change a filmography or add a same-name search result. Those cases should be re-checked after merge.

I've run this on my server since August. It has 1,127 names that belong to more than one TMDB person (2,271 people in total). Under the old fallback, each of those people whose provider IDs weren't stored yet when its first credit arrived would have been merged into the first person with that name.

Root cause: phase 3 of `BatchFindOrCreate`, and the last lookup in `FindOrCreate`, select by `LOWER(name)` alone and take the first match without looking at provider IDs.

## Approach

- The name lookups now read the candidates' provider IDs (TMDB, IMDb, TVDB, Plex GUID). `canResolvePersonByName` accepts a candidate only when the names match, no provider ID conflicts, and either the two share at least one provider ID or neither has any.
- This changes what happens to name-only placeholders. A person created from a credit without IDs, for example from an NFO file, is a placeholder.
  - An identified person no longer takes over a placeholder with the same name; it gets its own row.
  - A name-only credit no longer attaches to an identified person; it reuses an existing placeholder or creates one.
  - So a library with both kinds of credit for one person now has two rows for them, where before it had one. On my server that's 34 placeholders that share a name with an identified person, out of 152,101 name-only people.
- No API or client change. The native API and jellycompat read the same people rows, so the apps need nothing and no `docs/*-api.md` changes.
- Lookups by stored TMDB or IMDb ID run first and are unchanged. A shared TVDB ID or Plex GUID still resolves through the name fallback.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/catalog/ -count=1`: pass.
- `TestCanResolvePersonByName` is a unit test of the rule. It covers a shared TMDB or TVDB ID, two placeholders, disjoint IDs, IDs from different providers, an identified person meeting a placeholder, and different names with a shared ID.
- `TestPersonNameFallbackKeepsNamesakesApartPostgres` is a new database contract, listed in `scripts/ci/db-contracts.txt`. Through `FindOrCreate` and `BatchFindOrCreate`, it checks that:
  - a namesake with another TMDB or IMDb ID gets its own person;
  - a shared TVDB ID resolves to the stored person;
  - a second name-only credit reuses the placeholder.

  Against a migrated local PostgreSQL 18 database it passes on this branch, along with the other person database tests in `internal/catalog`. With `main`'s `person_repo.go` it fails: "FindOrCreate merged a namesake with another TMDB ID into person …".
- `go vet ./internal/catalog/` and `make lint-changed`: clean.
- On my server, the same change has run since August as part of my fork.
- CI on `b7c75b314`: [passed](https://github.com/Silo-Server/silo-server/actions/runs/37725634341), including `Go DB pins`, which runs the new contract and fails on a listed test that is missing or skipped.

## Benchmarks

Not applicable. The name lookups read four more columns from rows they already select, and still use the same `LOWER(name)` predicate.

## Evidence

Which person a credit lands on is visible on item and person pages, but I have no before-and-after capture from an upstream build: that needs a deploy of `main` and of this branch against the same data. What I can show is the database test above, which fails on `main` and passes here, and the counts from my server, which runs my fork at `6ce7fb5cc` with this change.

Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/pr-2082/

## Risks

- More person rows: a placeholder and an identified person with the same name stay separate, as described above.
- Existing merged namesakes stay merged. This only changes how new credits resolve.
- #1143 C1 and C2 passed with provider-identified fixture people. Those resolve by stored TMDB or IMDb ID first, which this doesn't change. A library that mixes name-only and identified credits for the same person can now show two people with that name in search.
- #1699, #1730 and #1733 also change `person_repo.go`, in the refresh and update functions and a comment near `FindOrCreate`, not in the name lookups. They may need a rebase but shouldn't conflict in logic.

## Checklist

- [x] I read and can explain the complete diff.
- [x] This pull request addresses one concern.
- [x] The Evidence section shows every change a user can see, or says there is none.

## AI Disclosure

- Harness: Claude Code (desktop app); the change itself first came from an OpenAI Codex session on my fork
- Tool(s): Claude Code, OpenAI Codex
- Model(s): claude-opus-5-5 (port, database test and description); the Codex model used on the fork commit was not recorded
- Involvement: AI-assisted
- Adversarial review: n/a. This ports a change my fork has run since August. I checked that `main`'s ID and name lookups in both functions are unchanged since then (only the enrichment step after them changed), and added the database contract.

AI-assisted with Claude Opus. I directed the task and designed the work.

author: ajianaz
body:
## What
CLI part of #1332 (validated Cora-scan findings, medium). Each was re-checked against the code first.
- **recall via server**: `POST /recall` has no field for `--strategy/--salience/--recency/--explain/--related/--depth/--context/--content-format/--where`; they were dropped silently, so the same command ranked or printed differently depending on whether a server was running. They now return the existing `"unsupported"` signal so the command runs against the local store; `--type/--enrich/--pack/--budget/--exclude-ids` (which the server does support) are forwarded.
- **list --entity/--category**: filtering ran on one already-paginated page. `--limit/--offset` now apply to the matches (paged scan of 200 rows).
- **doc list --tree** printed roots only (children were looked up among the roots). Now renders the whole forest, with a cycle guard.
- **doc export**: honours `--output` (it was ignored), the namespace (hard-coded `None`), and exports every document (stopped at 1000; core clamps `limit` to 1000). New `Uteke::doc_list_page` / `Store::list_documents_page` (stable order, id tie-break). JSON export is now an array of full documents (superset of the old summaries).
- **upgrade**: stages and verifies the CLI and both companions before installing any; a broken `uteke-serve` used to leave a new CLI next to the old server. Also fixed a misplaced doc comment from #1338.
- **verify-checksums**: line chosen by exact file name instead of substring.
- **batch import**: the "5 consecutive errors, zero success" bail-out counted the documents imported earlier, so it never fired; it now tracks the extraction loop only.
- **onboard**: the namespace is escaped in the generated TOML (quotes/newlines used to break out or inject keys); the TOML builder is now a pure function with round-trip tests.
- **migrate_content**: flat legacy keys are only recognised before the first `[section]`; a `model` inside `[extraction]` used to be moved to the embedding table and `[store]`/`[embedding]` were emitted twice.

## Why
Findings of the v0.19.1 review (#1332). Most are silent wrong-output or invalid-config bugs rather than crashes.

## Testing
- 22 new tests across the 8 items; the `migrate_content` ones fail on the old code. The `upgrade` test installs a bundle with a broken companion and asserts the installed binaries and staging files are untouched.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean; `cargo test --workspace` green (cli 109, core 643); vecq-only core build green (640).
- Not covered: end-to-end `uteke recall` against a live server for the fallback (the decision is unit-tested; the existing `unsupported` fallback in `main.rs` is unchanged); an upgrade of a real release archive.

Refs #1332

## Task
OPS-03 (follow-up to #82) — `create-vm.sh` looked hung with `--generate-key`

## What changed
- On a real host, `./create-vm.sh --generate-key` printed nothing for minutes: it was downloading the ~400 MB Debian image with `curl -s`. Each step now prints a `create-vm: …` line on stderr (download, checksum, key, create, start), and the download shows a progress bar when stderr is a terminal. `--dry-run` output is unchanged: commands only.
- The key is now made **after** the download and checksum, just before `qm create`. Before this, Ctrl-C during the download left `riot-proxy-dev-<id>` behind, and the retry (same next free id) stopped with "already exists". The existing-key check still runs before the download, so a real clash still fails fast.
- The closing hint showed only the laptop key path (`~/.ssh/<name>-<vmid>`), so `ssh -i` from the Proxmox host offered no key and got "Permission denied". It now prints the host command with the full key path (`/root/.ssh/riot-proxy/…`), the `scp` + `chmod 600` + `ssh -i` commands for another machine, and a one-liner that pulls the VM's IP out of `qm guest cmd`. With a static `--ip` it uses the real address instead of `<vm-ip>`. Both READMEs say the same.
- New `--image-dir` option (default unchanged, `/var/tmp/riot-proxy-images`), used by the tests.
- ADR-072 gains a bullet.

## How it was tested
- [x] unit tests added/updated: `deploy/proxmox/test.sh` — dry-run puts `ssh-keygen` after `curl`; a real run against fake `id`/`qm`/`pvesh`/`pvesm`/`curl`: a failed download leaves no key, the download is announced, a good run makes the key and passes it to `qm set --sshkeys`, every step is reported, and a second run refuses before downloading; the login hint has the full host key path, the copy-then-login for another machine, and the real address with a static `--ip`. The ordering and announcement tests fail against the old script.

author: mastewalb
body:
# Summary

Adds a way to reject unknown JSON fields for a single bind call, without turning on the process-wide `EnableJsonDecoderDisallowUnknownFields()`.

Today strictness is all-or-nothing: the global flag makes every JSON binding strict, so an app can't have one strict endpoint and one lenient one.

## Changes

- `binding.StrictJSON`: a JSON binding that always calls `DisallowUnknownFields()` on the decoder. It still honours `EnableDecoderUseNumber` and runs validation.
- `c.ShouldBindStrictJSON(obj)` and `c.BindStrictJSON(obj)`: shortcuts mirroring `ShouldBindJSON` / `BindJSON`.
- `docs/doc.md`: the new methods are added to the bind method lists.

Existing behaviour is unchanged: `binding.JSON` and the global flag work as before.

```go
var req CreateUserRequest
if err := c.ShouldBindStrictJSON(&req); err != nil {
	c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": err.Error()})
	return
}
```

Related
Refs #4335
Same goal as #4642, which has merge conflicts and does not build with -tags nomsgpack. This PR declares StrictJSON in binding_nomsgpack.go as well.

## Testing
New tests cover unknown top-level and nested fields, validation still running, abort vs. no-abort behaviour, and binding.JSON staying lenient. `go test ./...` passes with default tags, `-tags nomsgpack`, `-tags go_json`, `-race` and `-tags sonic`.

# Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Open your pull request against the `master` branch.

- [x] Tests are added or modified as needed to cover code changes.

author: viralbshah
body:
Fixes #1012. `map!` and `broadcast!` into a sparse array copied an input that has no stored entries, and `map!` with two or more inputs allocated whatever the inputs were.

**Before**:

```julia
using SparseArrays
A = sparsevec(Int[], Float64[], 10); X = similar(A)
map!(sin, X, A); map!(sin, X, A)
@allocated map!(sin, X, A)          # 64
M = spzeros(10, 12); Y = similar(M)
map!(sin, Y, M); map!(sin, Y, M)
@allocated map!(sin, Y, M)          # 224
@allocated broadcast!(sin, Y, M)    # 224, after the same warmup

P = sparse([1, 3], [2, 4], [1.0, 2.0], 10, 12); Q = sparse([1, 4], [2, 5], [1.0, 2.0], 10, 12)
map!(+, Y, P, Q); map!(+, Y, P, Q)
@allocated map!(+, Y, P, Q)         # 384
```

**After**: `0` for all four.

Empty buffers share one `Memory`, so `Base.mightalias(X, A)` is `true` for any `A` with an empty `rowval`/`nzval`, and `Base.unalias` copied it. The entry points now compare the buffers of the input with the destination one by one: a buffer with entries through `Base.mightalias`, an empty one by identity, so `map!(f, A, A)` on an empty `A` is still unaliased. The pattern of a fixed array is skipped as before, since it is not written.

The second allocation was in the same helper: `_unaliasargs(C, As...)` only passes `As` on to `map`, so Julia did not specialize it on the argument tuple and it built the result tuple dynamically for two or more inputs. It now takes `Vararg{Any,N}`, which forces the specialization. Nothing was copied in that case; broadcast was not affected.

The test in `test/higherorderfns.jl` that failed on Julia CI no longer draws a random array on `main`, so it is not flaky there; Julia's pinned copy still has the `sprand` version, and the SparseArrays bump picks up both changes. This does not need a backport.

author: lix42
body:
Implements `docs/tasks/web-msg.md`. Every rule for what a key means now lives in one backend-neutral function in the core, which the native build uses now and the web build will use next. **Key behavior is unchanged.**

## What's new: `crates/core/src/input.rs`
- **`Key { code, ctrl, alt }`** with the core's own small `KeyCode` (`Other` covers anything the calculator doesn't use). There's no `meta` field: the web build drops Cmd chords before it builds a `Key`, and terminals never report Cmd.
- **`Msg`**: `Apply(Action)`, `MoveFocus(Dir)`, `ActivateFocused`, `EnterQuickMode`, `LeaveQuickMode`, `CycleLayout`, `ResumeAuto`, `ToggleTheme`, `Copy`, `Quit`.
- **`key_to_msg(key, quick_mode)`** holds the four rules in order. This is the part to look at most closely:
  1. Ctrl-C quits. It's checked before the bare `c`, which clears.
  2. Quick-mode is checked before navigation. Esc leaves the mode whatever the modifiers. With no Ctrl/Alt, a mapped char types its button, and an unmapped nav letter (`h`) does nothing while arrows still navigate. Ctrl/Alt chords fall through.
  3. Navigation applies only with no Ctrl/Alt.
  4. Commands are not modifier-gated; anything else goes to `key_to_action`.
- **`apply_msg`** handles every `Msg` with no catch-all. `Copy` does nothing there because each entry point intercepts it (the clipboard is platform code), and a test pins that. `Quit` sets `app.should_quit`.
- **`activate`** moved over unchanged, ordering comments included. `key_to_action` and `focus_dir` were retyped on the core `KeyCode`.

## `src/main.rs`: 730 → 331 lines
Key handling is now `to_key(crossterm event)` → `key_to_msg` → `apply_msg`, with `Msg::Copy` intercepted for `do_copy`/arboard. Mouse, resize and paste routing are unchanged.

## Verification
- `cargo test --workspace`: **187 tests (182 core + 5 native).**
  - The 22 key tests moved to the core and now drive state through `key_to_msg` → `apply_msg`.
  - Five core tests are new: Ctrl-C vs bare `c`, the full command table, meaningless keys → `None`, Alt-Esc still leaves quick-mode, and Copy doing nothing in the core.
  - `main.rs` keeps the native-only tests: two for `to_key` translation, one end-to-end crossterm wiring test, resize routing, and `do_copy`.
- **Differential check against `main`** (scratch crate, not committed): the old `handle_event` key branch, verbatim, against the new path. It covered 106 keys × 6 modifier combinations × 5 starting states and compared display, focus, quick-mode, active pad, pin, theme, quit flag and effect count. **3,180 cases, 0 differences.** A deliberately planted bug produced 12 differences, so the check does catch changes.
- Clippy is clean (workspace and core alone), fmt passes, and the core builds for wasm32.
- Real-terminal smoke test: quick-mode `k d j m` then Enter gives the same screen as the `main` build, and Ctrl-C exits cleanly.

## Housekeeping
`test-support` now covers only `layout_index` and `override_layout`, the two getters the native tests still use. `focus` and `fever_score` are back to plain `cfg(test)`. `CLAUDE.md` (the `main.rs` and new `input.rs` entries), `docs/progress.md` and `docs/TASKS.md` are updated.

body:
Roadmap 2.15 (GR-6). A refactor with no change in behaviour.

## What

- The `_NEXTJS_APP_DIR_CONVENTIONS`, `_NEXTJS_ROOT_CONVENTIONS` and `_NEXTJS_EXTENSIONS` constants, the next.config check and `_is_nextjs_convention_entry` leave `engine/detectors/orphaned.py`.
- They become `NEXTJS_ENTRY_CONVENTIONS` in `frameworks/specs/nextjs.py`, set as `NEXTJS_SPEC.entry_conventions`.
- `EntryConventions` is a small frozen dataclass with `config_files`, `extensions`, `root_stems` (root or `src/`), and `route_dir` plus `route_stems` (anywhere under `app/`). It has two methods, `applies_to(package_root)` and `is_entry(rel_path)`, which keep the old matching rules exactly. The Next.js marker list stays `next.config.{js,mjs,ts}`, not the spec's detection list, which also has `.cjs`. That keeps behaviour identical.
- **Layering:** `test_detectors_layer_does_not_import_lang_layer` forbids `engine/detectors` from importing `desloppify.languages`, so the detector can't read the registry itself. Instead:
  - `EntryConventions` is defined in `orphaned.py`, and `frameworks/types.py` imports it for the `FrameworkSpec.entry_conventions` field.
  - `OrphanedDetectionOptions` gains `entry_conventions: tuple[EntryConventions, ...] = ()`.
  - `registry.framework_entry_conventions()` collects the conventions of the registered specs, and all four `detect_orphaned_files` callers pass it: the TS coupling phase, the TS `detect orphaned` command, and the shared structural phase and command registry.
- React Router conventions stay in `orphaned.py`, which has no spec for them yet. They get their own `_REACT_ROUTER_EXTENSIONS`, with the same set as before.
- I removed an unused `Iterable` import from `frameworks/registry.py` because the F401 gate covers files I touched.

## Tests

- The `_detect_nextjs_project` and `_is_nextjs_convention_entry` unit tests now run against `NEXTJS_ENTRY_CONVENTIONS.applies_to` and `.is_entry`. Every case is unchanged.
- The Next.js integration tests pass the conventions through the options.
- New tests: the spec (and the registry) exposes the conventions, and a caller that passes no conventions gets no Next.js exemptions.

## Manual verification (real CLI)

I compared copies of `/dev/shm/dsl/repos/commerce` (Next.js), scanning one with origin/main and one with this branch:

- `desloppify scan --path .` on an unmodified copy: 102 issues each, identical issue IDs, 0 orphaned findings on both.
- Second pair, with probe files added to both copies:
  - should be orphaned: `app/search/helpers.ts`, `lib/page.tsx`, `lib/shopify/middleware.ts`, `middleware.cjs`
  - should be exempt: `src/proxy.ts`, `app/foo/twitter-image.tsx`, `instrumentation.ts`

  Both copies had 107 issues with identical IDs. The 4 orphaned findings (IDs, confidence, summary, detail) were identical too, and were exactly the expected four.
- `desloppify detect orphaned --path . --json` on the probe copy gave byte-identical output on origin/main and this branch.

## Gates

- `pytest -n 8 -q`: 6421 passed, 2 skipped
- golden with the pinned tsc/knip (`DESLOPPIFY_REQUIRE_NODE_GOLDEN=1`): 31 passed
- `ruff check --select E9,F63,F7,F82 .`: clean. `ruff check --select F401,F841` on the changed files: clean
- `lint-imports`: 1 kept, 0 broken
- `mypy`: no issues

author: codyfinegan
body:
### Description

Fixes #400.

The Trivy repo and image scans have failed since late April 2026. trivy-action v0.33.1 installs Trivy v0.65.0 by default, and that release no longer exists on GitHub (releases v0.27 to v0.69.1 were removed). setup-trivy fails to download the binary, the scan step exits 1, and the SARIF upload then fails with `Path does not exist`.

Changes:

- Bump `aquasecurity/trivy-action` from v0.33.1 to v0.36.0 (pinned to commit `ed142fd`) in both workflows. v0.36.0 installs Trivy v0.70.0 and setup-trivy v0.2.6.
- Image scan: swap `format: template` with `@/contrib/sarif.tpl` for `format: 'sarif'`. Trivy now warns that the template is deprecated.
- Both scans: set `limit-severities-for-sarif: true`. Without it, SARIF output ignores `severity` and uploads every severity. This keeps the Security tab to CRITICAL and HIGH, as the old template did.

Trivy itself is left at the action's default v0.70.0. v0.75.0 is out but is only a week old.

### Testing Instructions

1. Check the "Scan repo for vulnerabilities" check on this PR passes.
2. Run the image scan against the branch, e.g. on a fork: `gh workflow run scan-images.yml --repo <fork> --ref ci/400-bump-trivy-action`
3. Check all 11 image jobs pass, the log shows Trivy v0.70.0, and there is no `sarif.tpl is deprecated` warning.

Both were run on `313838e`: repo scan run 37726376617 and image scan run 37726383764 (on the fork) passed.

After merge, re-check that both workflows are enabled. They were disabled while #400 was open.

同时修复本 PR 的两个 macOS CI 失败：

- Webpack 5.105.4 only-dev-server 在检查更新后加载异步 chunk，分开的 check/apply 调用会因状态回到 prepare 而拒绝，导致浏览器永久停在 ready。依赖补丁改为由 runtime 的 check(options) 等待 chunk 并应用更新，保留原有选项和错误回调；真实 Webpack watch/浏览器回归证明修复前失败、修复后通过。

锁文件仅调整 repoctl 必要依赖与 Webpack patch 身份，其他 importer 和已有依赖解析保持原样。补丁版本、上游实现、回归及移除条件记录在 demo-matrix README 和工程复盘中。本次仅调整开发依赖、发布测试与 CI 运行器，不新增公开包 change intent。

- CI 修复：5 个定向测试文件、24 项通过，包括真实 Webpack 热更新和 macOS 僵尸组。
- 两个失败目标的生产构建、首编译、replace/add/restore 与收尾通过；H5 刷新及计算样式通过。static 基线显式重新生成后无 diff，随后不更新复跑通过。
- 全工作区 frozen-lockfile 安装、32 包 build:ci、定向 ESLint、agents:check 和 git diff --check 通过。
- 本地验证环境为 macOS Node 24。远端提交 `f4487062f517ebfdcadd363b49011638a7fb5f63` 的全部检查已完成：215 项成功、14 项按工作流条件跳过，无失败、取消或未完成项；未执行本地全仓/全端验收或实际 npm publish。

author: rhomat27
body:
## Summary

Fixes the reasoning loss reported in #6736. On the translated Claude Messages → Responses route, a Responses provider's own `encrypted_content` was dropped on the way out (`outbound.ts` decodes only `ocxr1:` envelopes). Nothing could carry it back either: the body is `store: false` and Claude Code replays only the thinking block. So the routed model lost its own reasoning every turn. With Muse Spark that shows up as long reading phases before the first edit, with the model restating that it is ready many times.

- `src/responses/reasoning-envelope.ts`: new envelope field `nat` holds the provider's blob verbatim, plus the client-facing model it was minted for and the provider's item id. It follows the same pattern as `krc` for Kiro. A malformed `nat` is ignored.
- `src/claude/outbound.ts` (streaming and JSON): a reasoning item with a native blob is signed into its thinking block's envelope. It now gets a thinking block even when no summary arrived; before, most Muse items produced no block at all.
- `src/claude/inbound.ts`: a replayed thinking block whose envelope has `nat` becomes a reasoning item with that `encrypted_content` and `id`, but only when the request names the same model. Any other model gets the visible text alone, so `/model` mid-conversation can't hand a blob to a provider that can't decrypt it. Bodies that reason now send `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, the same field Codex sends to every Responses provider.
- Anthropic signatures (`sig`) and redacted blocks (`red`) behave as before. Nothing changes for native Anthropic passthrough.
- `structure/clients/claude-desktop.md` documents the rule. `tests/claude-integration/claude-native-reasoning-continuity.test.ts` is registered in the test layout on an existing line.

This covers the Responses-route fix in #6736. The issue also has a comment about Meta's Anthropic-format endpoint through the `anthropic` adapter (`src/protocols/opaque-state.ts`); that one is a separate design question and is not touched here.

Closes #6736

## Verification

Run on macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), Bun 1.4.0, branch rebased onto `dev` at bf9ecf3d7.

- `bun run typecheck`: pass.
- `bun test tests/claude-integration/claude-native-reasoning-continuity.test.ts`: 10 pass. With `src/` reverted to `dev`, 8 of the 10 fail. The 2 that pass either way check unchanged behaviour (an item with no native blob, a malformed `nat`).
- Neighbouring suites: `claude-outbound`, `claude-inbound`, `claude-inbound-tool-reference`, `claude-inbound-token-footer`, `responses/reasoning-envelope`, `providers/kiro/kiro-reasoning-roundtrip`, `adapters/bridge`, `adapters/anthropic/anthropic-opaque-strip`. Together with the new file: 338 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run structure:check`: pass. `bun run privacy:scan`: pass.
- `bun run test:changed` (before the rebase, `dev` at 18a8cda3c): 33,105 tests, 32,798 pass, 201 fail, 3 errors. Every failure sits in 26 files outside the changed modules (server auth and admission, lab, Kiro catalog, service).
  - Running those 26 files on an unmodified `dev` worktree gives the same failing test names: 656 pass, 183 fail in isolation on both trees.
  - This workstation runs a live opencodex and inherits Claude Code's `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. With those cleared, the same files drop to 56 failures, again identical on `dev`. I'm leaving the full-suite verdict to CI.

Live check: the same diff applied to an installed v2.80.0, route `meta-muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (Coding Plan).

- Recall test. The model is told a random 8-character code and asked to keep it only in its reasoning. On turn 2 the code is replaced with `[removed]` and the model is asked for it.

  | Turn 2 | Recalled |
  |---|---|
  | Same model, fix applied | 3 of 5 |
  | Control: same prompt, same provider, turn 2 sent as the `[1m]` alias, so the guard withholds the blob | 0 of 5 |

  Without the fix this route recalled 0 of 3 on the earlier test.
- A real Claude Code subagent on the Muse route, given a small test-writing task:
  - all 7 of its thinking blocks carried the native blob
  - first file edit at 15 s
  - no proxy errors
  - all 27 Muse requests in that window reported reasoning tokens. On our 2.76 install's log, only about 10–18% of Claude-route Muse requests did.

## Checklist

- [x] Scope stays focused and avoids unrelated cleanup.
- [x] Docs or release notes were updated when needed (`structure/clients/claude-desktop.md`).
- [x] Security-sensitive changes were reviewed for secrets, auth, and unsafe defaults. The blob is the provider's own opaque response data, already returned to this proxy. It goes back only to the model that produced it, and no credential or account data enters the envelope.

**Touched repo:** `moonblokz-configuration` (companion PRs in `moonblokz-blockchain` and `moonblokz-info`).

## Behavioural impact
Acceptance compared only *declared* literals against `BuildLimits`. A content that omits `active_chain_length` resolves `W` to its default 500, so a build with a smaller active-chain capacity (e.g. the BLS-small 300 profile) accepted a chain whose window it cannot hold. An absent caller-limited parameter (`max_block_utxo_output`, `active_chain_length`) is now measured through its code-baked default, exactly as a declared literal would be. A compile-time assertion pins that both parameters keep literal defaults, so the measured fallback is the resolved value.

On the reference limits (256 / 500) nothing changes; `config-encoder` output is unaffected.

## API / config changes
None to the API. Behaviour change: a build whose capacity is below a default now refuses content that leaves that parameter undeclared (FR8 exact evidence of invalidity).

## Verification
- `cargo test --workspace` — 59 + 20 + 1 passed (new test `an_absent_capacity_parameter_is_measured_by_its_default`)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace` — 0 warnings
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- `cargo tree -e normal | grep -iE 'embassy|alloc'` — empty

## Compatibility / risk
Consensus-relevant only for builds whose capacity is below a default; such a build could not represent the chain anyway. Ratified by the Project Lead on 2026-10-08 (Story 5.11, decision 1).

## Code review follow-ups (2026-10-08)
- The `CALLER_LIMITED_IDS` const block now requires each default to be `Literal(fallback)`. The value acceptance measures for an absent parameter is therefore exactly what resolution returns.
- It also bounds the list at the `u8` presence mask's 8 bits.

body:
## What
- **`frontend/wrangler.jsonc`:** an assets-only Worker serving `dist/`, with no script. `not_found_handling: "single-page-application"` serves client-side routes (`/runs/<id>/results`, `/help`) as `index.html` with a 200.
- **`public/.assetsignore`:** keeps `_redirects` and `404.html` (the fallbacks for other hosts) out of the Workers upload.
- **`public/_headers`:** caches Vite's hashed `/assets/*` for a year. The bundle keeps default revalidation, because its file names stay the same between exports.
- **Scripts:** `npm run deploy:preview` uploads a version with a preview URL that doesn't go live; `npm run deploy` publishes. Both run `build:static` and `check:static` first.
- **`StaticBundle`:** on a single-page-app host, a missing JSON file comes back as `index.html` with a 200. The app now reports it as "not found" instead of a JSON parse error.
- **README and PLAN:** document the host, the deploy commands, and the decision to publish review text scrubbed.

## Why Workers, not Pages
Cloudflare now points new static projects to Workers static assets. Static requests are free and unlimited on both, and the free plan allows 20,000 files at 25 MiB each; this build has 1,216 files, the largest 4.2 MB. The single-page-app fallback is a single setting here, and it returns 200 rather than 404.

## Checked
- **`wrangler dev` (the Workers runtime, locally):**
  - deep links return 200 with HTML;
  - `index.json` comes back as `application/json` and replays as `application/gzip`;
  - `_redirects` and `404.html` are not served;
  - hashed assets carry `Cache-Control: immutable`.
- **Chrome on the Workers-served build:** filtered reviews table, inspector, live replay filling, no console errors.
- **Build and tests:** `build:static` and `check:static` are clean; tsc and lint are clean; 83 of 84 tests pass. The exception is the 50K-grid timing test, which failed once while `wrangler dev` was using the CPU and passed 3/3 when re-run alone.

384 checks, 0 failed

body:
## SPECTRA v2.0

Turns the three-mode tracking viewer into a deeper computer vision studio. Everything still runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

### What is new
- **Four new modes on real MediaPipe models**, each loaded on demand and SHA-256 verified at setup: Face (478-point mesh, live expression meters, head pose), Segment (per-class cutouts), Gestures, and Fusion (pose, hands and face together, one worker per task).
- **Effects engine**: a small WebGL2 kit and eight effects driven only by live landmarks, masks and face data. They composite through the stage canvas, so Record and Screenshot capture them.
- **Lab**: measured inference latency (p50, p95, max), processed and render FPS, dropped frames, a CPU or GPU delegate switch that states what is really running, a 20 second benchmark with JSON and Markdown export, and model cards.
- **Shell**: seven-mode switcher, effects tray with intensity, keyboard shortcuts and command palette, immersive stage view, 390 px phone layout, first-run tips, installable and offline capable (each model cached only after first use).
- **Architecture**: modes, effects and panels are plugin registries; one frame state object; typed telemetry bus. See `docs/architecture.md`.

### Compatibility
- v1 flows are unchanged: `tests/e2e/studio.spec.ts` and `tests/tracker.test.ts` are byte-identical to before this branch and pass.
- Session export keeps every v1 key. New optional keys carry the new modes' data; the schema `version` is now `1.2.0`, numbers are rounded to five places and the file is capped at 1,000 frames or about 8 MB.

### Verification
Local, in CI order: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm run setup`, `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run check`, `pnpm run test` (146 tests), `PAGES_BUILD=1 pnpm run build`, `SPECTRA_TEST_PRODUCTION=1 pnpm run test:e2e` (29 tests against the production build, on system Chrome and on Playwright's bundled headless shell).

### Known limits
- Segment is slow without a GPU (hundreds of ms per frame on CPU).
- The gesture recognizer's own model card states no licence; `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` records what the Apache-2.0 attribution rests on.
- Not tested on a physical phone or mobile Safari.
- The demo video still shows v1.1.

Merge as a **squash**: the branch history contains work that was removed before review.

author: fakezhiyuanli
body:
Makes activity and bot restarts preserve results and lets the bot continue running while releases are prepared. #105 adds the deployment tool on top of this branch.

The game supports a same-port handover: SIGHUP drains the listener while existing matches finish; SIGINT/SIGTERM stop gracefully. Runtime status files and build identifiers let a deploy verify readiness. SQLite write transactions begin IMMEDIATE and use a busy timeout so overlapping processes wait for one another.

Daily, rush, and practice hand-ins retry connection failures and 502/503/504 responses with the same request body. Connection failures while reading a successful response are included. Fully received malformed JSON and nonretryable server refusals retain their existing behavior. Daily submissions name their day so a retry across midnight cannot be graded against the next day’s puzzle. Rush retains its ticket during recovery, duel results survive a handover close, and a quiet update chip offers a manual reload outside active play.

The bot reports readiness and in-flight work, stops politely, and synchronizes commands only when their payload changes. Deploy guides put the activity first, the site second, and a brief bot restart last when its files or changelog changed. Release notes: beta 0.21 and beta 0.23.

Validation on the updated branch:

- Bun suite: 2,030 passed, 104 expected skips, 0 failures. The untracked solutions fixture is absent.
- Typecheck, activity build, and puzzle database site build passed.
- Bot suite using the bot virtualenv: 293 passed.
- Hand-in tests cover interrupted response bodies for all three routes, identical retried payloads, aborts, retry exhaustion, malformed JSON, and nonretryable statuses.

When combining with #103, preserve beta 0.23, beta 0.22, beta 0.21, and beta 0.20 in that order. The first deployment needs a quiet moment because the existing server and open clients predate these protections; live deployment verification remains outstanding. Use direct Bun entrypoints and the process-manager grace settings in the guides.

author: sfaiug
body:
Opening a seat should cost as little of ak's own time as it can. `claude.sh interactive` started a Python on every new seat, reopen and model switch, only to make sure Claude Code's settings files are JSON objects before the pane they would be used in is replaced.

## What changes

- A new plugin hook, `checked(account)`: what a harness checks before a launch, in the launching process, refusing the launch with a `config.Error`; it answers the env pairs that tell the adapter it is done. By default nothing is checked and nothing told.
- `orch.command` calls it before it asks the adapter and adds what it answers to that one adapter call's environment.
- Claude's `checked` reads the same files `--check` did, through the one function `account_config` now reads them with too (`_settings`): the owner's `~/.claude/settings.json` and the login's `.claude.json`, and for a named login its own `settings.json` beside them. It answers `AGENTKIT_CLAUDE_CHECKED=1`.
- `claude.sh interactive` starts its `--check` Python only when it is not told so, as when it is run on its own.

A refused launch now says which file: `Claude's settings cannot be read: <path> is not JSON: …` or `<path> is not a JSON object`, where the adapter printed the tail of a traceback.

Unchanged: what a launch writes into those settings. The wrapper that runs in the pane (`python3 claude.py -- claude …`, `account_config()`) still pins bypass permissions, `crossSessionInbound=refuse` and `switchModelsOnFlag` and answers the first-run questions on both logins; only where its two reads come from moved into `_settings`. `tests/test_seat_refuses_native_peer.py` and `tests/test_seat_switches_model_on_flag.py` pass untouched.

Two sketches: the same check written with jq in the adapter (no new hook, but a second home for which files are read and what valid means, apart from the Python that then uses them), and the hook, which keeps one home. The hook won.

## Measured

The adapter's `interactive`, run by hand twelve times on this host at load 13 with the rulebook handed to it: quickest 62 ms and median 90 ms on its own, quickest 8 ms and median 11 ms when told. Reading this host's settings in the launching process (117 KB and 78 KB of `.claude.json`) takes 1 to 2 ms. In sandboxed seat opens with #703 and #704 in, that adapter call was 65 ms of a 134 ms open. This PR promises nothing else about how fast a seat opens.

## Test

`tests/test_claude_settings_checked_by_the_launch.py`, in a temporary HOME:
- a Claude seat's command line is built by `orch.fresh_command` with a `python3` first on PATH that refuses to run;
- settings that are not JSON refuse the launch, naming the file, before the adapter is asked; mended, the same launch goes through;
- a named login's own config is read for its launch and no other;
- the adapter run on its own still reads them and exits 2, naming the file.

All four fail on the code before this. 193 test files that reach a seat's launch, Claude or a harness plugin pass on this tree, and the 19 that read the docs.

author: claude[bot]
body:
<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested via [Slack thread](https://comfy-organization.slack.com/archives/C0A4XMHANP3/p1791441407831319?thread_ts=1791441407.831319&cid=C0A4XMHANP3)_

## Summary

Refs https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues/17124

**Before:** `invokeExtensionsAsync` mapped every enabled extension through an `async` function, so each call allocated a wrapper promise per extension even when the extension had no such hook, or the hook returned synchronously. It runs once per node def (`beforeRegisterNodeDef`), so nodes x extensions promises (about 6M on a 6k-node, 1k-extension install) piled onto the microtask queue at startup.

**After:** a plain synchronous loop. Extensions without the hook do no work, hooks that return synchronously are never wrapped or awaited, and only promises that hooks actually return are awaited. Based on the shape suggested by Austin Mroz.

How: per extension, read `ext[method]` and skip it if it is not a function, call it, and collect the result. If the result is a promise or thenable it gets a `.catch` that logs the error (same message as before). The call resolves with `Promise.all` over the collected results. `setup` keeps its `legacyMenuCompat` set/clear via a small async wrapper (set before the call, cleared in `finally`, so also on throw or rejection). The property read and call are inside a per-extension try/catch, so a throwing getter or Proxy trap is logged for that extension only, where previously a throwing `in` check rejected the whole call.

Preserved: same snapshot of `enabledExtensions` per call, in-order concurrent invocation, inherited prototype hooks, hooks added by an earlier hook mid-call, and the same error log message and context. Hook return values (sync or async, falsy values included) are still returned.

Behavior differences:
- The resolved array contains only the results of extensions that define the hook, so it is no longer index-aligned with the extensions (before, extensions without the hook left an `undefined` slot). Nothing in this repo uses the return value; all call sites discard it.
- Hooks that return synchronously are not awaited. They were already invoked synchronously within the call before, so start timing is unchanged.
- The hook is detected by reading the property rather than `in`, so a Proxy that only defines a `has` trap is no longer consulted. Non-function values are still skipped silently, as before.

Limitation: this only partially fixes the Firefox slowness (reporter measured about 110s to 61s on a real install); the remainder looks like a separate Firefox/SpiderMonkey issue. The unbounded `Promise.all` over node defs in `registerNodesFromDefs` (`app.ts`) is intentionally left as-is: chunking it was tried and dropped pending a Firefox and Chromium startup benchmark.

## Verification

- Tests: reworked `invokeExtensionsAsync` suite in `src/services/extensionService.test.ts` (35 tests pass), plus `src/services`, `app.test.ts` and `SelectionToolbox.test.ts`.
- `pnpm typecheck`, oxlint, eslint and oxfmt are clean.

author: nkyriazis
body:
Part of #72: this PR holds the answer on screen and shows a match one pair per line. Relaxing the pools' caps and bringing back the number-words match regenerates the pools, so that step gets its own PR and the issue stays open for it.

## Before

At the kiosk (1280×800), Ηλέκτρα taps «Δείξε μου» on four seven-digit numbers in order. She taps the answer to keep it, and nothing happens. The player closes by itself after 4.8 s, and the card is then done (○ ⭐0) and can't be opened again. A match of four pairs gets the same few seconds, as one run of text that breaks inside a pair («δυνατός –» / «ισχυρός») and puts a dash beside the words, which reads as a minus beside numbers. [video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/before-1280x800.mp4)

![before: ordering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/before-1280x800-A1-answer.png) ![before: match](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/before-1280x800-A3-match.png)

On a phone (390×844), the box keeps its 5rem side padding, so «Η σωστή / απάντηση:» wraps in a narrow column. This one also closed by itself, after 4.9 s.

![before: phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/before-390x844-B-2-answer.png)

## Problem

`AssignmentPlayer.tsx` closed the player 4500 ms after the answer appeared, on both paths («Δείξε μου», and the last try on the unforgiving rung). The overlay was `pointer-events: none`, so nothing she did could keep it. `answerText.ts` joined a match's pairs as `a – b, c – d` with ordinary spaces, so the browser broke lines anywhere, including inside a pair. The box's padding was fixed.

## Fix

- **The answer stays** (`AssignmentPlayer.tsx`). There is no reading timer: «Εντάξει» (a 48 px button that plays the close sound) or ✕ closes it. Tapping or scrolling the card does nothing. As a precaution, a backdrop over the stage takes stray touches in silence, so the finished exercise underneath never plays «nope». The header sits above the backdrop, so ✕, the owl and its «Να σου δείξω;» stay tappable. A 120 s safety close, by the same path and in silence, is for a kiosk left alone. It counts only while the answer is in sight: while a routine or an alarm covers the screen it stops, and it starts again from 0 when the cover goes.
- **One pair per line** (`answerText.ts`, test first). A match is now `a → b`, one pair per line, the same for maths and language. An ordering stays one run. Every «→» has a no-break space before it, so no line starts with an arrow. `tools/problem-gen` `revealed()` writes the answer the same way. Rerunning all four generators leaves `backend/exercise-pools` unchanged, so CI's regenerate-diff stays clean. The caps (60, or 40 for a match) and `match()`'s measure stay as they are, with comments that point to the follow-up.
- **The card fits small screens**. Its padding, icon and text scale with vw/vh, it is at most 92vw wide and stays within the stage, and a long answer scrolls inside the card while «Εντάξει» stays visible.
- **The owl**. While the answer is up, the tour is its own edition, `exercise-answer`, with one bubble on the card: «Διάβασέ τη όσο θες. Όταν τελειώσεις, πάτα «Εντάξει».» The owl offers it the first time an answer stays on screen. The bubble's voice clip is in the same commit and passes every check of the help-voice audit (PESQ 4.1, SI-SDR 24.6 dB, not flagged). Whisper hears «τι» for «τη», which sound the same.
- **Timers** (its own commit). The player's timers go with it. Before this, pressing ✕ during «+⭐1» left a 1.8 s close running, and it would close the next exercise if she opened one within that time.

## After

The same screens at the same sizes. In the video, she taps the card and then beside it, and nothing closes or makes a sound. The answer is still up after 20 s, and «Εντάξει» closes it with the close sound. [video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-1280x800.mp4)

![after: ordering, 20 s on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-1280x800-A1-20s.png) ![after: match](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-1280x800-A3-match.png)

The four-pair match is `g4-lang-syn-1`, a revision item from the Δ΄ pool that the scene put into Ηλέκτρα's slot. Ε΄ has language exercises of its own, so no kid gets this item today. The matches kids do get, like Γ΄'s times tables (three pairs), now show one pair per line instead of one run of text. On the phone, the same Γ΄ match is still up after taps on the card and beside it:

![after: phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-390x844-B-3-still.png)

The four-pair match on the small screens: the card fits, and a tap at the centre of «Εντάξει» lands on the button.

![after: 800×480](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-800x480-D-2-match.png) ![after: 390×844](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-390x844-D-2-match.png)

The owl's new bubble (it says the clip). At 1280×800 there is no room beside a card this size, so the bubble sits over the card's lower part, «Εντάξει» included, until «Το βρήκα!» closes it:

![after: owl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-1280x800-A3-owl.png)

The unforgiving rung, shown once in the same video: Ιφιγένεια is set to Αυστηρό over the admin API and back again afterwards. She gets a true-false wrong on her one try, and the answer stays until «Εντάξει».

![after: unforgiving](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-1280x800-C2-answer.png)

The safety close was played with nobody touching the screen (`after-safety.mjs`): the answer was still up at 110 s, the player closed by itself at 120.8 s, and no sound played.

A routine over the answer (`after-cover.mjs`): she taps «Δείξε μου», then her morning routine starts over it (a push) and stays 133 s, longer than the safety close. She closes the routine with ✕ and «Ναι», and the answer is still there. Nobody touches the screen after that, and the player closes by itself 119 s after the routine went, with no sound. [video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-1280x800-F.mp4)

![after: the routine over the answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-1280x800-F2-covered.png) ![after: the answer, back after 133 s under the routine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/girls_gamiefied_routine/pr-evidence/72/after-1280x800-F3-back.png)

## Blast radius

- **Kids' screen, exercise player only.** The group game never shows «Η σωστή απάντηση». The problem player's «Δείξε μου» already waited for «Συνέχεια →» and is unchanged. The header now sits above the stage (`z-index: 11` inside the player). The other feedback overlays («+⭐», «Δοκίμασε ξανά!») keep their timers and stay above everything.
- **A routine or an alarm over the answer** (#51): the player stays mounted under it, as before, and the answer is still up when the cover goes. The safety close stops under the cover and counts 120 s again from then (`after-cover.mjs`).
- **A STATE while the answer is up** only re-renders it. One arrived 10 s into the match's answer in the video, and the answer stayed.
- **Owl**: a new anchor (`exercise.revealed`), a new tour edition (`exercise-answer`) and a new bubble with its voice clip (`tools/help-voice/report.json` gains its entry; the other 88 clips are unchanged). Every kid will be offered it once.
- **Sound**: «Εντάξει» plays `close`, like ✕. There are no new sound files, and the unforgiving `wrong` sound is unchanged.

author: ondery
body:
## Summary

#20520 was closed because some backend nodes cannot take a Message node's output as their own input. This pull request keeps that constraint and still allows a custom status message between steps.

A workflow often has to tell the user what it is doing before the final answer exists. A product-support assistant is a concrete case:

1. Retrieval searches the product manual. The user would otherwise stare at a spinner.
2. A Message sends a fixed sentence such as "Looking through the product manual." That message can still read the node before it.
3. A second Retrieval searches the FAQ. The Message edge does not copy the status sentence into it.
4. A final Message renders the answer from the node before it, for example `{Agent:Answer@content}`.

Those middle sentences are not the model's narration and they are not the final answer. The graph already knows which step is next, so the product can say so in the author's words. Official templates only use Message as the last node of a branch, which cannot express this sequence. #20076 removed the outgoing handle for that terminal shape. The runtime itself does not stop at Message: `Message.Invoke` emits the text and returns. What breaks is the edge wiring. `AddInput` copies Message's output map (`content`, `downloads`, and any file or audio fields) into the next node. Retrieval expects `query`. Other nodes expect their own fields. That is the incompatibility called out when #20520 was closed.

A direct edge from START would also run a node when its branch was not selected. This change does not add that edge.

- The Message still publishes its text on the chat stream.
- An edge into a Message still copies the previous node's output. A status message and the final message can both read that node.
- The edge after a Message does not copy Message's output. If another predecessor already supplies data, the Message edge only waits. If Message is the only predecessor, the next node reads the workflow input without a direct edge from START, so an unselected branch does not run it.
- An Agent defers its stream only when every following Message ends the branch. A Message that continues is a status line, so the Agent runs normally and writes a real value instead of leaving an unopened stream.
- The next-step menu uses the same connection limits as a dragged edge. Message still cannot connect to Begin, another Message, Rewrite, or Categorize.
- Agent → terminal Message deferral is unchanged, so the final answer is not emitted twice.

## Test plan

- [ ] Connect Message → Retrieval, Message → Agent, and Message → Switch. Confirm the + menu does not offer Begin, Message, Rewrite, or Categorize.
- [ ] Run Retrieval → Message ("Looking through the product manual.") → Retrieval → Message (`{Agent@content}`). The status sentence appears before the second search. The status message can read the first retrieval, and the final message can read the answer node. The second retrieval does not receive the status sentence.
- [ ] Put that sequence on one Switch branch and leave the other branch empty. The second retrieval does not run when the first branch is not selected.
- [x] `go test ./internal/agent/canvas/ -run TestMessageReadsPredecessorOutput`
- [ ] An Agent whose only child is a final Message still streams through that Message and does not also emit the raw agent text.

body:
## Attendance tab: view toggle, threshold scale, merged absences card (v1.15.0)

Follow-up to the subjectwise meter row. Four review fixes folded in (merged `main` at 32504b3 first).

### View toggle (Subjects header, right)
Two-button icon toggle — graph (bar chart) ↔ table — as a real segmented control: bordered `join` of `btn btn-sm btn-square` with `btn-active` on the pressed side, clean 3-column grid icon, `aria-pressed` + `title` on both, `localStorage.attView` persistence, `hidden` attribute only for switching.

**Table view columns:** Code · Subject · Total · Attended · Margin.
Margin = `attended − ceil(0.75·total)` — faint oklch green (positive) / red (negative).

### Percentage scale (lower edge of the bar)
Threshold marks only: **`0%`** at the start, **`75%`** at the tick. The current % is the header figure (single source, no duplicate), `100` is the bar's end — both removed under the bar. Class counts stay on the upper edge (numbers vs percentages on opposite edges: they can never collide).

### Merged absences card
Absences + monthly breakdown → ONE card: per-month block = monthly attendance bar with that month's absence chips (`14 Jul · 4h`) wrapped beneath. The standalone `Monthly breakdown` `<details>` is gone (its rows ARE the card). 362px → 292px on the stress seed.

### Junk-row filter
Portal's `CL` / "CLASS IN CHARGE" marker row (2-of-4 hours → nonsense 50% meter) is dropped server-side in `index()` — filtered from both meters and table.

### 75%-mark width report — root cause
The 2px tick is pixel-perfect at 75.00% at every width (measured 11 widths). Real culprit: `.mrows` hard `min-width:768px` breakpoint snapped bars **650px → 345px** at a single pixel. Now `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))` — bars stay in a 270–345px band at every viewport.

### Seed realism
DUT self-seeds the real portal payload shape (pulled from prod, values fabricated): 9-char codes (`21CSC201J`), ALL-CAPS descriptions, plain-string hours, `MMM / YYYY` months, `DD-MM-YYYY` daily rows, plus the `CL` junk row.

### Screenshots (b18cd21-pinned, md5-verified against raw)

- `tests/test_att_dut.py` **11/11** (self-seeded; red-tested at 9/10 earlier) — toggle presence/persistence/round-trip, 5 columns, margin colours, row order, zero label overlaps at 393, merged months, no standalone details, CL filter

- Browser DUTs: `test_sw` 7/7 (zero CSP violations) · `test_xss` ALL PASS · `test_navbar` 18/18 · `test_feedback_dut` ALL PASS

body:
## Causa raiz

O novo projeto Supabase `ordax-platform` foi preparado com `private.handle_ordax_account_created()` ainda no comportamento bootstrap simples: criava `ordax_accounts` sem exigir aceite jurídico/recibo transacional. O runtime anterior já tinha implementação superior. A migração de provider não pode reabrir esse bypass.

## Correção real implantada (projeto de destino)

Reaproveitadas **as migrations versionadas existentes** do owner `infra/supabase/product/migrations/`, sem duplicar SQL, lógica, gateway, frontend ou autoridade. Aplicações registradas no ledger do Supabase novo:
- `account_registration_legal_receipt_v1`
- `account_registration_policy_projection_v1`
- `account_registration_legal_fk_indexes_v1`
- `public_login_legal_receipt_guard_v1`
- `account_legal_policy_activation_v1`
- `account_registration_intent_email_validation_v2` (correção da chamada impossível `chr(0)`)

A correção `chr(0)` foi aplicada **tanto no PostgreSQL novo quanto no Supabase anterior**, porque o problema existia nos dois. O teste negativo do RPC de legal intent agora retorna corretamente `registration-legal-policy-unavailable` quando não há política ativa, em vez do erro PostgreSQL 54000.

Cada lote teve compilação transacional real com `ROLLBACK` antes da aplicação.

## Provas no destino

- Uma única trigger `on_auth_user_created_ordax_product`;
- tentativa real de INSERT em `auth.users` sem intent de aceite recusada por `ordax-registration-legal-intent-required`, transação revertida, banco permaneceu com zero usuários;
- RLS nas três tabelas jurídicas privadas;
- apenas `service_role` tem EXECUTE nas RPCs de servidor; anon/authenticated negados;
- verificação de recibo de usuário inexistente resulta `false`;
- zero políticas jurídicas ativas, zero usuários, zero Edge Functions no projeto novo;
- Security Advisor apresenta apenas INFO de tabelas privadas RLS sem policies.

## SSOT e escopo desta PR

- Registra *destino em preparação* no contrato **existente** `docs/contracts/public-auth-hardening.json` sem substituir o `target` atual (runtime antigo ainda é o alvo da configuração de auth).
- Documenta o cutover real em `infra/supabase/product/README.md`.
- Adiciona regressão estática que impede public auth/cutover indevido sem provas.
- Nenhuma configuração secreta copiada; **sem dual-write**, sem auth público, sem novo backend paralelo.
- Sem alterações em Cloudflare, Vercel, User Cloud Storage ou migration PostgreSQL do Control Plane #68.

## Próximos bloqueios (não simulados)

Deploy verificável do gateway/OIDC same-origin no destino, confirmação de email/redirect/password, política jurídica publicada e aprovada, Turnstile, recovery e revogação E2E, e corte atômico de identidade. Sem essas provas, manter público fail-closed.

Refs #805 e #974. Dependências de migração: #1354 e #1355.

author: ayeshawaseemahmad
body:
Fixes #16275

## Problem

`medusaIntegrationTestRunner` accepts a `schema` option, but with a custom value every table still ends up in `public`. Running the full runner with `schema: "custom"` created 148 tables in `public` and none in `custom`.

There are two separate causes:

1. `configLoaderOverride` only applied `clientUrl` and `debug`, so `projectConfig.databaseSchema` was never set and the app kept using the default schema.
2. Module migrations ignore a custom schema even when `databaseSchema` is set. `mikroOrmCreateConnection` passes `schema` to MikroORM, which only uses it for the `mikro_orm_migrations` table. The migration SQL is unqualified, and the `SET LOCAL search_path` in `CustomDBMigrator` runs on a different connection than the queued queries, so it has no effect. Running the api-key module's migrations with `schema: "custom"` produced `custom.mikro_orm_migrations` and `public.api_key`.

The second cause also affects `medusa db:migrate` with a custom `databaseSchema`, not just tests. It is the issue pointed out in the review of #16279.

## Changes

- `mikro-orm-create-connection.ts`: when a custom schema is requested and the connection is not a shared one, pass `searchPath` in the driver options so unqualified migration SQL resolves in that schema. A shared connection already sets `searchPath`, and the default `public` schema is unchanged.
- `config.ts` (test-utils): `configLoaderOverride` accepts `schema` and sets `projectConfig.databaseSchema` for non-default schemas. The runner's default (`public`) does not override a `databaseSchema` already set in `medusa-config`.
- `medusa-test-runner.ts`: create the schema right after the database connection opens, before migrations run.
- Changeset for `@medusajs/utils` and `@medusajs/test-utils`.

## Testing

- New unit tests for `mikroOrmCreateConnection` (custom schema, driver options preserved, default schema untouched, shared connection untouched). The two custom-schema tests fail without the fix.
- New unit tests for `configLoaderOverride`.

author: tidum41
body: The archive grid sits under a transparent header, and a tap is supposed to enlarge one photo. Clicking was unreliable and the zoom felt mushy. This only changes that click path, plus the mobile zoom-button width. ## What was going wrong - The nav row is full width and transparent, so the empty part of the header was the thing under the cursor for the top ~92px of the first row. Those clicks never reached the photo. - A tap always landed on overview × 1.25. The focus scale was a clamp of the *current* zoom into a range, and from the overview the current zoom is below the floor, so every click snapped to that floor. On a phone that was 0.876 → 1.095. The photo barely changed size. - The camera animated `translate` and `scale` as separate CSS transitions, so the photo arced toward the corner. The focus outline was snapped to the final box immediately and also scaled up from nothing over 1.5s, so around 700ms it sat about 15px off the picture. - Which photo was focused was stored inside `startTransition` and only copied into a ref during render. A second tap a few hundred milliseconds later still saw the old photo, so it closed the gallery or toggled the wrong tile. The growing photo also slid under the cursor, and that second tap was treated as “click the open photo, so close it.” - Every pointer-up, including a tap that never moved, started a bounds spring before the click handler ran. That spring fought the focus zoom. - On a phone the − and + buttons were scaled 1.4× with the track, so they were wider than the desktop pair (about 48px vs 34px). ## What a click does now - Empty header space lets the click through. Links, the theme button, and the volume control stay clickable. While the intro is still playing, those controls stay inactive so invisible links don’t catch taps. - A tap zooms toward the size that fits under the nav and above the zoom bar, and never past the slider’s max (1.5). The open photo is placed in that clear area, so it doesn’t sit under the header. Neighbors stay on screen and can be tapped. - The camera eases in a straight line over ~680ms. The outline fades in and is repositioned every frame, so it stays on the photo (measured error 0px at 250ms and at rest). - Focus is recorded immediately. A second tap while the open animation is still running finishes the zoom instead of closing. After it settles, tapping the open photo or empty space returns to the grid. A drag still pans and does not focus. - The − and + buttons are 34px wide on both desktop and mobile. The track and thumb still grow on a phone so the grab target stays easy to hit. ## Simulation Playwright on the dev server, 1280×800 and 375×812, no page errors: - The top of the first photo focuses (desktop, the pixel under the header; mobile, the first pixel of the tile, which already starts below the header). - Tapping another visible photo switches to it. Tapping the same photo again before the zoom finishes stays on it and ends at scale 1.5. - Tapping the open photo, or real empty space, returns to the overview (desktop scale 1, mobile 0.876). - A 40px drag does not focus. A 4px jitter still counts as a tap. - Work, archive, about, the theme button, and volume all win their own hit tests. - The rightmost first-row photo opens fully on screen (top at 108px, under the 92px header; right edge at 1025 of 1280). - Zoom out and zoom in are both 34px wide at 1280 and at 375. [Desktop archive with a photo focused](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-749efd2c-162e-56a8-a276-f05e91300cc9/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Farchive_desktop_focus.png) [Mobile archive with a photo focused](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-749efd2c-162e-56a8-a276-f05e91300cc9/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Farchive_mobile_focus.png) [archive_gallery_click_focus_switch_dismiss.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-749efd2c-162e-56a8-a276-f05e91300cc9/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Farchive_gallery_click_focus_switch_dismiss.mp4) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: marwanelamami
body:
**Problem:** replies kept opening with «فاهمك» / «حاسس بيك», used «حاسس» (not Libyan), and once said «فاهمتك», as if Khutwa were a woman. The prompt required an acknowledgement in every reply, and its examples taught those openers.

**Changes in `khutwa-reflect.md`:**
- **Talks like a friend texting:** one or two short, informal sentences.
- **Stock empathy phrases** («فاهمك», «حاس بيك», «ربي يعينك») may open at most one reply per conversation. Other replies react in their own words («صعيبة هذي», «والله موقف يضايق») or go straight to the question, and no two replies start the same way.
- **Spelling and speaker:** «حاس», never «حاسس». Khutwa never uses feminine first-person forms like «فاهمتك».
- **Gender:** the reply addresses the user in the feminine when they write about themselves that way, or when the app says so (below).
- **Examples:** rewritten to match.

**Addressing:** `analyze` and `support` accept `addressing: "masculine" | "feminine"`, the user's «ولد / بنت» choice in the app (kept only in memory on the phone). With `"feminine"`, an `addressing: feminine` line goes first. Replies then use feminine forms, and drafts are written in her voice: «حابة نهدرز معاك». The risk check still sees only the message.

**Checked with gemini-3.8-flash-low:** a 3-turn conversation in a young woman's voice opened each reply differently, with no «فاهمك» or «حاسس». The drafts were feminine. Tests: 47 passed, 1 skipped (2 new).

The app side is on `android/native-app`.

**To go live:** merge, then restart `serve-public.sh`.

author: peanutboi710
body:
> ## ✅ 판결문 단계 무료 등급 백업 옵션 — 팀 구두 합의 완료
> 이 PR의 3번 항목(`allowFreeTierForJudgment`)은 기능이라기보다 **데이터 정책 변경**입니다. 지금까지 원칙은 "판결문 원문을 보내는 `extract` · `court`는 유료 키만"이었고, 이 옵션을 켜면 정규식 마스킹만 거친 원문(이름 · 지명 · 날짜 포함)이 무료 등급으로 가서 약관상 **사람이 검토할 수 있습니다**. 기본은 꺼짐이라 켜지 않으면 동작이 달라지지 않습니다.
> - [x] 팀이 "**이미 공개된 판결문에 한해** 무료 등급 백업을 허용"하는 데 동의 — **구두로 합의됨** (작성자 확인, 2026-10-08)
> - [x] 허용하지 않기로 하는 경우의 분리 계획(`11d40a1`만 되돌리거나 별도 PR)은 불필요해짐 (머지 조건 해제)
> - 운영 규칙: 이 옵션을 켠 설정 파일은 **공개된 판결문에만** 쓴다. 실행 때 나오는 경고와 `report.json`의 `usedFreeTier`로 실제 사용 여부를 확인한다
> - 주의: `court.model`이 `null`이면 extract 목록을 그대로 쓰므로, **extract에 켜면 court에도 같이 켜집니다.** 따로 두려면 `court.model`에 유료 모델만 명시합니다.

## 작업 내용

### 1. 비식별화 · 재판부 초안 모델 대체 체인 (`stages.extract.model` · `stages.court.model`)
- 모델 **목록**을 받음 (문자열 하나면 기존과 동일, court가 `null`이면 extract 목록 사용). CLI는 `--model`을 여러 번 지정
- 앞 모델의 호출이 **과부하 · 요청 한도 · 일 한도 · 크레딧 소진**으로 막힌 경우에만 다음 모델로 넘어감 (앞 모델의 BE-36 재시도를 다 쓴 뒤, 일 한도는 즉시). Claude SDK의 rate limit · 503 · 529 포함
- 품질 문제(스키마 불일치 · 안전 필터 차단 · 인용 검사 실패 · 서비스 대상 아님)는 대체하지 않고 기존처럼 멈춤
- 다음 모델은 같은 입력으로 **처음부터** 다시 요청 (부분 결과를 이어받지 않음, court는 재요청 횟수도 새로 셈)
- 시작 전에 목록의 모든 모델 API 키 확인(Claude는 `ant auth login`으로도 인증되어 예외), 외부 전송 안내에 체인 전체 공급자 표시
- 응답한 모델 · 건너뛴 모델과 원인(`overloaded` · `rate_limit` · `daily_quota`)을 `report.json` · `court_report.json`(`requestedModel` · `modelChain` · `fallbacks`)과 단계 결과에 기록

### 2. 무료 모델 자동 사용 (점검 · 생성)
- `free_models.json`: 무료 등급이 있는 Gemini 모델 목록 (출처 · 확인일 · 한도 확인 위치 · 데이터 사용 문구). `llm.has_free_tier` · `free_tier_model_list`가 읽음. 호출을 막지는 않고 안내만 함 (키가 무료인지는 알 수 없으므로)
- 파이프라인 시작 안내: extract · court에 무료 등급이 있는 모델이 있으면 "판결문은 유료 키로만" 경고, 점검 · 생성에는 `delay` · 교차 호출 확인 안내
- `generate.models` · `contamination.models`에 `"free:<공급자>"`를 적으면 목록의 무료 모델을 자동 사용. 최상위 `freeModels`(`max` 동시 사용 상한 기본 3, `include` 우선순위, `exclude`)로 조절
- 사용 중인 무료 모델이 **일 한도 · 크레딧 소진**으로 막히면 대기 모델이 자리를 채움. 새 모델은 **독립 투표자**로 자기 이름으로 처음부터 `runs`회 기록(재생성 중에도 `runs`회), 막힌 모델이 이미 끝낸 회차는 그 모델 이름으로 남아 선택 후보에 유지
- 대체 모델도 사전 학습 점검을 먼저 통과해야 참여. 점검 설정이 `stop`이어도 자동으로 들어온 후보 때문에 멈추지 않고 그 후보만 제외하고 다음 대기 모델을 봄
- 선택한 목록과 교체 내역(`replaced`)을 `state.json`과 generate 단계 결과에 기록. 이어 실행하면 같은 목록을 쓰고 `--rerun` · `--from contamination`은 처음부터 다시 선택(`--from generate`는 유지)
- `free:`는 기본으로 점검 · 생성에서만 가능. extract · court에서는 `allowFreeTierForJudgment: true`일 때만 목록 맨 끝의 마지막 백업으로 허용 (그 밖은 설정 검증이 거부). `generate.py` · `extract_case.py` · `court_draft.py` 단독 실행은 `free:`를 모름
- `generate_runs`에 `on_exhausted` · `replacement_runs` 추가, 점검을 `contamination_runs` / `contamination_verdicts`로 나눠 재사용

### 3. 판결문 단계의 무료 등급 백업 (선택, 기본 꺼짐)
> **주의 — 판결문 원문이 무료 등급으로 나갈 수 있는 옵션입니다.** 무료 등급은 입력을 제품 개선에 쓰고 사람이 검토할 수 있습니다. 비식별화(`extract`) · 재판부 초안(`court`)은 정규식 마스킹만 거친 원문을 보내므로 당사자 이름 · 지명 · 날짜가 그대로 나갑니다. **리뷰에서 이 부분을 따로 봐 주세요.**
- `allowFreeTierForJudgment`(**기본 `false`**)가 `true`일 때만 `stages.extract.model` · `stages.court.model` 목록 **맨 끝**에 `free:<공급자>`를 **마지막 백업**으로 쓸 수 있음. 꺼져 있으면 설정 검증이 거부
- 유료 모델이 하나 이상 앞에 있어야 하고(검증), 유료 모델이 **모두 막힌 뒤에만** 무료로 넘어감 (유료를 건너뛰고 무료로 가지 않음). 조건은 대체 체인과 같음(과부하 · 한도 · 일 한도만, 품질 문제는 대체 안 함)
- `freeModels`(`max` · `include` · `exclude`)로 개수 · 포함 · 제외 조절. 백업 공급자 키가 없으면 그 모델은 빼고 알림(실행은 막지 않음). `court.model`이 `null`이면 extract 목록 사용
- 경고: 시작할 때 단계마다 크게 표시 + 외부 전송 안내에 백업 공급자 표시, 무료 모델로 넘어가는 순간 · 실제로 응답했을 때 다시 경고
- 기록: `report.json` · `court_report.json`에 `usedFreeTier`(허용했지만 쓰지 않으면 `false`), 단계 결과에는 `true`일 때만 기록. 옵션이 꺼져 있으면 값 자체가 없음
- README에 위험과 "공개된 판결문에만 켠다"를 명시. 넘어가기 직전의 사람 확인은 없음(파이프라인이 비대화형)

### 4. 리뷰 반영
- 테스트 import 순서, court 보고서에 실제로 실패한 모델 기록, 모델이 하나일 때 원인 체인 보존, `stage_extract`도 `outputs["model"]` 기록
- `--from generate` 시 목록 유지 · 점검에서 자리를 내준 모델 제외, 재생성 중 대체 모델 회차 수, 대체 모델 점검 오류 시 생성 요약 보존, `rate_limit` 표시를 "요청 한도(429)"로 정정
- README(본문 · case-extractor) · `pipeline.example.json` 반영

## Jira

author: amankv1234
body:
## Description

This pull request fixes a silent authentication failure bug where users with an expired or invalid JWT token were redirected to the homepage (`/`) instead of the authentication page.

**Closes #581**

**Root Cause:** In the `verifyToken` function within `authContext.tsx`, the redirect path was incorrectly set to `navigate('/login')`, which is not a registered route. The application's wildcard route (`path="*"`) caught this and redirected the user to the homepage instead.

**Fix:** Updated the redirect route to `navigate('/auth')`, correctly routing the user to the authentication page upon token failure.

## Changes Made

* Changed `navigate('/login')` to `navigate('/auth')` inside `frontend/src/context/authContext.tsx`.

## Steps to Verify

1. Log in to the application.
2. Open **DevTools → Application → Local Storage**.
3. Delete or modify the `token` value to make it invalid.
4. Refresh the page.
5. The application correctly redirects to `/auth` and asks the user to log in again.

author: yipengfei329
body:
The old iOS toast sat at the very top, covered the navigation bar (back button) and could not be swiped away. Sheets and lightboxes each drew toasts in their own place (or not at all).

## Change
- **Placement**: toasts dock at the bottom, floating 8pt above the tab bar (and the resume bar), the keyboard, or the bottom safe area on sheets / full-screen pages. If a toast is posted right before a sheet closes, it follows down to the tab bar. Same convention as Material's snackbar; the top stays free for navigation and system banners.
- **Look & feel**: iOS 26 interactive liquid glass. Single line is a 52pt capsule, multi-line is a rounded rect, and the width hugs the text (max 440pt). Swipe down or tap to dismiss; dragging up is rubber-banded. Only one toast at a time (a new one replaces the old; the web still stacks up to 4). Success / error play haptics, VoiceOver announces the message and offers a "关闭" action, and Reduce Motion falls back to a fade.
- **One host for the whole app**: toasts render in a pass-through overlay `UIWindow`, so the same toast appears in the same place above sheets and full-screen covers. `sheetFeedback()` keeps confirm / prompt dialogs inside the sheet and forwards toasts to the root.
  - The window is only visible while a toast is shown, and it hands status bar / home indicator decisions to the app's top view controller. An always-visible overlay overrides the app's `statusBarHidden` (player, lightbox) — confirmed with a control experiment.
  - Hit testing only claims the toast's own frame; touches next to it, such as the back button and list rows, pass through.
  - Drag state uses `@GestureState`, so a cancelled drag (finger leaving the bottom edge) cannot leave the timer paused forever.
- **Consistency fixes**:
  - Three sheets posted toasts without `sheetFeedback()`, so error toasts were hidden under the sheet: clear watch history, torrent actions, subscription detail.
  - The gallery and photo lightboxes now use the shared toast instead of their own capsules. The "正在准备下载…" progress stays inline.
- The player's `PlayerHUD` (on-video OSD) is intentionally unchanged.

## Testing
- New `MovieClawUITests/ToastUITests` (4 cases), driven by real actions against a disposable local backend (`TEST_RUNNER_MC_TEST_TOAST_FIXTURE=1 MC_TEST_SERVER=… MC_TEST_PASSWORD=…`; it rotates an MCP token and changes then restores the password, so do not point it at a real server):
  - **Root**: docked above the tab bar; drag up springs back; swipe down / tap dismiss; rapid repeats leave a single toast; auto-dismiss at ~4s; touches beside the toast still reach the list and the back button.
  - **Sheet**: the toast shows above the sheet, docked to the bottom safe area, and swipes away.
  - **Keyboard**: the toast floats above the keyboard.
  - **Long message**: wraps to two lines and is not truncated; it lands above the tab bar after the sheet closes.
- Root and sheet cases passed 8 consecutive runs with debug logging (no stuck toasts); the full suite passed several more runs. Entrance / exit animations were checked frame by frame on screen recordings.
- `MovieClawMac` / `MovieClawTV` build. The shared `Feedback.swift` puts the UIKit parts behind `#if os(iOS)`.
- Not verified: the resume bar case (no watch history on the test server; placement uses the page's safe area, which should include it), iPad, and a real device.

author: s2x
body:
## What changed

A start-up `resume` (or `goto` to the saved state) of a paused run is refused while `orchestrator.workers` runs are active. The run stays paused. A run adopted by the orchestrator leaves `Manager.adopted` when it ends. The visit counts of the saved state are kept on a start-up `resume` and on a `goto` to that state. The paused runs are adopted before `Start` returns, so an answer given before the plan cannot start a second run of the same issue.

Closes #388

author: bdf1992-workstation[bot]
body:
A code cluster now opens into its files and then into their members, by room on screen alone, and links follow the groups they leave and enter.

- `scripts/graph_view.py`: a code cluster of two or more files is laid out as packed file discs; the view carries a `files` table.
- `references/viewer/index.html`: a cluster opens when it has room and its median file disc is at least 5 px on screen (`clusterOpens`); a file opens above 26 px. An open file has a faint ring and its name; an open cluster keeps its name, held at the screen edge when its ring's top is off screen. Links between open files are routed through file and cluster centres (Holten 2006, straightened by 0.85, 16 segments); closed file pairs get one line; a link inside one file runs straight; a selection's band across planes is routed. The pointer no longer opens clusters.
- `tests/test_view.py` class `Files`, `tests/test_viewer.py` classes `Routes` and `Opens`: geometry and the pure rules, each shown failing before its code.

Looked at twice in Chromium by a reviewer who did not build it, on the kept run (732 clusters, 21,328 nodes, 56,221 links), software GL at 1600 by 1000, against master 83ae4b4. Time inside draw over 40 moving frames, mean / worst ms:

| Sequence | This branch | Master |
|---|---|---|
| Whole view, nothing selected | 1.37 / 4.1 | 0.9 / 1.3 |
