author: deer
body:
`AbstractParser` could only stop at the first `ParseException`, so a grammar with several mistakes made the user fix and re-run once per mistake. A grammar can now opt in to recovery by catching a `ParseException` at a statement boundary, passing it to the new `report(ParseException)` (or `reportTranslated(RuntimeException)` for grammars that throw their own exception type), and moving the scanner past the damage before carrying on.

The new `runRecovering()` returns an `AbstractParser.Outcome` holding the possibly partial value and every error in the order reported, each translated by `translate(ParseException)`. A `ParseException` that escapes `parse()`, or comes from `registerFilters`, is recorded as the last error and the value is empty. Input left unconsumed is also reported as an error. `run()` is built on `runRecovering()` and still throws the first error, so existing grammars behave as before, except that `translate` now runs while the scanner is still open.

To make skipping practical, `Scanner.skipPast(String)` skips through the end of the next occurrence of a delimiter, or to the end of input when there is none. It works on the raw input, so a newline delimiter is found even when `Filter.WHITESPACE` is registered, and it always advances unless the input is exhausted, so a recovery loop cannot spin. `AbstractParser.skipPast(String)` exposes it to grammars.

This also fixes a bug in `LookaheadReader`: when a peek asked for more characters than the buffer could hold, the buffer was grown without carrying over only the unconsumed characters, so a later read could return stale content if some input had already been consumed. The grown buffer now keeps exactly the unconsumed content.

author: azank1
body:
Story 3.2: every export states what its signed receipt covers (FR-8, NFR-4, NFR-5).

**Stacked on the 3.1 draft** (`feat/criterion-step-coverage`), which sits on the epic 2 drafts. The base is not `main`, so **this PR runs gitleaks only. There are no test jobs and no `ci-complete`, and a green check does not mean the code was tested.** The CI prerequisite (`ship-ci-seam-deps.sh`) applies.

## What it does

Of the work done, a receipt commits to the tool calls in its steps and the verdicts signed beside them, and to nothing else: model calls and planning are not in it, and a call refused before it ran may appear as a failed step or not at all. That is now said wherever the record leaves the building, in one producer-neutral text, computed from the envelope by whoever reads it and never stored in it.

- **SDK:** `emerge.run_attestation.coverage_statement(envelope)` — the one statement, with the receipt's step count and distinct tools in first-appearance order. `orcha verify` prints a Coverage block; `--json` carries `coverage`.
- **Session export** (`GET /sessions/{id}/audit`): a `coverage` block in every export — chat and firing, sealed or not, with or without the SDK installed (a pinned copy, tested equal) — with the receipt's step count and tools, and how the export's own step list (the session's transcript, unsigned) relates to it.
  - **"The signed receipt" is said only after the stored envelope verified offline when the export was built** (`receipt_verifies`). A stored receipt that does not verify reads "A stored receipt for run X did not verify when this export was built; nothing is read from it" — no step count, no tools, no models read from it. With the verifier not installed it reads "could not check its signature".
- **Mailer:** a "What a signed receipt covers" section; that its own turn's receipt seals after it, so it is not the one described; per-step "structurally checked" / "failed" / "not checked" instead of "verified" ("failed" stays bare — the export does not say whether the check failed or never ran); it is a run summary, not the receipt, in its result line and tool description too; Metaorcha in sender and subject.
- **KYA evidence package:** the manifest carries the statement and per-leg step counts. Verification **fails** a stored statement that differs from the verifier's, recomputes each leg's reading from its envelope and fails a mismatch, and only *notes* a manifest written before FR-8 (no statement at all).
- **"Verified Runs" naming** replaced by "run evidence" in docstrings and the chat download tooltip.
- **`common/utils/tests/test_record_wording.py`** sweeps the tree for wording that calls the record complete ("complete/full/entire transcript|log|record|audit trail", "every action the agent", "everything the agent did"), whitespace- and comment-normalised, with one reviewed exception (RFC 0003 §Alternatives, where "complete" qualifies the chain-vs-tree step list). README is frozen under ADR 0008 and not swept.

## Evidence (local, 2026-10-05, at this PR's head)

| Command (dummy env) | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/unit/test_export_coverage.py` (superagent, new) | A sealed chat session states its coverage; an unreadable envelope is not counted; the fallback reads as the SDK does (pinned equal); without the SDK the export still states its coverage; a tampered envelope reads "did not verify" with no steps or tools; `receipt_verifies` on a golden valid / tampered / non-dict / SDK-absent envelope; the mailed summary carries the coverage. |
| `sdk/tests/test_coverage.py` (new), `test_evidence_package.py` (+2) | statement shape, distinct tools, `None` steps, CLI block and `--json`; KYA fails an altered statement and a per-leg mismatch |
| `pytest tests/unit` (superagent) | 786 passed, 8 skipped (3.1: 774 passed, 8 skipped) |
| seam list (CI's) | 474 passed (3.1: 462 passed) |
| sdk | 106 passed (3.1: 91) |
| common (`test_record_wording.py` new) | 102 passed (3.1: 99) |
| gateway 146 · validator 151 | unchanged from 3.1 |
| `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (changed files) | clean |
| `tsc -b`, `eslint` (changed files), `vite build` | exit 0 |

**Mutation checks** (each reverted change failed tests; measured at the final tree):

| Reverted change | Tests failed |
|---|---|
| the export never verifies the envelope (`verified = True`) | 2 |
| `run_models` ignores an unverified envelope | 1 |
| an unverified receipt's steps still counted | 1 |
| the no-verifier wording dropped | 1 |
| the statement's "commits to nothing else" clause regressed | 4 |
| the mailer says "structurally failed" again | 1 |
| the mailer's result says "Receipt sent" | 1 |
| KYA only notes an altered statement | 1 |
| KYA does not recompute per-leg coverage | 1 |

Measured at the pre-review tree (sites the review did not change): coverage always "no receipt read" (2); "read" with no envelope (1); the fallback statement differs by one word (4); duplicate tools counted (2); `None` steps read as 0 (10); CLI block not printed (3); `--json` drops coverage (3); the KYA manifest drops coverage (2); the mailer drops the coverage lines (2); `load_settlement` does not carry the envelope (2).

## Review

Four lenses, findings verified first-party. Fixed in this commit:

- **The export said "the signed receipt" without checking the signature.** It now verifies offline at export time and says so either way; a receipt that fails reads as not read.
- **The mailer said "structurally failed"** for a step whose check may never have run. "failed", bare.
- **The KYA package trusted its own stored statement.** A manifest edited after the fact passed; it now fails, and each leg is recomputed from its envelope.
- **"Receipt sent"** for what is a run summary.

## Notes

- **The coverage key's shape differs across the CLI, the export and the KYA manifest** (statement + counts in the export; statement + per-leg counts in KYA). Each is tested; unifying them is a follow-up.
- **The CLI's coverage block ships with the next `orcha-sdk` release** (PyPI release is gated; see `orcha-sdk-release-preconditions`).
- **RFC 0003's completeness wording** — the spec still reads as if the step list were complete in places the sweep exempts; the amendment is a spec change and is yours.

> **Overview**

Settlement loading now passes the stored **envelope** through for that check. **Gateway and frontend** types/tooling adopt the new field and relabel "Verified Runs" to **run evidence**.
>

author: dogkeeper886
body:
ollama37 runs batch-1 decode on the K80 through ggml's `mul_mat_vec_q`, the same quantized mat-vec kernel upstream uses on every card. That kernel is built around int8 dot products (dp4a), which the K80 lacks: it emulates dp4a with `vmad` (#522), and its int-to-float conversion runs at 1/6 of its FP32 FMA rate. So the kernel reads q4_K weights at about a third of what a die can deliver, and decode, which spends most of its time there, runs well below the hardware. This PR adds `mmvq_k80_q4_K`, which decodes each 4-bit value to FP32 with an OR and an FADD and takes over q4_K mat-vec at batch 1 on Kepler; CI decode rises 16–36 % on dense models.

- **Kernel:** `ml/backend/ggml/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq-k80.cu`. Each value goes into the mantissa of 2^23 and 2^23 is subtracted back out, which is exact and needs no int-to-float instruction. Each warp computes 4 rows, so it loads the input vector once for all of them. A ~5 µs prep kernel pre-scales the input, as `quantize_q8_1` does on the old path.
- **Gate:** 3 lines in `ggml_cuda_mul_mat`. The new path takes q4_K × F32 at batch 1, contiguous and 16-byte aligned, on NVIDIA cards below cc 5.0. Every other case, and every other card, keeps ggml's path.
- **Kernel speed:** 1.4–2.1× faster than `mul_mat_vec_q` at the llama3.1 shapes. It reads 79–109 GB/s against the die's measured 148–157 GB/s ceiling; ggml's kernel reads 49–61 GB/s.
- **Accuracy:** max relative error 2.4e-7 against a double-precision reference, versus 5.5e-3 for `mul_mat_vec_q`, which rounds the input to 8 bits first.
- **CI pipeline:** [run 37722489170](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/actions/runs/37722489170). Build, deploy and canary pass; the models test has 22 models and 29 replies, all judged, 0 failed.
- **CI throughput:** [run 37735178243](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/actions/runs/37735178243) against the #522 run. Decode changes:
  - dense models: +16 % to +36 % (`llama3.1:8b` 10.58 → 14.34)
  - MoE models: +4 % to +9 %
  - Q8_0 and MXFP4 models: within noise

  Prefill stays within ±3 %, except one unexplained −21 % on `gemma3:270m`, a Q8_0 model that never takes the new path. All 25 replies pass.
- **Replies:** 12 of 25 throughput replies match the baseline word for word; the rest match for 2–72 words, then drift, because the input is no longer rounded to 8 bits. I read every drifting reply; all stay coherent and on task.
- **Report:** `docs/reports/k80-q4k-fp32-mmvq-2026-10-08.md` holds the kernel, host and CI numbers. The lab program that produced the kernel numbers is `docs/reports/k80-q4k-fp32-mmvq/bench.cu`.
- **Porting guide:** `docs/porting-k80.md`:
  - corrects the flash attention example's numbers
  - replaces the stale benchmark steps with rules, since the steps live in skills and `cicd/README.md`
  - says to study on the host first, then confirm through CI
- **Issue amendments:** item 1's per-step `nvprof` profile can't run on this host; two other measurements confirm the premise instead. Step 3 is narrowed to batch 1 ([comment](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/issues/563#issuecomment-6054422519)).
- **Not covered:**
  - batch 2–8
  - q6_K layers
  - MoE expert layers (`mul_mat_id`)
  - formats other than q4_K
  - prefill

  These all keep ggml's path.
- **Upstream sync:** `Makefile.sync` copies ggml over with `rsync --delete`, so it would delete `mmvq-k80.cu` and the gate. #522's change carries the same risk.

Closes #563

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core decode matmul numerics (FP32 activations vs q8_1 rounding) on Kepler only, which can shift long outputs while improving throughput; scope is gated but touches hot ggml-cuda dispatch.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **Kepler-only** fast path for batch-1 **q4_K** matrix–vector multiply during decode, because ggml’s `mul_mat_vec_q` is a poor fit on K80 (no dp4a, slow int→float).
> 
> **CUDA:** New `mmvq_k80_q4_K` decodes 4-bit weights to FP32 with bit tricks (no `q8_1` input quantize), shares the input vector across four rows per warp, and is selected first in `ggml_cuda_mul_mat` when `ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq_k80` matches (NVIDIA cc < 5.0, q4_K×F32, batch 1, contiguous, 16-byte aligned). All other GPUs and shapes keep the existing kernels.
> 
> **Docs:** Benchmark report plus `bench.cu` lab harness document ~16–36% CI decode gains on dense q4_K models; `docs/porting-k80.md` fixes the flash-attention example and replaces stale workflow steps with benchmarking rules.

author: mi-no-kim
body:
## 상위 작업

Related to #3

- Work: w5 — 변경된 부분만 CI 검사하도록 조정

## 변경 결과

- `Formatting`은 모든 PR과 `main` push에서 Prettier를 실행하고, 백엔드 Spotless는 `Backend`의 Gradle `check`에서 검사합니다.
- `Frontend`와 `Backend`의 필수 job 상태는 항상 남기되, PR 변경 파일에 따라 무거운 검사 단계만 선택합니다. 변경 파일 판별 오류는 해당 job 실패로 처리합니다.
- 문서 전용 변경은 두 영역의 검사를 건너뛰고, CI 설정 등 공통·미분류 변경 및 `main` push는 두 영역을 모두 검사합니다.
- README, 기여 규칙과 개발 노트를 현재 CI 구성에 맞게 갱신했습니다.

## 계획과 달라진 점

- 계획: 문서·프런트엔드·백엔드 전용 PR에서 분기 실행과 필수 검사 상태를 각각 확인한다.
- 실제: 별도 검증용 PR은 만들지 않고 기존 commit의 변경 파일 목록으로 분기를 로컬 검증했다. 이 w5 PR에서 필수 검사 세 개의 원격 결과를 확인한다.
- 변경 이유: 검증용 PR이 닫힌 뒤에도 기록에 남으므로, 이후 실제 PR에서 문제가 드러나면 수정하기로 결정했다.
- 영향 및 후속 조치: 변경 유형별 실제 PR에서 검사가 선택되는지는 아직 직접 확인하지 않았다. 후속 실제 PR에서 예상과 다른 결과가 나오면 수정한다.
- 관련 개발 노트: `docs/dev-notes/2026-10-08-selective-ci-checks.md`

## 제외 범위와 남은 사항

- 문서·프런트엔드·백엔드 전용 임시 PR 검증은 수행하지 않았다.

## 검증

- 방법: 기존 commit으로 문서·프런트엔드·백엔드·공통·혼합 변경, 대상 브랜치가 앞선 문서 전용 변경과 `main` push를 분류했다.
- 결과: 예상 분류와 일치했고 SHA 누락·오류는 실패했다. Bash 구문, 저장소 Prettier, Git 공백 검사와 변경 문서의 내부 링크 27개가 통과했다.
- GitHub 필수 검사: PR #14의 `Formatting`, `Frontend`, `Backend`가 모두 통과했다. [실행 기록](https://github.com/Mi-no-Kim/RentalRoom/actions/runs/37741001066).

## 최종 squash commit message

```text
ci: 변경 영역에 따라 검사 선택
```

## 체크리스트

- [x] 올바른 부모 Issue 브랜치를 base로 지정했다.
- [x] 부모 Issue의 해당 Work 범위만 변경했다.
- [x] 로컬 검증을 실행하고 결과 및 원격 검증 예정 상태를 기록했다.
- [x] 관련 문서·계약을 갱신했거나 갱신이 필요 없음을 확인했다.
- [x] 부모 Issue의 Work 번호·내용과 이 PR이 일치한다.
- [x] squash commit message가 최종 diff와 일치한다.

author: screentinker
body:
Roadmap item 13. A **Room Display** widget for the screen outside a meeting room.

It shows:
- a large **Available / In use** state, carried by colour, an icon and a word, so it doesn't rely on colour alone
- the current meeting and the time left
- the rest of today's meetings
- when the room is next free

Portrait and landscape layouts, sized in vmin. Setup is described in `docs/room-booking.md`.

## Calendar sources
Each organization brings its own credentials, set up under **Settings → Meeting rooms**:

- **Microsoft 365** room mailboxes, through the org's own Entra app (client credentials, Graph `calendarView`). The docs recommend an `ApplicationAccessPolicy` scoped to room mailboxes.
- **Google Workspace** resource calendars, through a service account. Either share each calendar with it, or use domain-wide delegation with an admin to act as. The JWT is signed RS256 with Node's crypto, so there is no googleapis dependency. **The key's own `token_uri` is ignored**: every host is fixed.
- **Any ICS address**, read-only. This reuses the iCal resolver through a new opt-in `raw_events` mode, which carries the UID, CLASS, TRANSP and the organiser's name. The default output is unchanged.

Secrets and ICS addresses are encrypted with `secretbox` and never returned. The API answers `has_secret` and `ics_host` instead.

## Behaviour (`lib/rooms/service.js`)
- **Cache:** on demand, at most one upstream read per room per minute however many panels poll. The last good copy is kept in the `rooms` row. Errors back off from 30 s up to 15 min.
- **Privacy:** applied on the server. The default hides titles and organisers of private meetings; "never show" hides them all.
- **Book now:** 15, 30 or 60 minutes, or "until" the next meeting, clamped so it never runs into the next meeting. It is checked against a **fresh** read of the calendar, and only one action runs per room at a time, so a double tap books once.
- **End early:**
  - A meeting booked at the panel is shortened to end now.
  - Anyone else's meeting can be ended only if the org allows it. The room then declines it on Microsoft or leaves it on Google, and the organiser is notified.
- **Check-in and auto-release:** an org setting, off by default. It never releases panel bookings, all-day blocks, or meetings well past their check-in deadline.

## How a panel is allowed to act
- The panel capability is an HMAC over the widget, the device and **the device's own token**. Re-pairing or removing the screen invalidates it.
- The server sends it only over that device's authenticated socket, as `widget_panel` in the playlist payload.
- The player puts it in the widget URL's **fragment**, so it never appears in a log or a cache key.
- `/api/room-panel/:widget/action` checks:
  - the capability
  - that the device is in the widget's workspace
  - a per-device rate limit
- For a copied workspace in a scale-out setup, actions are forwarded to the primary, before the body is read. `scale-out-guards` asserts this.

**Player support for booking:**

| Player | Booking |
|---|---|
| Android (fullscreen, zones, walls) | ✅ |
| Web player (`index.html` and `legacy.html`) | ✅ |
| Native Pi / Windows player | ✅ |
| Tizen, webOS, BrightSign, Vega | read-only |

## The page (`lib/rooms/render.js`)
- It inlines the server's own free/busy function, so the state changes on time even with the network down. It uses the server's clock.
- It says when it is showing a saved schedule.
- It is served with a sandboxed CSP whose `connect-src` allows only this server.
- Calendar text is inserted as text, never as HTML.

## Tests
- `test/room-booking.test.js` (27 tests), run in-process against a fake Graph and Google:
  - free/busy edge cases: back-to-back meetings, overlaps, a meeting ending now, all-day blocks, DST and far-off zones
  - Graph mapping and token caching
  - Google JWT claims and signature, plus the fixed token endpoint
  - ICS recurrences, private and transparent events
  - privacy
  - book clamping, refusals, a booking made elsewhere in the meantime, and a double tap
  - end-early rules, check-in and auto-release
  - cache backoff, a secret that fails to decrypt (fails closed), and panel-capability binding
- `test/room-booking-e2e.test.js` (7 tests), against a real server, a real device socket and a mock Graph over HTTP:
  - no secret or ICS address leaks
  - cross-workspace rooms are refused
  - the CSP on the page
  - the capability arrives in the payload, for that device only
  - actions are refused without it, with another screen's capability, or from another workspace
  - booking and ending reach the calendar and the activity log
- Two bugs were found and fixed while testing:
  - Token caches were keyed on `updated_at`, which has one-second resolution, so a corrected secret kept the old token. They are now keyed on the credentials.
  - A temporal-dead-zone crash in the Settings card appeared only once a connection existed.
- Kotlin `WidgetUrlsTest`: `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` passes locally.
- A native engine test was added but **not run locally**: no PySide6 venv here, and CI doesn't run the native tests. It compiles.
- Full suite on Node 20, rebased on #520 and #521: 5317 tests, 0 failures.
- Headless UI check:
  - Settings card: connect, then Test
  - widget editor: Find rooms, add a room, read it now, save
  - panel: landscape and portrait, Book 15 flips to In use, a read-only screen shows no buttons, offline still shows the schedule
  - Settings at 375px: no overflow and no page errors

## Needs a live tenant
Everything is tested against mocks only. It still needs to be tried against:
- a real Entra app with room mailboxes: `calendarView` on a room, booking as the room, decline
- a Google Workspace with resource calendars, using both shared-calendar and delegated access

I haven't checked whether Graph's `Prefer: outlook.timezone="UTC"` returns times the way the mock assumes for every tenant.

author: dmccoystephenson
body:
## Summary

A documentation accuracy sweep (Stage A) was run against the tree at `b138a6e`. Two command descriptions were found to be wrong and are corrected here:

- **`USER_GUIDE.md` — "Accessing the Server Console" renamed to "Opening a Shell in the Container".** `docker exec -it dpc-mc-server /bin/bash` opens a Bash shell, not the Minecraft console, so a server command such as `stop` typed there is not understood. The Spigot console does not accept typed input at all, because `compose.yml` sets neither `stdin_open` nor `tty` for the `dpcmcserver` service. The section now says this and points to issuing commands in-game as the configured operator. The matching `COMMANDS.md` entry was clarified in the same way.
- **`COMMANDS.md` — "Rebuild the image".** It was described as rebuilding "from scratch" after updating plugin JARs. `docker build` reuses the layer cache (a real from-scratch build needs `--no-cache`), and building the image does not recreate the running container. `up.sh` runs `docker compose up -d --build`, which does both, so the entry now names `./up.sh` as the command that puts a change into service.

Everything else in the sweep checked out. `README.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, `COMMANDS.md`, `CONFIG.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `sample.env` were compared against `compose.yml`, `up.sh`, `down.sh`, `Dockerfile`, `resources/post-create.sh`, and `.github/workflows/build.yml`. The ports, container name, defaults, plugin lists, Testing sections, and the `main` branch target all matched.

## Related findings (not addressed in this PR)

- The sweep turned up a runtime bug: when a bundled JAR is bumped to a new version, a server with an existing volume ends up with both versions installed. It has been filed as #44 rather than fixed here, because the fix belongs in `resources/post-create.sh`.
- Open issues deferred this cycle, with reasons:
  - #38: part 2 was resolved by #43 (status comment posted). Part 1 needs an edit to `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, which needs maintainer authorization.
  - #35: the only remaining fix is in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, which needs maintainer authorization.
  - #34 and #33: these change `Dockerfile`, `compose.yml`, and `resources/post-create.sh`, which are on the do-not-auto-merge list and need a real server start to verify.
  - #21: the maintainer needs to choose between using the directory and removing it.
  - #6 and #4: feature-sized work.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test-wiring.sh` — `WIRING TESTS: PASS`
- [x] `tests/test-scripts.sh` — `SCRIPT TESTS: PASS`
- [x] `tests/test-post-create.sh` — `POST-CREATE TESTS: PASS`
- [ ] `docker build` was not run locally. This PR is docs-only (UNVERIFIED-not-applicable), and the CI `build` job on the PR head is the gate.

No tracking issue: these gaps were found during a documentation sweep.

author: danwright32
body:
Part of #4358. Part of #4369. Slice E4b of the cutover plan (plan v7 Phases 4 and 5, milestone 80): the queue engine's pieces, all UNWIRED. Nothing in the app constructs `QueueEngine`, so every screen reads exactly what it reads on main. E4d (the switch) wires them.

The 100 ms bar is not met until Phase E (#4343) says so. This is a #4275 plan step, not the cutover.

## What changed

- **The queue derivation** (`App/QueueEngineQueue.swift`, plan section 3's E4b row). `QueueEngineQueue.derivation(freezeWatch:)` hands the engine `QueueRenderPass.make` over its facts (E4a made `make` generic and nonisolated): shows in key order then identifier (L343), inquiries, answers and sources as their records in a declared order, struck addresses, producer corrections and town refusals as the values the pass already takes. Plus `differingFields` (the RenderData comparator), `nextChange` (`DueWork.nextChange` over the facts and the soonest Reached out moment, a lower bound under the 60 s floor) and `builtCardKeys`. The published value is `QueueEnginePass`: the RenderData, the card store's contents captured when the pass was derived (the verifier compares those on its own thread, never the class the main thread writes to), the next change, the sampled card key, and the cards the publish check replaced.
- **The signal inputs as a value** (`QueueEngineContextInputs`, on `QueueEnginePassInput` and on every `QueueEngineOutput`): Gmail, the client window, the run slots, the check's start and lookups, the reply run. The engine reads them through an injected reader with NO default (L168) whenever a pass derives, and the verifier rebuilds from the ones the output carries (L70). `QueueEngineContextInputsTests` holds the members to `QueueInputSource.byInput`'s `.signal` inputs both ways (L96).
- **The freeze watch on the engine's own passes** (#4357 step 8): the derivation's `onTheMainActor` form counts and times each turn's pass (`recordPass`, `recordPassCost`); the verifier's rebuild runs the plain `derive` and records nothing. The two existing guards (`EveryRenderPassIsCountedTests`, `AStallSaysHowLongItsPassesTookTests`) found the new `make` call site and required it.
- **The matrix's output arm now measures** (E1b printed it UNMEASURED). The change-kind matrix runs the engine with the queue's derivation and asserts, for every kind at 1, 60 and 300 rows, that the output equals the pass over the fresh read at the output's own instant, view and signal inputs: 63 lines, all `output equals the pass over the fresh read`.
- **The card check at publish and comparison (iv)** (item 8, #4357 step 9). `PassInputs.checksACardInThePass` (and `scope`'s `checksACard`) turn the in-pass check off for the engine only, because over retained facts its fresh build reads the very facts the card came from (L70); the memo path keeps it unchanged. At publish the engine samples the scope's riskiest built card, rebuilds it from the row the MAIN CONTEXT holds (resolved by identifier through the context, not the engine's members, L345), records a `cardDivergence` with the field names and draws the fresh card (C1, via `QueueEnginePass.card(for:)`). The verifier, once (i) and (iii) agree, rebuilds every built card from models a context of its own reads and returns `cardMismatch`, a new record kind: not corrected and not healable, so it is said apart from `cardDivergence`, whose reader says "corrected before drawing" (L11). E4c's gate refuses it and counts both new counters (`cardDivergences`, `cardMismatches`).
- **The engine as `ShowResolver`** (item 11): members by identifier; during the launch fill a row not yet held is found through the main context (`FactStore.Table.liveRow`, which fetches rather than trusting `model(for:)`, #4106 probe 2) and noted dirty; a faulted row is found and then refused with a fourth `ShowIdentity.Refusal`, `outOfStep`. `ShowResolver` gains `isOutOfStep(_:)`, false for rows a caller merely holds.
- **Reload this show** (item 12, no view): `QueueEngine.reload(_:)`, recovery's own refetch plus its throwaway-context heal check, refused by name while the main context holds an unsaved edit on the row. Six outcomes (`reloaded`, `alreadyInStep`, `unsavedEdit`, `stillOutOfStep`, `gone`, `unreadable`), each a test and a sentence. A reload that changed a value is Dan acting, so it publishes even mid-landing.
- **The landing generation** (item 4, #4369): `openLanding()` and `closeLanding(_:)`. While a landing holds, the intake reads at most `QueueEngineLandingSetup.batchSize` (150) rows a turn, Dan's noted rows first, and carries the rest (`carried`, registered in `identityKeyedState`); no output is published unless Dan acts (a noted row, a view input, a reload); one publish follows the close. The matrix's `scoutLanding` kind runs at 1, 60 and 300 rows with the batch forced to ONE row (L101), in three saves, asserting no publish while open, at least n batches, and one publish at the close.
- **The launch notice's sentences as values** (item 10): `QueueEngineNoticeCopy.verifierSentence` (zero matches says never checked, never clean), `faultSentence` (nothing when no row is faulted; a row stuck over an hour names the button), and `verifierLogLine` with the four nets, the fault summary and the match state for #4343's real-use day.
- **`RenderDataComparison` moved into the app** (`UI/RenderDataComparison.swift`), because the derivation is now one of its readers; one comparator for the oracle and the verifier (L263). A form taking captured card contents is added.

## For E4d, said here so it is not lost

- E4d wires: the derivation with the app's freeze watch, the live signal reader (the reads `makeRenderData` makes today, and the client window from `engine.facts`' sources), every landing entry point opening and closing a generation in a `defer`, the card row drawing `QueueEnginePass.card(for:)` so C1 reaches the screen, the fault row and its Reload button, and the notice sentences (which session's counts they are handed is E4d's: `queueVerifierMatchCount` is a lifetime count today).
- The card check is built against TODAY's card store shape (`CardStore.Contents`, `preamble`, and `card(for:)` called, not changed). E4a's second half (parallel) reworks `CardSources` and `card(for:)`; nothing here touches them, and `QueueEnginePass` is `@unchecked Sendable` only until that store is a value snapshot, with the reason written beside it.
- `liveShow` answering nil on a read that THREW during the fill is counted (`unreadRows`) but resolves as `gone`, whose sentence says the show is no longer in the queue. Recorded rather than fixed: saying it truthfully needs a fifth refusal the resolver has no channel for (L11).
- `fixtures/test-only-reachable.txt` gains exactly the three lines its scan finds (`CardDivergenceReport.swift:faultSentence`, `verifierSentence`, `verifierLogLine`), each naming E4d. The log line was first called `logLine`, a name other app files declare, so the scan could not see it (the review's catch); renamed so it does. The other new declarations live in `App/` or are mentioned elsewhere in their own file, so the ratchet (strict both ways) refuses lines for them.

## The five

1. **writer**: `QueueEngineContextInputs` is written by the engine's injected reader (tests: `EngineHarness.noSignals`; E4d: the live reader) and stamped onto each `QueueEngineOutput` by `runTurn` and `landFirstRead`. `QueueEnginePass` fields: `QueueEngineQueue.derive` writes `data`, `builtCards`, `nextChange`, `checkKey`; `checkAtPublish` writes `corrected`. The `cardDivergences` and `cardMismatches` counters and the `cardMismatch` record kind: `QueueEngine.checkedCard` and `finishVerification(.cardMismatch)`. `QueueEngineVerification.cardMismatch`: `QueueEngineVerifier.verify`. `landingBatches` and `heldTurns`: `rowsThisTurn` and `runTurn`. `carried`, `openLandings`, `heldReasons`, `changedByReload`: the landing API, `rowsThisTurn`, `runTurn`, `reload`. `ShowIdentity.Refusal.outOfStep`: `ShowIdentity.res

body:
MongoDB ran without a keyFile and without `authorization`, so anyone reaching port 27017 inside the VNet could read and write the blog data.

## Changes
- `main.bicep`: new required `@secure()` parameter `mongoDbReplicaSetKey` (generate with `openssl rand -base64 756 | tr -d '\n'`). It is passed to the DB CustomScript through **`protectedSettings`** (`vm.bicep`), so the key is not visible in the extension settings or the instance view.
- DB CustomScript: writes `/etc/mongodb/keyfile` (400, mongodb) and enables `security.keyFile` + `authorization`.
  - Rerun-safe: if the same key is redeployed, mongod is not restarted.
  - If a different key is deployed, the script stops with `mongoDbReplicaSetKey differs` and mongod keeps running.
  - On an existing pre-#36 member that already has data, the new config is staged as `/etc/mongod.conf.pending-auth` and mongod is not restarted.
- Post-deployment setup (`.sh` / `.ps1`):
  - Runs `rs.initiate` and creates the first user through the localhost exception, then authenticates every later call.
  - Treats existing users as OK, so reruns are safe.
  - Checks that unauthenticated reads are rejected (AUTHCHECK) and warns with a pointer to runbook 7.3 if they are not.
- Docs (JA + EN):
  - Day 1 and Day 2 checklists, quick-reference cards and the runbook now use authenticated `mongosh` commands.
  - New runbook §7.3: rolling migration with `transitionToAuth`, plus a downtime option, troubleshooting and key rotation.
  - `design/DatabaseDesign.md` updated.

## ⚠️ Breaking for learners / existing environments
- `main.local.bicepparam` must now set `mongoDbReplicaSetKey`; deployment fails with BCP258 otherwise.
- Existing environments must follow runbook §7.3 after redeploying.

## Merge order
Stacked on #49 (`fix/32-post-deploy-errors`): merge #49 first.

## Azure validation (japanwest), all passed
**New deployment**
- Keyfile identical on all 3 DB VMs.
- The key and passwords were not found in the extension GET, the instance view or the logs.
- Post-deploy run and rerun both exit 0.
- Unauthenticated `find` is rejected; the app API works with `authSource=blogapp`.

**Redeploys**
- Same key: mongod was not restarted, and the probe saw 0 errors in 762 requests.
- Wrong key: the deployment failed with the expected message and mongod kept running.
- Original key restored: mongod was not restarted.

**Migrating a pre-#36 environment (built from `main`)**
- Redeploying with the key staged `pending-auth` without a restart.
- Post-deploy pointed to §7.3.
- §7.3 Phases 1 and 2 ran with 0 errors in 485 probe requests, and the seed data was kept.
- Afterwards, unauthenticated reads are rejected and post-deploy reports "Access control is active".
- This found one doc fix: the former PRIMARY retakes the role after restart (commit b4508f9).

## Follow-ups (separate issues)
- App tier still has `mongoDbAppPassword` in public CustomScript settings.
- DB CustomScript `apt-get update` can fail on the apt lists lock held by platform agents (also on main).

Closes #36

author: cayetanobv
body:
## What changed

A collection the Iceberg backend writes keeps its `root` and `parent` links. `portolan check`
reports no `PTL-LNK` finding on an Iceberg catalog.

## Why

`on_post_add` re-saves the collection to write the `iceberg:` fields and the extension. pystac
points `root` at the object it saves, so that save made the collection its own root and dropped
`parent`:

```
root  ./collection.json
```

`portolan check` then reported two errors on every collection the backend wrote:

```
✗ PTL-LNK-001 missing required structural link rel:'parent'
✗ PTL-LNK-006 link rel:'root' href './collection.json' points to the wrong object:
              must point to the root catalog
```

A reader walks a catalog through `root` and `parent`. A collection that names itself as the
root ends the walk, while the catalog's own `child` link still lists it, so the tree looked
complete from above and broke from below.

Resolves #940.

## Verification

A catalog built from this branch with `tests/fixtures/realdata/fieldmaps-boundaries.parquet`:

```
$ portolan init cat --auto --backend iceberg --license CC-BY-4.0
$ portolan add --portolan-dir cat cat/b/fieldmaps-boundaries.parquet
$ portolan check cat | grep PTL-LNK
(no output)
```

The collection's links:

```
root         ../catalog.json
parent       ../catalog.json
agents       ./AGENTS.md
describedby  ./README.md
```

On `main` the same catalog gives `root ./collection.json` and no `parent`.

The Iceberg suite passes:

```
$ pytest tests/iceberg -m "not e2e and not e2e_slow" -q
156 passed, 9 deselected in 85.08s
```

`ruff`, `ruff format` and `mypy --strict` are clean.

## Implementation notes

The pipeline already repairs these two links after its own `save(SELF_CONTAINED)`, in
`finalization._fix_collection_links`. Its docstring names this exact failure:

> PySTAC sets root to self by default, so both structural links need repointing: `root` at the
> catalog root, and `parent` at whatever catalog contains this collection. [...] (rashid
> PTL-LNK-006, issue #711).

The hook was the one caller that skipped it. Calling it keeps one implementation of the repair.
Writing a second one in the backend would let the two drift, and #711 records what that costs
for a nested collection id, where `parent` is an intermediate `catalog.json` rather than the
root.

**This imports a private function across modules.** `_fix_collection_links` carries a leading
underscore. The alternatives are to promote it to a public helper in `finalization`, or to stop
the hook re-saving the collection at all. I took the import because a second copy of the repair
is the worse failure, but a reviewer may prefer the rename.

The regression test is `test_on_post_add_keeps_the_structural_links`. It asserts a `parent`
link exists and that `root` is not `./collection.json`, which are the two findings rashid
reports.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Preserved collection parent and root links when saving collections to an Iceberg catalog.

## What changed

The [Format and content](https://github.com/vasapolrittideah/flowspace-api/blob/main/docs/conventions/markdown-and-english-prose.md#format-and-content) rules require numerals for each number in prose, such as 11 instead of "eleven". If a number starts a sentence, the sentence starts with another word. "One" stays a word when it is a pronoun, such as in "each one", and ordinal words, such as "first", stay words.

The Markdown and English prose conventions file follows the whole convention file convention, because this PR changes it. author: lnds
body:
Part of #2372. Retires the `rc-effects-growth` pin of `local_hashmap_masks_mutable` (`0:6`).

## Cause

The native lowering of a `__proto_<op>` dispatcher (`lower_proto_dispatch`, `kir_lower_fns.kai`) calls:

```
kaix_proto_dispatch<N>(KIntV(proto_id), KIntV(op_id), KStrV(pname), KStrV(opname), args…)
```

Each `KStrV` is materialised through `kaix_str_n`: a fresh heap string on every dispatch, owned by the callee. The shim (`stage0/runtime_llvm.c`) read the ids and kept the names only for its panic message, then never released any of them.

So every runtime-dispatched op kept two strings. In `local_hashmap_masks_mutable`, two `put`s and one `get` hash a key, which is 3 × 2 = the 6 strings it grew by per run, on native only. The C backend's shim takes C string literals.

## Fix

The shim takes the ids as `i64` immediates and the names as `const char *` constants. `nemit_proto_dispatch` (`emit_native_ops.kai`) emits them with `llvm_build_string_span`, the same way `kaix_assert_check` gets its message. A dispatch now allocates nothing; the receiver and op args stay boxed, as the impl ABI requires.

A first version kept the boxed ABI and released the four args in the shim. That fixed the leak, but cost +7.3% instructions on `benchmarks/hashmap` (2.9M alloc/free pairs), so the names no longer exist as heap values.

## Fixture and pins

- `examples/perceus/proto_dispatch_args_release.kai`: 100 rounds of `put`/`put`/`get` on a HashMap. Pin `0:0`.

| | C | native |
|---|---|---|
| main, leaked per run | 0 | 600 |
| this branch | 0 | 0 |

- `local_hashmap_masks_mutable`: native growth 6 → 0, so its pin file is deleted.

## Performance

`benchmarks/hashmap/hashmap_vs_map.kai`, native, mean of 5 alternated runs:

| | instructions | user | leaked |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 10.043G | 0.728 s | 2,910,195 |
| this branch | 8.727G (−13.1%) | 0.640 s (−12%) | 1 |

Checksums are identical. The C backend is untouched.

## Verification (local, macOS arm64, llvm@18)

- `make tier0`: OK.
- `rc-leak-gate`: PASS on C and native, 661 fixtures. No other pin moved.

author: ioanbeilic
body:
Triaje: VÁLIDA — premisa verificada contra origin/main@d7d06ee (con #335 ya mergeada; rebasada después sobre 3a801df, que solo trae el release), síntoma reproducido en banco real (`ghcr.io/erplora/hub:dev` 1.1.31-dev.330 con el módulo de `origin/main`): los carriles eran solo «Eva Martín» y «Sin asignar», y las citas de las 11:00 (Bea, no reservable) y de las 12:00 (Luis, dado de baja) apuntaban a carriles que no existían, así que no se veían.

## Causa raíz
`schedulerResources` solo daba a `ok-scheduler` las profesionales **reservables** más «Sin asignar», y `ok-scheduler` solo pinta los eventos de los carriles que recibe. Al desactivar a una profesional en Personal (inactiva y no reservable) o darla de baja (`staff.members.delete`: pasa a terminada y se borra en blando, así que la lista de Personal ya no la devuelve), sus citas ya reservadas seguían en «Lista», pero en «Por profesional» desaparecían: el hueco parecía libre y las citas que había que pasar a otra persona no se veían.

## Qué cambia
- `ui/components/erp-appointments-list/erp-appointments-list.ts`
  - `keptLanes` (nuevo): un carril por cada `staff_id` de las citas del día que no está entre las reservables, con el nombre **actual** de Personal o, si ya no está en la lista (baja), la copia `staff_name` de la cita. Va detrás de las reservables y delante de «Sin asignar».
  - La fila lleva el nombre **tal cual**. Visto en el banco: `ok-scheduler` corta las etiquetas largas en su columna de nombre («Bea Ruiz · no r…») y saca las iniciales de la última palabra («LB» para «Luis Gómez · de baja»), así que la explicación va en un aviso encima de la rejilla: `ok-inline-feedback` tone=warning, testid `appointments-list-staff-view-kept`, «Bea Ruiz y Luis Gómez ya no admiten citas nuevas: sus citas del día siguen en su fila para que puedas pasárselas a otra persona del equipo.» (lista con `Intl.ListFormat`; con un solo nombre, la frase en singular por `Intl.PluralRules`, `ui.staffKeptLanesOne`).
  - `isBookableLane()`: tocar un hueco libre en una fila conservada abre el alta **solo con la hora**, sin preseleccionar a quien ya no admite citas. Soltar una cita en esa fila lo sigue rechazando el servidor (`staff_not_bookable`) y el bloque vuelve a su sitio.
- `locales/en.json` + `locales/es.json`: `ui.staffKeptLanes` y `ui.staffKeptLanesOne`.
- `ui/test/testids.test.ts`: el testid nuevo se declara en el contrato.
- `staff-view-load-states.test.ts` (de #323): **una línea corregida** que fijaba el fallo (con Eva no reservable y una cita suya del día esperaba solo `['unassigned']`); el porqué está en el comentario del test.
- `dist/` rehorneado con el toolkit anclado (OutfitKit 0.1.135): `erplora build . --check` → «exactly what a rebuild gives». `npx erplora contracts` → sin cambios (37 contratos).
- `WORKFLOW.md`, `workflow/agenda.md`, `docs/screens.md` y `docs/concepts.md` describen la fila conservada y el aviso.

## Tests (salida real)
- Nuevo `staff-view-non-bookable-lanes.test.ts` (10 casos). Contra el componente y las locales de `origin/main`, junto con `staff-view-load-states.test.ts`: **10 rojos / 7 verdes** de 17. Con el arreglo: 17/17.
- `npx vitest run modules/appointments-wt-334/ui/` → 55 ficheros, **798/798**.
- Suite ENTERA en copia aislada (`git archive HEAD` + customers/schedules/services/staff/taxes de `origin/main`, OutfitKit 0.1.135 enlazada) con `ERPLORA_TEST_PG_CONTAINER=erplora-test-pg-5433` y `ERPLORA_HUB_DIR` exportados: `erplora test . --against-hub dev` → **✓ 112 batería(s) en verde**, 0 sin correr (handler incluido). Contra `hub:stable` 1.1.30 la instalación de Citas la rechaza #329 (appointments#328, ya conocido en la familia), no esta rama.

### Mutantes (ejecutados con `mutants.py` contra toda la carpeta `ui/`; cada cadena comprobada a 1 aparición antes de aplicarla)
| Mutante | Cae (al menos) |
|---|---|
| M1 sin `...this.keptLanes` | `a professional switched to «not bookable» keeps her lane…` (+ `…who left the team…`, + el de #323) |
| M2 un carril por cita (sin deduplicar) | `two appointments of the same professional share one lane`, `the note names every kept professional once…` |
| M3 sin `bookable.has` (la reservable sale dos veces) | `…keeps her lane with her appointment…`, `a professional who is not bookable and has nothing that day gets no lane and no note` |
| M4 carril para una cita sin `staff_id` | `every appointment of the day lands on a painted lane` |
| M5 la copia del nombre antes que el de Personal | `…keeps her lane with her appointment, and the note names her` |
| M6 sin el respaldo `a.staff_name` | `a professional who left the team…`, `every appointment of the day lands on a painted lane` |
| M7 hueco: vuelta a `resourceId !== UNASSIGNED` | `tapping a free slot on her lane books the hour, not her…` |
| M8 `isBookableLane` = «no es Sin asignar» | `tapping a free slot on her lane books the hour, not her…` |
| M9 el aviso nunca sale | `…keeps her lane with her appointment, and the note names her` |
| M10 el aviso sale siempre | `a professional who is not bookable and has nothing that day gets no lane and no note` |
| M11 conservadas antes que reservables | `the bookable team comes first, then the lanes kept…, then «Unassigned»` |
| M12 `names.join(', ')` en vez de `Intl.ListFormat` | `the note names every kept professional once, in lane order, as a list in the hub language` |
| M13 tone `info` | `…keeps her lane with her appointment, and the note names her` |
| M14 el aviso no se pinta | `…keeps her lane…`, `…who left the team…` |
| M15 siempre la frase en plural | `…keeps her lane…`, `…who left the team…` |
| M16 siempre la frase en singular | `the note names every kept professional once…` |

16/16 muertos. Un mutante anterior, «sin `kept.has`», sobrevivía por ser **equivalente** (un `Map.set` con la misma clave solo reescribe la etiqueta con el mismo nombre): la comprobación se ha quitado del código (6116372) y la sustituye M2, que sí cambia el comportamiento.

## UI vista
Banco real: `ghcr.io/erplora/hub:dev` 1.1.31-dev.330 + este módulo (HEAD) + customers/schedules/services/staff/taxes de `origin/main`. Semilla por las órdenes públicas de cada módulo: tres citas el 09/10 (Eva 10:00, Bea 11:00, Luis 12:00); después Bea pasa a no reservable (`staff.members.update`) y Luis se da de baja (`staff.members.delete`). Modos `ios` y `md`, `es` y `en`, 3 tamaños: en los 12 casos las 4 filas salen pintadas («Eva Martín», «Bea Ruiz», «Luis Gómez», «Sin asignar»), las 3 citas en su fila, el aviso con los dos nombres, 0 errores de consola, y la sonda de `ui-clip-sweep.sh` (copiada tal cual en `scan.mjs`) sin nada cortado, estrujado ni partido. `ui-clip-sweep.sh` sobre `/m/appointments` → `OK 1 URL(s) × 3 sizes`.

Antes (main): /Users/ioan.beilic/.erplora/fleet/logs/appointments-334/ui/main-staffview-es-ios-1440x900.png

author: tylergannon
body:
Native adapter tests repeatedly generated equivalent Go applications and rebuilt successful outputs for separate assertions. Reuse immutable generated modules, compiled service inputs, and compatible successful artifacts. Distinct failures and signals retain private frontends, real native Kit builds, compiler calls, running services, receipts, cancellation, process-group draining, and directory cleanup.

Fixture builds omit unused compressed variants and client bundles only where the contracts consume neither. Native build output supplies Kit's generated types without a second sync, disposable binaries omit DWARF metadata, and ordinary build/test recipes share Node's compiled-module cache. Checker cases share one invocation per checker; publication assertions independently decode one real packed tarball. Compiler-overlay fixtures preserve caller flags, and configuration injections check their anchors.

Independent native mutations demonstrated that retained artifact, compiler, consumer-type, callback, cleanup, import-guard, and metadata assertions fail when their behavior is broken. Both valid and invalid controls were exercised. The latest local full adapter run passed all 44 named test events in 16.510s with zero skips/failures; adapter vet passed. The final inherited-flags refusal also passed with a caller-supplied flag.

Final exact-head CI passed on dd55c32, including the ordinary full Go suite and the Swift client job ([run](https://github.com/tylergannon/skgo/actions/runs/37776655404)). Adapter elapsed time was 113.997s and the full Go-test step took 272s. Earlier branch runs varied from 73.647s to 127.273s; isolated local timing does not establish the requested CI target below 20 seconds. That target remains unmet by 93.997s in this final run.

author: adrianstanca1
body:
Closes a mutation authorization gap on /api/assignments: only company admins (any company project) or an authorized project manager (own assigned project) may create, edit or remove assignments. Every assignment read/write checks canonical active organization, associated project and staff membership to block cross-company links. Adds validation, rate limits, audit entries, E2E checks for foreman/operative denial and PM assignment scoping, contract tests. Local `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, 11 targeted RBAC tests, and credential scanner passed. Follows #322 and #326. Does not touch production company data or user records.

author: investradarsk
body:
## Scope (phase 4/14)
- New independent `GeminiDiscoveryCandidateV1` identity normalization and deterministic directory dedupe gate.
- Rejection memory persisted by versioned SHA-256 fingerprints; only explicit review writes, read-only dedupe checks.
- Canonical lookup includes all `directory_profiles` statuses, including drafts and unpublished profiles, and public contact metadata.
- Four bounded audit outcomes: NEW, DUPLICATE, POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE and REJECTED_BEFORE.
- Events/help fail closed until their type-specific contracts (phases 9/10).
- Additive D1 migration `0114_gemini_dedupe.sql`; production workflow target `APPLY-0114-psipedia-sk-db`.
- Focused identity, matching, rejection, isolation and migration tests; Gemini CI scope enabled.

## Policy
Priority: rejected memory > canonical exact > possible > new. Strong match from phone/email or matching domain+name+city or URL+name without contradictory cities; name+city only is possible. Source evidence URLs are never treated as authoritative contact websites; a validated primary URL is a fallback when the explicit website is absent. Different cities on a shared domain are not automatically duplicates. Read-only scans fail closed above 10,000 canonical records.

## Intentional deferrals
No Notion API or sync, no Gemini call, no scheduler, no admin review, no concepts, no publishing, no legacy Tavily changes. Notion-only pages without D1 canonical mirrors are not looked up in this phase. Stage 5 must use this gate before creating a concept.

## Post-merge
Apply `0114_gemini_dedupe.sql` to production only after merge via the reviewed production D1 workflow, explicitly confirmed as `APPLY-0114-psipedia-sk-db`. **This PR does not apply production migrations.**

**Do not merge automatically. Auto-merge OFF.**

author: jasonkolodziej
body:
## Description

The GitHub wiki was a separate repository edited by hand. Wiki updates couldn't ride along with the PRs that made them necessary, and an automated session can't push to it at all, since a wiki can't be attached as a repository. This makes the main repo the wiki's source and publishes it on merge.

- **`wiki/` is the source of truth.** Imported from `anemoi.wiki` at `380c3b9`, plus the updates for #206–#208:
  - Decision Log #44–#46;
  - API: `X-Anemoi-Cache` and `Cache-Control: no-cache`;
  - Monitoring: when the calibration audit runs;
  - Operations Runbook: automatic cycles in production, where `anemoi-cycle` lives in the dashboard, and what to do when a scheduled cycle is missing;
  - Inference Cycle: single-flight live refresh.

  The #209 parts will land in #209 itself, so they publish when it merges.
- **`.github/workflows/wiki.yml`** publishes `wiki/` to the wiki on every push to `main` that changes it, or on demand (`workflow_dispatch`), via `.github/scripts/publish-wiki.sh`:
  - Each wiki commit records its source as a `Source-Commit:` trailer.
  - A publish **refuses to overwrite** the wiki if it was edited in the UI since the last publish, and names the files. Before the first publish, the wiki must still be at the imported commit (`IMPORTED_FROM`).
  - The whole tree is replaced, so a page deleted from `wiki/` is deleted from the wiki.
- **Console `/docs` builds from `../wiki`** instead of cloning the wiki repo; the clone is kept as a fallback for a console checked out on its own. `/docs` therefore always matches the commit being deployed.
- **The deploy plan treats `wiki/` as a console change**, even though it is all Markdown, so `/docs` redeploys on the same merge.
- `wiki/README.md` and `console/README.md` describe the new flow.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (`fix:`)
- [ ] New feature (`feat:`)
- [ ] Refactor (`refactor:`)
- [x] Documentation update (`docs:`)
- [x] CI/tooling change (`ci:` / `chore:`)
- [ ] Breaking change (add `!` after type, e.g., `feat!:`)

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- [x] I have added or updated tests for my changes — scripts exercised locally, see Testing
- [x] All existing tests pass locally
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation (README, plans, API docs)
- [x] I have checked for and resolved any merge conflicts
- [x] No secrets or credentials are included in this PR

## Testing

- `publish-wiki.sh` against a bare copy of the real wiki:
  - the first publish from `380c3b9` succeeds, adding the trailer;
  - an unchanged re-publish is a no-op;
  - a UI edit after a publish is **refused**, with the file named;
  - once that edit is undone, publishing works again;
  - an unknown `Source-Commit` is refused;
  - a wiki that moved before ever being published is refused;
  - a page deleted from `wiki/` is deleted.
- `deploy-plan.sh` in a scratch repo:
  - a `wiki/` push deploys the console only;
  - a `wiki/` PR tests the console;
  - a root `README.md` change deploys nothing;
  - console and API changes behave as before.
- `sync-wiki.mjs --force` renders all 26 pages from `wiki/`. The generated anchor for Decision Log #44 matches the links written to it.
- `svelte-check`: **0 errors**. The `routes/docs/*` errors seen before only appeared when wiki content couldn't be cloned.
- Not testable locally: pushing to `anemoi.wiki.git` with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`contents: write`). The first run after merge is the check.

author: blamechris
body:
## Cause

`resolveChroxyBin()` resolves the daemon entrypoint relative to the invoking file, so `chroxy service install` from any working copy points the launchd service at that copy. Re-verified on main (post #8324): #8324 (idle-only auto-deploy) never touched `service.js`, so the install path was unchanged.

What was still true of #7161:
- Install only refused when `service.json` existed, with no way to re-point deliberately and no message naming the trees. Deleting `service.json` (or an uninstall/install cycle from another checkout) re-pointed the service silently.
- `service.json` recorded the value passed in rather than what the wrapper actually execs, and nothing reported a disagreement once the two records had drifted.
- Nothing checked that the target tree could start. A tree with a missing dependency became a KeepAlive crash loop (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: 'openai'`).

## Fix (issue direction 2)

- `installService` refuses when any install artifact exists (service.json, wrapper, or plist/unit) unless `force` is set. The error names the tree it is pinned to and the tree it would move to, and flags a service.json/wrapper disagreement. Nothing is written on refusal. `--force` is a new `service install` flag.
- A forced reinstall boots out the loaded launchd job before bootstrapping (`daemon-reload` on systemd), since launchd refuses to bootstrap a loaded label.
- `service.json` now records the exec target parsed back out of the wrapper just written (`parseWrapperExecTarget`); install aborts if the read-back does not match. `chroxy service status` prints "Runs from" and warns on existing drift.
- Offline preflight (`assertChroxyTreeReady`, called by `service install` before any write): every runtime `dependencies` entry must resolve by Node's walk-up rule, and a linked package with a relative `main` must have that file (catches an unbuilt workspace `dist/`). No `package.json` found is a failure, not a pass. Takes a few ms on this repo, with no network and no `npm`.

Not done: direction 1 (a service-owned deploy worktree). #8324's deploy script already covers keeping the daemon tree current.

## Tests

- `tests/service.test.js`: new `service install pinning (#7161)` block, 20 tests, all with temp dirs and injected paths (`_stateDir`, `_servicePath`, `_exec`, `_skipRegister`). Never calls launchctl/systemctl or touches `~/.chroxy` or `~/Library`.
- `tests/cli/service-cmd.test.js`: `install --help` lists `--force`.
- `npm test -w packages/server`: exit 0, 19726 tests. All `lint-*.sh` and eslint pass.

## Mutation results

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| guard returns "not installed" always | red (5 tests) |
| plist signal dropped | red |
| wrapper-only signal dropped | red (first run survived because the plist also existed; test fixed to leave only the wrapper) |
| drift detection forced false | red |
| `dependencies` ignored | red (4) |
| `main` entry check disabled | red |
| no bootout on forced reinstall | red |
| state records a value other than the read-back | red (4) |
| CLI preflight call removed | red |
| CLI `force` not forwarded | red |

## Smoke

smoke: not applicable — CLI/service-install code only; touches no dashboard, app, desktop, protocol, store-core, or server handler/session/permission/ws file. Not run against a real launchd service by design.

**Owner-reserved check:** a real `chroxy service install --force` re-point on the daily-daemon host (bootout, then bootstrap, then `service status` shows "Runs from" matching the wrapper). Running it bounces the live daemon, so automation does not run it.

Closes #7161

author: freemilesarea-boop
body:
## 문제

`post_token`은 Google token endpoint가 거부할 때 운영자가 필요한 진단을 이미 만들고 있습니다:

```
oauth2.token(refresh_token) HTTP 400 · invalid_grant: Token has been expired or revoked.
```

그리고 `lib.rs`의 `From<LouverError> for CloudError`는 이미 그 `detail`을 보존합니다. 하지만 `refresh_access_token()`이 `e.message`만 손으로 꺼내 쓰면서 **그 변환기를 우회했고**, detail이 그 자리에서 버려졌습니다.

결과: 서버 로그와 API 응답에 사용자용 문장만 남아 **토큰 폐기 / 잘못된 client_secret / 시계 오차가 모두 똑같이** `"설정에서 YouTube 계정을 다시 연결해주세요"` 로 보였습니다.

## 수정 — `crates/louver-cloud/src/youtube.rs:318` 1줄

```diff
-        let tokens = self.tokens.refresh(creds, &refresh).map_err(|e| CloudError::Engine(e.message))?;
+        let tokens = self.tokens.refresh(creds, &refresh).map_err(CloudError::from)?;
```

새 코드를 쓰지 않았습니다 — 이미 있던 변환기를 쓰도록 되돌린 것입니다. 이 PR에서 **기존 코드에서 삭제·수정된 줄은 이 1줄뿐**입니다.

| 항목 | 상태 |
| --- | --- |
| 사용자용 message | 불변 (`ErrorCode::YoutubeAuthRefreshFailed`의 user_message 그대로) |
| ErrorCode / `CloudError` variant | 불변 (`Engine`) → HTTP 매핑 불변 |
| detail 없는 실패의 출력 | 종전과 글자 그대로 동일 (테스트로 고정) |
| secret | detail은 core에서 `mask_secrets()` 통과, `post_token`은 form을 detail에 넣지 않음 |
| `post_token` / `refresh_form` / `authorization_code_form` | **변경 0** (`http.rs` 미변경) |
| CCTV / FFmpeg / streaming / DB schema / recovery | **변경 0** |

같은 파일의 다른 세 곳(`seal`, 키체인 `get`, `channel_for`)도 같은 방식으로 detail을 버리지만, 이번 장애와 무관한 별개 문제이므로 **손대지 않았습니다**.

## 회귀 테스트 2개

- `u_a_refused_refresh_keeps_googles_own_reason_all_the_way_up` — **실제 `UreqClient`**(`token_endpoint` 오버라이드)를 로컬 소켓에 꽂아 `HTTP/1.1 400` + `{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Token has been expired or revoked."}` 를 응답합니다. `post_token`이 stand-in이 아니라 실제 테스트 대상입니다. 계정 토큰 만료를 강제해 refresh 경로로 진입시키고, 올라온 에러에 사용자용 문장 **그리고** `oauth2.token(refresh_token)`·`HTTP 400`·`invalid_grant`·`error_description`이 모두 있는지, **client_secret·refresh token·access token은 없는지** 단정합니다.
- `u2_a_failure_without_detail_reads_exactly_as_it_did_before` — detail 없는 실패에 괄호가 새로 붙지 않는지. 위 표의 "출력 동일" 보호막입니다.

실제 secret은 쓰지 않았습니다(기존 harness의 더미 값).

author: cardmagic
body:
## Why

The first run of the Context7 refresh workflow from #64 failed on `main`: curl timed out after 60 seconds with no response. Later calls returned HTTP 400 `{"error":"too-early","message":"Too early to refresh the project. Last update was 0 days ago. Minimum 10 days required between updates."}`. Context7 limits how often one library refreshes, so the workflow would fail on most pushes to `main`.

## What changes

- The request allows 180 seconds for a response and prints the body.
- A `too-early` answer ends the job with a workflow notice instead of a failure.
- Any other non-200 answer still fails the job.

## Validation

- `actionlint` and Prettier pass.
- Against the live API, the old script exited 56 on the too-early answer. The new script, extracted from the workflow file, exits 0 with the notice.

## Summary

Lote C, parte 1: **soundboard do servidor** (ver + tocar). Gerenciar
(criar/editar/apagar sons) fica no cliente oficial por ora.

- Botão Soundboard na barra da chamada (só em canal de voz de servidor,
  com a chamada conectada): abre o painel com os sons do servidor
  (emoji + nome), um clique toca na chamada. Carrega na primeira abertura;
  erro mostra Retry; servidor vazio mostra estado vazio; botões travam
  durante um toque em voo.
- `Command::Soundboard::{List, Play}` → rotas documentadas
  `GET /guilds/{id}/soundboard-sounds` e
  `POST /channels/{id}/send-soundboard-sound` (`sound_id` + `source_guild_id`).
- Estado limitado: 128 sons por servidor, bytes no orçamento de sessão,
  single-flight de lista e de toque, cache por servidor até erro.
- Tocar exige chamada ativa no canal, fase conectada e som conhecido +
  disponível; falha vira status sem derrubar a chamada.
- Chaves novas traduzidas nas 3 línguas (`Soundboard`,
  `Play server sounds to this call`, `Loading sounds…`,
  `No sounds in this server yet`).

## Verification

- Novos: `bounds_accept_documented_shapes_and_reject_overreach` (modelo),
  `sound_list_keeps_valid_rows_and_rejects_foreign_or_wild_ones` (wire),
  `soundboard_list_decodes_and_play_posts_ids` (transporte: resposta da
  lista + corpo do POST), `sound_list_loads_once_and_reloads_after_errors`
  e `play_needs_a_joined_call_and_a_known_sound` (estado).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — PASS; Clippy estrito — PASS.
- `cargo xtask check` — ver Risks (flake pré-existente, passa isolado).

## Before / after

Sem screenshot nativo: o painel exige chamada de voz ativa num servidor com
sons (o demo sintético não tem sessão nem sons) e o kittest não captura tela.
Evidência pelos testes. **Draft por esse motivo + flake abaixo.**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Soundboard: inexistente; tocar era só no Discord oficial | Botão na call bar lista os sons do servidor e toca na chamada |

## Performance

Not applicable — um GET por servidor (em cache) + um POST por toque; lista
limitada a 128 sons com bytes contabilizados.

## Risks / blockers

- **Draft**: `cargo xtask check` local falhou 1 teste flaky pré-existente e
  sem relação (`video::player_tests::a_looping_short_clip…`, timeout de
  mídia sob carga; passa isolado, verificado 5x). Draft até o CI/local dar
  verde limpo.
- Tocar som usa rota documentada mas entrega live segue não verificada
  (padrão do repo); conta normal precisa estar conectada ao canal de voz.
- Sem sons padrão do Discord nesta versão (só sons do servidor) e sem
  gerenciamento; follow-ups possíveis.

author: skyzbpt
body:
## 為什麼要改

原本只支援上市股票。查上櫃代號（例如 6488）時只抓得到即時價，估值、三大法人、走勢、基本面都是空的。另外上次檢查進度時，發現四個小問題。

## 改了什麼

### 1. 上櫃股（`worker.js`）
- **判斷市場**：`marketOf()` 統一判斷，`/api/stock`、`/api/extra`、`/api/command` 共用同一套規則，兩張卡片不會互相矛盾。
  - 上市全市場收盤檔裡有這個代號 → 上市。
  - 收盤檔裡沒有 → 看即時行情回報的市場。
  - 即時行情也沒有（盤前、興櫃、代號有誤）→ 收盤檔正常就推定上櫃；收盤檔也抓不到就先試上市，找不到價格再試上櫃。
  - 收盤檔要超過 100 筆才拿來判斷，避免它回空陣列時把上市股誤判成上櫃。
  - 沒有任何上櫃資料認得的代號（興櫃、打錯）不標成「上櫃」。
- **`/api/stock` 上櫃資料來源**：
  - 走勢與收盤：櫃買中心個股日成交 `afterTrading/tradingStock`
  - 估值：OpenAPI `tpex_mainboard_peratio_analysis`
  - 三大法人：買賣明細 `insti/dailyTrade`，支援 24 欄與 16 欄兩種格式，沒資料時往回找最近一個交易日
  - 即時價與今天的走勢補點，跟上市共用同一段程式
- **`/api/extra` 上櫃資料來源**：
  - 基本資料、月營收、季報、股利、重大訊息：`mopsfe_t187ap*_O`，欄位和證交所相同，解析程式共用
  - 融資融券：`tpex_mainboard_margin_balance`
  - 大盤改顯示**櫃買指數**（`tpex_index`）
  - 上櫃外資持股目前沒有資料源，會加註說明
- **櫃買中心可能擋 Cloudflare 機房**：有開源專案在 2026-08 實測回報，從 Cloudflare 打會回 520 並一路轉址到 `/errors`。所以上櫃資料都設計成選配：
  - 抓不到就降級成只顯示即時行情，並加註說明
  - **不跟隨轉址**：Cloudflare 每一跳轉址都算一次子請求（免費方案每次請求最多 50 次），所以看到 3xx 就直接當成連不上
  - 失敗後 1 分鐘內不再重試；觸發條件是逾時、5xx、3xx、403、429 或回傳非 JSON
  - 上市股完全不會去打櫃買中心
- **上市股速度不受影響**：估值與三大法人日報跟市場判斷一起發出；即時行情先確認是上市時，個股日成交也提早開始抓。
- **`/api/debug`**：
  - 上市、上櫃分開回報 `twseOk`／`tpexOk`
  - 新增 `?otc=` 參數，預設用 6488 檢查上櫃
  - 新增樣本查詢 `ds=tp_<資料集>`、`tpexInst`、`tpexDay`；沒給 `code` 時用 `otc` 代號
- AI 提示詞的資料來源改成「證交所／櫃買中心」，並告訴 AI 用 `market` 欄位分辨上市或上櫃
- **市場雷達維持只掃上市**：櫃買中心全市場報價檔約 4MB，可能超過 Cloudflare 免費方案的運算時間上限。等確認連得上櫃買中心再評估。

### 2. 網頁（`index.html`）
- 行情卡的代號旁標示「上市」或「上櫃」
- 基本面卡依市場顯示加權指數或櫃買指數
- 輸入提示、說明文字、資料來源改成上市與上櫃都適用

### 3. 小問題
- `/api/debug` 的訊息「近 5 個交易日」改成實際回推的 10 個交易日
- 即時行情加上 5 秒逾時，原本沒有設
- 網頁預設 Worker 網址設為 `https://stock.skyzbpt.workers.dev`，裝置上另外存過的網址仍然優先；清空網址時改回預設，狀態顯示與實際連線一致
- `pick()` 遇到同一個關鍵字時，先找名稱完全相同的欄位。這樣 `MarginPurchaseBalance` 不會誤抓到 `MarginPurchaseBalancePreviousDay`

## 合併前審查

三個面向（上櫃資料正確性、對上市股與 Cloudflare 限制的影響、網頁與 `/api/debug`）各自審查，每項發現再由另一位審查者嘗試推翻。確認的問題已在 `e4fa236` 修正：

- **（高）** 櫃買中心一路轉址時，每一跳都算子請求。上櫃代號的研究指令會在呼叫 Claude 之前就把 50 次用光而回 500，`/api/debug` 也會誤報上市資料源失敗 → 改為不跟隨轉址
- **（中）** 上市股查詢要等收盤檔判斷完才開始抓其他資料，冷啟動變慢（模擬 1.5 秒 → 2.7 秒）→ 改為同時發出，回到 1.5 秒
- **（中）** `/api/extra` 與 `/api/stock` 判斷市場的方式不同，收盤檔抓不到時兩張卡片會矛盾 → 統一用 `marketOf()`
- **（低）** 興櫃或打錯的代號被標成「上櫃」→ 沒有任何上櫃資料認得時不標
- **（低）** `/api/debug` 上櫃樣本沒有使用 `otc` 參數；清空 Worker 網址後狀態顯示與實際連線不一致

經驗證後判定不需修改：

- 即時行情 5 秒逾時的取捨
- `/api/extra` 多等一次收盤檔：結果不變，且被行情卡的等待時間蓋過
- `/api/debug` 在農曆年後特定時段可能超過子請求上限：條件太罕見，且只影響診斷頁

## 測試

- [x] 用模擬資料跑 17 個情境，全部通過。上櫃個股日成交用的是 twstock 套件錄下的**櫃買中心真實回應**（6223，2026 年 2、3 月）。涵蓋的情境：
  - 上市與上櫃各自的行情、法人、走勢、基本面
  - 盤前沒有即時成交
  - 櫃買中心回 520 時的降級與暫停重試
  - **櫃買中心一路轉址時，研究指令仍成功，子請求遠低於 50**
  - 上市收盤檔失敗或回空陣列（含「基本面也要走櫃買中心」）
  - 研究指令只判斷一次市場，行情與基本面標籤一致
  - 查無代號、興櫃代號不標上櫃
  - 16 欄格式的法人資料
  - `/api/debug` 與樣本查詢
- [x] 這次新增的 5 個測試，在修正前的版本上全部失敗、修正後全部通過
- [x] **回歸比對**：上市股 2330 在正常、盤前、收盤檔失敗三種情境下，新舊版的 `/api/stock`、`/api/extra`、`/api/screen` 輸出完全一致，只多了刻意新增的欄位
- [x] 無頭瀏覽器端對端測試，桌機 1000px、手機 390px：上櫃標籤、櫃買指數、法人、走勢圖正常顯示，沒有 JS 錯誤，手機不會左右滑動。也測過櫃買中心被擋時的畫面，以及清空 Worker 網址的行為
- [ ] **還沒用真實的證交所或櫃買中心資料驗證**，開發環境連不到這兩個網站。以下兩點是推斷的，需要部署後確認：
  - `mopsfe_t187ap*_O` 這幾個資料集名稱，是照證交所的命名規則推的，沒有現成套件可以核對
  - 上櫃三大法人的單位假設是「股」；如果欄位名稱標示「張」，程式會自動改用張

## 合併後請做

1. 部署 Worker。如果已設定 Cloudflare 自動部署會自動更新，否則執行 `wrangler deploy`。
2. 打開 `https://stock.skyzbpt.workers.dev/api/debug`，確認 `twseOk` 與 `tpexOk`。
3. 如果 `tpexOk` 是 `false`，看失敗的是哪幾項：
   - 全部失敗（錯誤訊息是轉址、520 或暫停重試），代表整個櫃買中心擋掉了 Cloudflare
   - 只有個別 `tpex:openapi:*` 失敗，代表那個資料集名稱不對，可以用 `/api/debug?ds=tp_<名稱>&otc=6488` 看細節

author: jimlundin
body:
This sets a baseline for how the app is layered. Commands and agent tools now share the functions that enforce the vault's rules, and the shell gets its own name.

**Commands and tools** (ARCHITECTURE.md, "Commands and tools"): a command is what Jim does from the UI; a tool is what the agent does, its input checked by a Zod `inputSchema`. What both do is one function that checks what the input means, so Jim and the agent follow the same rules.

- **Staging** (`app/shell/writer.ts`): the writer's `stage` refuses a path that isn't a vault file, and refuses deleting a file that doesn't exist. Before, only the agent's tools checked this, so the Edit page staged without the check.
- **Agent tools** (`app/extensions/agent/tools.ts`): `writeFile` and `deleteFile` call the writer and pass its error back to the model. `commit` leaves "nothing is staged" to the writer's commit, which already refuses an empty commit.
- **Audit**: `weekAudit` moves out of `Audit.tsx`, a UI file, into `app/extensions/audit/week.ts`, which the page and the agent's tool both import. `core/audit.ts` stays the general audit over any time span.

**`app/core/` → `app/shell/`**: `core/` and `app/core/` were two layers with one name. `core/` holds the vault's rules (pure; runs in the browser, CI and the tools), and the shell holds the app's frame (DOM, React; browser only). The shell now has the name ARCHITECTURE.md already uses for it. The imports, `vite.config.ts`, `components.json` and the docs are updated; git records the moved files as renames.

```
core/            the vault model (pure)
app/shell/       the shell
app/backends/    backends
app/extensions/  features
tools/           Node
```

**Node is for CI only**: `tools/audit.ts`, `tools/set-ext.ts` and `tools/capture.ts` are removed; the vault is worked only in the app, where the audit, rename (including `.md`/`.mdx`) and Captures are pages and agent tools. `tools/` keeps `check.ts` (the vault's CI) and `seal-secrets.ts` (the deploy). The check's `.md`/`.mdx` messages point to Rename in the app.

**No folder picker; Safari works in dev too**: the folder backend (File System Access, Chromium only) is removed, with its picker and the fallback to it. The app is GitHub through the encrypted IndexedDB cache in every browser. Dev runs that same path but skips the password: `npm run dev` gets the secrets from `.env.local` (`VAULT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, optionally `VAULT_OPENAI_KEY`, `VAULT_JINA_KEY`, the names CI seals), and a build gets none. A build with the token set has no trace of it in `dist/`.

New tests in `app/shell/writer.test.ts` cover both staging refusals and the refused empty commit. Lint (no errors), the type check, the tests (132; the 4 fewer are the folder backend's) and the build pass.

body:
Итоговая проверка первой очереди точности (шаг 7 `docs/plans/2026-10-03-accuracy-stage-1.md`).

## Что проверено

- **Сквозной сценарий на фейковом TestOps.** Уже было покрыто: prepare → analyze → summary → done, fix и лимит попыток, propose → apply/revert, remember → следующий прогон → reject, волны пакетов и `verify`, папка другой `schema` не продолжается. Добавлены только недостающие связки (`test_skill_queue_flow.py`, `test_skill_retries.py`):
  - пакет → `verify` → `propose` → `fix` по одному → summary → done → apply/revert → remember на одном прогоне;
  - запись базы знаний у трёх проблем (корпус `known_issue_symptoms`) через CLI: группа в брифе и `report.md`; после `reject` остаётся группа из двух, а проблема с отвергнутой записью идёт отдельно;
  - повторы через `prepare`/`next` доходят до `report.md`.
  Багов не нашлось.
- **Документация.** `CLAUDE.md` и `.claude/rules/` сверены с кодом. Поправлено: у реестра источников больше нет версии формата (`skill-analysis.md`); в `tests/eval/README.md` объяснено, какой итог печатает `run_eval.py` с `--heavy` и без него.
- pytest (1345 passed), ruff, mypy strict (0 ошибок), `run_eval.py --details` и `--heavy`.

## Эталон: шаг 1 (`dd17cc7`) → сейчас

| | precision · recall · скрыто · потеряно строк |
|---|---|
| dev `--heavy` | 0.987 · 1.000 · 1 · 13/73 (391 тест) → **0.988 · 1.000 · 0 · 0/78** (400) |
| dev | 0.930 · 1.000 · 1 · 13/33 (71) → **0.938 · 1.000 · 0 · 0/38** (80) |
| holdout | 0.739 · 1.000 · 3 · 7/9 → **0.739 · 1.000 · 0 · 0/9** |

«dev precision 0.987» в плане — это итог с `big_launch` (он идёт с `--heavy` или явным `--case big_launch`, а `baseline.json` включает его всегда), а `run_eval.py` без флага печатает 0.938. Ошибки в цифрах не было, они посчитаны на разном составе. Precision и recall по каждому сценарию с шага 1 не менялись; итог сдвинулся только от состава корпуса (+1 тест в `retries`, сценарий `known_issue_symptoms`). Цена улучшений — размер задания: максимум 5,9 → 8,5 тыс. символов.

## Стенд Qwen (`qwen3.8-flash`)

| Сценарий | Статус | Время | Токенов | Диагнозы |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E10 | inconclusive, все проверки прошли | 744 с | 1,91 млн | 4/4 по чек-листу `--analyses` |

- **A01: в сопоставимых условиях разницы нет.** A01 ×5 на текущем коде и на `abedb09` (до шагов 5–6), одновременно на Qwen Code 0.25.0: по 4 из 5 без провалов, у каждой серии один провал `report_verbatim` (мелкая правка текста). Небольшой эффект выборка не исключает. Диагнозы верны во всех 16 прогонах.
- **E09:** 503 (эталон — «окружение») назван «приложением» по правилу задания «5xx без лога — приложение». Купон (эталон — «данные», 5xx нет) — тоже «приложение»: данных об истечении в задании нет, правило этот выбор не объясняет.
- **E08:** склейка распознана («СОГЛАСОВАННОСТЬ: разные проблемы» с обеими причинами), но ПРИЧИНА и сводка подают NPE как причину всей группы.

1. Модель сама ищет код проекта вопреки запрету: E07 `glob`, E10 `glob`, A01 #3 `grep | sed` — уже три случая.
2. Бриф не всегда дословный — и до шагов 5–6, и после: мелкие правки текста (слово, окончание, запятая).
