author: coacht88
body:
Where am I in the week? The HQ answered that twice, in two places, each missing what the other had.

A dot row under the Today card said how many sessions were done and could not say which days. A seven-cell calendar down in the secondary block said which days and could not say how the week was going. Same week, a thumb-length apart. This makes it one surface, and makes that surface tell the truth for both cohorts.

## The week now has one answer, from the truthful source

`currentWeekCompletion()` feeds the canonical completion engine an authority-aware seven-slot array. For a member whose week comes from dated plans, a date with no attributable plan is `undefined`, which the engine already treats as "not a commitment the member made" and leaves out of the denominator. That is what keeps a midweek cutover honest: a member who cut over on a Thursday has no authoritative Monday, and feeding the recurring compatibility projection in instead would recreate at presentation time exactly the historical backfill storage correctly refused.

Pinned with exact arithmetic rather than an inequality. On Thursday 2026-03-12 at UTC a size member's target is **2** where the recurring projection would say **4**. An earlier version of that test asserted `target <= projectionTarget`, which passes when the two are equal, so a change that quietly handed the projection back survived it. Two mutations proved the assertion weak, not the subject.

Surfacing that denominator exposed a real render-ordering hazard, so `syncProgression('render')` moved to the top of `renderDashboard()`. The contract changed from *render some surfaces, classify, render the rest* to *classify first, then render every HQ surface from one settled state*. On the single pass where a member cuts over, the dot row used to read pre-cutover state while the calendar below read post-cutover state. PR C hid it because its projection write was a no-op on the column.

## One surface

`#hq-week-dots` and `#dashboard-grid` are gone, absorbed into `#hq-week-card`. Monday first, because the storage column is Sunday-indexed only because `notifyRules.js` needs it to be, and showing that to the member put the ISO week's last day in the leftmost cell.

The renderer decides nothing. Prescription, performance and satisfaction arrive already resolved as seven records from the pure model, and the `satisfied` array it reads is the same one that writes the label, so a cell and the fraction beneath it cannot disagree about a day. It no longer touches `persisted.schedule` or `completedDays` at all, which is precisely what let two surfaces diverge.

Four states: satisfied, pending, rest, unknown. Today is a modifier on top of whichever applies, not a fifth thing to learn. Rest borrows nothing from the unfinished treatment, because resting is how a rest day is satisfied. There is deliberately no missed state: a past unfinished day renders exactly as a future planned one, which says the same thing without the strip passing a judgement a day may not deserve.

## The interaction boundary

|  | authoritative | legacy / custom |
|---|---|---|
| cell is a button, a tab stop | no | yes |
| click / Enter | opens nothing | the day picker, on the weekday index |
| `assignDay()` | refuses | writes |
| day types in the modal | hidden | shown |
| completion toggle | hidden | shown |
| `toggleDayCompletion()` | refuses | writes |

Editing a derived projection would be an edit the next load silently overwrites. And the completion toggle goes with the day types, which reverses the cutover's call that completion is still theirs to record: `weekCompletion()` falls back to `completedDays[i]` when a day has no log entry, so a generic tick claims a specific dated prescription was satisfied with no record of what happened. Acknowledging work done outside the app needs a surface that captures *what* was done, and that is a later phase.

Nothing is withdrawn from the cohort whose column genuinely is their programme.

## Next up

New pure module `src/nextUp.js`, separate from `weekStrip.js` because the strip's contract is one ISO week and this answer regularly lands in the week after.

It walks forward from tomorrow through real local dates to the generation horizon, skipping rest, absent dates, unreadable records and support-only days. The surface it replaces walked the recurring column, so on a Sunday it announced a session from a projection rather than from a plan: plausible, because a week repeats, which is the dangerous kind of wrong. With the next week genuinely generated it names that Monday; with the week absent it drops the chip instead of inventing one. `daysAway` is returned so the caller can refuse a weekday name that no longer identifies a day, rather than the module shortening its own horizon to make somebody else's label work.

Legacy members keep the recurring walk, because a recurring week is exactly what they were promised.

## Copy that had become false

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `Your Weekly Schedule`, "Each day is assigned... Tap a day to view it and update its completion status" | `Your Training Week`, "Today stays front and center. Underneath it, the week view shows what is planned, what is complete, and when you are resting." |
| Manual `Weekly Calendar` with the same tap promise | Manual `Your Week`, describing what it shows and promising no interaction |
| "This sets your weekly schedule... You can change it any time from the Manual." | "This is what I build your week around, and what I lead with when you ask me something." |
| Two tour stops both titled "Your week" | One, on the one surface |

`Weekly schedule set for lasting longer.` and the schedule-replacement prompt are deliberately kept: they are legacy-only, and for that cohort the column genuinely is their weekly schedule. Banning the words would have deleted two true sentences to satisfy a guard.

## A defect found on the way

`tests/exerciseCopy.test.js` stripped `/* */` across the whole file, so `accept="image/*"` on a file input opened a comment that ran to the first real `*/` three thousand lines later. About seventy thousand characters vanished with it: every onboarding slide, the whole Manual, and the day modal. The banned-phrase scan was passing over all of it vacuously, which is the same as having no guard, and it was invisible because a test that sees nothing still goes green. Block comments are now stripped only inside `<style>` and `<script>`, and the extractor is checked against landmarks in each region it must cover.

Separately, eleven fixtures wrote `persisted.programme = null` meaning "legacy". It means *unclassified*, and an unclassified member gets classified and cut over on the next sync. They worked only because sync used to run after the render surfaces. Each was triaged individually against a `legacyProgramme()` sentinel that is classified custom; the ones that genuinely exercise classification still use `null`, and say so.

## Verification

```
npx vitest run           25 files, 1091 passed
E2E=1 npx vitest run     47 files,  946 passed
```

Fourteen mutations, all killed by named tests. Four on the authority-aware denominator and the render ordering; ten on the authority boundaries of this phase, covering the renderer ignoring authority in either direction, the interaction boundary inverted in either direction, a click sending the Monday-first position instead of the weekday, the canonical satisfied array not being passed in, the completion toggle surviving cutover, Next up walking the recurring column, Next up announcing rest, and the forward walk never leaving today. The working tree was verified byte-clean after every revert.

One mutation was deliberately not run and is documented rather than counted: the `daysAway > 6` rail in `nextUpChip()` has no reachable production path, since every current programme trains at least once in any six days, so a mutation would survive by equivalence.

## Out of scope

Carried forward unchanged: the reso

author: andugan
body:
An incoming text made no sound and no vibration, and nothing showed except the notification count going up.

## Why it was silent

The kiosk runs lock task without `LOCK_TASK_FEATURE_NOTIFICATIONS`. In that mode the system adds `DISABLE_NOTIFICATION_ALERTS` to the status bar's disable flags, and the notification service treats that as "no notification effects". So every app's notification is posted with no sound, no vibration and no heads-up. That includes the Messages app's notifications (`com.android.messaging` holds the SMS role, not Rist). Calls still ring because the ringer goes through Telecom, not through notifications.

Posting our own notification on a high-importance channel would be muted in exactly the same way. Turning on the notifications feature would bring back the shade, which the kiosk deliberately withholds.

## What this does

`RistNotificationListener`, which is already connected, sees the Messages app's notification when it is posted. While the system has muted notifications, `TextAlert` alerts for it:

- **Banner:** a drop-down overlay at the top of whatever screen is showing. It has the same window type as the floating home button and uses the current theme. It shows the sender and the first line of the text. Tap opens that conversation through the Messages app's own content intent. Swipe up dismisses it. It goes away by itself after 6 s. A newer text replaces the one showing. On a locked phone it says only "New message". With the screen off there is no banner, only sound and vibration.
- **Sound and vibration:** decided by Android's own rules.
  - Ringer NORMAL: notification sound on the notification ("Alerts") volume, plus vibration if the channel vibrates.
  - Ringer VIBRATE: vibration only.
  - Ringer SILENT: neither.
  - Do Not Disturb: the notification's ranking decides (`matchesInterruptionFilter`, peek suppression). If the ranking is not available, the interruption filter decides.
  - A channel turned down below default: nothing.
  - During a call: banner only.
  - Vibration uses notification usage, so the system applies the "vibrate for notifications" strength, including off.
- **No double alerts:** when lock task is not muting notifications, Android alerts by itself and this code does nothing. A re-post of the same message (same key, time and text) does not alert again, and neither does an alert-once update.

Nothing is stored, logged or sent. Only a hash per notification key is kept, to catch re-posts. The SMS boundary still holds: no `SMS_RECEIVED`, no content observer, no new permission.

## Tests

`TextAlertTest` (21 tests) covers:
- the banner's name and preview
- locked-phone wording
- tap opens the conversation
- swipe up dismisses
- the 6 s timeout and replacement
- each ringer mode
- DND, with and without a ranking
- a low-importance channel, an active call and the screen off
- no alert when the system is not muted
- re-post and alert-once deduplication
- other apps and group summaries
- when lock task mutes notifications

Full suite: 1451 tests in each variant. Release passed with 0 failures. Debug had one failure, in BoxCreateTest (known to be flaky under load); it passed 24/24 when rerun alone.

## Check by hand on a device

1. With the kiosk up and the ringer on normal, a text plays the sound and vibrates, and the banner drops down over Rist and over an allowlisted app such as Maps.
2. Tapping the banner opens that conversation in Messages.
3. Swiping it up dismisses it.
4. With vibrate mode, silent mode and DND on in turn, the phone behaves as the settings say.
5. On a locked phone with a PIN, the sound plays. Check whether the overlay shows over the keyguard; it may not.
6. During a call, a text makes no noise.
7. `Settings.canDrawOverlays` is true for the app; it is already needed for the home button.
8. The Messages app's channel importance and sound are used as expected.
9. One text gives one alert, not two.

author: gigurra
body:
## Summary

Generic fields retain their declared Go representation even when specialization collapses a union. A `Box[Int]` field declared as `(T | Int) => Int` expects `func(any) int64`, while its checked callback has type `func(int64) int64`. Adapt field values at construction, read, and copy boundaries.

## Example

```bork
type Box[T] = { callback: (T | Int) => Int }
fn main() {
  box: Box[Int] = Box { callback: n => n + 1 }
  println(box.callback(2))
}
```

This prints `3` instead of failing to compile generated Go.

## What changed

- Extend the existing field adapters to collapsed unions, including callbacks and containers, eager/lazy/computed fields, and sealed-variant payloads.
- Adapt parents during nested copies and restore their declared field representation when writing them back, including lazy-cell types.
- Share runtime membership analysis between checking and generation, using the precise contract and dictionary analysis from #526.
- Document specialization of generic fields.

## Dependencies and scope

- Builds on the #531 call-boundary adapters, now merged to main.
- The shared checker helper is identical to #526's file and can merge in either order.
- Nominal identity and type-test erasure remain separate work.

## Decisions to review

No language or syntax changes. Specialized field values use the existing conversion machinery; lazy callbacks remain deferred and memoized.

## Testing

- New `generic_union_field_abi` golden/run fixture: record and sealed fields, destructuring, copies, lazy/computed fields, callback unions, nested containers, direct union fields, Float32, and nested eager/lazy parent copies.
- New contract-dictionary regression checks error and success members with `T = Int | String`.
- Focused generic, union, tuple, method-reference, lazy-field and computed-field regressions pass.
- Types documentation snippets, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. CI runs the full suite.
- Field cold review found missing nested-copy adaptation; fixed and independently verified both eager and lazy repros. Re-review clean.
- Separate shared-analysis review clean, including the new dictionary regression.

author: mxkeaton
body:
## Problem

Auto transparency is computed once on the root `Bar` from `Hyprland.focusedWorkspace`, but the root spawns **one `PanelWindow` per monitor**. The transparency of *every* bar surface therefore follows whichever workspace has focus. With two monitors — say two windows on workspace 1 / monitor A and one window on workspace 2 / monitor B — switching focus or workspace between them repaints **both** bars, including the monitor whose workspace did not change.

## Fix

Decide the background per surface, from the workspace that surface's own monitor shows:

- `BarPanel` derives `tiledWindowCount` from `Hyprland.monitorFor(screen).activeWorkspace`, through a new root helper `tiledWindowCountForScreen(screen)`.
- `BarPanel.panelTransparent` is the per-surface `tiledWindowCount !== 1`, unless a manual toggle is in force.
- The manual toggle (double-click / `omarchy bar transparent`) is now an explicit `manualTransparency` hold on the root: it applies to every surface and is cleared on the next relevant Hyprland event, after which the per-surface rule resumes — the same lifetime the old global rule had.

The focused workspace still drives the shared text-colour sampling (`barForeground`) and the auxiliary drag surfaces, so those are unchanged.

## Result

- Monitor A (2 windows) → transparent
- Monitor B (1 window) → opaque
- Moving focus between monitors leaves both bars alone

## Known follow-up

`barForeground` (the `omarchy-bar-text-color` sample) is still computed once from the focused workspace's screen, so `ActiveWindow` text on a transparent surface can use the colour sampled for another monitor's wallpaper. Making that per-surface too means moving the sampling into each panel; deliberately left out of this change.

---

Tested on Omarchy 4.0.4 / Quickshell 0.3.1 with two monitors.

author: ino-bagaric
body:
## Review in 60 seconds

- **Bug (KRTX-1722, scenario D):** a person signs a lost phone out from **Settings → Security → Devices**. The sign-in ends, but the phone's push token stays, so its lock screen keeps showing session titles and up to 140 characters of each agent question. "Sign out other devices" (GoTrue `signOut({ scope: 'others' })`) has the same gap. Account deletion also left the person's tokens behind.
- **Fix:**
  1. **Schema:** `kortix.push_device_tokens.auth_session_id uuid NULL`: the sign-in (`auth.sessions.id`) that registered the token. One generated, schema-qualified `ADD COLUMN`; metadata-only, no backfill, no index (deletes filter on the indexed `user_id`).
  2. **Register:** `POST /v1/notifications/device-token` records the caller's sign-in: the JWT `session_id`, only for a user JWT and only when it is a UUID. A personal token records none.
  3. **Send (the root fix):** `listByUser`, the push sender's only read, returns a token only while its sign-in exists in `auth.sessions` (and `not_after` has not passed). This covers every way a sign-in ends: the API's device sign-out, GoTrue's sign-out of other devices, and an expired session. A token with no recorded sign-in counts as live; the app re-registers on every signed-in launch, which fills the column.
  4. **Clean-up:** `signOutDevice` (`DELETE /v1/accounts/me/devices/:sessionId`) deletes the tokens that sign-in registered. Account deletion deletes the person's tokens with their login.
- **No foreign key into `auth.sessions` on purpose:** a token registered by a just-ended sign-in would fail its insert, and the schema would depend on GoTrue's DDL. `listSignedInDevices` already reads `auth.sessions` the same way.
- **Docs:** `/docs/accounts` gains "Signed-in devices": what **Sign out** and **Sign out other devices** stop.

**Risk:** low. A token keeps getting pushes unless its recorded sign-in is gone; rows registered before this change keep today's behavior until the next launch. The migration adds one nullable column.

**Verified:** flow PUSH-2 (new) through the real routes; real-PostgreSQL suites for the store filter and the account-deletion erase; each red on dev's code. Full `pnpm test`.

Still open on KRTX-1722 (Phase 2): the offboarding module (revoke and re-home a leaver's computer connections), reminder hand-over with an audit event, and the member-footprint endpoint and removal dialog.

author: brooooooklyn
body:
## Summary

`.jsx` and `.tsx` files in a `"type": "module"` package ran as CommonJS: oxc_resolver's `ESM_FILE_FORMAT` consults the nearest `package.json` `"type"` only for `.js` and `.ts`, so `resolution.module_type()` returned `None` for `.jsx`/`.tsx` and the resolve hook fell through to `"commonjs"`.

That had two visible symptoms (issue #797):

- `typeof require`/`module` were `function`/`object` instead of `undefined`
- the automatic JSX runtime was emitted as `require("react/jsx-runtime")`, going through Node's CommonJS resolution — the resolve hook, and with it tsconfig `paths`, never applied

The fix supplies the package `type` where `module_type()` has no answer, bounded to what Node's `ESM_FILE_FORMAT` treats as package-type territory plus the source extensions `register.mjs` claims:

- **extensionless files** — Node answers them with the package type
- **`.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.es`, `.es6`** — registered source extensions Node itself would reject (`ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION`); we deliberately run them, so the package type is the only consistent answer
- **explicit answers still win**: `.mts`/`.mjs`/`.cts`/`.cjs`/`.node`, the resolved file's tsconfig ESM `module` override (`default_module_from_tsconfig`), and `module_type()` all take precedence
- **`.wasm` and unknown extensions keep the prior `commonjs` default** — reclassifying them would feed non-source files through the transformer as ES modules

Running as ESM additionally means `import =`/`export =` in such a file surface the TS1202/TS1203 load-time error (merged with #800) instead of a runtime `ReferenceError`, matching `tsc` and Node's type stripping.

Under `OXC_TRANSFORM_ALL`, the resolve hook now also answers formats for `node_modules` files Node.js cannot classify (`.jsx`/`.tsx`/`.es`/`.es6`, extensionless) — previously they died with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` before `load` could transform them. Formats Node.js *does* classify (`.ts`/`.cts`/`.mts`, `.wasm`, addons) still defer to its loaders, so Node's own errors and load paths are preserved.

Closes #797

## Test plan

New `packages/integrate-vitest/__tests__/resolved-format.spec.ts` (temp-project/subprocess pattern) plus a `.jsx` row in `helper-imports.spec.ts`:

- issue repro verbatim: `a.ts`, `b.tsx`, `c.jsx` with no module syntax in a `type: module` package all print `undefined` for `typeof require`/`module`
- `.tsx`/`.jsx` **entry points** (no parent URL → the other resolve path) run as ESM
- `type: commonjs` and no-`type` packages still run `.tsx`/`.jsx` as CJS
- a tsconfig `module: commonjs` cannot demote a `.tsx` file in a `type: module` package
- `.es`/`.es6` and extensionless files follow the package type in both directions
- `.wasm` and `.txt` keep `commonjs` even in a `type: module` package (asserted via `createResolve`'s reported format — the fallback boundary)
- the automatic JSX runtime resolves through tsconfig `paths` (the second symptom)

Verified: `vp fmt` + `vp check`, `cargo test`, `pnpm test` (all integrate-* suites, 127 tests) green; the issue repro prints `a.ts: module undefined undefined` / `b.tsx: module undefined undefined`.

author: ymote
body:
## Why

#373's `--offload` kept Home's test suite on the Mac, because three shell tests failed on the Linux host (EC2 c5d.18xlarge, 72 vCPUs on two sockets). This PR fixes them and moves the suite to the host.

## The three failures

**`backend_data_aliases_cannot_reuse_a_stale_peer_with_the_current_handle` depended on test order.**
- `auth.*` is a macOS and Android host API (`oauth-service/src/host_catalog.rs`).
- Once any test in the process has registered the auth catalog, a Linux host refuses `auth.backend.*` as `api_unavailable`, before the account check the test asserts. Alone, the test passed.
- It now accepts `api_unavailable` only where the catalog says this platform lacks the method. On macOS it still requires the account-scope refusal ("account changed"). On every platform it still checks that the stale peer reached no backend service.

**The two `photos_preview_*` tests ran out of makepad's 64 ms Splash budget.** Each entry into a Splash isolate gets 64 ms of wall-clock time. Measured on the host with instrumentation:

| Case | Photos preview entry |
| --- | --- |
| Alone | 6 ms |
| ~1,000 shell tests in one process, 18–72 threads | 65–1,100 ms |

- **Where the time goes:** waits on makepad's process-wide LiveId interner mutex. The tokenizer takes it ~12,700 times per entry, giving 90–230 ms of waits, mostly futex time. Page faults also stall in `lock_mm_and_find_vma` behind other threads' memory-map changes.
- **Other tests:** a few other Splash tests fail the same way now and then.
- **Not new:** #357 trimmed a test for the same reason ("under concurrent CI load").
- **The fix:** [makepad#109](https://github.com/OctoSense-org/makepad/pull/109) adds `MAKEPAD_SPLASH_BUDGET_MS`, read once. Unset, the budget stays 64 ms. Only phone.yml's test step sets it (10 s). The change rides as stacked runtime patch 19 (`makepad-splash-budget.patch`, the same lines as #109) until the next makepad sweep, so makepad `main` does not move for it.

## The offload

`tools/ci_local.py` now keeps only the Apple icons, asset catalogs and the macOS compile of Home on the Mac. Building and running Home's and App Hub's tests goes to the host. `docs/local-ci.md` is updated to match.

## Checks

- Home's test command on the Linux host, with the stacked patch, at the default 72 threads: **5 of 5 runs green**, 1,449 tests, ~42 s each.
  - A control run without the override failed both Photos tests, as before.
  - Run times match with and without the override, so no test was depending on the budget running out.
- `python3 tools/setup.py --check --cargo`: green.
- `python3 -m unittest tools/test_ci_local.py`: 33 pass.
- `tools/ci_local.py --check-drift`: clean.
- makepad#109: `cargo check -p makepad-widgets` gives no warnings in makepad-widgets. Its existing lib tests show the same 6 Linux failures as makepad main without the change (desktop_style, grid, menu_bar, widget_tree).
- Local CI (`--only apps,desktop,phone --linux-host --offload`): running. The result will be posted as a comment.

author: claudiosenior
body:
## Linked issue
Closes #1341

## What changed

`#1336` fixed `filled_stake_usd` to use the CLOB fill size instead of the
intended `stake_usd` for full fills, but its own formula
(`filled_shares * placed_limit_price`) was itself still an upper bound on
the real cost — not the "partial fill" issue it looked like, but a **price**
issue: a GTC BUY that crosses the spread fills at a *better* price than its
own limit, and Polymarket's CLOB is a hybrid off-chain-match /
on-chain-settlement exchange, where part of an off-chain-matched trade can
fail to settle on-chain (`py_clob_client_v2.client`'s own
`FAILED_TRADE_STATUS = "FAILED"`, already used internally by
`post_order()`'s settlement-hash resolution). Both make
`filled_shares * placed_price` wrong, sometimes by 50%+ of the stake.

**Verified against real production data** (not just unit tests), per the
issue's own ask:
- Position **#97**: stake $3.00 placed at 0.37. Pulling the market's public
  trade history (`data-api.polymarket.com/trades?market=...`) around the
  entry timestamp shows our wallet's actual match: **8.11 shares @ 0.22**
  (true cost ≈ $1.78), not the $3.0007 the old formula recorded
  (`8.11 * 0.37`).
- Position **#101**: stake $3.00 placed at 0.45. Same method shows the
  actual match: **6.67 shares @ 0.40** (true cost ≈ $2.67), not the
  $3.0015 the old formula recorded (`6.667 * 0.45`).
- In both cases `filled_shares` (from `get_order_fill_size()`/`size_matched`)
  was already correct — the bug is specifically the price multiplier, which
  is why "cleanly full-filled" rows in the issue's own evidence table were
  correct to the cent (their execution price happened to equal their placed
  price) while others diverged by up to $1.5 of a $3 stake.

### Fix
- `LiveTrader.get_order_fill_cost_usd()` (new): walks an order's own
  `associate_trades` (via `client.get_order()`) and resolves each one via
  `client.get_trades(TradeParams(id=...))` — the same `TradeParams`/
  `get_trades` machinery `py_clob_client_v2`'s own `post_order()` already
  uses internally to resolve settlement hashes. Sums `size * price` over
  every trade that is **not** `status == "FAILED"`. This is the exchange's
  own record of what actually executed, queried synchronously at the same
  call site that already checks fill state — no later reconstruction job
  needed.
- `copy_live_executor.py`: both the full-fill and partial-fill paths now
  call this first and use it when it returns a positive cost; they fall
  back to the old `filled_shares * placed_price` approximation only when no
  resolved-trade cost is available yet (logged, never silent — same
  "never silently drop a fill's cost" contract this module already has).
- `copy_live_settle.py`'s ghost-order recovery path had the exact same
  `filled_shares * fill_price` formula for a later-confirmed ghost fill —
  fixed identically so it doesn't reintroduce the same bug for that path.

### Out of scope (per the issue)
- Backfilling existing wrong rows — blocked on this fix landing first, and
  a separate operator decision (flagged in #1341, tracked by #1342 for the
  historical-recovery side). This PR does not touch
  `src/scripts/copy_live_fill_cost_backfill.py` or its tests.

## How to test

```bash
pytest src/tests/test_partial_fill_tracking.py src/tests/test_copy_live_executor.py \
       src/tests/test_copy_live_settle.py -v
```

New/relevant coverage:
- `TestGetOrderFillCostUsd` (`test_partial_fill_tracking.py`): multi-leg
  trade summation, FAILED-trade exclusion, actual-vs-placed price,
  lookup-error isolation (one bad trade-id doesn't zero the rest),
  trade-id mismatch defensiveness.
- `TestActualFillCostPreferredOverApproximation`
  (`test_copy_live_executor.py`): full-fill and partial-fill paths prefer
  the actual cost, including a case shaped exactly like production
  position #97 (8.11 shares, 0.37 placed / 0.22 actual); a lookup-raises
  case still falls back to the approximation rather than failing the fill.
- `test_recovered_fill_prefers_actual_cost_over_approximation`
  (`test_copy_live_settle.py`): the ghost-recovery path gets the same fix.

Full suite: `pytest src/tests/ -q` (ran clean for every file this PR
touches; the 59 unrelated failures seen on a full `src/tests/` run — JS
clipboard tests, dashboard, emos_retrain, `ensure_worktree`,
`shadow_low_rollout`, etc. — reproduce identically on unmodified
`origin/master` in this sandbox and are pre-existing/environmental, not
caused by this change).

## How to deploy
- [x] **Code only** — `git pull` + restart `meteoedge-copy-signals` (runs
  `copy_live_executor.py` via `copy_signal_loop`) and
  `meteoedge-copy-live-settle.service` (runs `copy_live_settle.py`'s ghost
  recovery; it's timer-triggered hourly, so no immediate restart is
  strictly required, but doing so picks up the fix sooner for any currently
  still-ambiguous ghost rows)
- [ ] Dependencies changed
- [ ] DB schema change
- [ ] One-off script(s) to run after deploy
- [ ] Config / env change
- [x] **Post-deploy validation** — watch `logs/bot.log` for
  `[copy-live] order ...` / `[copy-live-settle] fill-cost lookup failed`
  warnings (expected only when a trade hasn't resolved yet at query time);
  for a sample of newly-filled rows, confirm `filled_stake_usd` in
  `copy_live_positions` is no longer clustered right at `stake_usd` for
  fills whose placed price and actual execution price diverge (re-run the
  issue's own on-chain reconciliation method, or a subset of it, against
  fills recorded after this deploy)

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass locally (`pytest src/tests/ -v`)
- [x] No secrets or credentials committed
- [x] PR body includes `Closes #N` linking the issue
- [x] Project board status updated (In review)
- [ ] Docs updated if this PR adds/changes env vars, DB schema, API
  endpoints, or run modes — N/A (no schema/API/env change, just the
  internal cost-computation logic)
- [x] **How to deploy** section filled in

body:
用户临时打开网页解析不同抖音作品时，跨域 JSON POST 会先产生 OPTIONS 预检。网页改用 URL 编码表单，并在打开页面时提示浏览器预连接 HTTPS API，减少首次提交时的请求及连接开销。Worker 保留现有 JSON 调用，响应增加固定的 worker、resolve、primary 计时，便于区分上游与 Worker 外部等待。

保留请求大小、输入长度、URL 校验和限流；作者、封面、音乐、画质、解析完整性条件和下载流程保持一致。新前端遇到旧 Worker 的 HTTP 415 时仅回退一次 JSON；长文案编码超限时直接用 JSON。预连接不调用业务接口，也不等待连接提示完成。兼容 Worker 已部署，前端合并后生效。

验证：`npm run check` 通过（115 项测试），跨域生产配置前端构建通过；3 条真实作品修改前后共 18 次上游解析，资源数量和元数据存在性一致；浏览器跨域请求无 OPTIONS。实际保存 1 个普通视频、3 个实况 MP4、3 张 JPEG，全部完整解码通过。带服务端计时的同版本小样本 A/B 中，Worker 外部开销中位数从 0.866 秒降至 0.637 秒；上游波动明显，无法承诺固定的整体提升比例。手机真实保存仍待验收。

body:
## 做了什麼（#1314 P1＋P2，丙案，範圍說明已「過」）

- **章節模式**（沒有任何篩選時）：**逾期章**永遠攤開（`GET /invoices?overdue=true`，伺服器分頁），章名旁「N 張 · 待收 NT$ X」；**已繳清章**收著、展開才抓，張數＝繳清＋多退，多退排最前、狀態字寫「多退」。
- **P2 色面**：「10 月應收 NT$ X，已收 N%。」＋長條（桌機）。`billed=0` 時不報百分比、不畫長條。
- **作廢**：「另有 N 張已作廢 · 顯示」一行（`byStatus.void.count`），點了切到 `status=void` 的平面表。
- **舊篩選暫留**：學生／狀態下拉／催繳三選一一動，就回到原本那張平面表（所有欄位不變）。等「7 天內到期／還沒到期」兩章（1506 補 `dueSoon`／`notDue`／`dueState` 後第二支）接上再退場。
- `invoices.service.ts` 加 `summary()`；`payments.util.ts` 加 `daysOverdue`、`lastPaidOn`（純日期字串，不走本地時區）。

## 金額欄位逐欄表（請 reviewer 裁非保留類）

| 位置                         | 顯示                                                     | pipe／運算                                      | 來源                     |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| 色面標題「應收」             | `summary.month.billed`                                   | `toLocaleString`（原樣）                        | API                      |
| 色面標題「已收 N%」          | —                                                        | **前端一次除法**＋`Math.round`；`billed≤0` 不除 | `month.received／billed` |
| 長條下「已收 NT$」           | `month.received`                                         | `number`                                        | API                      |
| 長條下「還差 NT$」           | `billed − received`                                      | **前端一次減法**，`Math.max(0, …)`              | `month`                  |
| 逾期章名「待收」             | `summary.overdue.outstanding`                            | `number`                                        | API                      |
| 逾期章名「N 張」             | `summary.overdue.count`                                  | —                                               | API                      |
| 已繳清章名「N 張」           | `paid.count + overrefunded.count`                        | **整數相加（非金額）**                          | API                      |
| 逾期章每列右側金額           | `outstanding(invoice)`                                   | `number`；函式**未改**                          | 既有                     |
| 已繳清章每列右側金額         | `invoice.total`（繳清）／`overRefunded(invoice)`（多退） | `number`；`overRefunded` **未改**               | 既有                     |
| 平面表（篩選模式）全部金額欄 | 應繳／已收／尚欠                                         | **模板該區塊未動一字**                          | 既有                     |

沒有新增任何前端加總（除一次除法、一次減法）。

## 刻意的判斷／中間狀態

- 章節模式下**只看得到逾期與已繳清**；「還沒逾期」的未繳帳單暫時只能走舊篩選（未繳清／快到期）看。第二支接上兩章後補齊。
- 章節模式的列只剩：學生名、逾期天數（或繳清日／多退）、金額。**開立日、期限、應繳、已收四欄在章節模式暫時只在詳情抽屜裡**；已記進 P3 的順序約束（「放棄整列可點」那支不得早於學生檔案帳單章能看到這四欄）。**P3 的列內提醒／收款／收據鈕不在這支**。
- 已繳清章展開時用兩支請求（`status=paid` 分頁＋`status=overrefunded` 一次抓，第 1 頁才接），因為列表一次只收一個 `status`；多退只在第 1 頁出現。分頁器只數繳清的。
- 逾期章的列是 `<button>` 列（≥44px）而不是 `app-responsive-table`（章不需要欄收合）；點列開既有詳情抽屜，行為不變。
- 章節模式的逾期章名數字用 `summary.overdue`，列表總數是 `meta.total`——兩者同一個判準（後端 `isOverdueOn`／`whereOverdue`），示範庫實機都是 32。

## 證據

- 本機：`nx test web`（payments 82 綠，新增 6 條：色面、billed=0、彙總失敗退回頁名、章名數字、已繳清展開與多退順序、作廢一行；舊的「預設不送 overdue」那兩條改成章節模式的新斷言）、`nx typecheck web` 綠、`npm run harness` 綠、**`npm run test:timetravel` 綠**（web＋api，1497 條）。
- 截圖（本機示範庫 1440＋360）：色面標題／長條／逾期章（32 張 · 待收 NT$ 116,890）／已繳清展開（8 張）。
- **沒拍到什麼**：示範庫沒有作廢與多退帳單，所以「另有 N 張已作廢」那行與多退列只靠 spec；`month.billed=7,800`（示範庫本月只開了幾張）所以長條是 0%；沒做計算樣式傾印（整頁換形）；搜尋／學生篩選的平面表沒改、沒重拍。

後續：「7 天內到期」「還沒到期」兩章（等 1506）→第二支；P3 列內鈕／放棄整列可點／學生檔案帳單章；P4／P5。

author: btagliani
body:
Lets each profile pick which of `gh`'s accounts it uses for Code review and for the pull request that Ship opens.

Both run as whichever account `gh` has active. If you are signed in to more than one account, the only way to change it is `gh auth switch`. That command also changes the account every terminal uses.

## What changes

- **Settings.** **Settings > General > GitHub** has one row, **Account for each profile**. With one profile, the row is named **Account**. Folded, the row shows each profile's stored pick. Opened, it gives each profile a select of `gh`'s accounts.
- **Taking a pick back.** The first option of each select is **gh's active account**, followed by that account's login. Choosing it removes the pick.
- **Menu.** In the Code review **⋯** menu, if `gh` is signed in to two or more accounts on github.com, a **GitHub account** section lists them. The account in use is checked.
- **Column head.** The Code review column's head shows the account in use beside the title. If there is more than one profile and enough room, the profile's name comes first.
- **Per profile.** A pick is saved for the profile, like pins and review instructions. That profile's pull request lists, searches, reviewer, questions, and posted review use that account.
- **Ship.** A pull request shipped from one of the profile's checkouts is looked up and opened as that account. This covers `gh pr view` and `gh pr create`.
- **One account.** If `gh` is signed in to one account, the menu is unchanged.
- **No pick.** A profile without a pick sends every read and write as it does on `main`.

## How it works

- **Listing.** `gh auth status --hostname github.com --json hosts` lists the accounts. This needs gh 2.81 or later. With an earlier gh, no accounts are offered.
- **Sending as an account.** A call for a picked account runs through a short `/bin/sh` script. The script asks `gh auth token --user` for the token and starts `gh` with it in `GH_TOKEN`. The token passes from `gh` to `gh`. Realm doesn't read or store it, and `gh`'s active account doesn't change.
- **No injection surface.** The command, the login, and the host reach the script as positional parameters, never as script text. The login is checked against `GhLoginSchema` at the wire.
- **What you see is what posts.** The page sends the account with each read and with the review. A review posts as the account shown beside **Submit**, even if another window changes the pick.
- **Ship resolves the account on the server.** `workspace.ship` names its checkout, the checkout's space names its profile, and the profile's pick is handed to the ship. A ship that names no checkout uses `gh`'s active account.
- **Shared hand-off.** The script lives in `workspace/gh-account.ts`, pure and import-free like `github-remote.ts`, so Code review and `git-write` share it without Code review importing `git-write`. The structure test still holds.
- **Caches.** The server holds each account's reads apart, because one account can see what another can't.
- **A picked account that is signed out.** The profile uses `gh`'s active account until that account is back. An account that `gh` couldn't check because GitHub was unreachable stays listed.
- **A token in the environment.** If `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, no accounts are offered, because that token decides the account.
- **A pick reaches every window.** The server stores a profile's picks in the order they are asked for, then broadcasts `codeReview.accountChanged`. An open Code review page asks for its status again, and the Settings row reads the stored pick again.
- **Answers out of order.** The page doesn't draw a status answer that it asked for before a pick it has since heard of.
- **Settings asks `gh` only while the row is open.** Listing accounts makes `gh` check every stored token with GitHub, so the folded row reads only Realm's settings store. The open row asks again when the window comes back and when the server reconnects.
- **Refresh.** **Refresh** also asks who is signed in, because a terminal can switch `gh`'s active account. If `gh` can't be reached, the page and the request being read stay as they are.
- **Controls stay in place.** A select that the open row has drawn stays until the row is folded. A later answer from `gh` can't remove the control that has keyboard focus.
- **The head stays one row.** The stylesheet states the yielding order. The title and the menu button keep their widths. The profile's name gives way first and whole, and then a long login is cut. One sentence that names both is the line's tooltip and its text for a screen reader.
- **RPC.** `codeReview.accounts` answers `{ accounts, active }`, and `codeReview.setAccount` accepts `login: null`.

## Behavior to know about

- **The push is unchanged.** `git push` authenticates however git is set up: an SSH key, or a credential helper. Only the two `gh` calls of the pull request leg take the account.
- **Agents and terminals are unchanged.** `gh` run by an agent or in a terminal uses `gh`'s active account.
- **Ship uses the `gh` that Code review is configured with.** That is the same `gh` unless `REALM_GH_BIN` names another.
- **One extra `gh` call when the page opens.** The page lists `gh`'s accounts once, and the server holds the answer for a minute. This applies with one account too.
- **One extra `gh` call for each call sent as a picked account.** `gh auth token` took 60 to 80 ms on my machine.
- **Profile switch.** The page is one page per profile, so switching profiles shows the pending column for one status round trip.
- **A pick reloads the open page.** The page is keyed by the account's login. A pick heard from Settings or another window reloads it, as a pick from the menu does.
- **The profile's name needs room.** At the default sidebar width, the head often has room for the login only. The profile's name appears when both fit, and the tooltip names both.
- **A long login is cut.** At the default sidebar width, a login longer than about 15 characters ends in an ellipsis.
- **A take-back waits its turn.** If an earlier pick for the same profile is still being checked with `gh`, the take-back is stored after it.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` passes.
- 121 tests added across eight test files. The Settings row's tests are in `settings-github.test.tsx`. The stand-in `gh` scripts answer `auth status` and `auth token` and record which account a call was sent as, never a token.
- The tests were checked against 144 hand-written mutants of the code they cover. Each mutant failed at least one test.
- Live, read-only, against gh 2.102.0 signed in to two accounts: `accounts()` lists both, and a call sent as the second account answers as that account. An unknown account reads as signed out, and `gh`'s active account is unchanged afterwards.
- `pnpm test`: 10,306 pass and 3 fail. None of the three is in code this change touches. See the following section.
- Static renders in headless Chrome with the repo's stylesheets. The head stays one row of the same height at every sidebar width from 200px to 448px, and the search field under it doesn't move. The Settings row doesn't overflow at page widths from 360px to 1100px, in the dark and light themes. That holds with one profile and with several, including a 39-character login.
- In a running app: I ran a local build of `main` with #112, #113, #114, and #116 merged, on a scratch home. `gh` was signed in to two accounts. The Settings row listed both accounts, stored a pick, and took it back. The head, the menu, and the Settings row each followed a pick made in another of them. With a second profile, the head showed the profile's name at the widest sidebar and the login alone at the default width.
- Not verified: a live ship. The menu is tested through the in-app HTML menu, not the native one.
- Not verified: `apps/desktop/scripts/page-heads-live.mjs` and the `code-review-*-live.mjs` scripts. I compared what `page-heads-live.mjs` reads for Code review wit

## Summary

I audited the visual E2E specs for tests whose contract is editor state rather than browser or Electron behavior, and moved those to `TestEditor`. That removes 7 visual tests, about 33 s of CI test time.

- `editor.spec.ts`: removed the Shift-click undo test and the select-and-drag undo test; `EditorHistory.test.ts` already had both with the same assertions. Removed the "Shift released **after** mouseup" test, which `Select.test.ts` covers. The "before mouseup" variant stays, because only a browser can produce that event order.
- `deletion.spec.ts`: Shift+Backspace contour fragments and Backspace / Shift+Delete on a cubic handle are now tests in `KeyboardRouter.test.ts`. One real keyboard Delete test and the native menu Delete test stay in E2E.
- `glyph-view.spec.ts`: UPM framing for empty and extreme-width glyphs is now in `EditorZoom.test.ts`. I checked that it fails when the fit is removed.

Everything else stays in E2E: goldens, sidebar and DOM UI, cursors, native menus, pointer and wheel events, and timing. Several specs had already been thinned to browser-only checks, which is why only 7 tests moved.

## Notes

- The framing test calls `fitGlyphFrame` directly. The call made when a glyph opens (in `Editor.tsx`) is now covered only by the canvas goldens.
- The new gap-deletion test uses a straight contour; gaps across cubics are covered in `DeletionTopology.test.ts`.

## Issue

No issue — CI maintenance.

## Testing

- `pnpm check`
- `node scripts/check-e2e-projects.mjs`
- `playwright test --project=visual --list` → 200 tests in 31 files
- Removed E2E coverage is listed above; the rest runs on this PR's CI.

body:
Refs sdr-classroom/sdr-labs#114

Some properties are about traffic rather than about what a node says of itself: how many messages a change costs, or who is still talking once things have settled. The journal has always recorded every send; `Events` left them out, and a checker is not told where the run was written, so it could only rebuild the run directory by guessing how the suite names it.

`Events.sends` carries `(t, src, dest, body)` for every message one node sent another, in the order they left. An observation is not a send, as before.

**Not a journal change**: nothing is written differently. A caller that builds an `Events` by hand would have to add the field; none does here.

## Verified

`cargo test --all` exits 0:

```

test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed
```

author: aitrawog
body:
## Summary

Make the pacman-family guest provisioning actually install what it declares, and fail loudly when it
cannot — `opencharly/charly#832`.

An Arch-family cloud image can ship **no populated pacman keyring**. The rendered provisioning ran a
bare `pacman -Sy --needed --noconfirm <union>`, which then failed signature verification:

```
$ ./bin/charly vm ssh check-local-vm -- 'sudo -n grep -nE "pacman|error" /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | head -30'
130:warning: curl-8.22.0-1 is up to date -- skipping
131:warning: tar-1.35-5 is up to date -- skipping
132:warning: sudo-1.9.17.p2-6 is up to date -- skipping
141:Packages (29) aardvark-dns-2.1.0-3  abseil-cpp-20260817.0-2  catatonit-0.2.1-2  conmon-1:2.2.1-1  containers-common-1:0.69.2-1  criu-4.2.1-1  crun-1.30.1-1  db5.3-5.3.28-7  gtest-1.18.0-1  hwloc-2.14.0-1  libblake3-1.8.7-1  libdrm-2.4.134-1  libnet-2:1.3-2  libpciaccess-0.19-1  netavark-2.1.0-3  onetbb-2023.1.0-1  passt-2026_10_02.cba3570-1  perl-5.42.2-2  perl-error-0.17030-3  perl-mailtools-2.22-3  perl-timedate-2.35-1  protobuf-36.1-1  protobuf-c-1.5.2-15  python-protobuf-36.1-1  zlib-ng-2.3.3-1  git-2.56.0-1  go-2:1.27.1-1  openssh-10.6p1-1  podman-6.1.3-1
179:warning: Public keyring not found; have you run 'pacman-key --init'?
181:error: keyring is not writable
192:error: required key missing from keyring
193:error: failed to commit transaction (unexpected error)
$ ./bin/charly vm ssh check-local-vm -- 'cloud-init status --long | head -4'
status: done
extended_status: done
errors: []
```

Because a failed `runcmd` entry does **not** make cloud-init report `status: error`, the guest came up
**silently missing every composed package** — the three the image already shipped reported
`up to date -- skipping`, the 29-package transaction never committed:

```
$ ./bin/charly vm ssh check-local-vm -- 'for p in sudo go git podman; do printf "%-8s " $p; pacman -Q $p 2>&1 | head -1; done'
sudo     sudo 1.9.17.p2-6
go       error: package 'go' was not found
git      error: package 'git' was not found
podman   error: package 'podman' was not found
```

and every bed needing them failed somewhere else, reading as that bed's own defect (the observed
first failure: `exec: "git": executable file not found in $PATH` inside `check-local-vm`'s in-guest
nested step).

**The acceptance, two-sided, in the issue's own words:** (1) a guest comes up with its **declared
packages present**, and (2) a failure to install **fails loudly instead of cloud-init reporting done**.
This change delivers both at the layer that performs the install: the keyring init makes the
transaction commit (acceptance 1), and the trailing `pacman -Q <union>` makes a non-committing
transaction fail the chain, naming each missing package, instead of the guest reporting success
(acceptance 2).

**The change** (`vmshared/cloud_init_render.go`, the ONE shared renderer — so every pacman-family
`kind: vm` guest is repaired at once): the install entry chains three steps in one `runcmd` entry —

```
pacman-key --init && pacman-key --populate && pacman -Sy --needed --noconfirm <union> && pacman -Q <union>
```

- the **keyring init+populate** is the cure. `--populate` takes NO keyring argument deliberately: it
  populates every keyring the image ships under `/usr/share/pacman/keyrings` (`archlinux`, or a
  derivative's own), so no distro→keyring table has to be maintained here (R3).
- the trailing **`pacman -Q <union>`** is the render-side loudness this issue asks for: a
  non-committing transaction now fails the chain *at the place that performed it*, naming each missing
  package on the first line of the guest's own cloud-init output, instead of surfacing later as an
  unrelated `executable file not found`.

The `-Sy --needed` (not `-Syu`) rationale and the sshd try-restart resync are untouched, and the
`packages:` key stays omitted for the pacman family exactly as before.

Closes `opencharly/charly#832`.

## How tested

```
$ gofmt -l .
gofmt exit=0
$ go vet ./...
vet exit=0
$ go test -count=1 ./...
test exit=0          # 15 packages ok
```

Mutant control (R7 — the test must fail without the change): restoring the pre-change render makes the
updated assertion fail, exit 1; restored → exit 0:

```
$ python3 -c "p='vmshared/cloud_init_render.go'; s=open(p).read(); open(p,'w').write(s.replace('pacmanCmd := pacmanInstallCmd(packages)','pacmanCmd := \"pacman -Sy --needed --noconfirm \" + strings.Join(packages, \" \")'))"
$ go test -count=1 ./vmshared/ ; echo "MUTANT exit=$?"
--- FAIL: TestRenderCloudInit_PacmanFamily_RunsPacmanNeeded (0.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestRenderCloudInit_PacmanFamily_RunsPacmanNeeded/arch (0.00s)
        cloud_init_render_test.go:384: runcmd[0] = "pacman -Sy --needed --noconfirm openssh curl tar htop", want "pacman-key --init && pacman-key --populate && pacman -Sy --needed
MUTANT exit=1
$ cp /tmp/bv/cir3.bak vmshared/cloud_init_render.go
$ go test -count=1 ./vmshared/ ; echo "RESTORED exit=$?"
ok  	github.com/opencharly/sdk/vmshared	0.109s
RESTORED exit=0
```

**Boundary proof on the EMITTED artifact** (R8) — a throwaway spike renders the pacman-family
user-data for a spec carrying `cloud_init.package: [sudo, go, git, podman]`, with the pre-change
render as its control (the spike was deleted before the commit):

```
$ go run ./vmshared/spike_832      # the FIXED render
INSTALL ENTRY: - pacman-key --init && pacman-key --populate && pacman -Sy --needed --noconfirm openssh curl tar sudo go git podman && pacman -Q openssh curl tar sudo go git podman
$ # pre-change render restored, same spike:
$ go run ./vmshared/spike_832
INSTALL ENTRY: - pacman -Sy --needed --noconfirm openssh curl tar sudo go git podman
```

```
$ git rev-parse HEAD
433815a
$ git diff --stat $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)..HEAD
 vmshared/cloud_init_render.go      | 37 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-
 vmshared/cloud_init_render_test.go | 16 +++++++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 51 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

**What the armed-local-replace run proved, and what it did not — corrected.** The third verdict is
right that I dismissed the runnable path without a rule, so I ran it: with
`replace github.com/opencharly/sdk => <this worktree>` armed in `charly/charly/go.mod` and charly
rebuilt, the seed ISO this tree emits for the consuming bed's guest carries the fix VERBATIM —

```
$ ./bin/charly vm build eval-host-vm
Wrote /home/atrawog/Sync/Atrapub/a/dsh/opencharly/.worktrees/bed-venues/charly/image/eval-host-vm/seed.iso
Wrote VM box localhost/charly-eval-host-vm:2026.281.0850
$ xorriso -osirrox on -indev image/eval-host-vm/seed.iso -extract /user-data /tmp/bv/seed2-user-data
$ grep -n "pacman" /tmp/bv/seed2-user-data
5:    - pacman-key --init && pacman-key --populate && pacman -Sy --needed --noconfirm openssh curl tar sudo go git podman && pacman -Q openssh curl tar sudo go git podman
```

so the changed renderer provably executes in the real guest-provisioning path (`charly` requires the
plugin modules, so the local replace propagates to `plugin-vm`'s build — nothing is mocked). **The full
bed did not finish:** `charly check run check-local-vm` reached `check-live`, where the guest SSH became
unreachable and the run wedged with its run dir at `status: RUNNING` for 2.5h (plugins killed by a
signal at 11:01); the run and its VM were then stopped and destroyed with the scoped verbs. So the
guest-level end-to-end claim is NOT made: this PR stays at `analysed on a live system`, now with the
renderer proven at the emitted-artifact boundary in addition to the module gate and the mutant control.
The 43-repo `schemaparams`/wrap chain re-keys `plugin-vm` afterwards; the durable consumer change is
still that pin.

**The consumer chain, so it can be sequenced** (producer-first: this PR → merge+tag → `plugin-vm`'s SDK
pin bump → then every pacman-family `kind: vm` entity on the umbrella):
`opencharly/sdk` (this PR) → `opencharly/plugin-vm` (its `github.com/opencharly/sdk` pin) → the
umbrella's pinned `@github.com/op

author: caseyro
body:
My mistake in #23, and it broke the release for d73cd1d. I bumped three
actions to their current majors and assumed all three publish a moving major
tag. checkout and setup-python do. astral-sh/setup-uv does not: it has v1
through v9 and then stops, so `astral-sh/setup-uv@v10` resolves to nothing
and the release job died in "Set up job" with "unable to find version v10"
before a single step ran.

Nothing shipped as a result -- no tests, no tag, no image, no deploy webhook
-- so production stayed on v0.1.11 rather than serving something half-built.
That is the failure mode CLAUDE.md warns about: the run goes red after the
merge, main carries an unreleased change, and nobody notices unless they
check that the v* tag appeared.

Pinned to the exact release tag instead of guessing at a moving one. ci.yml
already pins setup-uv by digest, which is why ci.yml was unaffected and
stayed green through all of this.

Carries no skip marker on purpose: this release has to fire, because it is
also the one that ships the dependency bumps from #24.

Decisión del calendario de turnos del Hito 6.

- **Dónde:** PostgreSQL, por planta, con versiones con fecha de entrada en vigor (como pronto, mañana) y excepciones por día. Turnos en horas en punto, la resolución del histórico.
- **Cómo se aplica:** al consultar, hora a hora, en la hora local de la planta. Solo cambia `STOPPED` en hora de turno, que pasa a ser la parada «Detenida en turno». Fuera de turno, la regla de hoy (las horas extra cuentan). Sin calendario, el resultado es idéntico al actual.
- **El pasado no se reescribe:** versiones y excepciones solo a futuro.
- **Agregador:** anota también las paradas `STOPPED` para poder contarlas.
- **API:** lectura con `viewer`, cambios con `admin` y auditoría.
- **Demo:** turnos de mañana y tarde de lunes a viernes.

Se descartan un fichero versionado, un calendario externo, guardar los segundos de turno en los agregados y calcular desde los cambios de estado (detalle en el ADR).

`docs/indicadores-de-planta.md` incorpora la regla y dos ejemplos nuevos.

Refs: LF-121

author: shikaruki0
body:
## Summary
Two fixes, one commit each.

### 1. `fix(auth)`: PKCE for Google sign-in (27d122a)
- "Continue with Google" now starts from a dedicated **PKCE** helper client. Supabase sends back only a one-time `?code=`, so access/refresh tokens never appear in the URL.
- The code is removed from the address bar before the main client starts. It is then exchanged using this browser's verifier, and the session goes to the main client, which stays the only owner of the session.
- The helper saves only the verifier to localStorage. Its own copy of the session stays in memory.
- **Email links (password reset / confirmation) still use the implicit flow**, so they keep working when opened on a different phone or laptop. Moving them to PKCE would break that.
- If a code can't be exchanged (sign-in finished in a different browser, or the code expired), the user sees a friendly "try again" message instead of nothing happening.
- No Supabase dashboard changes needed. The redirect URLs are unchanged.

### 2. `fix(sync)`: shared-device account isolation (ebbd2a5)
Before this fix, these paths could leak data between accounts (each has a test that **fails on `main`** and passes here):
- A signs out → A's progress stayed on screen as "local" data → B signs in → **A's data was uploaded or merged into B's cloud row**.
- Guest progress taken over by A could later also be taken over by B.
- A push or pull started for A that finished after switching to B could write B's data into A's row, or merge A's row into B.
- The writes made while wiping data during an account switch scheduled a push. Combined with A's leftover `lastCloudPushAt`, this could overwrite B's newer cloud progress.
- A running focus timer could give XP or a session to the next account.
- "Export backup" included other accounts' device caches and snapshots.

Fixes: an account epoch plus ticket checks after every await; no push unless local data is bound to the signed-in account; push/pull upgrade to a full login sync until the first sync after a switch finishes; re-bind writes don't trigger pushes; sync bookkeeping resets per account; timers reset on switch; export is scoped to the current account; the UI redraws after a re-bind.

## Validation
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `vitest run`: **45 files / 537 tests pass** (was 43 / 516; +2 new files, +21 tests)
- `npm run build`: OK
- Checked against the real `@supabase/supabase-js` 2.110.8: the verifier is stored under `nf-google-pkce-code-verifier` and the authorize URL includes `code_challenge` + `code_challenge_method=s256`.

## Behaviour change to note
After **Sign out**, the app now shows the account screen with a clean profile instead of the previous account's progress. That progress is safe in the cloud and in the device cache, and comes back on the next sign-in.

body:
## Summary

When the destination of `atomic_write_text` was a symlink, `os.replace` renamed onto the link itself. The link became a regular file and the file it pointed at kept its old contents. `Path.write_text`, which this helper replaced, writes through the link. This PR makes the helper write through the link too. Sibling of python-async-llm-pipelines#157 / #158.

## Repro (origin/main)

- `atomic_write_text('link.md', 'new\n')` with `link.md -> real/f.md`: `islink False`, real file still `'old\n'`
- `bench_streaming.py --n 3 --out out.json` with `out.json -> real/b.json`: rc 0, `out.json` is now a regular file, `real/b.json` still `{}`

## Fix

`_resolve_symlinked_target` resolves a symlinked final component with `os.path.realpath` before the temp file and rename target are chosen. The rest of the writer is unchanged:
- The #128 NAME_MAX cap now applies to the resolved basename.
- The #247 `0o666`/umask create and the existing-mode copy still apply, now to the file actually written.

Other cases:
- A plain path is unchanged.
- A dangling link creates the file it names.
- A link loop stays unresolved, so the mode copy's `os.stat` raises `OSError` (ELOOP) and the temp file is cleaned up. The write-seam guards already turn that `OSError` into exit 2.

All callers go through this one helper: `dump_summary_json`, `dump_aggregate_json` and `run_eval.write_runs`. There is no other `os.replace` writer in the package.

## Tests

`tests/test_atomic_write_symlink_destination.py` has 10 cases, each run with `Path.write_text` as well so the lock checks parity:
- relative and absolute links: written through, link survives, linked file's 0640 mode kept, no temp left behind
- dangling link
- link loop
- linked file with a 255-byte (NAME_MAX) name
- plain-path control
- `bench_streaming --out link.json` end to end

**Revert probe** (main's `io_utils.py`, `__pycache__` cleared): 10 collected, 5 red (4 atomic arms + bench e2e), 5 green controls (3 `write_text` parity arms, loop, plain path).

Gates: `pytest -m "not pg"` 1949 passed (re-run after commit); `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

Closes #296

author: jensdewulfvintecc
body:
## What and why

Implements ADR-0010 §2's breached-password check, together with its 2026-10-08 clarification (an unreachable list accepts the password). The privacy terms are those of ADR-0012 §8: only the first 5 characters of a hash, which isn't personal data.

`checkBreachedPassword(password)` asks Have I Been Pwned's range API, through the guarded client (ADR-0017 §6, SEC-5), whether a password is in a known breach:

- only the first 5 characters of the password's SHA-1 hash leave the server, never the password or whose it is;
- it asks for a padded answer (`Add-Padding`), so the response's size gives nothing away, and padding lines (count 0) don't count as a breach;
- it returns `breached`, `not-breached` or `unknown`. `unknown` covers an unreachable list, a timeout or an error status.

What to do with `unknown` belongs to the caller: setting a password accepts it and logs the miss. Logging comes with the logger foundation, and wiring this check to setting a password comes with password sign-up.

## Checklist

- [x] An accepted ADR covers this change, or it needs none (PROC-1 to PROC-3)
- [x] Does what the ADR says and nothing more (PRIN-2, PROC-9)
- [x] Tests added or updated (TEST-1 to TEST-6)
- [ ] Works with keyboard only and a screen reader; 320 px and 200% text checked (UI-6 to UI-16): not applicable, no UI
- [ ] Every new text in English and Dutch (UI-20): not applicable
- [ ] Behind a release flag, or the flag is removed (CODE-20): not applicable, no caller yet
- [x] No new personal data or third party, or the ADR and data inventory cover it (SEC-10, SEC-11): ADR-0012 §8 lists Have I Been Pwned
- [x] ADRs and standards still match what was built (PROC-11)
- [x] `pnpm verify` passes

## Notes for review

- **No new dependency.** It uses `node:crypto` for SHA-1 and the guarded client for the request.
- **Tests** swap the request for a fake and check that:
  - only the 5-character prefix is sent (the suffix and the password never appear in the request), and padding is asked for;
  - a password on the list is found, and a padding line with count 0 is not;
  - an unlisted password passes;
  - an unreachable list, a timeout and a 503 all give `unknown`.

  The known SHA-1 of the word "password" serves as the fixture (TEST-8).
- **Self-hosted instances:** the switch that turns the check off for instances without outbound access (ADR-0021 §5) belongs with the wiring.

https://jira.xwiki.org/browse/XWIKI-25199

# Changes

## Description

Backport of https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/pull/6639 on 18.4.x:

* Add `R180407000XWIKI25199DataMigration`, which executes `R180100000XWIKI23827DataMigration` and `R180405000XWIKI24357DataMigration` again to fix the passwords put back in their legacy storage on instances upgraded before XWIKI-25203 (a user profile cached before those migrations and saved after them, e.g. by `XClassMigratorListener` when the `XWikiUsers` class gets its new `underline` field, was overriding the migrated password with its legacy `StringProperty`). Both only handle the values that are not migrated yet, so executing them again is harmless.
* Skip the repair migration for DBs coming from 17.10.14 or a later 17.10.x, where the password migrations were executed with the cache flush of XWIKI-25203 (the master counterpart, also skipping 18.4.7+, is https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform/pull/6659).
* Only select, in `R180100000XWIKI23827DataMigration`, the objects still holding a `StringProperty` for one of the password fields, instead of every object of the classes having a password field: the objects already migrated (e.g. when the migration is executed again by the repair migration) are not processed anymore.
* Name the actual legacy algorithm (e.g. `SHA-512`) in the log about outdated algorithms for passwords not re-encoded yet, instead of `XWikiLegacy`, which is the name of the re-encoded format.
* Stop logging twice the usage of a deprecated algorithm when computing a hash.

## Clarifications

* Adapted to the 18.4.x names: the repair migration is `R180407000XWIKI25199DataMigration` (version `180407000`) and relies on `180405000XWIKI24357`; the `migrate()` test is added to the existing `R180405000XWIKI24357DataMigrationTest`.
* The root cause analysis is in the master PR description.

N/A, no UI change.

* `mvn clean verify -Pquality` in `xwiki-platform-oldcore` (1206 tests passing, checkstyle, coverage and revapi checks passing)
* Manual check on a 18.4.6 jetty/hsqldb distribution patched with these changes (and XWIKI-25203):

* Prefers squash: Yes

body:
## Root cause

`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` runs `sudo apt-get update` against the runner's apt mirror list on **every** run, and apt has no overall deadline. In the hung runs, `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` did not answer, apt fell back to `archive.ubuntu.com`, fetched the InRelease files, and then printed nothing more until the run was cancelled or hit the six-hour default job limit (chrona run 37691162409 sat for exactly 6h; signal run 37689707686 was cancelled after 20 min; same signature on signal#21, signal#22 and summa#21). It was not an apt lock wait (no "Waiting for cache lock") and not a version mismatch (Playwright is pinned exactly to 1.63.0 in the lockfile).

The apt run bought nothing the suite needs: a green run's log shows every Chromium library "already the newest version" on the runner image. apt only added optional fonts and Mesa upgrades. The browser was also downloaded fresh on every run (no cache).

## Fix

- **Cache by version key.** `~/.cache/ms-playwright` is cached under the `playwright-core` version read from `package-lock.json`, which fixes the browser build. A stalled cache restore gives up after 2 min (`SEGMENT_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MINS`).
- **No apt on the normal path.** Chromium is downloaded without `--with-deps`, only on a cache miss, with `timeout-minutes: 5`.
- **Deterministic OS deps.** `ldd` proves offline that every library the Chromium binaries link against is present. Only if a future image lacks one does apt run, with per-request timeouts, retries and a 5-minute deadline. The check then runs again and fails, naming the missing library.
- **Fail fast.** The job has `timeout-minutes: 20` (a normal run takes about 2 minutes).

Tests are unchanged. The browser suite still runs on every push and PR.

Praxis work item: WI-0055. (This was first captured as WI-0037, but the concurrent requirements-capture work took and merged the same ID first. Main's record keeps that ID, and this fix was re-attributed to WI-0055 when main was merged in.)

author: jensvandewalle
body:
[AB#47981](https://dev.azure.com/skyline-cloud/9be23a94-030f-4558-a657-001bcf297fcf/_workitems/edit/47981)

## Summary
Follow-up on #367. When lowering a resource's concurrency would quarantine jobs, the DevPack reported "would move one or more jobs to quarantine." without any job IDs on a real DataMiner Agent. As a result, the Resource CRUD script could not show which jobs are impacted.

## Root cause
A real Agent rejects such a resource update with `ResourceUpdateCausedReservationsToGoToQuarantine` and reports the impacted reservations in `ConflictInformation.ConflictingUsages`. `MustBeMovedToQuarantine` is empty. `CoreResourceHandler.ResolveImpactedJobIds` only read `MustBeMovedToQuarantine`.

#367 was only validated against the in-memory simulation. The simulation encoded the same (incorrect) assumption, so the tests passed. The `alpha044` tag build skips integration tests, so no real-DMA run happened before release.

## Changes
- `CoreResourceHandler`: resolve impacted reservations from `ConflictInformation.ConflictingUsages` (filtered on the updated resource) in addition to `MustBeMovedToQuarantine`, de-duplicated per reservation.
- `ResourceManagerStore` (simulation) now mirrors a real Agent:
  - rejected resource update: reservations reported as conflicting usages, `MustBeMovedToQuarantine` empty
  - forced resource update: reservations are quarantined without trace data
- Tests (`ResourceConcurrencyTests`):
  - new `…CoreReportsTheReservationAsConflictingUsage` pins the raw SRM response, so a real-DMA run catches simulation drift
  - forced-update test asserts no trace data is returned
  - tests no longer assume which overlapping reservation SRM picks for quarantine (on a real Agent this is not always the last one)

## Validation
- `ResourceConcurrencyTests` (17): all pass against a real DataMiner Agent. With the old handler, 2 of them fail on the real Agent with exactly the reported symptom.
- Full suite in-memory: 1860 passed.
- Verified end-to-end with the Resource CRUD script (SLC-S-MediaOps.Plan#896) on a real system: the popup now lists the impacted jobs.

## What changes (new in this PR)
| Issue | Change |
|---|---|
| #1031 AbortController | `createMetricsFetcher()` (format-utils.js) passes an `AbortSignal`. Starting a new request (manual refresh, R) aborts the previous one, and its rejection is ignored (`superseded`), not logged as a failure. |
| #1032 request timeout | Metrics requests abort after 4s and fail with "Timed out after 4s", which counts toward the connection state like any failed fetch. |
| #963 Page Visibility | Polling pauses while the tab is hidden and fetches at once when it's shown again. A manual Pause stays paused. |
| #1015 interval control | 5s / 10s / 30s picker in the refresh bar, remembered in localStorage. `scheduler.setInterval()` restarts a pending wait with the new length. |
| #1010 / #952 shortcuts | `1`–`5` switch tabs, `R` refreshes. Ignored with Ctrl/Meta/Alt (Ctrl+R still reloads), in form fields/contenteditable, and during IME composition. Advertised with `aria-keyshortcuts`. |
| #1034 remembered tab | The last active tab is restored on load. A `?tab=` / `#tab` deep link wins. Unknown or hidden tabs are ignored. Storage errors (privacy mode, file://) are swallowed. |
| #953 touch targets | Tab buttons, refresh-bar buttons and the select get `min-height/min-width: 44px` on `(pointer: coarse)`; tab buttons also get it at ≤640px. |

## Verification
- `node --test Scraping_project/dashboard/tests/`: 71/71 pass. The new `refresh-nav.test.js` uses fake timers to cover timeout, supersede, HTTP errors, `setInterval`, pause, the shortcut rules, initial-tab precedence and the markup/CSS contract.
- Headless Chrome, driven over the DevTools protocol:
  - key `3` switches to Performance and stores it; `1` while the interval select has focus does nothing
  - choosing 30s stores it and the countdown shows 30
  - after a reload, Performance and 30s are restored; `?tab=activity` overrides the remembered tab
  - no console errors
- Only `Scraping_project/dashboard/` changes.


### Also closes (added)
Closes #503: keys 1–5 switch tabs except in form fields (ARIA tabs from #153 are already in place), and a small on-screen hint (`#shortcut-hint`, text follows the visible tab count; hidden on touch devices).
Closes #767: AbortController with a 4 s per-fetch timeout, so a hung fetch is aborted before the next interval. Exactly one request is pending at a time (no unbounded promises), and a timeout is logged as its own `timeout` activity type (styled, and spoken as "Timeout:").
Closes #741: a hidden tab is paused, so no fetch happens after the current interval; becoming visible triggers one catch-up fetch. There is no leader election in the app, so the "if present" clause doesn't apply.
Closes #735: `serve.py` bound `("", 8080)`, i.e. **every interface**. It now binds `127.0.0.1:8080` by default; override with `--host/--port` or `CC_HOST`/`CC_PORT`, and a wildcard bind must be explicit and prints a warning. `make_server(host, port, handler, server_factory)` is injectable. Tests assert the exact address passed to a mocked factory (no listener), port overrides and validation, and that `main()` never falls back to a wildcard.
Closes #721: missing assets get a plain 404 (no filesystem paths, never the app shell). Directory listings, dotfiles, `tests/` and non-asset files (`serve.py`, `*.md`) are also 404, while existing assets and `/version.js` are still served. body:
## Qué cambia

Rediseño completo del sitio con el concepto **"Neón y oficio"** (el techo de hexágonos LED, los sillones rojos y el poste de barbero del local), hecho por fases:

1. **Base de animación** (`js/fx.js`, único punto de entrada): GSAP + ScrollTrigger + SplitText + Lenis por `importmap` con versión fija (jsDelivr). Reveals con `data-fx="title|image|fade"`. Preloader con logo, anillo, contador y cortina.
2. **Hero 3D** (`js/hex3d.js`): techo de hexágonos LED en Three.js con bloom, inclinación con el mouse, tubos que parpadean en rojo y cámara que avanza con el scroll. Título letra por letra, neón en "ESTILO", cifras animadas.
3. **Secciones**: marquee que responde al scroll, servicios apilados (sticky) con parallax, galería fijada del local con cierre a todo el ancho, poste de barbero en 3D (`js/pole3d.js`), cursor propio, botones magnéticos y nav que se oculta al bajar.
4. **Barberos**: 9 tarjetas 3D con recorte (fundador 2×2), carrusel con puntos en celular, "Reservar con él" deja elegido al barbero. Sale José Ojeda (web, formulario y `supabase/schema.sql`); se borraron las fotos viejas.
5. **Logo circular HD** en nav, hero y footer (moneda que gira); `og-image.jpg` nueva.
6. **Pulido**: accesibilidad, rendimiento y caché (`?v=`).

## Por qué

Dar al sitio la identidad del local (neón, hexágonos, poste) sin perder rendimiento ni accesibilidad.

## Para revisar

- **Base de datos (importante):** la web ahora ofrece 9 barberos, pero la base de Supabase solo tiene a Oswaldo, Esteban y José Ojeda. **Hasta correr `supabase/schema.sql` en Supabase, reservar con los 6 nuevos falla.** Además, `jose-gregorio` y `jose-gregorio-ojeda` son la misma foto: si es la misma persona, conviene renombrar su fila en vez de dar de baja una y crear otra.
- **Respaldo**: sin JS, sin WebGL, en equipos débiles (≤4 núcleos o ≤4 GB) o con "reducir movimiento", el contenido se ve completo y quieto. Three.js solo se descarga con `import()` dinámico, y no se descarga en esos casos.
- **Celular**: el 3D del hero va en calidad baja (5×4 hexágonos, sin bloom).
- **Lighthouse móvil (local)**: rendimiento 84–85, accesibilidad 100, buenas prácticas 100, SEO 100. Conviene confirmar con PageSpeed Insights ya publicado.
- **Commits previos**: la rama se creó desde `fix-fotos-servicios`, así que el PR incluye también sus 4 commits, que no estaban en `main`.

## Pendiente

- Probar en un celular real.
- El logo del footer gira sin fin y solo lo detiene el mouse (WCAG 2.2.2).
- En escritorio el JS de librerías ronda los 260 KB gzip (presupuesto: ~250 KB).
- La foto del equipo en el cierre de "El local" es vertical y se ve algo blanda a todo el ancho.
- Archivos que ya no se usan (`VideoCorteLucas.mp4`, `poster-corte.*`, algunos `el-local-*`) siguen en el repo.

author: bubblebee1408
body:
**Draft — for review. Backend half of the composer's source picker.**

## Investigation (reported before coding)
1. **What `sources` did in `conversation.send`: nothing.** Type-checked as a list (`gateway/verbs.py` `_conversation_send`), then dropped: `_task_args` sent `ask` only `{"question": text}`. It never reached retrieval and was not recorded, despite the field saying "Recorded". Its documented ids were `sources.list` *data-feed* ids (held/client/external sites), not bodies of law. Inside `ask`, `sources` only fed the cache key (`_cache_lookup` / `_cache_store`), and `ask` did not declare the field. What actually decided answered/refused bodies was the question's wording (`checker/ask_scope.read`); retrieval (`agents/research_question.evidence`) only ever searches the held CA2013 corpus.
2. **Wall System → `conversation.send`: not connected.** `file_ids` are sha256 ids from `documents.upload`, read from `ctx.documents` / `store.get_document`. `vault.upload` writes a separate vault record (uuid + sha256 in the file store), which `conversation.send` cannot read: such an id comes back CANNOT_READ. Not built here.

## Decisions (owner, 2026-10-08)
- A verb named `sources.list` already existed (data feeds; used by two screens, MCP `themis.sources.list`, docs). **Additive:** it gains a `bodies` array; its existing fields are unchanged.
- `searched` is an **optional** field on `answer_envelope.v1`. Old stored envelopes still validate and mean what they meant, the same reasoning the schema used to widen `task`.

## Design
- `sources.list.bodies` is **generated from `checker/scope.BODIES`**, never a second list: id, name, `issuer` (= regulator), status and covers come from the register. `short` is the register's own abbreviation, or its key when it lists none (nothing invented). Note: held → the register's note; otherwise "Choosing it is refused, with the reason: " + `scope.refusal_for(id)`. `selectable` is true for every body; `default_on` only for IN_CORPUS (CA2013).
  - `client_documents` (tier CLIENT): a research question does not read them, and the note says so.
  - `web`: `available=false`, `selectable=false`, reason "web text cannot make an answer VERIFIED".
- **`ask.sources`** is declared in the verb table, so REST, MCP and CLI carry it; the parity test is green. Retrieval runs only when a HELD body is chosen. With none, `ask` refuses `OUT_OF_SCOPE_LAW` in the register's words and never touches the held corpus.
- **`conversation.send`** resolves with the same function:
  - an unknown id is `BAD_REQUEST` naming it;
  - absent or empty means the default (held bodies), stated as `defaulted: true`;
  - the choice is forwarded to `ask`.
- **`envelope.bodies`**: each chosen unheld body is refused by name with `scope.refusal_for` (NOT_HELD, or CURRENT_ONLY for LODR). An unchosen CA2013 is NOT_ENGAGED "not chosen … not searched", never "nothing on point was found".
- **`envelope.searched`** = `{bodies: [{id, status, read}], as_of, defaulted}`, in register order. `read` is true only for a held body.
- **Cache:** chosen sources are part of the key, order-insensitively (resolved to register order). The default keeps the pre-existing key, so answers already in a live cache stay valid.

## Tests (18 new, `gateway/verbs.py` 560/560)
- Bodies are generated from `scope.BODIES` in order, with the register's own name, coverage, status and issuer. Only CA2013 is on by default.
- DECLARED is selectable and its note says it will be refused and why; web is unavailable, with the reason; `sources.list` serves `bodies`.
- An unknown id is `BAD_REQUEST` naming it.
- **Only LLP2008 → no citations at all** (retrieval did not run). LLP2008 is NOT_HELD by name; CA2013 is NOT_ENGAGED "not searched"; `searched` records it.
- **CA2013 + LLP2008 → answers from CA2013**: Companies Act citations only, LLP2008 refused in the register's words, status PARTIAL, `searched` = [CA2013 read, LLP2008 not read], and the envelope validates.
- An empty list → the default, `defaulted: true`.
- **Cache keys differ by sources**, and listing order does not split the cache.

Gate: `HARNESS_RESULT suites=319 failed=0 floor_breach=0 status=GREEN`; floor `gateway/verbs.py` 541 → 560.

## Not in this PR
- The `decompose` path does not yet carry `sources`.
- Non-research tasks ignore `sources`, and `searched` is only recorded for research questions.
- Wall System documents in `conversation.send` (see investigation item 2).
