body:
The geometry shader expanded every cable on the map in three passes, also off screen, and the engine rebuilt the cable VAOs on every draw. This change culls cables outside the view in the shader, keeps the VAOs between draws, and makes the once-per-second update cheaper.

**Why:** Turning cables off took a ~1150-unit replay from 52.2 to 56.3 FPS (+8%) at 4K with MSAA 8. Most of that is GPU time. Measured on Zero-K v1.14.10.1 with Recoil 2026.07.04. Not measured again on current master.

**Behaviour:** No visible change. A cable on terrain raised more than ~30 elmo above the map's highest point can pop in late for about one second.

**Testing:**
- In-game: a replay of a ~1000-unit game at full graphics, on Zero-K master `1dd7cb0d7`. No Lua errors. Simulation checksums and unit counts are the same as master. The screenshot is the same as master.
- In-game, camera on a base with cables (Nuclear Winter replay, 60 s at 1x): checksums and unit counts are the same as master, no Lua errors. The screenshot shows the same cables as master.

**Related:** ZeroK-RTS/Zero-K#5743 (cables hang AMD/Mesa GPUs; still open). This PR edits the same geometry shader as the merged AMD fix attempt ZeroK-RTS/Zero-K#5756, so it needs a test on AMD or Mesa before merge. Licho in #zkdev (2026-04-30).

**AI disclosure:** Claude Code wrote this change and its tests. I reviewed the change. The in-game tests ran automatically on Windows with an RTX 3080.

body:
## Summary

- **Biome is replaced by Oxlint and Oxfmt**, through Ultracite, so shouldertap matches pcobooster and sites.
  - `oxlint.config.ts` uses the core, react, tanstack and vitest presets.
  - `oxfmt.config.ts` replaces Biome's formatter. Both keep Biome's ignores.
  - `@biomejs/biome` and `biome.jsonc` are removed, and `bun run check` / `fix` (`ultracite`) now pick up oxlint and oxfmt.
- **Biome's exceptions carry over:**
  - Barrel entry points are allowed.
  - PascalCase files are allowed in `apps/server/src` (the Alchemy resource convention).
  - `max-classes-per-file` and `no-redeclare` are off for Effect's error classes and schema-plus-type names, as in sites.
  - The three `biome-ignore` comments became `oxlint-disable` comments with the same reasons.
- **The test-quality plugin from pcobooster#323 and sites#24 is added.** `lint/oxlint-plugin-test-quality.mjs` covers every `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.spec.ts(x)`, and all 9 existing test files already pass. Its 21 RuleTester cases run in CI as `bun run test:lint` under Node 24, because RuleTester doesn't run on Bun. A `setup-node` step in the `check` job covers both oxlint's JS plugins and those tests.
- **Bun and Playwright tests are exempt from Vitest-specific rules.** Bun's test globals and the Playwright specs in `apps/web/e2e` are excluded from Vitest-only rules such as `prefer-importing-vitest-globals`, `prefer-each` and `consistent-test-filename`.
- **The ~310 new findings are fixed in code:**
  - `function` components became arrow components. In each route file, `export const Route` moved below its component so nothing is used before it's defined.
  - JSX apostrophes became `'`, so the rendered text is identical.
  - Shadowed names were renamed.
  - Regexes got the `u` flag.
  - `forEach`/`reduce`/`sort` became `for…of`, `toSorted` and similar.
  - Render-time ref writes moved into effects.
  - Smaller fixes: `role="status"` became `<output>`, and three `useState` calls with no setter became `useMemo`.
  - Effect's `forEach`, `catch` and `TaggedError` factories trip some unicorn and promise rules. Those are disabled with reasons.

## Why type-aware linting is off

pcobooster and sites lint with type information, but here oxlint's TypeScript-Go checker resolves `yield* new TaggedError(...)` in Effect generators, and Drizzle query results, as `any`. That produced about 250 false `no-unsafe-*` errors that `tsc` (TS 6.0.3) doesn't report. `bun run check-types` stays the type gate, as it was under Biome. Revisit after upgrading to TypeScript 7.

## Risk

- Risk tier: medium. It touches 75 files, mostly mechanical.
- Main failure modes:
  - A route component reordering could break module load. The web build passes, and `check`'s Playwright download flows exercise it.
  - `useMemo` replaced `useState(loader)` for one-time `localStorage` reads in `landing.tsx`, `join.tsx` and `tap.tsx`.
  - `revokePairing` (web) now swallows rejections inside a try/catch.
  - `live.ts` reconnect logic was restructured for `addEventListener` and `const` functions.
- Rollback: revert.

## Verification

- `bun run check` (oxlint + oxfmt), `bun run check-types`, `bun run test:lint` (21), `bun test scripts/cloudflare` (21), `packages/domain` and `packages/client` tests, and the `apps/web` build all pass.
- The `apps/server` tests (40) passed during the fix pass. Note: that suite includes `integ.test.ts`, which deployed and destroyed a temporary Cloudflare stack.
- This PR's own `check` and preview `deploy` runs exercise the rest.

## Follow-ups

- The AGENTS.md pointer to the plugin is left out to avoid conflicting with #46. Add it after #46 lands.
- This PR conflicts with #45 in `deploy.yml`, which splits out `e2e`. Rebase whichever lands second.

This pull request introduces support for exact-time synchronized compressed image input for multicamera rigs in the `okvis_ros` package, along with configuration and build/test updates. The pull request also adds new configuration files and updates documentation to describe the new feature.

The most important changes are:

**Synchronized Compressed Image Input:**

author: aniketvish0
body:
Part of armoriq/armorCodex#117, the armorClaude half.

## Problem

Usage sync kept one state file per data directory. Logging in as another user changed the upload key but reused the previous user's progress, so the new user could post nothing or inherit another user's history.

## Change

- Resolve the key's user through `POST /iap/validate-key`. Store progress separately for backend, product and user. Key rotation for the same user keeps that progress.
- Keep the process lock per data directory. The request marker contains a key fingerprint. A running pass leaves a request made with another key for that key's next launch.
- A fresh installation uploads full history. If another user already synced here, a new user skips hours before their first sync hour.
- A returning user skips only the hours between their previous sync hour and return hour. Their own earlier failed or unposted hours remain eligible. Persist each skipped window in their state.
- The switch hour remains eligible. Within one org, the backend's hourly upsert replaces the previous user's row with the latest user's row. Across orgs, each org has its own row.
- If the backend cannot resolve the user, upload nothing and write no state.
- Drop the unreleased shared state file. Credential loading stays in the SDK.

The dashboard's explicit earlier-history request is implemented in #274.

## Tests

The full suite passes 499/499 in a guarded temporary home. The protected-home snapshot and credential hash are unchanged.

The real CLI tests use a local backend and cover fresh-install history, A to B isolation, a returning user's skipped interval, a new message after return, retrying A's failed rows after A to B to A, rejected or unresolved users, a request arriving while another key's pass is running, URL normalization, and owner-only state storage.

Both switch-back regressions fail on `9902507` and pass on `453e335`. Earlier regressions fail on the corresponding prior commits: shared state on `6d209cb`, history attribution on `cb8c66a`, and the pending-request race on `ec8426f`.

Changed functions remain at complexity 10 or below. `syncUsage` retains its existing complexity of 21, tracked in #245.

## CI

The stack's Node checks fail because the published `@armoriq/sdk-dev` lacks `sessionTranscriptPaths`. Local verification uses the SDK tarball containing that export. The required SDK release is pending.

## Follow-ups

- #271: a new user's request waits for that user's next hook when another key's pass is running.
- #272: an in-place request-marker write can be read before its contents arrive.
- #275: alternating keys can lose the end of an hour.
- #276: a backwards clock jump can repeatedly look like a user switch.
- #277: resetting or invalidating the state loses skipped-hour restrictions.

- #282: use the actual login instant to assign messages before hourly aggregation. The current first-sync-hour cutoff does not meet that requirement. This needs coordination with the login owner.

author: ewraj
body:
Implements foundations **F4** and **F5** from `PHASE_6_OVERVIEW.md` §3 (#17). This matters on its own today, and it is a precondition for sync and the `.annotatecode` format.

## The problem

- **F4.** The tree was listed at whatever the branch pointed to when the repository was opened. Each file was then fetched *by branch name* when first scrolled to, possibly weeks later. A source could hold text from several commits, and two devices opening "the same" source would anchor the same annotation against different code.
- **F5.** GitHub treats `Facebook/React` and `facebook/react` as one repository. The source id `github:${owner}/${repo}@${ref}` did not, so pasting a differently-cased URL started an empty twin.

## Decisions (reverse cheaply if wrong)

| Call | Why |
|---|---|
| **The id stays keyed by ref, not commit.** The commit lives in `origin.commit` | Reopening "react at main" after main moves must still land on the annotations. The commit decides what is *read*, not what is *found*. No existing id changes |
| **Reopening from a URL re-pins to the branch's current commit** | That's what pasting a URL did before (refresh the tree). An explicit "stay on this commit / update to latest" control is follow-up work |
| **Cached text survives a reopen only while its blob SHA is unchanged** | Otherwise one source mixes commits again. A dropped cache costs one re-read, and the anchor ladder places existing annotations or sends them to the displaced tray, as designed |
| **Edit overlays always survive, and keep `edited: true`** | Before, a reopen kept an overlay's text but reset `edited` to false, so it passed itself off as upstream text. Fixed here because the same function decides both |
| **Canonical casing applies to new opens only** | If a source already exists under another casing (and no canonical one exists), it keeps its id: `findStoredSpelling`. Owner and repo compare case-insensitively; the ref compares exactly, because refs are case-sensitive |
| **Three API calls per open** (was two, or one with a named ref) | `/repos` for `full_name` and the default branch; `/commits/{ref}` with `Accept: application/vnd.github.sha` (40 bytes, not the commit's diff); the tree at the SHA. That's 20 opens an hour on the anonymous limit instead of 30. A URL that already names a full SHA skips the commit call |
| **Old sources without a commit keep reading their ref** | They gain a pin the next time they are opened from a URL. Reopening from recents makes no network calls, as before |

Verified against the live API before writing it: `/commits/` with an encoded slash in the ref (`docs%2Fphase-6-plans`) resolves; the `sha` media type returns a bare SHA; trees accept a commit SHA; raw.githubusercontent serves files at a SHA; CORS allows the custom `Accept`. **An unknown ref returns 422, not 404**, so both now map to "has no branch, tag or commit called …".

The recents list shows the pin: `github · main · 22e9257`.

## Tests

- `src/sources/github.test.ts`: 52 tests (was 23). Covers the three calls and their URLs, the SHA `Accept` header, refs with slashes, a full-SHA ref skipping the lookup, canonical casing and its fallback, unknown ref (422), a non-SHA answer, a rate limit on the commit call, truncated trees, pinned and legacy reads, a `findStoredSpelling` table, `withSourceId`, a `carryCachedContent` table, and two IndexedDB integration tests (reopen under legacy casing; branch moved, with changed blobs dropped and unchanged ones kept).
- **Mutation-checked:** reverting the pinned read, the blob check, or the legacy-casing lookup each turns specific tests red.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (290 passed), `npm run build`, `npm run test:e2e` (29 passed).
- Live smoke test via `vite-node` against the real API: `EWRAJ/annotate-code` opened as `github:ewraj/Annotate-Code@main`, pinned to `22e9257…`, and README read at that commit.

## Follow-ups (not here)

- An explicit "update to latest" action, so re-pinning becomes a choice rather than a side effect of pasting a URL.
- `parseRepoUrl` still can't tell `/tree/release/2.0/src/x` apart (an existing limitation). Opening such a URL now fails with the clearer "no branch, tag or commit" message.

author: bhav-ya-h
body:
`encodeContentDispositionFileName` only replaces non-ASCII characters in the fallback `filename`, so a DQUOTE in the file name closes the quoted-string early and the rest becomes more `Content-Disposition` parameters: a part generated with `name` of `upload` and file name `x"; name="other` reads back from Jetty's own parser with `name` of `other`, which the fix stops by limiting the fallback to RFC9110 `qdtext`, the exact name still arriving in `filename*` (noticed because the sibling `name` parameter in `customizePartHeaders` is quoted with `QuotedCSV.quote`).

AI tooling was used to help prepare this change.

body:
## Summary
This adds the agentic part of SASS: reviewing student essays against the Missouri Learning Standards (ELA MVP). It comes as two folders, synced from Justin's lab repo ([GrouchoLarks/csci-5030-project](https://github.com/GrouchoLarks/csci-5030-project) at `67b74fa`). Each folder has a `SYNCED_FROM.txt`. **Please make changes in the lab repo, not in these folders**, so the next sync doesn't overwrite them.

| Folder | What | Who it's for |
|---|---|---|
| `AgenticAI/` | **Production.** LangGraph review workflow, an HTTP service (FastAPI) the backend calls, the Postgres schema (Flyway `db/migrations` V1–V6), Dockerfile + `docker-compose.yml` | Backend integration |
| `AgenticLab/` | **Lab.** Synthetic classrooms (labels, assignments, essays), essay generator, evaluation against labels, Streamlit demo | Mock LMS seeding, demos |

`AgenticAI/` never imports `AgenticLab/`; a test enforces this. The `AgenticAI` placeholder file is replaced by the folder. `Backend` and `Frontend` are untouched.

## How the backend talks to it
The API is `contracts/agentic-api.yaml` in the lab repo; a separate draft PR proposes contracts for discussion. Endpoints:
- `POST /events/submission-graded`
  - The grading webhook (`X-SASS-Webhook-Secret`); returns 202 with a `run_id`.
  - Only one review per (submission, attempt).
  - The event is a notification only: the service fetches the submission itself.
- `GET /runs/{run_id}`: run status (`Authorization: Bearer <AGENTIC_API_TOKEN>`).
- `GET`/`PUT /review-policy`, `GET /health`.
- Results are **not** returned over HTTP. Findings are written to Postgres, and the backend reads them there by `lms_submission_id` + `attempt`.
- `POST /sweeps` and `/trend-analyses` return 501 for now.

Until the mock LMS exists, the service reads submissions from `AgenticLab/data/synthetic`. Its README maps each field to the mock LMS contract, so the same data can seed the mock LMS. All data is synthetic.

## Try it
```bash
cd AgenticAI
cp .env.example .env          # fill in WEBHOOK_SECRET, AGENTIC_API_TOKEN; set FAKE_LLM=1 for no API keys
docker compose up -d --build  # postgres + flyway + agentic on :8000
curl localhost:8000/health
```
Python (3.11): `pip install -e "AgenticAI[dev]" -e "AgenticLab[dev]"`. The Streamlit demo with no keys: `python AgenticLab/demo/run_demo.py --fake`.

## Privacy
SASS never stores essay text. Only IDs, short observation reasons (at most 12 words), findings, and teacher responses are persisted. Errors and logs never include submission content.

## Test plan
- [x] Fresh venv from this branch: `AgenticAI` 193 passed (including Postgres tests), `AgenticLab` 68 passed
- [x] Compose file validates; the service image builds and reviews a synthetic submission end to end (fake models)

author: tolunayozturk
body:
This PR fixes two problems that an agent test against the live 1.3.0 deployment found.

## MCP fetch tool

`SKILL.md` tells agents to name a page with the `/consumer/{en|cn}/doc/<catalog>/<path>` prefix. `fetchHarmonyOSDocumentation` rejected this form, and also the Huawei URL, with "Unsupported HarmonyOS documentation path". It accepted only `<catalog>/<path>`. The problem started in July.

The tool now accepts all three forms for every catalog. A URL or a `/consumer` path sets the language. With `<catalog>/<path>`, the `language` argument sets it. The CLI and the MCP tool now use one parser for this input. The CLI rules do not change.

## Document ETag

Huawei signs each image URL again on every request (`HW-CC-Date`, `HW-CC-Sign`). A page with images therefore had different bytes and a different ETag on each fetch, so conditional requests did not work for these pages. The ETag now leaves out the signature and the time of signing. It keeps the day of signing, because the image links expire one day after signing. Thus the ETag stays the same on one day and changes when a saved copy can have expired links. The ETag is weak, because equal tags mean the same content, not the same bytes.

## Tests

`tests/document-requests.test.ts` calls the MCP tool with each form for each catalog, against an intercepted Huawei API. It also fetches one page four times: twice with the image signatures from the live bug, once with changed text, and once with a signature from the next day. The agent check against a local Worker and the real Huawei API also passes.

author: xe-nvdk
body:
Fixes #1152.

## Summary

- `POST /api/v1/compaction/trigger` ran a full compaction cycle on **whatever node received it**. It consulted the cluster-wide pause and this process's own running-cycle flag, and nothing else — not the node role, not the compactor lease. Only the *scheduled* cycles ever consulted the gate (`internal/compaction/scheduler.go:205`), and `compaction.enabled` defaults to **true**, so every node in a cluster built a compaction manager and served a live, unguarded trigger.
- The trigger now consults **the same gate value the schedulers hold**, re-read per request so a lease hand-over or a demotion takes effect without a restart.
- A node that may not compact answers **503** with `role`, `can_compact: false` and `lease_holder`.

### Why it corrupts, and why it needs no second node

The partition lock is a per-process map (`internal/compaction/manager.go`), so a trigger on a non-lease node can select the same partition as the lease holder and delete the same inputs.

With `cluster.replication_enabled` on it is worse, from a **single** request: `completionDir` is set on every role, so `Job.clusterMode()` is true and `deleteOldFiles` runs unconditionally — but the completion-manifest watcher, which issues `RegisterFile` for the output and `DeleteFile` for the sources, starts only `if capabilities.CanCompact || IsActiveCompactor()` (`cmd/arc/main.go`). So the sources leave storage while nothing records either the new output or the deletions: phantom manifest entries plus an orphan output, which nothing re-registers and an enabled reconciliation sweep then deletes.

### Design notes

**Two interface variables over one gate pointer.** The schedulers take `compaction.ClusterGate`; the handler takes `api.CompactionGate`, which adds `LeaseHolder()` so a refusal can name the holder. Both are assigned from the same pointer, so the manual and scheduled paths cannot disagree, and `setCoordinator` upgrades both to lease mode at once. **Both must stay interface variables** — declaring either as `*compactionClusterGate` would hand OSS a non-nil interface wrapping a nil pointer, which passes the handler's nil check and then panics in `CanCompact`. That is the #713 shape, and `TestCompactionGateNilInterfaceConversionIssue1152` pins it, typed-nil counter-example included.

**The refusal distinguishes the two reasons `CanCompact()` is false**, because the remedies differ:

| State | Message |
|---|---|
| Lease held elsewhere | names the holder, points at `POST /api/v1/cluster/compactor/assign` |
| No lease at all (**the default**, `cluster.failover_enabled=false`) | says the static role refused; does **not** recommend `assign` |

That second row was a real bug in the first draft of this fix: `assign` answers `this cluster does not manage a compactor lease` in exactly the state the message described, so it sent the operator to an endpoint that refuses. Verified live (below).

**503, not 409.** This endpoint already answers 409 for a paused cluster and for a running cycle, and arcli maps *any* 409 here to "a compaction cycle is already running (cycle N)" reading only `cycle_id` — a role rejection has none, so it would print "cycle 0". `backup_routes.go` and `delete.go` chose 503 over 409 for the same overload. The remedy rides in the `error` field because arcli renders `error` and discards `message`.

## Configuration matrix

`compactionGate`/`compactionAPIGate` are non-nil iff `cfg.Cluster.Enabled`. `setCoordinator` — what switches `CanCompact()` from static role to FSM lease — runs only when all five hold: cluster enabled, `licenseClient != nil`, license has `FeatureClustering`, coordinator constructed, `Start()` succeeded.

| Configuration | Reaches new code? | Result | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| OSS standalone, no cluster (**the default everyone runs**) | no — gate is a nil interface | unchanged | **live, twice** (200, cycle ran) |
| Cluster, `role=writer`, lease elsewhere | yes | reject | **live** (503, 4/4 body fields) |
| Cluster, `role=writer`, **holds** lease | yes | allow | **live** (200) |
| Cluster, `role=reader` | yes | reject | **live** (503) |
| Cluster, `role=compactor`, holds lease | yes | allow | **live** (200, cycle 1) |
| Cluster, `role=compactor`, lease elsewhere (standby) | yes | reject | **live** (503, `role: "compactor"`) |
| Failover off, `role=compactor`/`standalone` | yes | allow (static) | **live** (200) |
| Failover off, `role=writer`/`reader` | yes | **reject** (static) | **live** (503) |
| Cluster configured, license missing | yes | reject on writer+reader | traced; deliberate, in release notes |
| Corpse lease | yes | reject everywhere | traced; `assign` is the lever, in release notes |
| **Default `cluster.role` (all standalone)** | yes | **still allows every node** | **#892, not closed here** |
| **2× `role=compactor`, failover off** | yes | **both still allow** | documented; enable failover |

The last two rows are honest gaps, stated in the release notes rather than papered over. A writer *holding* the lease is correctly allowed — `canHoldCompactorLease` includes writers and failover deliberately falls back to one.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./cmd/... ./internal/...`, `gofmt -l`, `go vet` — clean
- [x] `go test ./internal/api/ ./internal/compaction/ ./internal/storage/` — green **after rebase onto #969** (PR #1158 landed mid-work and touches `compaction/job.go` + `storage/`)
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/api/` — green
- [x] 8 new tests, **no skips**; mutation-tested by disabling the gate call: 3 fail. The 2 survivors are the rows that assert *unchanged* behaviour (nil gate, read routes), so no test passes on a wrongly wired gate
- [x] Per-request evaluation proven by flip test, and again live: the same handler answered 200 then 503 purely because the lease moved — no restart
- [x] **OSS binary run** (required, touches `cmd/arc/main.go`): clean start, `POST /trigger` → 200 + cycle. Re-run after the `main.go` change
- [x] **5-node enterprise cluster**, replication on, failover **on**: all six lease rows, including moving the lease to a writer and re-testing with no restart
- [x] **5-node enterprise cluster**, failover **off**: the no-lease wording, with the precondition capturing the bug one line above the fix — `assign` returning `this cluster does not manage a compactor lease` next to a refusal that no longer recommends it
- [x] Preconditions established before every verdict: license tier active, cluster formed, lease holder identified, and the writer's `/compaction/stats` returning 200 so a 503 cannot be mistaken for "not initialized"

Harnesses: `cluster-1152-lease-gate.sh`, `cluster-1152-nolease-wording.sh`.

## Out of scope

- **#1153** — the predicted `cycle_id` and the non-atomic `IsCycleRunning()` pre-check, three lines from this edit, deliberately untouched.
- **#892** — a default-role cluster is all-`standalone`, which cannot hold the lease, so the static capability allows every node. The invariant this PR preserves is that the trigger and the scheduler agree; #892 moves both.
- A cluster-wide partition lock. The per-process lock is *why* the gate matters; replacing it is a much larger change.
- arcli could give the 503 a dedicated message instead of rendering `error` generically.

author: sdcarlson
body:
Follow-up review of #60 (Plate IX · Living ink) through four lenses: thermo-nuclear code quality, ponytail, Karpathy guidelines, Elon principles, plus a correctness pass and the kit/v2 rules. Only `src/site/sketch-plate.js` changes. The look is unchanged.

## Changes
| # | Lens | Change | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | correctness, Elon (delete the part) | Removed the `gTrunk` growth term. Trunk and rings now always use the full stroke. | A newly committed stroke started at age 0, so `ease(0)=0` cut the trunk to 2 points. The stroke you (or the ghost) had just inked vanished and regrew over about 0.9 s. Every committed stroke was already shown in full while inked, and seeds start grown, so this glitch was the term's only visible effect. Rings start at 0.35·GROW, when the term was already 1, so ring growth is unchanged. Measured bright trunk pixels across mouse-up: before 7190 → 5626; after 7251 → 7242. |
| 2 | correctness | Reduced motion: `up` draws after `live` is cleared. | Before, `commit()` drew while `live` was still set, so the newest stroke was inked twice (additive blend). With no next frame in reduced mode, it stayed overbright. Bright pixels after release: 13971 → 9914, which matches the animated look. |
| 3 | thermo, ponytail | One `ghost = { pts, t0 }` object. `frame()` computes the inked slice and passes it to `draw(now, inking = live)`. | Before, ghost state was split across `ghost` and `ghostLive`, plus an unused `ghost.i`, and cleared in three places. |
| 4 | thermo | Pruning of dying strokes moved from `draw()` to `frame()`. | `draw()` is now pure rendering. Time advances in `frame()`. |
| 5 | thermo | One `hue` variable holds the next stroke's hue. | Before, `hue0 + 47` was computed in both `commit` and `draw`. |
| 6 | thermo | Dying: `strokes.slice(0, -MAX).forEach(s => s.dying ??= born)`. Reduced mode uses `slice(-MAX)`. | Removes the single-index `strokes[len - MAX - 1]` arithmetic and the reduced-mode `born = -1e9` / filter step. |
| 7 | ponytail | `commit(raw, born)` with `GROWN = -Infinity`. | Replaces the seed loop that overwrote `born` after each commit, and the extra `draw` calls. |
| 8 | ponytail | Removed dead code: stroke `seed` and `fade`, the live stroke's `nrm`/lazy `normals()`, `path`'s `append` flag, `ring`'s `upto`, and the `raw[0] \|\| [0.2,0]` fallback. | None of these were read. |

## Rejected
- Deleting `.home-sketch__copy h2 em` as a duplicate of kit `.sy-display em`: it is not a duplicate. `src/syberlabs.css` animates `.sy-display em` at `background-size: 220%`, and this rule pins the full static spectrum. Deleting it changed the heading in screenshots, so I reverted it.
- Kit rule 2 (canvas `pointer-events:none`): this plate is meant to be drawn on. It stays `aria-hidden`, and no copy sits on it.
- Dropping the IntersectionObserver/ResizeObserver feature checks: they follow the same convention as `site.js`.
- Unmount race on the dynamic import: already guarded by `canvas.current`, and the site does not use StrictMode.
- Bucketing sprouts by generation, and `getBoundingClientRect` vs `clientWidth` in `size()`: cosmetic.

Round 2 re-review found only cosmetic items, so ponytail says lean already.

## Net
`sketch-plate.js`: +42 / −46 (**net −4 lines**), with 3 fewer pieces of state (`ghostLive`, `hue0`, `gTrunk`) and 2 glitches fixed.

## Checks
- `corepack pnpm build:site`: ok
- `node scripts/site-chrome.mjs --check`: 11 pages up to date
- `node scripts/qa.mjs`: 17 pages, 0 errors, 0 warnings

## Screenshots (puppeteer-core, Chrome, `--disable-accelerated-2d-canvas`)
I captured `#sketch` idle, just after release, and 3 s after a mouse drag, at desktop 1440×900, phone 390×844 and desktop with reduced motion. I compared them with https://syberlabs.io/#sketch:
- Idle and drawn plates match production: the same mandala, sprouts, rings, conic ring and heading spectrum.
- Reduced motion gives a still, inked frame. The new stroke is drawn grown at normal brightness instead of doubled.
- No console errors in any run.

author: moss-orbit-9f339e
body:
Every terraform update ran ChangeTextureBlock for each block, and DrawGenesis made one `gl.RenderToTexture` call per changed 8×8 block. This change makes the bookkeeping cheaper and uses one render call per square.

**Why:** ChangeTextureBlock was 0.4% of the main thread at maximum replay speed. The harness shows 82% fewer RenderToTexture calls. No in-game FPS number.

**Behaviour:** No visible change. The output and the bookkeeping state are the same.

**Testing:**
- In-game: a replay of a ~1000-unit game at full graphics, on Zero-K master `1dd7cb0d7`. No Lua errors. Simulation checksums and unit counts are the same as master. The screenshot is the same as master. Limit: the replay terraforms during the window (7 terraform orders), but not inside the camera view, so the texture updates ran without being seen.

**Related:** ZeroK-RTS/Zero-K#4889 (this does not do the redesign)

**AI disclosure:** Claude Code wrote this change and its tests. I reviewed the change. The in-game tests ran automatically on Windows with an RTX 3080.

author: wedeueis
body:
Closes **#69**.

## The gap

`SceneManager` had two lifetimes and needed a third. `push_scene` keeps what is
beneath alive, but `switch_to` unwinds the whole stack — so a run-wide HUD,
minimap or status overlay had to be torn down and re-pushed on every floor
transition, losing its state each time.

A roguelike floor change is *"swap the world scene, keep the HUD"*, and that
was the one thing the manager could not express.

```python
manager.add_layer("hud")
manager.switch_to("floor2")   # the stack unwinds; the HUD does not
```

A layer lives **outside** `_stack`, which is the whole mechanism: `switch_to`
unwinds the stack, so something not in it is untouched. `remove_layer` goes
through `_exit_scene`, the one teardown path, so a layer gets exactly what any
other scene gets — `on_exit`, teardown callbacks, owner-scoped subscriptions,
coroutines, systems, DI scope.

## The decisions that were not forced

**Layers render above the whole stack, in `order` then insertion order.** One
rule rather than interleaving them with pushed scenes: a modal that must cover
the HUD is a layer with a higher order, not a stack push. Insertion breaks ties,
which is the only non-arbitrary answer for two layers at the same order.

**Above an in-flight transition, too.** A persistent HUD that blinks out during
every floor change defeats the point of persisting it. A game that wants one
covered by the fade can remove it for the duration — the inverse is not
available if the transition always wins.

**They keep updating during a transition**, when the stack does not, so a
layer's own animations do not freeze mid-fade.

**`pause_below` does not reach a layer in either direction.** A layer neither
pauses the stack nor is paused by it. Freezing the HUD behind a pause menu is
`pause_layer()` — explicit, because a HUD that keeps animating while paused is
just as often what a game wants. A paused layer still renders: pausing stops
its updates, not its pixels.

**One scene cannot be in the stack and be a layer.** Each would enter and exit
it independently, so `add_layer`, `switch_to` and `push_scene` all raise rather
than allowing it — a double `on_exit` on a shared scene is a bug that surfaces
nowhere near its cause.

## Smaller details

`cleanup()` exits layers first, since LIFO means the thing drawing on top goes
first. The `previous_position` snapshot moved into `_snapshot_interpolated()` so
layers get it without the loop being written twice.

## Verification

Verified in a clean detached worktree at `b6a7726`:

- ruff: pass
- mypy: 329 source files, clean
- **4585 passed**, 1 skipped (+22)
- `games/validate_demos.py`: all PASSED

Removing the layer render and update loops fails 7 of the new tests, so they
are load-bearing rather than asserting the absence of a feature.

Closes #69.

author: supernovaia
body:
## What

**Dark theme**
- Base raised from 16 % to 22 % lightness. Surfaces, rules and secondary text move with it.
- Body text eased from 95 % to 92 % to cut glare (13.6:1).
- Secondary text set to 86 %, so it stays distinct from body text.
- Every text pair re-checked for WCAG AA. Body is 13.6:1, control borders 4:1.

**Article reading** (from a readability audit)
- Phones (≤ 720 px): body goes from 20 px to 18 px with line-height 1.65. That takes lines from about 33 to 37 characters.
- Phones only: hyphenation, using `lang="es"`. Headings, code and tables never break words.
- Bold goes from 600 to 550, so posts with a lot of bold don't spot the page.
- Lists are tighter inside an item (1.55) than between items (0.75em), so a wrapped line stays with its item.

Justified text was tested and rejected. On phones it opened wide gaps between words; on desktop it stretched lines even with hyphenation.

Light theme and the desktop article layout are unchanged.

## Check
Open any article in dark mode, on desktop and on a phone.

author: cccs-mdr
body:
This PR adds elasticsearch scroll support to the Howler API and Client.

---

This pull request introduces support for Elasticsearch scroll context management in the search API, enabling clients to control deep paging sessions more robustly. It adds a new endpoint to clear scroll contexts, allows clients to specify custom scroll keep-alive durations, and ensures field-level security for user searches during scrolling. Comprehensive tests are included to validate the new functionality and error handling.

**Elasticsearch scroll context management:**

* Added a new `/api/v1/search/scroll` DELETE endpoint to allow clients to explicitly clear Elasticsearch scroll contexts, with proper error handling and response propagation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-681915e05cf4c2813589199b8ddfa7b1ed32cc7a3bf9855de38a0ac6f297ec53R36-R110) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-96f5dcf3dbe27f94b68dbc024feed149b8c2c3b27c1386afedbb9b7757646b5cR231-R244)
* The search API now supports a `scroll` parameter for deep paging, allowing clients to specify the scroll keep-alive duration, which is passed through to Elasticsearch for both opening and advancing scrolls. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-681915e05cf4c2813589199b8ddfa7b1ed32cc7a3bf9855de38a0ac6f297ec53R125) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-681915e05cf4c2813589199b8ddfa7b1ed32cc7a3bf9855de38a0ac6f297ec53R143) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-681915e05cf4c2813589199b8ddfa7b1ed32cc7a3bf9855de38a0ac6f297ec53R168-R177) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-96f5dcf3dbe27f94b68dbc024feed149b8c2c3b27c1386afedbb9b7757646b5cR80-R81) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-96f5dcf3dbe27f94b68dbc024feed149b8c2c3b27c1386afedbb9b7757646b5cR91-R92) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-96f5dcf3dbe27f94b68dbc024feed149b8c2c3b27c1386afedbb9b7757646b5cL156-R166) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-d12cb37c70d47bc80d94f7a53ad5f003fad8c476650c69d50e4524559257ee36L762-R847)

**Field-level security improvements:**

* Implemented logic to safely select and prune user fields returned during scroll-based user searches, ensuring sensitive fields (e.g., passwords, API keys) are never exposed, even when using wildcards or lists in the `fl` parameter. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-681915e05cf4c2813589199b8ddfa7b1ed32cc7a3bf9855de38a0ac6f297ec53R36-R110) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-681915e05cf4c2813589199b8ddfa7b1ed32cc7a3bf9855de38a0ac6f297ec53R196-R220) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-96f5dcf3dbe27f94b68dbc024feed149b8c2c3b27c1386afedbb9b7757646b5cL32-R34) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-96f5dcf3dbe27f94b68dbc024feed149b8c2c3b27c1386afedbb9b7757646b5cL47-R49) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-96f5dcf3dbe27f94b68dbc024feed149b8c2c3b27c1386afedbb9b7757646b5cR58-R61)

**Testing and client updates:**

* Added integration and unit tests covering scroll keep-alive handling, field-level security during scrolling, and the clear scroll endpoint, including error scenarios. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6e060af9907c48422df0e89f528dca4b2a1837cf25264f9201fb813bc2d793fbR73-R201) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d12cb37c70d47bc80d94f7a53ad5f003fad8c476650c69d50e4524559257ee36L762-R847)
* Updated the client library to expose the new scroll functionality via the `Scroll` class. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-edd7bb819c6a52834e4ea3d68cca870098035ca9ca965379520cbad7aded7666R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-edd7bb819c6a52834e4ea3d68cca870098035ca9ca965379520cbad7aded7666R22)

author: pylaterreur
body:
Removing the first WAN's path through the control API, which is what OpenMPTCProuter's `005-mqvpn-path` does when that WAN fails, tears the whole tunnel down and reconnects. Abandoning that path like any other keeps the tunnel up. Two WANs (4 Mbit/s, 20 ms each way), a TCP upload and a 20 Hz ping through the tunnel, netns testbed in a VM:

| event on the first WAN | `dev` (22b2c5f) | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `remove_path` through the control API | 6.5 s and 6.5 s, a reconnect each time | 0.4 s and 0.3 s, no reconnect |
| silent failure, then `remove_path` 3 s later (omr-tracker's sequence) | 6.3 s and 9.9 s, a reconnect each time | 5.5 s and 4.0 s, no reconnect; 0.9 s and 0.2 s with Ysurac/xquic#1 applied too |
| carrier loss (the platform drop, which already abandons path 0) | 0.3 s and 0.4 s, no reconnect | 0.3 s and 0.3 s, no reconnect |

Longest interval without a ping reply, and reconnects; two rounds per case, QEMU without KVM. After the `remove_path`, the TCP upload stayed below half its rate for 11.5 s and 9.5 s on `dev`, 5.5 s and 2.0 s with this PR.

### Mechanism

`mqvpn_client_remove_path()` closes the whole connection (`xqc_h3_conn_close()`) when the removed path carries xquic `path_id` 0, the path the connection was opened on; `tick_reconnect()` then rebuilds it over another path after `ReconnectInterval`. This special case came with `4761c5e` (May 2026, for Ysurac/openmptcprouter#4271 and Ysurac/openmptcprouter#4273), whose message describes a ~15 s stall of datagrams on the remaining paths after `xqc_conn_close_path(path_id=0)`. On the current `dev` that stall does not happen:

- `mqvpn_client_on_platform_path_dropped()` (carrier loss, link deletion) already abandons path 0 with `xqc_conn_close_path()` like any other path, and the tunnel keeps running (table above);
- with this PR, `remove_path` of path 0 does the same, with no stall (table above, and the e2e tests below);
- upstream (mp0rta/mqvpn `main`) abandons path 0 on `remove_path` as well.

This PR abandons path 0 like the other paths and closes the connection only when xquic refuses the abandon (for example on the last active path), which is the only case where `initial_path_removed` is still needed. `025fef0` (#1) made the reconnect after removing the initial path use a live path; that rotation still covers the reconnects that remain (server restart, idle timeout, a refused abandon). Its e2e test, `run_primary_removal_test.sh`, now expects the tunnel to stay up over the other path without a reconnect. In `test_api`, `get_send_handle_skips_removed_primary_with_xqc_path_id_zero` becomes `remove_initial_path_keeps_drop_window_semantics`: during the drop window, a send for path_id 0 now resolves to the dropped slot, exactly as for a removed secondary path, which the test checks side by side.

The remaining few seconds when the WAN fails silently before it is removed come from xquic, which keeps sending on a path that has stopped answering; Ysurac/xquic#1 fixes that, so this is best merged together with it or after it.

- RFC or draft: Not applicable (PATH_ABANDON of path 0, as the platform drop already sends)

Refs #1

### Validation Cases

- `scripts/ci_e2e/run_primary_removal_test.sh` (as updated here), in a VM: `dev` FAIL (`removing the initial path tore the connection down`; the client logs `removing initial path (path_id=0 ...): closing connection` and then reconnects); this PR PASS for both cases (two paths; path plus backup path).
- `run_path_api_test.sh` (removes the initial path through the API) and `run_path_bounce_test.sh`: PASS. In the first, `tunnel ping works after removing path A` after 5 s on `dev` (the reconnect) and after 0 s with this PR.
- Connection-lifecycle suite from CONTRIBUTING.md, run in the same VM on an ASan/UBSan build of `dev` with every PR of this series merged (and the xquic fixes): `run_dellink_test.sh`, `run_8paths_dellink_test.sh`, `run_carrier_flap_test.sh`, `run_addr_del_failover_test.sh`, `run_admin_down_test.sh`, `run_validation_blackhole_test.sh` and `run_route_gate_test.sh` PASS, no sanitizer report. `run_reconnect_test.sh` fails at its first ping on every build in that VM, plain `dev` included: it pings 3 s after starting the client, and the emulated VM (no KVM) needs longer to bring the tunnel up. `run_control_api_test.sh` gives the same result with and without the series (Release builds: phases b, f and h pass; a, c, d, e and g get empty control-API answers in that VM on plain `dev` too).
- Library client and server over loopback (two paths, 20 Mbit/s of 1300-byte datagrams, reconnect on), path 0 removed through the API 4 s into the run, 3 runs per direction: `dev` closes the connection and reconnects every time (download: no delivery for 5.10-5.15 s); this PR keeps the connection every time (longest gap between two deliveries 0.06-0.45 s upload, 0.14-0.21 s download).
- sanitizer `ctest`: 57/57.

### Compatibility surfaces

- [x] Connection lifecycle
- [x] Log wording: the INFO line `removing initial path (path_id=0 iface=...): closing connection for clean failover to secondary` is gone (no test matched it besides `run_primary_removal_test.sh`, updated here); the WARN for a refused abandon now also covers path 0.

author: bhargavikvmpl-2001
body:
<!-- If you are new to contributing or want a refresher, please read ./pull_request_guidance.md -->
**What changed?**
The ContinueAsNew decision validator (`validateContinueAsNewWorkflowExecutionAttributes` in `service/history/decision/checker.go`) now rejects a `RetryPolicy.JitterCoefficient` that is NaN, below 0 or above 1 with a `BadRequestError`, using the same message as `common.ValidateRetryPolicy`.

Fixes #8615

**Why?**
`JitterCoefficient` was added to `RetryPolicy` in #8583 / #8604, and `ValidateRetryPolicy` rejects out-of-range values. ScheduleActivityTask, StartChildWorkflow and the frontend/history start paths all call it, but the ContinueAsNew decision never validated `RetryPolicy`, so an invalid coefficient on a client-issued ContinueAsNew was accepted and persisted on the new run's started event and mutable state.

The retry-storm concern from the issue is already prevented at runtime: `getBackoffInterval` only applies jitter when `0 < jitterCoefficient <= 1` (covered by the "jitter greater than 1 is ignored" case in `TestGetBackoffIntervalWithJitter`). This change closes the remaining gap so the decision path is consistent with the other entry points.

Only the jitter coefficient is checked, not the full `ValidateRetryPolicy`. Calling the full validator would enforce its other rules (e.g. `InitialIntervalInSeconds > 0`, `MaximumAttempts` or `ExpirationIntervalInSeconds` set) on ContinueAsNew for the first time and could start failing workflows whose decisions are accepted today. Happy to switch to full validation if maintainers prefer (question raised on #8615).

**How did you test it?**
Added a table test, `TestValidateContinueAsNewWorkflowExecutionAttributes_RetryPolicyJitterCoefficient`, covering: nil policy, jitter 0, 0.5 and 1 (accepted); jitter 5, -0.1 and NaN (rejected); and a policy that full `ValidateRetryPolicy` would reject but with a valid jitter (still accepted, so existing decisions behave the same).

```
go test -race -v ./service/history/decision/ -run TestValidateContinueAsNewWorkflowExecutionAttributes
go test -race ./service/history/decision/...
make .idl-status
make pr
make build
make test
```
All pass locally with Go 1.25.14, and `make pr` leaves no diff.

**Potential risks**
Low. No API/IDL, schema or dynamic config changes. The only behaviour change is that a ContinueAsNew decision carrying an out-of-range `JitterCoefficient` now fails with a `BadRequestError` instead of being persisted. Valid and unset coefficients behave exactly as before, and the other `RetryPolicy` fields are not newly enforced. Rollback is a plain revert.

**Release notes**
ContinueAsNew decisions now reject a retry policy `JitterCoefficient` that is NaN or outside [0, 1], matching ScheduleActivityTask, StartChildWorkflow and StartWorkflowExecution. (#8615)

**Documentation Changes**
N/A

author: awu05
body:
Follow-up to #18, from new `stream-diag` logs on a Flussonic portal server (segment names like `…/2026/10/08/20/42/14-06474.ts`).

**What the logs showed**
- At a restart, `MEDIA-SEQUENCE` jumps ~10 ahead with no new content ("source moved 13 segments ahead in 5.9s", then "skipped … 9 missed", which were numbers that never had files).
- After the break, new files re-cover content already listed: 20:42:03 and 20:42:09 were listed after 20:42:14, about 17 s of replay. PTS also jumped back 14–23 s.
- The old 20:42:14 file then 404s, so the player retried it 4× (the 502s).

#18 judged segments by the source's sequence numbers and only the segment right after a discontinuity, so it couldn't catch any of this.

**Fix** (`lib/restartSmoother.js`)
- Players get their own numbering: a new segment (by path) gets the next number the first time it's seen and keeps it. Renumbering upstream changes nothing for players.
- A new segment that mostly repeats content up to the end of the newest kept one is left out.
- Start times come from the time-based name when present (one clock across restarts); otherwise from PTS after a discontinuity, as in #18.
- Guards:
  - a clock more than 60 s back counts as a new clock;
  - at most 45 s left out in a row, then resync with a discontinuity;
  - a repeats-only window keeps the last playlist;
  - a hole starts the window after it;
  - BYTERANGE and LL-HLS pass through.
- Discontinuities go in our own `EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY-SEQUENCE`. Unchanged playlists still pass through byte for byte.

**Tests**: 7 new smoother tests, including the exact renumber + re-cut sequence from the logs. All 181 backend tests pass. An end-to-end run through the real proxy against a mock Flussonic source that restarts with a renumber and an 11 s re-cut gives a player timeline with no replay and no numbering jump: `41:36 → 41:42 → 41:49 → 41:55`. The #18 timestamp-based scenario still passes end to end.

691 H&E-stained lung histology images (1200x1600 px, 20x or 40x) from 45 surgical patients, taken with a microscope camera, labelled as normal lung, adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, each tumour type further graded as well, moderately or poorly differentiated (seven classes). An accompanying CSV links each image to its anonymized patient ID.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Modality** | brightfield |
| **Dimensionality** | 2D images · channels: 3 |
| **Voxel / pixel size** | unknown |
| **Data format** | jpeg |
| **Size** | 670.4 MB (confirmed from a complete file listing) · 691 images/volumes |
| **Sample** | Homo sapiens · H&E-stained lung tissue (normal, adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma) from 45 surgical patients, Hospital Clínico de Valladolid |
| **Annotations** | classification · dense coverage · manual · format: seven-class image labels (per paper; patient-ID CSV alongside) |
| **ML tasks** | classification · splits provided: no |
| **Access / license** | open · CC-BY-4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) |
| **Hosted at** | Figshare 25459174 · DOI [10.6084/m9.figshare.25459174](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.25459174) |

**Notes:** Figshare lists one file, LungHist700.rar (670 MB); a RAR cannot be listed with peek_archive, so the JPEG format, 691 images and the patient-ID CSV come from the paper (Data Records) and the figshare description. Classes (7): normal, and adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma each with well, moderately and poorly differentiated grades. Images are camera photos (Leica DM2000 with ICC50 W camera) of selected fields, not whole-slide scans; they come from surgical patients, so normal areas are from cancer patients. Pixel size is not stated on the figshare page or in the paper. The paper trains with an 80/10/10 patient-wise split, but no split is released as files that were seen. Classification labels only, no pixel annotations. enricher: RAR block headers at the start of the archive show data/data.csv and data/images/aca_bd/aca_bd_20x_<n>.jpg (class folder, magnification in the name).

| raw | `data/images/*/*.jpg` · jpeg | ? (axes not stated) | unknown | jpeg | — | — | not-applicable |
| label | `data/data.csv` · csv | ? (axes not stated) | unknown | none | — | other | not-applicable: Image-level class from the class folder name (data/images/<class>/, e.g. aca_bd); data.csv links each image to its patient ID (paper, Data Records). |

author: jeremy
body:
Running a subcommand from the command line never told anyone which subcommand it was. `kamal app boot` gave its hooks `KAMAL_COMMAND=app` and no `KAMAL_SUBCOMMAND`, and an output logger named its file `…_app.log` rather than `…_app_boot.log`. The OTel logger's command was `app` as well.

`subcommand` looked only at the first invocation Thor recorded. Run through Main, that's Main's own `app`, which dispatches to App's `boot`, so the subcommand always came out nil. The tests didn't notice because they call `Kamal::Cli::App.start` directly, where App's invocation is the first one.

When the first invocation is Main running a subcommand, this looks up that subcommand class's own first invocation instead. Top-level commands are unchanged: `kamal deploy` still has no subcommand, even though it invokes `app boot` along the way, and `kamal proxy reboot` is still `proxy reboot` through the `app boot` it invokes. The lookup doesn't add an entry to Thor's invocations hash, so it can't affect the `invoke` bookkeeping that `reset_invocation` relies on.

The new test runs `kamal app boot` through `Main.start` and checks both the hook's environment and the `modify.kamal` payload the output loggers name their files from. It fails on main (`{"KAMAL_COMMAND" => "app"}`).

Unit suite: 861 runs. The only failures are the 7 that also fail on main without a Docker builder (CliBuildTest ×4, CommandsBuilderTest ×2, ConfigurationBuilderTest ×1). RuboCop is clean.

author: 1devteam
body:
## Purpose

First production refactor driven from the Ajenda ASCII v2 graph as the primary architectural map.

ASCII v2 identified `backend/api/routes/mission.py` as a high-pressure boundary:
- 39 outbound production imports
- 60 neighboring source files
- 20 direct test relationships
- only one production importer: `backend/api/router.py`

Targeted source verification then showed the critical compatibility constraint: many tests patch runtime/repository dependencies directly at `backend.api.routes.mission.*`.

## Change

Extract the declarative API contract layer from the route monolith without moving runtime behavior:

- move all 51 Pydantic request/response/read-model classes verbatim to `backend/api/routes/mission_contracts.py`
- move the two pure normalization helpers used only by those validators
- keep all 34 route handlers in `backend/api/routes/mission.py`
- keep every repository/service/runtime/queue dependency at its existing patchable module path
- re-export every moved contract name from `backend.api.routes.mission` so current imports remain valid

`mission.py` drops from 3,086 lines to 2,254 lines.

## Pre-CI invariants

Programmatic comparison against main:
- 51/51 moved class bodies are byte-for-byte identical
- 59/59 remaining top-level function bodies are unchanged
- 34/34 route decorators are unchanged
- no moved contract re-export is missing
- only two pure validator helpers intentionally leave the route module

## Research objective

This PR is also a practical GRAFT R&D proof: determine whether ASCII v2 contains enough structural information to select a safe, useful refactor boundary and accurately identify the source locations that require targeted verification.

If CI or runtime proof exposes a structural assumption we missed, do not weaken the gates; the PR can be closed and the miss becomes evidence for the ASCII/GRAFT map.

## Observed post-refactor result

All required workflows on head `f944e4b6aff7e5f4c099cf93cbe3608398ae1ed2` are green:

- CI — Pull Request Gate
- Architecture — Canonical Dependency Graph
- Architecture — PR Invariant Classifier
- Architecture — Selective Proof Shadow
- Architecture — GRAFT Runtime Contract Adjudication
- Recovery Hardening Validation
- Security — Vulnerability Scanning
- Pre-Merge Live Runtime Proof

The regenerated graph is 1,643 nodes / 4,709 edges versus the ASCII-v2 baseline of 1,642 nodes / 4,706 edges.

The structural delta is intentionally small:
- add `backend/api/routes/mission_contracts.py`
- move the mission -> compliance dependency through the contract module
- preserve all 20 direct mission test relationships
- preserve all runtime/service/repository route dependencies

Important: this pass reduces responsibility/LOC, **not dependency blast radius**. The mission route source remains the operational hub because all 34 handlers stay in place. That is a result, not a hidden limitation: the next blast-radius reduction must move an actual route responsibility cluster after this preparatory cut.

## ASCII-v2 interpretation result

ASCII v2 was sufficient to:
- identify `mission.py` as a high-pressure module;
- identify its single production importer;
- enumerate the direct test neighborhood that required verification;
- bound the source inspection needed before editing.

Targeted source inspection was still required to discover the exact patch seams inside those tests. No canonical JSON was required to choose the refactor boundary.

author: justinmaurerdotdev
body:
## Summary
packages.reason.com now also works as a read-only Composer repository for `reason-dev/*` packages. It serves `/packages.json`, `/p2/reason-dev/<slug>.json` and `/dist/reason-dev/<slug>/<slug>-<version>.zip`, all behind `SIMPLE_UPDATE_KEY` sent as a Bearer header. The existing update-checker route that legacy WordPress sites use is unchanged.

## Why
No Asana task.

vnext sites install Reason plugins with Composer, so they need a Composer repository. `wp-site-template` (`docs/plugin-distribution.md`) and `reason-edge-delivery` already document this branch as the canonical distribution mechanism (see `docs/plans/2026-10-06-composer-routes-review.md`). The longer it sits unmerged, the more those downstream docs can drift from what is deployed.

## Changes
- `includes/Wpup/ComposerRepository.php` adds a router with no side effects. It takes a path and headers and returns a response, or `null` for paths it doesn't own. It only reads S3.
  - It serves only the `reason-dev` vendor, and never serves `meta/`.
  - It reads the key only from `Authorization: Bearer` (the scheme name is case-insensitive) and never from `?key=`.
  - If the key is empty, it returns `503`, so a stage with no key is never an open repository.
  - It rejects bad slugs, bad versions, path traversal and dist filenames that don't match their slug with `404`, before making any S3 call.
  - A download redirects (`302`) to a presigned S3 URL that expires after 15 minutes.
  - An S3 error other than not-found (for example access denied) returns `500` with a log line, not `404`.
- `includes/Wpup/ComposerResponse.php` adds the response value object.
- `includes/composer-routing.php` and `index.php` try the Composer routes first. Otherwise `Wpup_Request` would read `p2`, `dist` and so on as plugin slugs. Every other request falls through to `Wpup_LambdaS3UpdateServer` exactly as before. `index.php` keeps calling `Wpup_LambdaS3UpdateServer::guessServerUrl()`.
- `loader.php` loads the two new classes.
- `serverless.yml`:
  - Keeps tests, docs and IDE folders out of the Lambda package.
  - Corrects the `SIMPLE_UPDATE_KEY` comment: set the key with `aws ssm put-parameter` at the exact path the deploy reads, because `bref secret:create` doesn't document where it writes.
- `tests/check.php`, `tests/composer-repository-test.php` and `tests/index-routing-test.php` are plain-PHP tests. They use the AWS SDK's `MockHandler`, so they need no S3 access.
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs the tests on PHP 8.4 for every pull request and every push to master.
- `tests/acceptance/composer-smoke.sh` is an end-to-end smoke test for a deployed stage. It uploads a throwaway `reason-dev/wpup-smoke` package, runs `composer install` with Bearer auth, checks the lockfile, and checks that a key sent in the query string is refused.
- `docs/runbook.md` covers the routes, the append-only storage rule (and its one exception, the smoke package), and how to rotate the key.
- `docs/plans/` holds the implementation plan and the downstream review notes.

**Also in this PR: two commits that were on local `master` but never pushed.** `a9a456c` is a `composer update`. `555d9c7` builds an absolute `download_url` (without it, WordPress fails updates with "A valid URL was not provided"). This branch builds on `555d9c7`.

## Alternatives considered
- **Accept the key in `?key=` on Composer routes, as the update-checker route does.** Rejected: a key in a URL ends up in `composer.lock` files and access logs.
- **Leave the Composer routes open when no key is set, as the update-checker route is.** Rejected: a stage with a missing key would quietly become a public package repository. Failing closed with `503` is safer.
- **Add the Composer routes inside `Wpup_LambdaS3UpdateServer`.** Rejected: it would change the class that legacy sites depend on. A separate router that returns `null` for paths it doesn't own leaves that class untouched.

## Testing
- `php tests/composer-repository-test.php`: 37 checks, ALL PASSED (local PHP 8.5.11).
- `php tests/index-routing-test.php`: 5 checks, ALL PASSED.
- CI runs both on PHP 8.4, the Lambda runtime.
- `curl https://packages.reason.com/packages.json` returns `400` today. Production is still running master, which reads `packages.json` as a plugin slug.

**Not run as part of this PR:**
- The plan's dev-stage acceptance steps (Task 3, steps 2–4): deploy `dev`, run `composer-smoke.sh`, confirm the update-checker `download_url` is absolute. I couldn't confirm whether they ran, so treat them as outstanding.
- The production deploy and check (Task 4, steps 2–3).
- Negative controls were not re-run here.

## Not in this PR
- **Deploy order:** run the dev smoke test (plan Task 3) before the production deploy (plan Task 4). After the production deploy, `/packages.json` should return `503` until the key is enforced, or `401` once it is.
- **Before enforcing `SIMPLE_UPDATE_KEY` in production:** the plugin fleet pins a `wp-update-checker` that predates key support. Re-lock and release the fleet first, and run the plan's Task 0 pre-flight check on each legacy site. If a site's first-loaded checker predates key support, it sends no key and loses updates for every Reason plugin.
- **Follow-ups from the review notes:**
  - Write down the p2 "publish contract" in the runbook: package `name`, `type: wordpress-plugin`, `extra.installer-name`, a `require` list taken from the plugin's own `composer.json`, and dist zips with no `vendor/`. Do this before plan 2 builds the publish pipeline.
  - Mark `scripts/rebuild-composer-index.sh` in the runbook as "lands with plan 2". It doesn't exist in `reason-wp-repo-actions` yet.
  - Accept a second key (`SIMPLE_UPDATE_KEY_PREVIOUS`) during rotation, so rotating the key doesn't break the fleet for a window.
- The publish side (writing `p2/`, `dist/` and `meta/`) is plan 2, in `reason-wp-repo-actions`.

author: thesherwood
body:
Part of #2219: the binding rule recorded there, as its first PR.

A §14 child binds its import manifest **strictly**: an import that no grant satisfies refuses the spawn. That stays the default. This PR gives a parent a way to leave an import out on purpose, an **empty grant**, and makes a refusal say which import was unmet. Once self-spawns go (#2219 slice 3), every child binds strictly, and #1234's lenient same-module binding goes too. An empty grant is what replaces it.

## What changes

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Grant records (`temen-interp`) | `GRANT_EMPTY` (`0xC000_0000`) as a record's `handle` grants nothing under the record's name. The child's import of that name binds to an empty slot, which `CapFault`s on use, instead of refusing the spawn. The name may be the import's, `*` (every import nothing else satisfies), or a prefix ending in one `*` (`vm_jit_*`, `link.*`). Only an empty grant may carry a pattern, so a pattern never grants authority; a real handle under one, or a misplaced `*`, fails the spawn closed. |
| Precedence | A concrete grant beats an empty one, whatever the order. An empty grant fills only an import nothing else binds, and never unbinds one. |
| One step per record on every engine | `Host::can_grant_entry` (the check) and `Host::grant_entry_into_child` (the grant) replace the per-engine loops: the tree-walker's detached and carve arms, the bytecode engine's admission, and `spawn_child_powerbox`, which the Cranelift JIT, the named-child and exec builders and the browser's op-13 marshal use. |
| Durability | The child's name directory records an empty grant as `(name, GRANT_EMPTY)`. That directory is what a freeze captures and a fork copies, so the empty grant reaches a thaw's re-bind with no snapshot format change. The lookups that resolve a name to a handle skip it: `resolve_cap_name`, which backs `self.resolve`, plus `cap_label` and `cap_name_of_slot`. |
| Refusals name the import | A run's domains share a list of **notes** (`Host::take_notes`; a child's and a fork twin's host share their parent's). The binder notes the import it couldn't satisfy, since the guest only sees `-EINVAL`. `temen_run::Run` carries the notes, and the `temen-run` CLI prints them after the guest's stderr. |
| C | `VM_EMPTY` in `<temen.h>` and `posix_libc`'s `spawn.c`, with the rule beside the grant-record docs. |
| Docs | IMPORTS.md §3.3 gains the empty-grant row and the rule. |

## Decisions to review

1. **The tag lives in the `handle` field**, as #744's self-serve tag does. The record's `flags` word is documented as ignored, because the C shims and hand-built records leave it unzeroed. The value `0xC000_0000` has the `11` top bits of an `-errno`, but sits far outside that small range, so a parent passing a failed lookup by mistake still gets a refused spawn.
2. **Empty grants live in the child's name directory** rather than a new field. That's what lets them ride a fork and a freeze without a codec change. The cost is that every reader that maps a name to a handle has to skip them; there are three, and each now does.
3. **The browser doesn't show notes yet.** Its on-ramp builds outcomes in 29 places, and putting host notes into the guest's stderr would make interpreter and JIT outputs diverge in the differential tests. The playground will surface them when its cards spawn module children (#2219 slice 1), the first time a card can be refused this way.

## Tests

| Where | What | Engines |
|---|---|---|
| `temen-interp/tests/spawn_every_driver.rs` | On an op-17 record with a granted module: refused with no grant; admitted by an exact, a `*` or a prefix empty grant; still refused by a prefix that misses. An emptied import faults on use. A concrete grant wins in either order, and an empty grant under its own name doesn't unbind it. A pattern under a real handle, a `*` inside a name, and `**` fail closed. The refusal's note names the import, and an admitted spawn leaves none. | oracle, cooperative, parallel, debug scheduler, `Vcpu` |
| `temen-run/tests/detached_child_jit.rs` | The same admissions and refusals, and the same note, on the Cranelift JIT as on the tree-walker. | tree-walker, Cranelift |
| `temen/tests/durable_detached_thaw_guards.rs` | A child admitted only by an empty grant freezes and thaws. Without the directory capture, the thaw's strict re-bind refuses it. I checked that by filtering the empty entries out of the capture: the cells frozen on the interpreter then fail. | tree-walker, Cranelift, each pair through the codec |

## Verification

- `scripts/ci/local-gate.sh` passes on CI's toolchain (1.97.0): fmt, clippy, the stack-check lane and the excluded crates. The windows-gnu cross-check was skipped locally because there is no mingw.
- `cargo test`, before merging the latest main:
  - all of `temen-interp` (72 suites) and all of `temen-run` (42 suites);
  - in `temen`: `instantiate_record`, `durable_detached_thaw_guards`, `durable_detached_jit`, `c_fork`, `fork_manager`, `fork_import`, `unit_instantiator`, `child_jit_grant`, `instantiate_granted`, `lifecycle`, `jit_child_offer`, `pipe_cross_domain`, `instantiator_authority`, `domain_end_running_vcpus` and `jit_killpath`;
  - in the browser crate: `attenuation_cards`, `forth_asset`, `coop_tierup_driver`, `link_run`, `pg_libc_asset`, `exports_abi` and `onramp`.
- After merging main (#2217, #2218), which touched the driver harness: `spawn_every_driver` (39) and `detached_child_jit` (21) pass again.

body:
## What

`university.medicalstudent.ai` (SWA `univercity-dashboard`, deploys `prod`) is the production B2B dashboard. Every backend baked into its bundle is stopped since the 2026-10-08 cutover, so sign-in and everything after it fail:

| Backend | Before (stopped) | After (same PRODUCTION service on AWS) |
|---|---|---|
| IAM | `msa-api-iam.azurewebsites.net` (forwarder retired 2026-10-08 19:24 UTC) | `https://auth.medicalstudent.ai` |
| Learning | `medai-prod-learning-api…azurecontainerapps.io/local` | `https://api.medicalstudent.ai/local` |
| Agent-v2 (upload formats) | `medai-prod-learning-api…azurecontainerapps.io` | `https://api.medicalstudent.ai` |
| Tutor | `msa-api-tutor.azurewebsites.net` | `https://tutor.aws.medicalstudent.ai` |
| Notifications | `notification-service…azurecontainerapps.io` | `https://notify.aws.medicalstudent.ai` |

Tokens from `auth.medicalstudent.ai` keep `iss=https://msa-api-iam.azurewebsites.net` and kid `test-key-1`; the login here is a plain `POST /login` (no OIDC SDK, no issuer check), so only the address changes.

## Verification

- `vite build` locally: bundle names only the five AWS addresses above; none of the stopped Azure hosts.
- CORS from `https://university.medicalstudent.ai`: `auth.medicalstudent.ai` `/login` and `/user` preflight 204 with the origin echoed; notify preflight 204 + `GET /readyz` 200 with the origin; tutor `*`; learning `*`.
- Every IAM path the dashboard calls answers the same on `auth.medicalstudent.ai` as on the old forwarder (`/users/me`, `/invites`, `/promo-codes`, `/team-members`, `/tenants` → 401 without a token).
- Known gap: agent-v2's `API_CORS_ORIGINS` lists the SWA default host but not `https://university.medicalstudent.ai`, so `GET /v1/documents/formats` fails CORS from the custom domain. The client treats that as "unknown" and keeps the upload picker permissive (same as today). Fix is an infra change (add the origin), not in this PR.

Merging deploys to university.medicalstudent.ai — owner only.

author: lemonfiber-release-train[bot]
body:
A workflow this repository pins moved in the spec at `v1.0.52` (`67242eb72bafaa25b3bb735ff3f5c3a50e0006d6`).

`workflow-pins` names it on every pull request opened here until it is taken, so this is opened for you rather than owed to you.

**Only the pins whose own workflow moved are in the diff.** A pin is measured against the one file it names — the scripts these workflows run are checked out at `main` on every run and reach here whatever the pin says — so a pin several numbers back whose file has not changed is current and is left where it is.

Opened from the tag rather than from a schedule, which is the difference between this and the dependency bot: a proposal computed on a timer names whatever number existed when it ran, and can land already behind one published since.

author: austinorphan
body:
Closes #993.

## What changed

- **The Teams outcome carries each slot's team.** `GameplayOutcome`'s `'teams'` variant gains
  `teams: number[]`, indexed by slot like the counts and read off `Tank.team` in `loop.ts`
  (`slotTeamsOf`). `'ffa'` and `'teams'` are now separate union members over a shared
  `VersusTally`, so only a Teams outcome has to carry it.
- **The results table groups by that array**, not by `teamOf(slot)`. It shows one row for
  each team at least one slot played on, in team order. A team nobody chose gets no row of
  zeroes, so a 2v1v1 shows three rows and a 2v1 still shows two.
- **Rows use setup's letters**: "Team A", "Team B", "Team C", from `TEAM_LABELS` (the same
  letters the stock strip shows).

## A judgment call to check

**The winner title uses the letter too: "Team B wins", not "Team 2 wins".** The issue only
asks for the table rows. Lettering the rows and not the title would put "Team 1 wins" above a
"Team A" row, which is worse than today, where both are numbered. It is one line in
`versusOutcomeTitle`, plus its test in `hud.surfaces.test.ts` and the
`screen.ending.versus.teams.played` expectation in `tools/screens/states.mjs`. To keep the
numbered title, revert those three.

## Evidence

The same match on two builds, `main` (469152f4) against this branch: the built page in
headless Chromium 151 (Playwright 1.62.0), 1280x800, seed 7, with only the stored setup
changed. Provenance and figures:
[`pr-media/issue-993/README.md`](https://github.com/AustinOrphan/tanks/blob/pr-media/issue-993/README.md).

**A A B.** Before, the winning side is charged the loser's only death: parity puts P1 with P3,
who was on the other team.

![Before: Team 1 wins, Team 1 row 1 kill 1 death 20%, Team 2 row 0 0 0%](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AustinOrphan/tanks/pr-media/issue-993/aab-before.png)
![After: Team A wins, Team A row 1 kill 0 deaths 20%, Team B row 0 kills 1 death 0%](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AustinOrphan/tanks/pr-media/issue-993/aab-after.png)

**A A B C (2v1v1).** Before, team C has no row, and both rows mix players from different teams.

![Before: Team 1 wins, two rows: Team 1 1 2 7%, Team 2 2 1 17%](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AustinOrphan/tanks/pr-media/issue-993/aabc-before.png)
![After: Team A wins, three rows: Team A 2 1 18%, Team B 0 1 0%, Team C 1 1 10%](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AustinOrphan/tanks/pr-media/issue-993/aabc-after.png)

The default A B A split looks the same before and after apart from the letters, because parity
happens to match it. The FFA ending is byte-identical at 1280x800 and 390x844.

## Local candidate verification (standard risk: `src/game`, tests, manifest, screen-state data)

- `npm run verify:quick`: 311 test files passed and 14 skipped; 6916 tests passed and 215

author: szhekpisov
body:
## What

A mutant is no longer routed to covering tests that fail together on unmutated code, which reported it KILLED whatever it did. Lines covered only by such a group now run their package's whole suite.

## Why

Per-test routing runs a mutant with `-run=^(A|B|…)$` over the tests the coverage map lists for its line. #110 left out tests that fail **alone**. Tests that each pass alone can still fail **together**: one leaves state behind that breaks another, and the full suite runs a test in between that resets it. The survivor re-check from #110 can't catch this, because it only runs for LIVED mutants.

Found while benchmarking v0.6.2-rc0 on google/uuid:

- `TestSetRand` sets the package's random source to a `strings.Reader` and never restores it. In the full suite a later test resets it.
- The mutant removing `Must`'s `if err != nil { panic(err) }` (`uuid.go:211`) is routed to 7 tests that include `TestSetRand` and `TestVersion7Monotonicity` but not the resetting test.
- That selection fails on unmutated code (`panic: unexpected EOF`), so the mutant reads KILLED. No test can kill it: the full suite passes with it applied.
- v0.6.1 does the same when given an import path. Since #110 turns routing on for `./...`, the bug now reaches the default case.

## How

**Check groups while the map is built** (`BuildTestMap`, new step 5):
- `testGroups` collects each distinct group of two or more tests covering a line, per package. A single test already passed alone in `processWork`.
- `checkGroups` runs each group once against its compiled binary (`groupPasses`: `-test.run=<group>` plus the binary's usual arguments), in parallel over `Workers`, bounded by `TestTimeout`.
- `dropGroups` removes a group that fails or times out from every line whose tests in that package are exactly that group. A line that runs some of those tests alongside others keeps them, because its own group was checked separately.

**No runner changes.** Everything reads the map through `TestRefsFor`/`TestsFor`:
- A line left with no tests runs its package in full, under the global ceiling, because its timing sum is incomplete.
- Under `--integration`, only the importer's failing group is removed. The mutant's own package stays routed, and the importer's suite still decides any survivor through the re-check.

**Cost is bounded.** `BuildOptions.Lines` (from `pendingLines` in `main.go`) limits the check to lines with mutants to test. The cost is one binary run per distinct group, with no compiling.

**Warning.** When a group fails, a warning names the first one, which points users at order-dependent tests:
`test groups that fail when run together without any mutant: N, so mutants on their lines run whole suites instead; first: <pkg>: <tests>`

**Cache.** `SchemaVersion` goes from 8 to 9, because a v8 KILLED entry can be such a false kill.

`LineKey` is now the one place that formats the map's `file:line` key; `addBlocks`, `TestRefsFor`, `TestsFor` and `main` all use it.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows convention (`feat:`, `bug:`, `fix:`, `doc:`, `chore:`, `test:`)
- [x] `go test -race ./...` passes locally
- [x] `go vet ./...` and `golangci-lint run` clean
- [x] New/changed behavior covered by tests
- [x] Coverage threshold met (`./internal/...` = 100%, with and without `-short`)
- [x] Mutation efficacy threshold met on changed lines (`gomutants --changed-since main ./internal/...` = 100%: 64 killed, 0 lived, 1 timed out)
- [x] No new dependencies (or justified)

## Notes for reviewers

**Tests that guard against regression:**
- `TestRunGroupFailingTogetherLives` (main_test.go) runs end to end. `TestBreak` leaves state that fails `TestUse` unless `TestReset` runs in between; both cover `Max` and check nothing. With the group check disabled, the mutant reads KILLED; with it enabled, LIVED.
- `TestIntegrationGroupFailingTogetherLives` covers the same case under `--integration`, with the failing group in the importing package. With the check disabled: KILLED, no re-check. With it enabled: LIVED after its re-check.
- `TestBuildTestMapDropsTestsFailingTogether`, `TestGroupPasses` and `TestGroupPassesTimesOut` use real compiled binaries. `TestGroupPasses` covers source order (`TestBreak, TestReset, TestUse` passes) and the binary's `testArgs` (`-test.short`).
- `testgroups_test.go` has unit tests for `testGroups`, `dropGroups` (exact-match rule, cross-package lines), `checkGroups` (worker bound, sorted failures), the `Lines` filter, and cancellation during the check.

**uuid, rc0 against this branch** (1 warmup + 1 run each, 1,762 mutants):

| | Wall | Killed | Lived | Re-checked |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.6.2-rc0 | 126.2 s | 865 | 484 | 229 |
| this PR | 135.6 s | 864 | 485 | 230 |

- **Warning:** the branch reports exactly the one 7-test group.
- **Verdicts:** `uuid.go:211` goes from KILLED to LIVED. Four other mutants changed verdict, all in clock-dependent code in `time.go` and `version7.go`. Re-run in isolation, each one changes verdict between runs under either version, so they're flaky tests, not this change.
- **Timing:** these are single runs. Two identical rc0 runs differed by 10 s, so the wall-time gap is within the noise.

**Known limitation:** if a package's tests hang when run together, each of its groups can wait out the full `TestTimeout`. Solo runs stop after one timeout per package (`stalledPkgs`); groups don't yet. This could be a follow-up.
