author: dedsecwatch-ally
body:
## Summary

A pass over the whole browser covering security, privacy, the Google sign-in flow, performance, and UI finish. It fixes many existing bugs, several of them silent.

## Security & privacy
- **Web content locked down:** every `<webview>` is forced to sandbox + context isolation, no Node and no preload (`will-attach-webview`). Navigation is limited to `http(s)`, `about:blank` and `blob:`.
- **Trusted IPC:** every handler checks that the sender is the browser UI. Web pages have no bridge at all (verified: `window.electron`, `require` and `process` are all `undefined` in pages).
- **Permissions** (`src/main/permissions.ts`): camera, mic, location etc. were previously **auto-granted**. They are now prompted per site and remembered (in memory only for private tabs); unknown permissions are denied.
- **Password vault** (`src/main/vault.ts`): passwords were stored in **plaintext in localStorage**. They are now encrypted with the OS keychain via `safeStorage`, plaintext never reaches the renderer, and the clipboard is cleared 30s after copying. Existing passwords are migrated automatically.
- **Ad/tracker blocking fixed:**
  - Raw Electron `details` were passed to `match()`, so the filter list likely never matched. It now uses `fromElectronDetails`.
  - The allowlist used a URL-substring match, which was bypassable. It is now hostname-based.
  - The filter engine is cached on disk.
  - Top-level navigations are never blocked.
- **Other privacy additions:**
  - HTTPS upgrades with automatic fallback
  - Global Privacy Control
  - A working Clear Browsing Data option
  - Private-tab data is wiped when the last private tab closes
  - A real-version reduced user agent (Chrome 142, correct platform)
- **Chromium flags:** removed flags that weakened site isolation or wasted battery. `enable-features` is now passed once; Chromium only honoured the last of several occurrences.
- **UI hardening:**
  - Strict production CSP (no inline scripts) injected at build time
  - Local avatars instead of a third-party image service
  - The fake randomized "trackers blocked" counter is replaced with real counts

## Sign-in
- Google account state now comes from session auth cookies + `ListAccounts` in the main process (`src/main/account.ts`), replacing fragile DOM scraping.
- **Sign Out now actually removes Google cookies.** Previously the profile auto re-logged in.
- New account popover.

## Performance
- **Rendering:**
  - A stable `dispatch` plus selector-based subscriptions replace whole-store subscriptions, which re-rendered everything on every change.
  - Fixed the toolbar remounting the address bar on every render (it lost focus and typed text).
- **Persistence:** localStorage writes are debounced, transient tab data is no longer persisted, and restored tabs load lazily.
- **Webview events:** replaced events Electron has removed (`crashed`, `new-window`, `before-input-event`). Crash recovery, `target=_blank` → new tab, and shortcuts inside pages now work. Shortcuts are routed through the main process, and macOS gets a proper app menu (⌘W closed the whole window before).
- **Battery:** removed the always-running FPS loop, which could permanently enable Low Power Mode, and added a memory saver for background tabs.

## UI
- Design tokens as RGB channels: ~100 Tailwind opacity-modifier classes (e.g. `text-underlay-text/40`) previously generated no CSS.
- Light/dark themes, reduced motion and visible focus rings.
- Rebuilt components:
  - tab strip (favicons, audio indicator)
  - toolbar and address bar (history/bookmark suggestions, configurable search engine)
  - site-info popover and permission prompt
  - settings (every control now works)
  - command palette and context menu
  - crash page
- The weather widget is now opt-in.

## Testing
- `tsc` and `vite build` pass.
- Drove the real Electron app under Xvfb with Playwright against a local test page:
  - page isolation and sandboxing confirmed
  - both tracker scripts blocked and never requested
  - `target=_blank` opens a tab
  - Ctrl+T works with page focus
  - onboarding, settings, profile and palette render correctly in dark and light themes
- **Not tested:** Google sign-in itself (no internet in the test sandbox).

## Known limitations
- History/Downloads overlays, the Library page and onboarding still use hardcoded dark colors in light mode.
- On Linux without GNOME Keyring/KWallet, passwords can't be saved (Settings explains why).
- `npm install` builds the native addon against Node rather than Electron. The browser now falls back to a JS URL filter instead of crashing.
- Widevine/Netflix requires a Widevine-enabled (castLabs) Electron build.

body: Closes #120 (part of #117). ## What it does A lab bench on the bunker's north wall for three **fictional** products, each made through its own small mini-game. Everything is made up: products, ingredients and steps. | Product | Kit (stays) | Uses up | Mini-game | Then | |---|---|---|---|---| | 💎 Glimmer, 10 g | burner + flask set | 2 blue gloop, 1 fizzium salt | **Burner:** hold the flame (button or Space) to keep the needle in the green band for 20 s. More time in the band means higher quality. If the needle reaches the red, the batch boils over and is lost (with a puff of smoke). | cools for 30 s, then **Break it up** | | 💊 Fizz tabs, 8 g | tablet press | 2 fizzium salt, 1 moon syrup | **Press:** slide the mix until it matches the shade on the card, then press 8 tablets as the marker sweeps through the zone (button or Space). | dries for 15 s, then **Bag the tablets** | | 🧪 Nebula, 6 g | flask set | 1 stardust, 1 moon syrup, 1 blue gloop | **Drops:** watch the drops, then repeat them in the same order (click or 1/2/3). Three rounds of 3, 4 and 5 drops. | swirls for 20 s, then **Bottle it** | - Quality (0–1) comes from the game. The product goes into the stash as a normal `ProductUnit`, ready for packing. - You can only start a recipe once you have its kit and ingredients. The panel marks anything missing in red and disables **Start**. You can have one batch on the bench at a time. - The server only accepts a score once the recipe's minimum play time has passed since the start. A score above 1 counts as 1. If you walk away mid-game, the batch is thrown out. A batch that never gets finished (for example, the page closed) spoils after 5 minutes. - **3D bench:** a steel bench with a pegboard. Your burner (with a flask on a ring stand), the second flask and its three little bottles, and the tablet press only show up once you own them. While a batch is on the bench, its flask fills, the flame burns while it's heating, the press head moves while pressing, and steam rises (lighter while it rests). - `lab.help` explains the games in the bunker's help. There is no info text under the panel (#92). Toasts go through `ctx.event('lab.…')`. ## Files Only the lab's own files: `src/shared/bunker/lab.ts`, `src/server/bunker/lab.ts`, `src/client/world/drugbunker/lab.ts`, `src/client/ui/bunker/lab.ts` (CSS through `bunkerStyle`), `src/client/i18n/bunker/lab.ts` and a new `tests/bunker-lab.test.ts`. **No changes** to `index.ts`/`items.ts` or any shared file. author: kedrzu
body:
Sets `"useDaemonProcess": false` in `nx.json`.

nzyme is checked out as a submodule in several product repos and their worktrees, and each copy started its own Nx daemon. The daemons never exit and keep watching the file tree: seven ran at once on one machine, one at 100% CPU for 21 days, with `fseventsd` at ~65% CPU.

In Nx 23.2.1 (`DaemonClient.enabled()`) the top-level `useDaemonProcess: false` disables the daemon unless `NX_DAEMON=true` is set explicitly; nothing in the repo (scripts, `.env`, CI, docs) sets it, and there is no `tasksRunnerOptions` override.

Verified: `nx show projects` lists all projects and leaves no `nx/dist/src/daemon/server/start.js` process behind.

Consumer repos pick this up when they bump the submodule pointer (separate step).

author: hadrienpatte
body:
`GetScopeFromKey` assumes every key follows the `cilium/state/<resource>/<version>` layout and extracts the third and fourth path segments as scope. Keys with fewer than four segments are instead truncated to their first 12 bytes, which produces confusing label values for several well-known keys:

```
cilium/kvstoremesh-lock          -> cilium/kvsto
cilium/.initlock/<random>        -> cilium/.init
cilium/cluster-config/<cluster>  -> cilium/clust
cilium/.heartbeat                -> cilium/.hear
cilium/synced/<cluster>          -> cilium/synce
```

Synced keys (`cilium/synced/<cluster>/cilium/state/<resource>/<version>`) are long enough to take the regular path, but the extracted segments are the cluster name and "cilium", which yields one series per remote cluster and loses the resource information altogether.

Rework the logic to match the known key layouts, guaranteeing bounded cardinality:

```
cilium/{state,cache}/<resource>/<version>[/...] -> <resource>/<version>
cilium/synced/<cluster>/<key>                   -> synced/<scope of key>
cilium/<name>[/...]                             -> <name>, without any leading dot
anything else                                   -> other
```

Scopes for state and cache keys are unchanged.

Here's a sample of what the truncated labels look like on the metrics endpoint today:

```
# HELP cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_events_queue_seconds Seconds waited before a received event was queued
# TYPE cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_events_queue_seconds histogram
cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_events_queue_seconds_bucket{action="create",scope="cilium/.hear",le="0.002"} 1
cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_events_queue_seconds_bucket{action="create",scope="cilium/.hear",le="0.005"} 1

[...]

cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_operations_duration_seconds_bucket{action="Get",kind="read",outcome="success",scope="cilium/clust",le="10"} 294
cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_operations_duration_seconds_bucket{action="Get",kind="read",outcome="success",scope="cilium/clust",le="+Inf"} 294
cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_operations_duration_seconds_sum{action="Get",kind="read",outcome="success",scope="cilium/clust"} 0.7620097370000003
cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_operations_duration_seconds_count{action="Get",kind="read",outcome="success",scope="cilium/clust"} 294
cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_operations_duration_seconds_bucket{action="Lock",kind="set",outcome="fail",scope="cilium/kvsto",le="0.005"} 0
cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_operations_duration_seconds_bucket{action="Lock",kind="set",outcome="fail",scope="cilium/kvsto",le="0.01"} 0
cilium_kvstoremesh_kvstore_operations_duration_seconds_bucket{action="Lock",kind="set",outcome="fail",scope="cilium/kvsto",le="0.025"} 0
```

author: pusewicz
body:
Handling a `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` notification took longer the more documents were open, though it is about one document. `DiagNotification()` found the buffer by its file name, and Vim compares that name with every buffer's name: `bufnr()` did it as a file pattern, and since #51 `bufexists()` and `bufadd()` still compare the name with every buffer's name, case-insensitively on macOS. Nothing else on the path depends on the number of documents. That includes signs, text properties, the location list and `LspDiagsUpdated`. The per-cursor-move paths don't either: the status-line diagnostic, `lsp#lsp#ErrorCount()` and `:LspDiagCurrent`. Storing 100 diagnostics in every other buffer doesn't change that.

The URI is now looked up in the server's `docBufnrs` registry of open documents (from #50), first as the server sent it, then as this plugin escapes it. clangd and typescript-language-server send our URIs back unchanged, even for file names with special characters. gopls leaves `+ @ ; = , & $` unescaped, and those URIs match on the second lookup. Only a document that isn't open on the server still goes through `util.BufnrExact()`, as before. That covers workspace diagnostics and the empty publish after `didClose`.

"Before" is `main`, with #50 and #51. MacVim 9.2.0699, best of 7. The lookup rows time the lookup alone, with buffers added by `:badd`. The other rows use clangd 22 with N open documents and a notification with 100 diagnostics.

| | before 10 | 100 | 500 | after 10 | 100 | 500 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| lookup, open document | 95 µs | 125 µs | 249 µs | 0.5 µs | 0.5 µs | 0.5 µs |
| lookup, open document escaped differently | 96 µs | 124 µs | 249 µs | 46 µs | 46 µs | 46 µs |
| lookup, document not open | 97 µs | 125 µs | 251 µs | 100 µs | 128 µs | 254 µs |
| `DiagNotification()` | 1.23 ms | 1.30 ms | 1.43 ms | 1.13 ms | 1.10 ms | 1.10 ms |
| `processMessage()` of the notification | 1.76 ms | 1.83 ms | 2.03 ms | 1.47 ms | 1.46 ms | 1.50 ms |

On `main` before #51, `DiagNotification()` took 1.25, 1.68 and 3.39 ms. The 46 µs of the second lookup is `util.LspUriToFile()`.

`Test_PublishDiagnostics_FoundByOpenDocumentUri` fails without this change. `Test_PublishDiagnostics_UnopenedDocumentFoundByFileName` covers the documents that aren't open, and it passes both with and without the change.

body:
## Summary

Builds on #312 (one process, a window per file), now merged.

**Pages sidebar and zoom level**
- A column of page thumbnails down the left edge for documents with pages. It opens by itself for more than one page and stays shut for one. A toolbar toggle (the usual sidebar icon, shaded while open) overrides that either way, and keeps you on the same spot of the page while the content box resizes.
- Thumbnails are small decodes of their own, made as they scroll into view and freed when far away. They have a soft drop shadow, and the current page gets an accent ring. Clicking one goes to its page, and the column follows the page showing.
- The column scrolls with otto-kit's `ScrollView`, like every other view: fling, rubber band, notched wheel, overlay scrollbar. A gesture stays with the pane it began over.
- The toolbar shows the zoom level between − and +, as a percentage of actual size (a page at one point per point, a picture at one pixel per point). Fit moves to the end of the zoom group. In narrow windows the page controls move right rather than overlap it.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy -p otto-preview --tests`: clean.
- `cargo test -p otto-preview`: 9 passed, including new tests for the sidebar layout (hit testing, scroll-into-view) and the toolbar layout (no overlap at minimum width).
- Run in a live Otto session on an 8-page PDF: sidebar, thumbnails, ring, shadow, scrollbar and the toggle all checked from screenshots. A release build is installed locally and in use.
- Not checked on screen: the zoom label (seen and approved by hand) and the toggle unshading when the sidebar closes.

## Notes

- Per CLAUDE.md, run the `otto-reviewer` agent before merging.

author: bill10
body:
## Summary

When an update is available, Settings' "Version x is available" line now ends with a **What's new** link. It opens a modal window listing every CHANGELOG section newer than the running version, up to and including the latest, newest first. The window has **Update** (the existing update action) and **Close**. Esc, Close or a click on the backdrop closes it. Focus stays inside while it is open and goes back to the link afterwards. On a phone it is a full-screen sheet with 44px buttons.

- `GET /api/update/changelog` (owner-only, like `/api/update`) answers `{ version, latest, notes }`, or `{ error, url }` when the notes can't be fetched. The window then says it couldn't load them and links to the CHANGELOG on GitHub.
- A ~40-line markdown renderer (`renderNotes` in settings.js) handles what CHANGELOG.md uses: `##`/`###` headings, lists (nested one level), paragraphs, **bold**, `code`, and https links. It escapes first and wraps after, so nothing from the file becomes markup. No new dependency.
- Update in the panel is now the gold primary button, matching the one in the window.

### Where the notes come from, and why

**GitHub raw at the latest release's tag** (`raw.githubusercontent.com/bill10/agent-007/v<latest>/CHANGELOG.md`). It works the same for an npm install and a checkout. The release workflow tags `v<x.y.z.w>` before it publishes to npm, so the tag exists by the time npm reports that version. It needs no change to package `files` and no extra tarball download. A checkout's `git show origin/main:CHANGELOG.md` would need a fetch and would only cover checkouts. A release's CHANGELOG never changes, so it's cached per latest version. Windows opened together share one fetch, and a failed fetch isn't cached.

## Screenshots (real app, VERSION set to 0.56.0.0 so npm's 0.58.0.0 is newer)

**Before**, the version box (desktop and phone, dark and light):

![before-desktop-dark-panel](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/before-desktop-dark-panel.png?raw=true) ![before-phone-dark-panel](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/before-phone-dark-panel.png?raw=true)
![before-desktop-light-panel](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/before-desktop-light-panel.png?raw=true) ![before-phone-light-panel](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/before-phone-light-panel.png?raw=true)

**After**, the version box:

![after-desktop-dark-panel](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/after-desktop-dark-panel.png?raw=true) ![after-phone-dark-panel](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/after-phone-dark-panel.png?raw=true)
![after-desktop-light-panel](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/after-desktop-light-panel.png?raw=true) ![after-phone-light-panel](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/after-phone-light-panel.png?raw=true)

**After**, the What's new window:

![after-desktop-dark-window](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/after-desktop-dark-window.png?raw=true) ![after-phone-dark-window](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/after-phone-dark-window.png?raw=true)
![after-desktop-light-window](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/after-desktop-light-window.png?raw=true) ![after-phone-light-window](https://github.com/bill10/agent-007/blob/bill10/settings-a-what-s-new-link-when-an-updat/docs/screenshots/whats-new/after-phone-light-window.png?raw=true)

## Dev run

With VERSION at 0.56.0.0 and npm's latest at 0.58.0.0, `/api/update/changelog` returned the sections 0.58.0.0, 0.57.0.0, 0.56.2.0, 0.56.1.0, 0.56.0.2 and 0.56.0.1, and not 0.56.0.0. The window showed the same six. Clicking What's new opened it. Esc closed only the window, not Settings, and focus went back to What's new. I checked this in Playwright, in both themes, on desktop and on a phone.

## Design review (impeccable)

The critique ran two independent passes: a design review, and the detector with in-page contrast and focus checks. These are fixed:
- The dialog opened at the top-left: the CSS reset removes the dialog's `margin: auto`.
- What's new was crowded between two buttons. It moved onto the "Version x is available" line.
- The dates and the version subtitle were 3.9:1 in the dark theme. They now use `--text-muted`.
- The type scale was flat (h4 12 / body 14 / h3 15). It's now 12 / 14 / 16, with a 20px title.
- Update was styled differently in the panel and in the window. Both are now the gold primary button.
- Touch targets were under 44px on phones. Fixed with `@media (hover: none)`.
- Loading is now announced with `aria-busy`. The shadow is lighter, and list markers are dimmer.

The detector's cramped-padding finding on the `<dialog>` is a false positive: the dialog has `padding: 0` on purpose, and its sections carry their own padding.

## Test Coverage

- `test/self-update.test.js` covers:
  - only the sections newer than this version, up to the latest
  - unreleased sections and headings without a version are skipped
  - one fetch per release, and windows opened together share it
  - a new fetch once a check finds a newer latest
  - the fetch-failure answer with the GitHub link, retried on the next call
  - nothing asked when up to date or under npx
  - slicing the headings that `scripts/release.js` writes
- `test/client-settings-version.test.js` covers:
  - the link shows only when an update is available and none is running
  - markdown: headings, bold, code, https-only links, escaping, nesting, and bold or code that wraps onto the next line
  - the repo's own CHANGELOG renders with no leftover `#` or `**`
  - the failure body links to GitHub
- Still untested here: the dialog, focus and Esc flow (checked by hand in the dev run above, since happy-dom handles `showModal` poorly), the route's `ownerOnly` guard (it serves the public CHANGELOG), and the one-line "no notes" message.

## Pre-Landing Review

The review found three problems, all fixed:
- Bold, code or links that wrap onto the next line showed as raw markdown. Each item or paragraph is now formatted as one block.
- Dragging a text selection out onto the backdrop closed the window.
- A slow, older fetch could overwrite a newer result.

The adversarial pass (Claude subagent) found four more, also fixed:
- The window's Update button showed even with no update, or while one was running.
- The subtitle came from the panel's cached data rather than the server's answer.
- Concurrent opens each fetched the CHANGELOG. They now share one fetch.
- An npx install still asked npm and GitHub.

Outside review: Codex was unavailable (usage limit until Oct 25), so Gemini ran instead. Its one finding, concurrent opens each fetching, is the same as above and is fixed.

Noted, not changed:
- A checkout updates with `git pull` of main, which can be ahead of npm's latest. Its notes then stop at npm's latest.
- A prerelease npm version would give a "could not load" window. This repo doesn't publish prereleases.

## Verification Results

`npm test`: 2314 passed, 3 failed. The 3 failures are the same on origin/main on this machine: `server.test.js` /api/browse and the Bearer-token case, and `mcp-endpoint.test.js` "lets a real user through". They are local 5 s timeouts. The same main commit is green on Ubun

author: twaldin
body:
Three unreleased fixes on top of v0.2.4: easl samples its own main-thread stalls, updates install where macOS won't let easl change the installed app's dates, and a managed `scripts/rotate-lead.ts` hands a fresh lead session its handoff.

## Summary

```text
main-thread turn >= 1 s (watchdog, utility queue)
  Metrics.claimStall          # same lock as turn end: claim + register, or refuse an ended turn
  /usr/bin/sample <own pid>   # empty env, 15 s then SIGKILL; failed attempt deleted; newest 20; <= 1 per 5 min
  turn end (one critical section) -> log line + longest.cause name stalls/<file>; survives metrics reset
```

```diff
 update helper (runs from the old app)
-  touch installed app          # denied on a managed Mac: update stopped, nothing replaced
-  mv app -> .easl-previous-…
+  mkdir .easl-previous-….protection   # exclusive; its date stands in for the rollback's
+  mv app -> .easl-previous-…           # old date kept
   mv incoming -> app
 launch cleanup (AppUpdate.removeStaleLeftovers, shared by app and tests)
-  delete copies over an hour old
+  delete only when max(copy, protection) >= 1 h; unknown date = young; never the running bundle; log failures
```

```text
rotate-lead.ts
  wait idle/done boundary     # only within deadline minus a 300 s post-boundary reserve
  agent.restart --mode fresh  # never --force; refused without the reserve
  prove new session + live pid + same model/thinking (+ restart command flags), unread done kept
  tell once with a stable id -> require message ACK -> recheck identity
```

## Evidence

All at head `08c123e`:

- **Updater.** Before: on the Work Mac, the 0.2.4 helper's `touch` of the installed app was denied, so the update stopped with nothing replaced.
  **After:** the real `AppUpdate.helperScript` ran against an owned app whose ACL denies writeattr. `touch` was denied, the helper exited 0 with outcome installed, 0.2.3 was installed, and 0.2.2 was archived whole with its mtime unchanged. Cleanup at the first-rename boundary kept the rollback, and no hidden leftovers remained.
- **Sampler** (bundle built at this head, run on the CanvasTest screen, guarded, 0 focus reverts):

- **Rotation, native canary:**

  - The tile and scratch were removed afterwards.
- **CI** (run 37844423544): `swift run CanvasCoreTests` passed 1019 tests in 136 suites. The new correlation regressions are `aShortTurnClaimedBeforeItsEndWasPublishedStillGetsItsFile` and `theNextTurnsClaimDoesNotTakeTheEndedTurnsPlace`. `bun test scripts/rotate-lead.test.ts` passed 25/25 (now in CI), and the easld and conformance jobs are green.

Claude Opus 5.5 reviewed the code GPT-6.1 Sol wrote, including the original sampler; GPT-6 Astra reviewed the sampler fixes Opus wrote. Every final delta is READY, and the model metadata was checked with no fallbacks. The xAI pass couldn't run because the account is out of credits.

**Door:** two-way. Nothing migrates data. The first update from 0.2.4 still runs 0.2.4's own helper, and the CHANGELOG gives affected users the Releases zip or `brew upgrade --cask easl`.

body:
## Human comments

## What was wrong

#5022 made the timeline wait to insert a fetched older page until scrolling had been idle for 200 ms, with no touch in progress. The wait applies on every platform. Desktop wheel and trackpad scrolling (including macOS momentum) keeps firing `scroll` events, so the prefetched page stays uncommitted for as long as the reader keeps scrolling. `isLoadingOlderTimelineRows` stays true until the commit, so readers scrolling up now reach the "Loading older messages…" indicator and stall there. Before #5022, rows were inserted as soon as the response arrived, so the 600 px prefetch margin usually hid the load. Only one load can be pending at a time, so the next page also can't prefetch while the reader keeps scrolling.

## What changed

Reverts #5022 (9cb923ae37) in full. One conflict in `useThreadTimelineController.ts` was resolved by keeping #5068's removal of the `useRef` import. This brings back the behaviour #5022 fixed: the iOS momentum-scroll jumps and the stale scroll-anchor yank reported in #4793.

body:
### Summary
Existing Fivetran blueprints in the repository (`fivetran-sync-parallel-dbt-core.yaml`, `fivetran-dbt-cloud.yaml`) focus on triggering active ELT sync pipelines.

This blueprint provides data pipeline governance by querying Fivetran's `connectors.Status` API on a schedule. It evaluates connector setup state, pause status, active sync failures, and Fivetran's own freshness calculation without triggering a sync. It classifies connector health into `HEALTHY`, `WARNING`, `CRITICAL`, or `UNREACHABLE`, alerts Slack before downstream data goes stale, and records an audit log on every run.

### What it does
`Schedule trigger (disabled: true)` ➔ `io.kestra.plugin.fivetran.connectors.Status` ➔ `io.kestra.plugin.core.debug.Return (4-tier classification)` ➔ `io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.Switch (HEALTHY / WARNING / CRITICAL / UNREACHABLE)` ➔ `Slack Alert / Log` ➔ `Audit Log`

### Hacktober Requirements
- [x] $\ge 3$ runnable tasks (Status probe, Return classification, Switch, Log audit)
- [x] $\ge 1$ flow task (`io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.Switch`)
- [x] $\ge 1$ trigger (`io.kestra.plugin.core.trigger.Schedule`)
- [x] $\ge 1$ non-core plugin (`io.kestra.plugin.fivetran.connectors.Status`)

### Reproducing & Testing
1. Obtain API credentials from your Fivetran account (Free tier supported).
2. Configure `FIVETRAN_API_KEY`, `FIVETRAN_API_SECRET`, and `SLACK_WEBHOOK` secrets.
3. Pass your target connector ID in `connector_id` and execute flow.

**Static Verification Output:**
- `yaml.safe_load`: Passed (syntax parsing verified)
- Trailing whitespace check: 0 lines
- `metaDescription` character count: 147 chars (<= 160)
- Forbidden string scan (`secrets(`, hardcoded passwords, invalid Slack classes): Passed

Closes #748

author: alejoamiras
body:
## What changed and why

A full backup of a password profile holds its master secret and every key in plain text, and until now Download Backup saved that file at once (#34). This builds the owner's pick, **option D**: split by profile type.

- **Password profile (option A).** Download Backup stays disabled until the file is encrypted. The ready banner becomes the instruction: "Protect your backup. Encrypt the file with your profile password before you download it. Without a password, anyone who opens the file controls this profile." Protect with Password stays the primary button and reuses the password already typed, so encrypting costs one press. The page's download writer refuses a plain file for a password profile again, behind the button.
- **Passkey profile (option B).** The flow stays as it is. Its plain file reaches no funds without the passkey, so Download without a password opens a confirmation: pre-title "Not encrypted", title "Download without a password?", "This file will show your accounts, contacts and activity to anyone who opens it. It holds no key that can move funds without your passkey." Cancel comes first; "Download anyway" second, in red. The banner reads "Backup is ready. Protect it with a password before you download it. Without a password, the file is saved in plain text." The confirmation's callback downloads only from the run the person was warned about (the page's `generation`, the `finished` status, a passkey profile).
- **The red button.** `@nulo/design`'s `Button` gains a `destructive` variant: the regular button's type and padding on red. Primary and `destructive` share one type rule, so the two cannot drift, and size and padding stay with the size classes. "Download anyway" uses it at medium, Cancel's size.
- **A profile switch made in another window** used to leave this page holding the previous profile's backup, judged by the new profile's type (a password backup, switched to a passkey profile, passed the passkey confirmation). The page now ends the run, scrubs what it made, ends a pending passkey prompt, and returns to its agreement step for the new profile.
- **ConfirmPopup** takes an opt-in `confirm_variant` for its confirm button. `confirm_color: "red"` never coloured that button (it reached the Button as a `type` attribute), so the eleven existing destructive confirms render exactly as before.

## Owner sign-off

- Decision page, 2026-10-08 (`implementations-plan/security-ui-1/OWNER-ASKS.md` § Answers): "1. #34 unencrypted full backup: **D**, split by profile type: A on password profiles, B on passkey profiles".
- Result page, signed off 2026-10-09 12:50 UTC (§ Answers: result page, 2026-10-09):
  - "r1. The red "Download anyway" button: **C**, a red variant of the regular button"
  - "r2. A profile switch in another window resets the export page: **Yes**, ship as built"

One render note for the owner, not a new call (§ Answers: result page): the red button's hover follows the regular button's, which lightens the red in the dark theme (white label about 3.6:1 at rest, 3.1:1 under the pointer). No shot shows a hover.

UI impact: the full-backup export page (both profile types) and its confirmation, as above; after a cross-window profile switch the page shows its own first step. No other screen changes.

## Screenshots

The passkey confirmation with the new red button, Chrome, taken through the e2e harness (`passkey-backup.test.ts` with `NULO_E2E_SHOT_DIR`):

| Light | Dark |
|---|---|
| ![Confirmation, light](https://github.com/nulo-sh/nulo/blob/3211d169eb91445b4919846894893480ed33c134/apps/extension/pr-screens/export-full-confirm-red-light.png?raw=true) | ![Confirmation, dark](https://github.com/nulo-sh/nulo/blob/3211d169eb91445b4919846894893480ed33c134/apps/extension/pr-screens/export-full-confirm-red-dark.png?raw=true) |

The ready and encrypted states of both profile types are unchanged since the decision page's shots; `security-backup.test.ts` and `passkey-backup.test.ts` reproduce them.

## Validation

All local, on this branch's head:

- `bun run audit:vue` (typecheck:all ∥ test ∥ lint, then build), `bun run test:all`, `bun run lint:actions`, `bun run check:plans`: pass.
- Component tests: a password profile's Download is disabled until encryption, a forced press writes nothing, the encrypted file downloads; a passkey profile's Download opens the confirmation, Cancel writes nothing, Download anyway writes the plain file; a confirmation answered after unmount, after encryption, or after a profile switch writes nothing; a switch resets the page and ends a pending passkey prompt; ConfirmPopup's variant reaches only the confirm button, at Cancel's size. `Button.test.ts` adds five cases for `destructive`: its class, and four read from the style block (vitest maps every CSS-module name, defined or not): it shares primary's type rule, neither variant sets a size and it stays out of the CTA contract, it fills red with white text, hover and press skip a disabled or loading button. Each fails under its mutation.
- Smoke e2e after the red button, `--retry=0`: Chrome `security-backup`, `passkey-backup` (5/5; `passkey-toolbar-panel` skips on Chrome); Firefox the same three (10/10, the panel export that presses Download anyway included).
- Earlier on this arc, `--retry=0`: Chrome smoke `security-backup`, `passkey-backup`, `backup-imported-account`, `legal-acceptance`, `backup-roundtrip`, `passkey-retry`, `own-window`, `contacts-import` (37/37); Firefox smoke the same plus `passkey-toolbar-panel` (42/42); network e2e (`e2e:agent`, proverless) Chrome `account-balance-orphans`, `backup-import-stalled-network`, `backup-migration-roundtrip`, `backup-restore-integrity`, `backup-restore-sw-restart`, `import-handshake-note`, `import-handshake-note-matrix`, `same-token-concurrent-sends` (28/28), Firefox the six that run there (23/23).
- Review: Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, high) three rounds on the arc, the last with no production finding; on the red button, two rounds, the second clean; one Opus review each time. Verdicts and resolutions are in `implementations-plan/security-ui-1/plan.md` § Audit verdicts.

This branch merged `dev` (the only conflict was `implementations-plan/index.md`).

E2E delta: password-profile helpers and specs now protect, download and open the encrypted file in Node with the restore's own codec (`openFullBackupText`); passkey plain downloads press the confirmation's Download anyway. `security-backup` pins that Download waits for encryption; `passkey-backup` pins the confirmation (Cancel writes nothing, Download anyway writes the credential-id-only plain file).

Closes #34

author: lilfedor
body:
This PR adds no code — just two bug tickets.

1. **A broken recurring job looks fine until it runs.** If a recurring
   job is set up so its only step is handed to a person instead of an
   agent, `coga validate` says it's fine. Then every scheduled run fails
   with a bare error code and no explanation. The ask is for Coga to catch
   that setup when it checks the job, not when it runs.
2. **The weekly skill-update job can erase your work.** It opens a pull
   request with skill updates. If you push your own fix onto that pull
   request, the next week's run rebuilds the branch from scratch and
   silently throws your fix away. The ask is for it to keep or refuse to
   overwrite commits it didn't make itself.

author: d-morrison
body:
Before: `preview.yml` and `publish.yml` were inline copies of the preview and publish steps, so qwt missed [gha#1022](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/pull/1022)'s stale-freeze pruning, and a preview rendered only HTML unless a `revealjs`, `pdf` or `docx` label was added. Change highlighting and tracked-changes Word files ran from five Python scripts under `.github/scripts/`.

After: previews are built by `preview.yml` (a caller of gha's `preview.yml@v3`) and published by the new `preview-deploy.yml` (gha's `preview-deploy.yml@v2`). The site is published by a caller of gha's `quarto-publish.yml@v3`. The time zone is `America/Los_Angeles` as before, now through gha's `timezone` input ([gha#1026](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/pull/1026)). Previews render every format `_quarto.yml` declares (`formats: default`), so slide decks, PDF handouts and Word files are built in every preview. Publish keeps its bare render of every format and now also saves the freeze cache through `freeze-cache: true`. Five scripts are deleted; the per-page banner script stays (see below). This mirrors [qmt#10](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/qmt/pull/10).

How: each step of the old workflows, and what replaces it. Remaining gaps are on [gha#1025](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1025).

| Old step | Now |
|---|---|
| Preview: `pull_request` types, label-event filter (`revealjs`, `pdf`, `docx`, `no-preview-highlights`, `clear-freezer`) | Same `types` in the caller; gha's built-in filter, plus `extra-preview-labels: '["no-preview-highlights"]'` |
| `concurrency` group `preview-${{ github.ref }}` | gha's build job has the same group and `cancel-in-progress` |
| `TZ` env and "Set timezone" step (preview and publish) | `timezone: America/Los_Angeles` on both |
| Checkout (preview: full history; publish: recursive submodules) | gha's checkout. Preview submodules are now `recursive` (gha's default; the old preview checked out none). Publish: `checkout-submodules: true`. History for the comparison comes from gha's own fetch of `gh-pages`. |
| Set up Quarto, TinyTeX | `tinytex: true` on both |
| Set up R and packages (knitr, rmarkdown, tibble) | `use-renv: false` and `r-packages` (publish: `setup-r: true`). `install-package: false`, `apt-packages: ''`, `setup-chrome: false` keep what ran before. |
| Restore freezer; `clear-freezer` label | gha's restore; label is now `clear freezer` |
| `clear-changed-freezer.py` (prune changed pages) | gha's stale-freeze pruning ([gha#1022](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/pull/1022)); script deleted |
| Render HTML | `formats: default` (preview); bare render in publish (`formats: ''`, as before); `render-profile: ''` because `_quarto.yml` selects `website` by default |
| Optional Reveal.js, PDF and DOCX renders on the `revealjs`, `pdf` and `docx` labels | `formats: default` renders every declared format every time, so the labels are no longer needed |
| `detect-changed-chapters.py`, `highlight-html-changes.py` | `highlight-changes`, off while the PR has `no-preview-highlights` (expression in the caller), `changed-chapters-glob: '**/*.html'` |
| `inject-preview-metadata.py` and the second render | Dropped. Nothing in the repo reads the `preview-changed` key, so the second render did no work. |
| Install python-docx; `create-docx-tracked-changes.py` | `docx-tracked-changes: true`, `docx-tracked-changes-glob: '**/*.docx'` (files are `<stem>-tracked-changes.docx` beside the original, as before) |
| Home-page banner | `changed-chapters-banner: true` |
| Per-page "Changes in this PR" and "Other Formats" banners | **Kept local**: `page-banners` job running `.github/scripts/add-page-banners.py` (renamed from `add-home-banner.py`) |
| Save freezer | gha's save, plus `freeze-cache: true` in publish, which only saved before |
| Deploy `pr-preview-action`, sticky comment, remove on close | `preview-deploy.yml` |
| Publish: `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action`, keeping `pr-preview/` | gha's deploy keeps `pr-preview/` |

Kept local: gha has no banner listing the changed pages on every page, nor one linking a page's tracked-changes Word file and slide deck (gap 5 on [gha#1025](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1025)). The `page-banners` job downloads gha's `pr-preview-site` artifact, runs the script on `preview_artifact/site`, and re-uploads it under the same name, path and settings as gha's own upload (gha sets no `include-hidden-files`, so no dotfiles are lost). The deploy workflow runs only after the whole build workflow finishes, so it publishes the edited artifact. The script now:

- adds nothing to a page that already carries its banners, so a re-run is harmless;
- fails (exit 1) when `HTML_DIR` is missing or holds no HTML, instead of exiting 0;
- skips the changed-pages list on the home page, where gha's `changed-chapters-banner` already writes one;
- takes the changed pages from gha's `changed-chapters` and `detection-status` outputs, rather than treating every page with a tracked-changes Word file as changed (gha now writes one for every page).

Things that change:

- The `revealjs`, `pdf`, `docx` and `clear-freezer` labels are replaced by `clear freezer` alone (README updated). A `clear freezer` label has to exist on the repo before it can be applied; I created it. The old labels are left in place and can be deleted.
- Previews now always build slides, PDF and Word, so a LaTeX or slide error breaks a preview where it used to need a label.
- The `**/*.html` glob also treats `index.html` and the `-slides.html` decks as pages to compare and highlight (gap 6); the old script skipped both. gha's highlighter skips `<script>` and `<style>` content.
- Publishing now force-pushes `gh-pages` (the deploy action's default, `force: true`), where the old step set `force: false`. gha keeps the force push on purpose and serializes publish with preview deploys instead ([gha#611](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/611)). `gh-pages` is generated output, so only its old commit history is lost; `pr-preview/` is still kept.
- The build job is read-only; only `preview-deploy.yml` writes. That workflow starts previews only once it is on `main`, so previews begin working after this merges.

Checks run: actionlint (clean); zizmor `--offline` (no findings beyond unpinned `@v` references to gha, the lab convention, and `workflow_run`, which is the deploy half's design); all workflow YAML parsed with a duplicate-key-rejecting loader; the banner script run on a small fake site (missing directory exits 1, home page gets no changed-pages list, slides pages are skipped). I did not render the site or run the workflows.

Related: [gha#1022](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/pull/1022), [gha#1026](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/pull/1026), [gha#1025](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1025), [qmt#10](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/qmt/pull/10).

## What

The `scoutlens-jtt.26` evidence backfill left five `scoutlens-uze.4` acceptance criteria unproven. Each now has its own assertion, and each assertion was shown failing on a tamper before it was trusted.

| uze.4 AC | Assertion | Tamper that fails it |
|---|---|---|
| AC2 | `frozen-question.spec.ts`: the same line-box ink measurement at the exact **640×512** reflow viewport, and at **769, 1024, 1280 and 1440**. Before, it measured 640 px only at 800 px tall, and above 48rem it had only a pixel baseline. | The pre-F-1 fixed track fails at 640×512. A 1rem wide-layout track fails at 769×900. |
| AC3, readable size | Running text must stay **≥ 10 px** at every frozen width and at 640×512, and must **never shrink as the viewport narrows**. Display type over 20 px may scale. Running text is any element with 20 or more characters of its own text, measured on one page load against 1440. Today the smallest is 10.56 px at every width. | A narrow-width 0.8rem rule on the experiment conclusions fails on both routes. |
| AC3, truncation | No ellipsis or line clamp cuts text off. | A two-line clamp on the landing confound fails. |
| AC3, stretched content | A stretched-content fixture for `/` and `/science`. The uze.7 fixtures stretch only the Lab. Caveats, sources, claims, card titles, the chip and the headline are grown to three times their length, plus the longest published team join. The page is then checked for overflow, edge crossings, unwrapped text and truncation at 320 px and at 640×512. | Removing the wrap fix below fails it. |
| AC4 | Nav targets must be **≥ 44 px wide**, not only tall. | A 30 px max-width fails on both routes and both projects. |
| AC6 | New `reduced-motion.spec.ts`: an **instant** scroll under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and a smooth one without it, so the check is not vacuous. No animation or transition runs under reduce after every disclosure is toggled and every control is hovered and focused. | Removing `base.css`'s reduce rule fails the scroll test on `/` and `/science`. An ungated 2 s colour transition fails the animation test. |

## The one CSS change

The stretched-content check found a real defect. The `/science` frozen-question heading's display-size words overflowed its 144 px track at 320 px (155 px of ink).

`science.css` now gives that heading `overflow-wrap: break-word`. That leaves min-content sizing alone, so copy that fits today renders exactly as before; the landing and `/science` visual baselines pass unchanged.

author: hugloss
body:
## Summary

Generalize the Harbor component-ablation framework introduced in #200 so the analyzer is driven by an explicit matrix-level component contract instead of hardcoded `task_evidence` subject names, then dogfood the generic path with a second component: `find`.

## Why this is the next slice

The existing semantic-localization tasks intentionally ask *which implementation owns behavior*. Hashmarks' canonical MCP instructions say that case should route to `task_evidence`.

Those tasks are therefore the wrong population for testing `find`, whose canonical routing contract is:

> known exact symbol, path unknown → `find`

This PR adds a separate exact-symbol task population instead of blurring those two semantics.

## Explicit component-ablation authority

A component matrix now declares:

```json
{
  "ablation": {
    "component": "task_evidence",
    "arms": {
      "bare": "none",
      "full": "hashmarks",
      "remove": "hashmarks-no-task-evidence",
      "only": "hashmarks-task-evidence-only"
    }
  }
}
```

Admission requires:

- exactly one non-empty component
- exactly four unique declared arm subjects
- `bare = none`
- `full = hashmarks`
- remove arm excludes exactly the declared component
- only arm includes exactly the declared component
- the component exists in the observed canonical Hashmarks MCP catalog

The exact ablation contract is frozen in model-free preflight and transported into every Harbor trial receipt.

## Generic analyzer

`agentscookbook.harbor-ablation-report.v2` is component-neutral.

The same analyzer now handles:

- task-evidence ablation
- find ablation
- future single-component MCP ablations using the same four-arm contract

It still requires strict matched quartets over:

- campaign
- task
- harness
- model
- replicate

It still validates the frozen treatment catalogs and checks observable ATIF calls against them.

Positive necessity/sufficiency signals require observable invocation of the declared component. The report does not consume model reasoning and keeps:

```
positive_causal_proof_claimed = false
observed_catalog_advertisement_proven = false
```

Pre-#201 task-evidence ablation receipts remain readable through a bounded legacy fallback based on the previously frozen subject identities.

## New `find` controls

Three task definitions are added beside the held-out suite:

- `lookup-known-symbol-paths-under`
- `lookup-known-symbol-sync-remove-stale-paths`
- `lookup-known-symbol-run-poll-delay`

Every prompt explicitly supplies the exact symbol and asks only for its path.

These tasks are intentionally **not** added to the canonical held-out `experiment.json`. The native benchmark remains the same 12-task experiment; these are Harbor-only component controls.

New profiles:

```
harbor-find-ablation-smoke
  1 task × 3 harnesses × 4 arms × 1 replicate
  = 12 trials

harbor-find-ablation-full
  3 tasks × 3 harnesses × 4 arms × 3 replicates
  = 108 trials
```

The four `find` arms are:

```
none
hashmarks
hashmarks-no-find
hashmarks-find-only
```

## Execution

Smoke:

```sh
make benchmark-check MATRIX=harbor-find-ablation-smoke
make benchmark-new MATRIX=harbor-find-ablation-smoke
```

Full:

```sh
make benchmark-check MATRIX=harbor-find-ablation-full
```

## What / why

`SaveClaimsWhenDatabaseHasConcurrentImmediateTransactionDoesNotMisreportCorruption` failed on main CI when a concurrent `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` made sqlite3 fail in a shape `ExecuteSqlite` did not recognize as busy. That path threw `InvalidDataException` (corrupt cache) instead of a lock failure.

author: wdonray
body:
## What
The home page still loaded partially scrolled down on mobile Safari even after PR #76. This fixes the actual root cause.

## Why
PR #76's `window.scrollTo(0, 0)` ran in `useEffect` (after paint), but iOS Safari applies its own scroll positioning asynchronously during load as its toolbar settles, overriding the effect. `history.scrollRestoration = 'manual'` only affects history navigation, not fresh loads, so it never helped here. Additionally, `<main className="min-h-screen">` uses `100vh` (the large viewport), which mismatches iOS's dynamic toolbar viewport and contributes to the offset.

## How
- `src/app/page.tsx`: scroll reset moved to `useLayoutEffect` (runs before paint, no flash of wrong position), plus a `requestAnimationFrame` re-pin loop (2 frames) that re-asserts scroll 0 after Safari's toolbar settles. Cleanup cancels the pending frame on unmount.
- `src/components/SiteChrome.tsx`: `<main>` changed from `min-h-screen` to `min-h-dvh` so the content height tracks the dynamic viewport on mobile instead of the toolbar-hidden height.
- Tests: page tests cover the immediate pin, the rAF re-pin count, the unmount cleanup, and the manual scroll-restoration branch. SiteChrome test updated for the `min-h-dvh` class. Both changed files at 100% coverage.

A workflow this repository pins moved in the spec at `v1.0.52` (`67242eb72bafaa25b3bb735ff3f5c3a50e0006d6`).

`workflow-pins` names it on every pull request opened here until it is taken, so this is opened for you rather than owed to you.

**Only the pins whose own workflow moved are in the diff.** A pin is measured against the one file it names — the scripts these workflows run are checked out at `main` on every run and reach here whatever the pin says — so a pin several numbers back whose file has not changed is current and is left where it is.

Opened from the tag rather than from a schedule, which is the difference between this and the dependency bot: a proposal computed on a timer names whatever number existed when it ran, and can land already behind one published since.

author: wieslawsoltes
body:
## Implemented
- Standalone local Node gateway CLI: credential-free, non-overwriting configuration initialization; loopback default; rotated private access token; optional private token file; trusted HTTPS/WSS; graceful session shutdown.
- Explicit browser gateway selection, endpoint-change secret clearing, bounded authenticated target discovery, redirect rejection and stale-request cancellation. No deep-link/profile-supplied gateway redirects.
- Exact-origin CORS and WebSocket upgrade checks, strict Host binding, legacy private-network preflight handling. Existing target allowlist, verified TLS/CredSSP, stream framing, rate limits and backpressure preserved.
- Browser-only static build with relative URLs under /RDP/, no server/private configuration files, CSP, .nojekyll and deployed-commit manifest.
- GitHub Pages deployment workflow plus a separate Chromium integration workflow and in-app setup/troubleshooting documentation.

## Verified before merge
- Full-tree syntax, Node tests and general protocol fuzzing passed: https://github.com/wieslawsoltes/RDP/actions/runs/37844807330
- Chromium browser gateway integration passed: https://github.com/wieslawsoltes/RDP/actions/runs/37844807366
- Browser test exercises the static /RDP/ app -> separate-origin local WebSocket gateway -> TCP/TLS/NTLMv2 CredSSP -> activated co-developed RDP fixture, secret clearing, local lab resize and mobile viewport. No browser security overrides used.
- Additional actual-socket tests exercise both TLS-only and NLA flows, CORS/token/Host denial paths and bounded static dependency packaging.

## Deployment and limits
Pages deployment runs after merge; this PR does not equate a committed workflow with a verified live site. The gateway runs on the user's machine, not GitHub Pages, and is trusted with credentials. Public-HTTPS-to-loopback permissions differ by browser; trusted WSS and same-origin local hosting are documented alternatives. The browser CI scenario uses HTTP loopback and Canvas, not public HTTPS, physical GPU hardware or an independent Windows RDP server. No full RDP conformance claim. All projects on the same Pages hostname share one origin.

body:
The fourth PR of the claims sweep covers `commands/`,
`advanced/adopt-and-reset` and `advanced/adding-a-service`. I read each
factual claim against the core's and the media stack's `origin/main`, as
pinned. New guards hold three of the claims.

**False claims, now fixed**

| Page | Said | Fact |
|---|---|---|
| global-flags | `--confirm` appears on `quality set`, `quality upgrade`, `reset`, `support` | 14 commands take it, `companion certificate` through `update stack` |
| global-flags | `--service` appears on `up`, `down`, `backup` | `update stack` takes it too |
| global-flags | two environment variables are read | the Docker variables `DOCKER_HOST`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY`, `DOCKER_CONFIG` are read as well |
| commands index | `ui` serves the JSON API, and `--assets <dir>` serves a web app beside it | the web app built into the binary is served unless `--assets <PATH>` names another |
| the-tui | seven panels, and three keys | nine panels (Front door, Waiting on you); the action keys `u d s t p a m k c f w`, each opening a list and asking before it acts |
| the-web-console | lists what it does not do yet | every action is one of the web API's actions; the page links to that list |
| adopt-and-reset | eight states a seed finds | the contract's `SeedState` has 14, `wired` through `refused` |
| adopt-and-reset | no way to declare an area unmanaged | `LEMONFIBER_UNMANAGED` takes `area=reason` pairs |
| adding-a-service | a `[[service]]` entry in `stack.toml` | the entry is a `services/<id>.toml` file named in the root's `include` |
| adding-a-service | the Sonarr block, copied | the copy had drifted (tag, digest, networks); the page now renders the block from the pinned `compose/tv.yml`, and Sonarr's service file beside it |
| adding-a-service | the licence and capability checks | lemonfiber's own images carry `Hippocratic-3.0`; the capability field is `grants`. The page now links to the stack's own list of checks instead of keeping a copy |

**New guards**

- `flagTableViolations`: each recurring-flag row on global-flags lists every command that takes the flag, and only those. It reads the generated reference.
- `panelViolations` (`src/lib/terminal.ts`): the TUI page names every panel the dashboard draws, and states their number.
- An inventory holds the seed-state table to the contract's `SeedState`, in both directions.
- `Vendored` takes a `service` and shows that one Compose service, read by `serviceBlock` (`src/lib/compose.ts`).

Every new guard was hand-mutated until no mutant survived. The flag rows and the panels are read a line at a time, anchored at both ends, so neither pattern backtracks.

The spec workflows move from v1.0.51 to v1.0.53, because `hygiene.yml` and `spec-check.yml` both changed and `workflow-pins` requires the move.

The Shot inspector hides Camera for a slider. `fixedShotCamera` keeps a slider's camera still (static, intensity 0, float 0) after every store edit and in `sanitizeDoc`, so a document that already had a camera move on a slider gets its native loop back.

## 3. Frames fits a 30 s shot

`framesAssetIds` shows the first screenshots whose period fits 30 s at 0.20 frame heights per second: 10 with 3 rows (4:5, 9:16, 1:1), 8 with 2 rows (16:9, 4:3). `framesDuration` counts only those, so it never passes 30 s and the speed stays under the limit. The inspector says "Shows the first 10 screenshots, so the loop fits in 30 s.", as the slider does past 18.

## Tests

- New guards: `layouts.test.ts` "is balanced at rest"; `slider-presets.test.ts` (camera move undone, no-op edits stay no-ops, loaded slider gets a still camera); `frames.test.ts` "Frames fits a 30 s shot" (3 tests); e2e `slider.spec.ts` "a slider shot has no camera controls" and `frames.spec.ts` "more screenshots than fit 30 s". Each fails when its change is reverted (table in the evidence README).
- Local: typecheck, lint, `npm test` (33 files, 491 tests) and build pass. `slider.spec.ts` and `frames.spec.ts` pass (10/10). Full local e2e: 166 passed, 1 failed: `editor.spec.ts:28`, the full flow, which changed the camera on the demo shot. That shot is Desktop Slider, which no longer has a Camera section. The test now checks that the Camera section is hidden on the slider, then switches the shot to a single device through the Layout picker before the camera step; it passes (3.4 min), as do `timeline.spec.ts` and the rest of `editor.spec.ts`.
- `timeline.spec.ts:119` (25 transition screenshots, 45 s timeout) timed out on both CI runs of this PR. It had been running out of headroom since D1 made the slider the demo: 29.6 s on main before D1, 42.5 s on #30's CI, 37.5 s on main after #30. It asserts nothing about the template, so it now applies Quiet Hero first, as the stage playback tests do (14.7 s locally, down from 24.5 s). The timeout is unchanged.
- **CI: all 8 checks green** ([run 37848357267](https://github.com/jesseleechan/mockup-motion/actions/runs/37848357267)). Shard 3 first failed on `audio.spec.ts:223` (loop wrap, on the known-flaky list) and passed when re-run once.
- Visual: no baseline changes expected (every still uses 5 screenshots or no slider).

Docs: quality bar §2.2 and §4, contracts §5, and `follow-ups.md` (the three items move to Done).

Merged on the owner's "merge #31 when it passes".

body: ## What - `.github/workflows/build.yml`: `inputs.hugo-version.default` `"0.147.0"` → `"0.161.0"`, plus a `description` and a comment recording why. Both `build` and `cleanup-build` (the PR-closed rebuild path) read the same `${{ inputs.hugo-version }}`, so they move together — no second pin exists. - `README.md`: - the Tailwind opt-in recipe no longer tells a site to override `hugo-version` — the default now satisfies `css.TailwindCSS`'s ≥0.161 floor; the `with: hugo-version:` override stays documented (also shown in the caller snippet) for sites that need a different version; - the `security.exec.allow` regex now explicitly includes `node`: `^(go|node|npm|npx|tailwindcss)$`. Hugo ≥0.161 spawns `node` to run the Tailwind CLI, and the docs-literal `^(go|npm|npx|tailwindcss)$` form fails the build — found in the sitebrewhq/sitebrew-api#299 theme prototype; - the stale "executor doesn't bake in a `tailwindcss` CLI" sentence is replaced — it does since executor v0.1.7 (2026-10-07); the sandbox still denies `npm install`/`npx` at runtime. - No script or test fixture asserts the default version string (`grep 0.147 scripts/` is empty), so nothing to update there. ## Why Decision **D14** in the refactor map (sitebrewhq/sitebrew-api#288): one Hugo version platform-wide — the executor image already verifies on 0.161 while production sites still built on 0.147. Evidence: sitebrewhq/sitebrew-api#311 — all 8 real/production sites plus the canary were built locally on `hugo v0.161.0+extended` with `--gc --minify` in a scrubbed env (the executor's command shape): **exit 0 on every one**. Output diffs vs 0.147 are minifier-only (generator meta, a dropped newline after ``, `currentColor` casing, one empty CSS rule dropped on Tiketo). See the per-site table in that issue's comment. ## Blast radius - Every `@stable` caller — ~127 live site repos (the workflow's own comments say ~170 incl. staging/pr forks) — builds on 0.161.0 extended after promotion. None of them passes `hugo-version`, so this single default moves all of them. - Verified on the 8 real ones (7 `@stable` callers + `site-rekap`, which has its own inline pin and needs a separate PR). - Two new deprecation warnings appear on every bootstrap-derived site, both **non-fatal**, no removal version announced: - `languageCode` → `locale` (`hugo.toml`) - `.Language.LanguageCode` → `.Language.Locale` (`layouts/index.html` / `baseof.html`) - The pre-existing `found no layout file for "html" for kind "taxonomy"` warning is unchanged (identical on 0.147). - Tailwind-opted-in sites: none exist yet (no real site has a `package-lock.json`), so the `npm ci` step still fires nowhere. ## Ordering **This must land before the bootstrap/site deprecation fixes.** The fix (`locale = "cs"` + `.Site.Language.Locale`) builds clean on 0.161 but **fails hard on 0.147** (`can't evaluate field Locale in type *langs.Language`, tested in #311). So: promote this first, then fix `sitebrew-site-bootstrap` and the existing sites. ## Merge instructions **Do not merge without Jakub's explicit go — promotion is production.** Merging to `main` triggers `promote.yml`: canary run on `sitebrewhq/sitebrew-canary-site`, then the floating `@stable` tag moves and every customer site pulls 0.161.0 on its next push. This PR is step 1 of the maintenance sequence; `site-rekap`'s inline pin and the deprecation fixes follow as separate PRs. ## Verification - `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` (local, Node v22.22.2): **20 tests, 20 pass, 0 fail** — same as baseline on `main`. - `build.yml` re-parsed as YAML (Ruby `YAML.safe_load`): `hugo-version` input resolves to `{description, type: string, default: "0.161.0"}`; jobs `build, deploy, cleanup-build, cleanup` intact. - `actionlint`: **not run** — not installed locally (`brew`), and the npm `actionlint` package exposes no executable via `npx`. The YAML/structural change is a single scalar + comment, no expression or job changes. `ci.yml` runs only the node tests, so CI won't lint it either. - Hugo 0.161.0 itself is exercised by `promote.yml`'s canary run on merge, not by this PR's CI. --- Need help on this PR? author: furqanagwan
body:
A source whose executable is a different game now says which game it is:

> This is 007: Blood Stone (ID). This build is for Quantum of Solace (ID).

instead of two bare title IDs.

- **Build name:** codegen records the original XEX's XDBF title as `PPCImageInfo::source_title_name` (trademark signs stripped as the window title does). Builds generated before this keep the ID-only message until regenerated.
- **Source name:** decoded only when the title IDs differ, from the bytes the checksum pass already reads: AES-CBC (retail, then dev-kit key), basic or LZX compression, then the XDBF title string in the default language. The file is whatever the player chose, so this uses its own bounded reader rather than the runtime's XEX loader and XDBF parser, which trust a loaded title. The game loader is unchanged.

Validation
- Synthetic named XEX plus six malformed variants (resource outside the image, truncated image, oversized string, wrong resource name, delta compression, no XDBF magic); two-name and ID-only messages.
- Local test (`REXGLUE_TITLE_XEX`) decodes the retail executables (encrypted, LZX): "Quantum of Solace", "007: Blood Stone", "007™ Legends".
- Debug CTest: 2,711 selections; two failures, both recorded before this change (tessellated-quad GPU fixture, `ppc_corpus.instr_mtmsrd` Debug abort).

Refs #154

author: pedrosantos0806
body:
## O que estava acontecendo

**A tela branca.** O `env.ts` montava o objeto `env` chamando uma função que lança quando a variável falta. Como `env` era um `const` de módulo, o erro acontecia na avaliação do import — antes de o React montar. A tela de "falta configurar" que o `main.tsx` já tinha era código morto: nada chegava a renderizar.

Junto disso, as variáveis na Vercel ficaram com os nomes `SUPABASE_URL` e `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, e o Vite só entrega ao navegador o que começa com `VITE_`. Então mesmo depois de configuradas, o app não as enxergava.

**O desenho.** Faltava boa parte do que o protótipo do Artifact entrega — a barra inferior inteira, as telas de momento (sua vez / entrou na fila / jogo iniciado), e as três telas principais estavam numa versão simplificada.

## O que mudou

### A tela branca

- `env.ts` não lança mais no import: as chaves viraram getters, então só quem realmente usa a URL vê o erro, e `isConfigured()` pode ser chamado com segurança.
- `main.tsx` confere a configuração **antes** de carregar qualquer coisa que toque o Supabase (o app virou `boot.tsx`, importado dinamicamente). Ganhou handlers globais de `error` e `unhandledrejection` que pintam uma mensagem legível em DOM puro — nunca mais uma página em branco.
- `vite.config.ts` injeta as três variáveis aceitando os nomes **com e sem** o prefixo `VITE_`. Não precisa renomear nada na Vercel.

A lista no `define` é fechada de propósito: um `envPrefix` genérico `SUPABASE_` exporia uma eventual `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` no bundle que todo mundo baixa. Conferido com build: a variável existindo no ambiente, a string não aparece em `dist/`.

### O protótipo

| | |
|---|---|
| **Barra inferior** | Quadras · Placar · QR/NFC · Perfil, visível dentro de um parque, com o botão de leitura saltando do meio. O "Placar" aponta para a última quadra aberta. |
| **Quadra** | Placar com a cor do piso, a linha da rede com a bolinha no rali, cronômetro de 104px, os dois lados lado a lado, e a fila com a posição em 36px e a pilha de raquetes de 88×66 à direita. |
| **Home do parque** | Assinatura + avatar, "Escolha sua quadra", botão de trocar parque, faixa de números e os cartões com a caixa verde do cronômetro. |
| **Perfil** | Cabeçalho verde com cantos arredondados, prévia grande da raquete com encordoamento, as duas paletas de seis cores e a pilha de exemplo. Cada escolha salva na hora. |
| **Leitura** | Tela cheia com abas QR/NFC, moldura com cantos em ocre e a linha varrendo — separada da folha de entrar na fila, como no protótipo. Antes eram uma coisa só. |
| **Momentos** | Sua vez, raquete na pilha e jogo iniciado. |

### Dois ajustes que o desenho exigiu

- **`my_profile_summary()`** passa a devolver `racket_frame_color`, `racket_grip_color` e `avatar_tone`. A função nasceu na Sprint 2, antes de a Sprint 3 criar essas colunas — então a tela de perfil abria sempre com a raquete padrão e **descartava a escolha do jogador na primeira edição**. Migration nova + teste de regressão.
- **`useLiveCourt().refresh()`** devolve o estado que acabou de ler, e chamadas simultâneas compartilham a mesma ida ao servidor: quem entra na fila precisa da posição na hora, para a tela de sucesso mostrar o número certo.

## Sobre a fonte da assinatura

A assinatura "Neqst" do protótipo usa a **Chancery Cursive - DGL**, que traz `© 1998 Digital Graphic Labs - All Rights Reserved` dentro do próprio arquivo. Sem licença de redistribuição, ela não pode ser publicada junto com o site, então não a incluí.

No lugar entrou a **Italianno** (Google Fonts, licença aberta), escolhida comparando as duas lado a lado — é a parente livre que acerta o traço do N e o rabo do q.

Se você tiver a licença, é um arquivo só: coloque o TTF em `web/public/fonts/chancery-cursive.ttf`. O `@font-face` já aponta para lá e a assinatura fica idêntica sem mexer em código.

## Como foi conferido

- **A tela branca, nos dois cenários**, com Chromium headless sobre `vite preview`: sem variáveis, a tela explica o que falta; com `SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` sem prefixo, o app sobe e cai em `/entrar`.
- **As telas**, em 390×844 com as fontes carregadas, servidas sobre dados de exemplo com os mesmos números do protótipo.
- **O SQL**, contra um Postgres 16 de verdade: as quatro suítes passam, e o `db/full_setup.sql` aplica duas vezes seguidas sem erro.
- `tsc -b` e `npm run build` limpos.

## Uma decisão que ainda é sua

O protótipo não tem tela de resultado — a partida simplesmente acaba. O backend precisa saber **quem ganhou** para o "quem ganha fica" funcionar, então a tela da quadra pergunta no momento de encerrar. Hoje, se ninguém responder até o slot acabar, a quadra é liberada sem vencedor e ninguém fica. Se a regra do parque for outra (por exemplo: sem resposta, quem estava em quadra continua), é só dizer que eu ajusto.

author: jeremy
body:
Supersedes #1782, #1783 and #1785. Stacked on #1963; GitHub retargets this to `main` once that merges.

A `pre-configure` hook runs before Kamal loads the configuration. Each `NAME=value` line it writes to `$KAMAL_ENV` is set in Kamal's environment for the rest of the run. That's the same contract as GitHub Actions' `$GITHUB_ENV`. If one of those lines is `KAMAL_DESTINATION`, Kamal loads that destination instead of the one given with `-d`.

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Deploy to staging unless a destination is given
if [ -z "$KAMAL_DESTINATION" ]; then
  echo "KAMAL_DESTINATION=staging" >> "$KAMAL_ENV"
fi
```

The motivating case is a pool of shared review destinations (`beta1`…`beta16`, each with its own `deploy.betaN.yml`). `kamal deploy -d beta` should lease a free one and deploy there, and `kamal app logs -d beta` should go to the one you already hold. That takes something that runs before the config is chosen and knows which command is running. It also covers defaulting a destination, and feeding computed values into `deploy.yml` without ERB that reaches outside the file.

### Why one PR instead of four

#1782, #1783, #1784 and #1785 grew around that one need, and each added a mechanism:

- an output channel for every hook, accumulated across a run
- a `KAMAL_MESSAGE` side channel for printing
- a hook that used the channel to rewrite the destination
- external commands
- `.kamal/bin` prepended to every hook's `PATH`

Taken back to first principles, only one of those has to live in Kamal: something must run *before the configuration exists* and be able to change *which configuration loads*. Everything else either already exists or belongs to the app. So this PR is that one thing, done carefully: one hook, an env-file for its output, the destination rewrite, and enough context about the command for the hook to decide what to do.

What was dropped, and why:

- **`KAMAL_OUTPUT` for every hook, accumulated across hooks (#1782).** No use for it turned up beyond picking the destination. Anything the pre-configure hook exports is already in the environment of every later hook, the config's ERB and `.kamal/secrets`.
- **`KAMAL_MESSAGE`.** It was a second output path that ignored `hooks_output: quiet` and passed terminal control characters straight through. Kamal now announces a changed destination itself. A hook that wants to talk to the user can already do so with `hooks_output: { post-deploy: verbose }` (#1758).
- **Dotenv parsing.** It quietly mis-read `export FOO=bar` and ignored malformed lines. The format is now strictly `NAME=value` per line, with blank lines and `#` comments allowed. Values are taken as written, quotes included, and are never evaluated. Anything else, including a NUL, fails the hook before any variable is set.
- **Prepending `.kamal/bin` to every hook's `PATH` (#1785).** That changed what every existing hook runs. An executable `.kamal/bin/ruby` would take over `#!/usr/bin/env ruby`, and `.kamal/bin/git` would take over `git`. A hook can call `.kamal/bin/claims` by its path.
- **External commands (#1784)** continue separately, as an independent feature. Nothing here depends on them.

### Behaviour

- **When it runs.** The first time a command needs the configuration, and only once for it (an alias is two commands; see below). `kamal version`, `kamal init`, `kamal docs`, `kamal secrets fetch` and `kamal secrets extract` never load it, so they never run the hook. `--skip-hooks` skips it. It is always `.kamal/hooks/pre-configure`, since `hooks_path` lives in the configuration that hasn't loaded yet.
- **What it gets.**
  - `KAMAL_DESTINATION` is set only from `-d`. A value inherited from the caller's environment is cleared, so a nested `kamal` run from another hook can't pass its destination along by accident.
  - `KAMAL_COMMAND` and `KAMAL_SUBCOMMAND` name the command, e.g. `app` / `boot`. This holds even when `--hosts`, `--roles` or `--primary` load the configuration while the CLI is still initializing, before Thor has recorded anything, and an abbreviation is named as Thor will run it (`kamal app --hosts x bo` is `boot`).
  - `KAMAL_ENV` is the path of a private tempfile.
- **Output.** The hook runs quietly unless `-v`, because any command can trigger it, including `kamal server exec --raw`, whose stdout has to stay byte-clean. When it fails, its output is in the `HookError`. A changed destination is announced on stderr: `Using destination beta3 from the pre-configure hook`.
- **Aliases.** An alias is found by reading the raw configuration, so the hook runs before that lookup, which has to see the destination and variables the hook provides. It then runs again for the command the alias expands to. The first run has `KAMAL_COMMAND` set to the alias's name, so a hook with side effects, like taking a lease, can save them for the commands it recognises. The sample hook says so.
- **Failure.** A failed hook raises `HookError` and nothing it wrote is applied. If a caller rescues that and asks for the configuration again, the hook runs again rather than Kamal falling back to the destination it refused. A hook that succeeded is never re-run, even if the configuration then fails to load.

### Depends on

#1963 (`fix-subcommand-env`): on `main`, `KAMAL_SUBCOMMAND` is never set for a subcommand run from the command line, and a hook that should treat `kamal app boot` differently from `kamal app logs` can't tell them apart without it. This PR adds the same naming for the case where the hook runs while the CLI is still initializing.

### Tests

- `test/cli/pre_configure_test.rb` covers:
  - rewriting and setting the destination
  - variables reaching the config's ERB
  - the environment the hook gets, including through `Main` with selectors before and after the subcommand, and an abbreviated subcommand
  - running once
  - running before alias lookup and again for the expansion, with the alias's name first
  - invalid lines, a NUL and non-UTF-8 values
  - failure, `--skip-hooks`, commands that never load the config, and no hook at all
- `test/commander_test.rb` covers when the destination resolver runs, and what happens after it fails.
- Unit suite: 880 runs. The only failures are the 7 that also fail on `main` without a Docker builder (CliBuildTest ×4, CommandsBuilderTest ×2, ConfigurationBuilderTest ×1). RuboCop is clean. The Docker integration suite wasn't run.
- Also checked by hand against a real lease hook: `kamal app boot -d beta` leases `beta1` and deploys there, a later `kamal config -d beta` loads `beta1` without leasing, and `kamal server exec --raw -d beta` keeps the announcement off stdout.

body:
### Description of your changes

Introduce a new field on compositions, `spec.revisionHistoryLimit`, which controls how many unused revisions to keep. This is analogous to the `revisionHistoryLimit` on packages, with the nuance that packages can have only a single "in-use" (active) revision while compositions can have many in-use revisions.

Implement a garbage collector that, on each Composition reconcile, deletes unused revisions that aren't the latest, keeping at least `revisionHistoryLimit` unused revisions. A revision is in use if an XR references it, if it's the newest revision matching an XR's revision selector, or the if it's the newest revision matching the XRD's default revision selector.

Fixes #4837

author: dac-ai-worker
body:
## Summary

Several shared client-side utilities read `window.top` **unguarded during page/form load**, which can throw when `window.top` is transiently `null`:

- `library/js/xl/formatting.js` — `window.top.jsGlobals` in `I18NDateFormat`, `DateFormatRead`, `TimeFormatRead`, and `window.top.oeFormatters` at the IIFE registration (script-eval time)
- `library/js/xl/jquery-datetimepicker-2-5-4-translated.js` — `window.top.xl` / `window.top.jsGlobals` / `window.top.oeFormatters` in `datetimepickerTranslated()`
- `library/validation/validation_script.js` — `window.top.xl` at module load and `window.top.jsGlobals.date_display_format` on submit

## The problem

The tab system reuses iframes by repointing `contentWindow.location` (`interface/main/tabs/js/tabs_view_model.js`). When a reused tab iframe is re-navigated, the new (often nested) document can begin executing its init **before the frame tree has reconnected to the top browsing context**. During that sub-millisecond window `window.top` is literally `null`, so an unguarded read like `window.top.jsGlobals` throws.

The existing `|| {}` / `|| function(){}` fallbacks guard the *property* (`jsGlobals` undefined) but **not** `window.top` itself being null, so they do not help here.

Observed impact: on the encounter form (`interface/forms/newpatient`) the throw happens inside `init()` during datepicker setup, **before the Save/Cancel click handlers are bound** — the form paints but the buttons are dead. On other screens the same throw silently breaks a datepicker or field validation. It is intermittent (the null recovers on its own in <1ms) and gets noticeably worse under slow/variable network conditions, which widen the load-timing gap.

## The fix

Fall back to the current `window` when `window.top` is `null` so these load-time reads **degrade gracefully** (missing globals resolve to the existing defaults — e.g. a default date/time format for that one render) instead of throwing. When `window.top` is available there is **no behavior change**. `datetimepickerTranslated()` also gets an `xl()` fallback, matching the pattern already used in `validation_script.js`.

This is deliberately minimal and defensive: it does not try to fix the underlying iframe-navigation timing (a far larger change) — it just makes the shared load-time code tolerant of a momentarily-null `window.top`.

## Notes / possible follow-up

A few other files share the same `window.top.jsGlobals` anti-pattern (e.g. the `library/js/oeUI/insurance/*` controllers) but are far more localized; they can be addressed in a follow-up if desired. This PR covers the universally-loaded form utilities.

## Testing

- `node --check` passes on all three files.
- Changes are style-consistent with the surrounding code (no new lint rules triggered; `eslint.config.mjs` enforces no `no-var`/`prefer-const`).
