## Qué pasa
El botón «Sincronizar» de cada banco pedía siempre el histórico completo (730 días). Con CaixaBank eso puede pasar del minuto, y la sincronización terminaba en «el backend no respondió en 60 s» aunque solo faltaran los movimientos de unos días.

## Qué cambia
- Si la conexión ya recibió movimientos (`lastNewest`), la sincronización manual pide 90 días, o desde una semana antes del último movimiento recibido si hace más tiempo. Es la misma lógica que ya usaba la sincronización automática.
- El histórico completo queda para la primera sincronización de cada conexión.
- El mensaje de tiempo agotado es neutro («no hubo respuesta en 60 s; vuelve a intentarlo en un rato»), porque `bankFetch` también se usa para la copia del servidor.

body:
# Summary

Fixes https://linear.app/cowswap/issue/FE-773/signing-window-closed-message-show-even-though-i-sign-fast

Second half of FE-773. The first half, the countdown wrongly declaring a fast signature expired - went in with #8323. This is Anxo's other point: the screen the user lands on is not good.

Confirming a Solana swap in the wallet after the signing countdown has run out means the order cannot be placed. Until now that ended on the generic failure screen — a modal titled **Error**, the raw sentence in red, and a **Dismiss** button that threw the user out to the swap form, losing the trade they had set up.

It now has its own screen, per design:

- titled **Signing window expired**
- **No order was submitted** as the headline, so it is clear nothing was placed and nothing was spent
- the trade the attempt was for shown underneath (`1 USDC for at least 0.008273 WSOL`)
- **Back to swap** returns to the review screen with a refreshed quote, not to the swap form

That last point makes both ways out of an expired window behave the same: cancelling the wallet prompt after the countdown already returned to review, and now confirming too late does too.

Every other failure is untouched — including a wallet or simulation error after confirming, which still shows the generic error screen. That one is FE-703.

<!-- TODO: screenshot -->

# To Test

Needs a sponsored swap on Solana. The signing countdown is ~30s.

1. Start a swap, let the countdown reach `00:00` with the wallet prompt still open, then **confirm** in the wallet.

- [ ] The screen is titled **Signing window expired**, not **Error**
- [ ] It reads **No order was submitted**, then "The signing window closed before the transaction was signed. Please try again."
- [ ] The sell amount and minimum receive amount of that attempt are shown below, with the right token logos and symbols
- [ ] There is no "Show technical details" row
- [ ] No order shows up in the orders table or in **My orders**

2. Press **Back to swap** on that screen.

- [ ] You land on the swap **review** screen, not the swap form, with your amounts still in place
- [ ] You are asked to accept the refreshed price, and confirming again places the order normally

3. Repeat step 1, but **reject** the wallet prompt after `00:00` instead of confirming.

- [ ] Straight back to the review screen, no error screen in between (unchanged)

4. Start a swap and sign **within** the countdown.

- [ ] The order is placed as usual, no error screen

5. Trigger any other failure — reject the prompt while the countdown is still running, or hit a wallet error.

- [ ] Still the generic **Error** / **Dismiss** screen, still returning to the swap form

6. Look at the countdown screen itself, before `00:00`.

- [ ] The amounts row under the timer looks the same as it did before this change

7. Regression on an EVM chain (e.g. Mainnet): place a swap, and make one fail by rejecting in the wallet.

- [ ] Nothing changed — same screens as before

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - xAI's `/v1/models` now returns image-generation models (e.g. `grok-imagine-image`) with `pricing` as an **array** of per-(quality, resolution) tier objects, per the xAI REST reference.
  - `compatible::ModelEntry` deserialized `pricing` directly into `ModelPricing` (a struct of `Option<String>` rates). serde read the array positionally into the struct and failed on the first tier object with `invalid type: map, expected a string`, which failed the **entire** catalog fetch for any credentialed xAI alias. That surfaced to operators as a failed or timed-out model fetch.
  - `pricing` now deserializes leniently. The per-token object shape (OpenRouter / Kilo Gateway) parses exactly as before. Any other shape, or an object with non-string rates, becomes `None` (unknown pricing) for that entry only, and the listing succeeds.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not map xAI's native integer price fields (`prompt_text_token_price`, USD cents per 100M tokens) into `ModelPricing`; that is a separate feature. No change to the models.dev / OpenRouter fallback order, auth, timeouts, or any other `/models` consumer.
- **Blast radius:** Every OpenAI-compatible provider that lists models via `compatible::ModelsResponse`, plus the Responses-wire `list_models` that reuses `parse_model_ids_from_bytes`. For responses that previously parsed, behavior is unchanged. Responses that previously failed on an unrecognized `pricing` shape now list their models with unknown pricing for the affected entries.
- **Linked issue(s):** None filed.

### What this does, simply

When you open the model picker or run `zeroclaw models refresh` for a configured xAI provider, ZeroClaw asks xAI for its list of models. xAI recently started describing image-model prices in a new format (a list of prices per image size and quality). ZeroClaw only understood one price format, so a single unfamiliar entry made it throw away the whole list, and you got no xAI models at all. Now an unfamiliar price format just means "price unknown" for that one model, and the rest of the list loads normally. Price formats ZeroClaw already understood work exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`. The failure only reproduces against the live xAI API with a real key.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw models refresh`). The `tui` model picker and `web` catalog call the same `list_models_with_pricing` path through `config/catalog_models`.

- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw models refresh --model-provider xai.<alias> --force`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `✅ N models`, status `ok`, detail `catalog fetched`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `❌ error: xAI model list returned invalid JSON: invalid type: map, expected a string at line 1 column <n>`, with a non-zero exit.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Rust CI (fmt, clippy, test) covers the changed crate. No platform-specific code is touched.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI cannot reach the live xAI API; I covered that with the manual A/B below.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  New tests fail on `master` and pass on this branch:
  ```
  # before fix
  test compatible::tests::models_with_pricing_keep_object_pricing ... FAILED
  test compatible::tests::model_ids_parse_despite_tiered_array_pricing ... FAILED
  test compatible::tests::models_with_pricing_drop_unrecognized_pricing_shape ... FAILED
  # after fix

  test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1935 filtered out
  ```

  - Ruled out network causes: the xAI `/v1/models`, `auth.x.ai` discovery, `models.dev/api.json`, and OpenRouter catalog endpoints all respond in under 3s from the test host.

# What does this implement/fix?

`helpers.h` no longer includes `alloc_helpers.h`; the re-export was kept for external components after the heap allocating helpers moved in 2026.5.0 and was scheduled for removal in 2026.11.0. Code that calls `str_sprintf`, `str_snprintf`, `format_hex`, `format_hex_pretty`, `format_bin`, `value_accuracy_to_string`, `base64_encode`, `get_mac_address` and the other allocating helpers now needs `#include "esphome/core/alloc_helpers.h"`. author: hani64
body:
## Problem
Home's Made for you shelf previously guessed playlists by searching for four English names through the shared Web API app. Shared-app rate limits could leave the shelf loading or in an error state, and search results did not reliably match Spotify's personalized shelf.

## Change
Read the account's actual `homeSection` through the existing playback session first, retaining Spotify's order and localized titles. Cache successful results for ten minutes, respect `Retry-After`, and keep visible cards when a refresh fails. A 60-second deadline bounds the complete Home read while concurrent refreshes still share one request. The Web API context token is checked against the playback account before and after token resolution, including reauthorization. Omit Spotify DJ's special playlist URI because librespot cannot play that context; ordinary playlists with “DJ” in their names remain visible.

If the session read fails or local playback is unavailable, search for Spotify-owned playlist names through the shared Web API as a fallback. The shelf remains **Made for you**, although these search results are approximate and may differ from Spotify's personalized Home order. The shared fallback can itself be rate-limited.

The primary route uses Spotify's undocumented Pathfinder endpoint with the playback session's Login5 credential and client token, plus an already verified Web API grant for Home context. Its contract and persisted-query hash can change without notice. This does not change the librespot fork or log credentials. Psst's [Home change](https://github.com/jpochyla/psst/pull/745) is a precedent, but an explicit maintainer decision on whether this route fits Spotifast's honest-integrations policy would be welcome. Related to #698. Spotify staff [identify the DJ URI](https://community.spotify.com/forum/en/discussion/6110281/getting-dj-is-not-available-in-your-country-error/p1); [librespot issue #1604](https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot/issues/1604) records the unsupported context.

## Validation
- Rust formatting and Clippy with warnings denied passed.
- Serial Linux library tests: 941 passed, 3 ignored; one unrelated HTTP-proxy test was skipped after stalling in WSL.
- An earlier Windows test build loaded personalized Home cards. Scrolling the shelf showed Daily Mix 6 followed by Discover Weekly and Release Radar, with no DJ card.
- [Before and after screenshots](https://github.com/crmne/spotifast/pull/802#issuecomment-6069800027) are embedded in the PR discussion.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * The Home **Made for you** shelf can show Spotify’s personalized playlists in Spotify’s order when local playback and a valid account grant are available.
  * If personalized recommendations are unavailable, the shelf shows approximate matches for Discover Weekly, Release Radar, Daily Mix, and daylist. These may differ from Spotify’s selection and order.
  * Spotify DJ is not shown in the shelf.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Previously displayed recommendations remain visible if a refresh fails. **Retry** appears after an initial load failure.
* **Documentation**

author: griffinwork40
body:
## Problem

The REPL `--` flag-completion menu never opened for skills from **flat-installed** plugins, e.g. `/pr-triage` and `/tackle-issues` from `software-factory`. Typing the flags worked; only the menu was missing.

`afk plugin install <github-repo>` installs flat at `~/.afk/plugins/<name>/` by design. Only marketplace relative-path plugins land under `~/.afk/plugins/cache/`. Skill discovery (`scanAllPluginRoots()`) covers both, so the slash command registered, but flag harvesting (`harvestPluginSkillMetadata`) walked only `cache/` plus the bundled dir. The command registered with no `flags`, and `src/cli/input/trigger.ts` only opens the menu when `flags` is non-empty.

## Fix

- `harvestDiscoveredPluginSkillMetadata()` in `src/cli/slash/plugin-skills/flags.ts` walks the marketplace cache, the bundled dir, and **every root `scanAllPluginRoots()` returns** (flat, project-scope, imported). Flags union per skill name; categories are first-write-wins with the cache first (same precedence as before). Discovery errors fail soft back to cache + bundled.
- The walker skips `.git` and `node_modules`.
- `registerPluginSkills` (`dispatch.ts`) and `harvestAllPluginSkillFlags()` (detail view) both use it; the inline two-walk merge in `dispatch.ts` is removed.
- Regression test: `src/cli/slash/plugin-skills-harvest-flat.test.ts`.

## Verification

- Live probe against the real `~/.afk/plugins`: `pr-triage` went from `null` to its 7 flags and `tackle-issues` to its 5, in about 113 ms.
- `/review`'s flag set is identical before and after (its body-scan noise was already there).
- `pnpm lint` (tsc) is clean, and 1096 tests across 45 plugin-skills, slash and input test files pass.
- `audit:env`, `audit:filesize`, `audit:funcsize` and `audit:module-state` pass, and all 9 pre-push audit gates passed.
- The full-suite run had one timeout in `scheduler.test.ts`; it passes on its own and is unrelated.
- A devil's-advocate review compared this with carrying flags through discovery (`SkillManifestEntry` to `ProviderCommandInfo`). It kept this smaller fix for now; that refactor plus the web-UI flag gap are tracked in #3332.

## Follow-up

#3332: parse flags and category once during discovery, and attach flags in the web UI slash menu.

Canonical RK factories currently evaluate gradients and physics on the accepted
Field rather than each RK stage, so coupled nonlinear or derivative-dependent
models receive stale inputs. Publish all stage fields together into the fixed
allocations already used by FD/halo/spectral evaluators, prepare the evaluator,
scatter at the owned-origin offset, and restore accepted contents on success or
preparation failure. Pointwise physics must not throw inside the canonical
OpenMP loop. The model RHS and existing tuple protocol remain unchanged.

The multi-field stepper now owns reusable stage vectors and passes references.
Fixed input/output sizes, Field addresses, duplicate aliases and differing
layouts fail explicitly. The raw-size factory requires explicit evaluator
`bind_stage(vector)` support; the mutable Field factory preserves existing
bound-view and zero-argument halo callback contracts.

Each Field RHS performs **three full-buffer copies per field per stage**:
accepted-to-backup, stage-to-field and backup-to-accepted. This compatibility
cost is documented. Fields/evaluator/model must outlive the stepper with fixed
storage; factories are non-reentrant and evaluators must be bound to the
provided fields. Re-prepare derivative caches before independent accepted-state
reads after an attempt.

author: mitchell5584dm-tech
body:
## Problem
The last remaining blocker for the macOS release build: the **"Smoke test app window"** step fails with `smoke: page did not become ready` after 60 s. Linux and Windows pass the whole workflow, and macOS passes tests, executable build and the command-line smoke test.

## Cause (read from the macOS runner)
The smoke check swallowed every error. With it rewritten to print what it sees, the log shows on every attempt:

> `EvalError: Refused to evaluate a string as JavaScript because 'unsafe-eval' ... is not an allowed source of script in the following Content Security Policy directive: "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'"`

The page's policy forbids `eval`. On macOS (WKWebView) pywebview's page-to-Python bridge uses `eval`, so the bridge never comes up and the page never becomes ready. This is very likely a **real bug for macOS users**, not only a CI artifact: the app window would not work.

## Change
- `page_html()`: **on macOS only**, add `'unsafe-eval'` to `script-src`. Everything else in the policy is unchanged on every platform: `default-src 'none'`, `connect-src 'self'` (no server is started, so no network), `form-action 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`, no external sources. Windows and Linux keep the stricter policy.
- `_smoke()`: on failure prints the page's `readyState`, whether the bridge exists, the ready flag, the location and the last error; progress lines every 10 s. This is what made the cause visible and is worth keeping.
- Test: `eval` is allowed on macOS only and all other restrictions are present on every platform.

## Security trade-off (for the owner to judge)
`'unsafe-eval'` makes script injected into the page slightly more capable on macOS. The page only loads local, bundled content and has no network path, which limits the impact. If you would rather not accept it, the alternative is an upstream pywebview bridge that avoids `eval`, which I did not find.

## Verification
- Local: `pytest restore` -> 102 passed, 2 skipped.
- **macOS runner** (throwaway workflow, not in this PR): built the real `Arcalume.app` and ran its window smoke check: `smoke: window ready, app name 'Arcalume'` (about 7 s; it failed after 60 s without this change).
- Next: re-run `restore-release` on `main` after merge; all three platforms should pass.

author: gerald-guledew
body:
Built on #17, which should be merged first.

## What was seen

Tried twice on a MacBook, with location allowed.

- **First**, the start found for you landed about 80 metres from where the laptop was.
- **Second**, with the first half of this change in place, the browser rated its guess as good to about 90 metres and was about 130 metres out. The real spot was outside the circle drawn for it.

Both distances were measured from screenshots against LINZ address points.

That is not an error in the app. A laptop has no GPS. It works out where it is from the Wi-Fi networks it can see, and this is ordinary for that. The fault was in how the screen showed it: an exact-looking pin called "My location".

## What changed

- **A dot and a circle of doubt.** The browser reports how far out it thinks it could be. A dot marks where it places the device, with a circle of that radius around it.
- **The map frames the circle** when a start is found for you. Before, a start that fell inside the view moved nothing, so at city scale the pin looked exact.
- **A line under the start** when the doubt is more than 20 metres: "Your browser guessed this spot. By its own estimate it is good to about 90 m, the circle on the map. It can be further out than that. Drag the pin to where you really are."
- **Any pin can be dragged.** It keeps its name and its place in the list. A plan worked out for the old spot is dropped.
- **Dragging the pin the browser placed tells the app where you are.** The dot goes with the pin, the circle and the line go away, and search looks from the new spot.

Dragging also helps with a pin dropped on a building with no road beside it, which the API refuses to route to. It can now be nudged to the street instead of being removed and added again.

Frontend only. The API is unchanged.

## How it was checked

**On a real laptop, by hand.** The map zoomed to the street, the dot, the circle and the line appeared, and the pin could be dragged. The screenshot from that run is also the only check by eye. It was made before the last commit, so it covers the first four points above and not the fifth.

**With a stand-in for the browser's location**, which also says how sure it is. It lived in a config file used only for the check and was never committed. The window used was minimised, so positions, sizes and colours were read from the page, and drags were played back with scripted mouse events.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Located, sure to 93 m | Map zooms to street level. Dot and circle drawn, 93 m in radius. The line says "about 90 m" |
| That pin dragged 130 m | The dot goes with it. The circle and the line go. The map does not jump. Name and list position kept |
| Search after that | Looks from the dragged spot, and says "Nearest to where you are first" |
| A stop dragged | Only the stop moves. Dot, circle and line stay |
| A start that was clicked, not found, dragged | Only the pin moves. Dot and circle stay on the browser's guess |
| Click inside the circle | Adds a place as usual. The circle does not swallow the click |
| Route planned, then a stop dragged | The plan is dropped |
| Located, sure to 8 m | No line. Map zooms no closer than street level |
| Located, sure to 5 km | The line says "about 5 km". Map zooms out to show the whole circle |
| Start clicked first, location arrives later | Start kept. Map does not move. The dot and circle appear |
| Location refused | Nothing drawn, nothing said |

## Worth knowing

- **The circle is the browser's claim, not a limit.** On the laptop above it said 90 metres and was 130 out. The line now says so.
- **A correction lasts until the page is reloaded.** Then the browser guesses again. Remembering where you said you are belongs with saved places, #2.
- **Dragging the browser's pin a long way also counts as a correction.** Search then looks from wherever it was dropped. That spot is the start as well, so the results are the ones the start would have given.
- **A phone will do far better.** With GPS the circle is a few metres and the line does not appear.
- Still no frontend tests. This is the third pull request checked by hand, and a test runner should come next.

author: skyphusion-rollins
body:
## What

`mcp/src/tools.ts` emitted `field: field ?? null` in every `mailbox_search` result.
`field` selects the column for mode `substr` only, which the tool's own description
already said. So a caller sending `mode: hybrid, field: subject` got `field: "subject"`
back, which reads as confirmation that the search was restricted to subjects. It was not.

An echo is how a caller checks that a parameter was understood, so echoing an ignored
parameter is worse than omitting it. The caller has no other way to tell.

## The choice, and why

#651 offered omission or refusal; the dispatch also offered an explicit `fieldApplied: false`.
This PR **refuses** the call.

Refusal is the rule this repo already applies to an accepted-and-ignored parameter. #632 F1
made an unknown key a refusal rather than a strip, and the comment in `registerTools` states
the reason: a supplied filter that is silently dropped is worse than one that is rejected,
because the caller reasonably believes it applied. The two softer answers both leave the
unrestricted search running and put the burden on the caller to notice:

- **Omission** gives the caller an absent key to detect. An agent does not diff the response
  shape against what it sent, so this trades a false positive for a silent one.
- **`fieldApplied: false`** is honest, but it is reported after a search already ran and
  returned plausible results, which is the shape a caller acts on before reading the flag.

Refusal costs the caller one round trip and tells it exactly what to change. The error names
both remedies: pass `mode=substr`, or remove `field`.

The refusal lands BEFORE `client.search`, so no unrestricted search runs under a name the
caller would misread. `mode` is optional and defaults to `hybrid`, so `{ query, field }` with
no mode at all is the likeliest way in; it is refused too, and there is a test for exactly
that case.

The echo now appears only in the mode that honors it, so the key's PRESENCE carries
information and three states are distinguishable:

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `mode: substr, field: subject` | `field: "subject"` |
| `mode: substr`, no field | `field: null` (substr with no column named) |
| any other mode | no `field` key at all |

A `null` in a non-substr answer would have been a fourth, false reading: "understood,
unrestricted".

## Verification

Nine new tests in `mcp/test/search-field-mode.test.ts`. Six FAIL on current `main`, three
pass as controls. Run with the source reverted to `main` and the test file in place:

```
### SOURCE REVERTED TO MAIN, TEST ONLY ###
 FAIL  test/search-field-mode.test.ts > mailbox_search field is refused outside substr mode (#651) > refuses mode=hybrid with field, and runs NO search
AssertionError: promise resolved "{ query: 'invoice', …(16) }" instead of rejecting
 FAIL  test/search-field-mode.test.ts > mailbox_search field is refused outside substr mode (#651) > refuses the DEFAULTED mode too, where the trap is worst
AssertionError: promise resolved "{ query: 'invoice', …(16) }" instead of rejecting
 FAIL  test/search-field-mode.test.ts > mailbox_search field is refused outside substr mode (#651) > refuses field on fts and semantic as well, not just hybrid
AssertionError: promise resolved "{ query: 'x', mode: 'fts', …(15) }" instead of rejecting
 FAIL  test/search-field-mode.test.ts > mailbox_search field is refused outside substr mode (#651) > names both remedies in the error, and is a PosternError
AssertionError: expected null to be an instance of PosternError
 FAIL  test/search-field-mode.test.ts > mailbox_search field echo in the mode that honors it (#651) > omits the field key entirely in the modes that ignore it
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 FAIL  test/search-field-mode.test.ts > mailbox_search description states the refusal (#651) > says field is refused outside substr, not merely ignored
AssertionError: expected 'for mode substr only: which column to…' to match /refus/i
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  6 failed | 3 passed (9)
```

The first failure is the defect stated as the issue states it: the call RESOLVED, and
`out.field` was `"subject"`.

**Control.** The three that pass unchanged are the legitimate path, so a change that refused
everything would not look like a fix: substr still forwards `field` to `client.search` and
still echoes it, substr with no field still echoes `field: null`, and a non-substr search
with no field still never sends `field` on the wire.

With the fix applied:

```
 Test Files  12 passed (12)
      Tests  146 passed (146)
```

`main` was 137 passing before; 137 + 9 = 146, so nothing regressed. `npm run typecheck` in
`mcp/` passes (`tsc --noEmit` plus `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`).

## Scope

No worker change. `inbound/src/routes.ts` is untouched, so no `routes:emit` is owed.
`mcp/README.md` line 38 is updated so the documented contract matches: `field` is REFUSED in
any other mode rather than ignored. The stale phrase "ignored by other modes" is gone from the
tool description, and a test asserts it cannot come back, because a stale description is how a
caller learns the wrong contract.

Closes #651

body:
## Description

QA's Camera Streaming loopback self-test (NVBug 6840404, DevTest task P1236_T152992) failed on two config problems that are not code bugs:

- **`replay.yaml` could not run under `loopback`.** It shipped `fps: 0` with `width`/`height` commented out, but `loopback` forces `source: rtp`, which requires all three (`config.py` and `rtp_h264_sender.py`). They are now pinned to the shipped clip (1280x720 at 30 fps), so `./camera_viz.sh loopback configs/replay.yaml` runs as documented. Direct mode is unaffected, since those are the clip's native values.
- **`v4l2.yaml` is a ZED Mini template.** On a RealSense or webcam host it fails to open (`requested 2560x720, got 640x480`) and the viewer only shows `submit/s 0.0`. The config header and the loopback docs now say to use the config that matches the camera (`realsense.yaml` for a RealSense).

The docs also now state that `loopback` does not forward `--mode`, so a desktop window needs `display.mode: window` in the YAML. Fixing that in `camera_viz.sh` is left for a separate change.

NVBug 6840404 (no GitHub issue). A `release/1.5.x` cherry-pick PR will follow once this merges, since QA tests that branch.

- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

x86 workstation, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RealSense D435i, `./camera_viz.sh loopback` with `display.mode: window`:

- `replay.yaml` before: `ValueError: camera 'replay' needs explicit width/height when source: rtp`. After: sender and viewer both at 30 fps, clip plays.

author: quyifan1234
body:
This PR optimizes the application's performance by reducing package sizes, lazily loading heavy routes, and avoiding unnecessary React renders.

### Changes made:
1. **Code splitting**: Modified `vite.config.ts` to implement manual chunking. `react`, `react-dom`, `@tanstack/react-router`, `@supabase/supabase-js`, and `lucide-react` are now extracted into individual chunks.
2. **Lazy routing**: The main route components (`apps`, `assets`, `keys`, `skills`, `mine`) have been renamed to `*.lazy.tsx` and modified to use `createLazyFileRoute` to load on-demand, lowering the main bundle cost.
3. **Memoization**: Row rendering loops inside the main lists are now handled by newly created `React.memo` row components (`AppRow`, `AssetRow`, `SkillRow`, `KeyRow`).
4. **Stable Props**: Callback props passed down to these row components are now correctly wrapped using `React.useCallback` in the parent scope.

All TypeScript and Build checks pass flawlessly. No visual regressions introduced.

author: 0xenca
body:
## Resumen

Corrige 2 alertas de CodeQL `py/stack-trace-exposure` en `main`:

| Alerta | Ubicación | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| #1 | `admin.py:221` | `POST /api/admin/rules/preview` |
| #2 | `admin.py:233` | `POST /api/admin/rules` |

**Problema:** ambos endpoints capturaban `RuleError` y devolvían `str(e)` en el JSON. Para regex inválidas, ese texto venía directamente del mensaje de excepción del parser de `regex`.

Usa el mismo enfoque que el PR anterior para los endpoints de IA ([0xenca/DHTSearch#2](https://github.com/0xenca/DHTSearch/pull/2)): la validación devuelve el mensaje para el admin sin lanzar ninguna excepción.

## Cambios

**`hiderules.py`**
- Nueva función `check(term, scope, mode)`. Hace las mismas comprobaciones que `validate()` y devuelve `(term, None)` o `(None, mensaje)` sin lanzar excepciones.
- `validate()` ahora llama a `check()` y lanza `RuleError(mensaje)` igual que antes. Sus otros usos no cambian: la carga de reglas en `RuleBook` y `migrate_es.py`.
- Nuevo método `RuleBook.try_add(...)`. Devuelve `(rule, None)` o `(None, mensaje)` y cubre también "At most 500 rules" y "An identical rule already exists". `add()` se apoya en él y sigue lanzando `RuleError`.
- Una regex inválida ahora da un mensaje fijo: *"Invalid regular expression (check brackets, parentheses, escapes and quantifiers)"*, en lugar del texto de la excepción del parser.

**`admin.py`**
- `_rule_input()` devuelve el posible problema en lugar de lanzar una excepción.
- `/rules/preview` y `/rules` usan `check()` / `try_add()` y responden 400 con el mensaje. Ya no hay ningún `except ... as e` + `str(e)`.
- Se elimina el import, ya sin uso, de `RuleError` y `validate`.

## Impacto

Los mensajes que ve el admin en el panel son los mismos que antes, con una excepción: en una regex inválida ya no aparece la posición exacta del error (p. ej. *"missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 0"*), sino el mensaje genérico de arriba.

## Pruebas

- `tests/test_admin.py` y `tests/test_search.py`: **ALL OK**. `test_admin` ya cubre el 400 al crear una regla con regex inválida (`"("`).
- Manual: `try_add("(", regex)` → mensaje genérico; añadir una regla duplicada → *"An identical rule already exists"*; `add()` y `validate()` siguen lanzando `RuleError` con el mismo mensaje.

author: donz-dev
body:
A fourth Hunter profile, specified by the ruleset owner as "largely the same as LW melee" — same race, class, combat style, gear, raid buffs and consumables — with "the same APL except Summon Hawk will be used above Wing Clip", and **two allocations to choose between**.

**Hawk Melee 824.4, second of twenty-five and the top Hunter.** The other twenty-four are identical to the decimal.

## The two builds differ on one thing that matters

Whether to keep Lone Wolf's 20% or drop it for a pet. Both readings were live until they were measured.

| Build | DPS |
| --- | --- |
| **16/11/24, Lone Wolf AND the hawk** — shipped | **824.4** |
| 16/10/25, the pet instead of Lone Wolf | 803.8 |
| LW Melee — Lone Wolf, no hawk | 779.7 |
| 16/10/25 with Summon Hawk out of the list — the pet, no hawk | 733.5 |

**The pet loses and the hawk wins, independently.** The pet and its Claw and Bite were 13.2% of the 16/10/25 profile and did not cover the 20% they cost — that build is **−46.2 against LW Melee** once its hawk entry is removed, so trading Lone Wolf for a pet is a loss on its own. The hawk is worth having on either base, and the build that takes both is the one that shipped.

## Five points that do nothing, left alone on purpose

| Talent | Points | Why it is inert |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `improved_aspect_of_the_monkey` | 3 | "Dodge from an Aspect no damage profile uses" — a live gap |
| `pathfinding` | 2 | `scope: 'positioning'` — a permanent ruling, not a gap |

It wins by 20.7 anyway. **The allocation is left exactly as the owner wrote it** — a preset that quietly re-spent five points would stop being the build they specified — and a test names both talents and fails if either ever becomes modelled. The losing build wasted points too: Endurance Training's three are pet health and armor, worth nothing to a profile nothing attacks.

## It takes Lone Wolf *and* Summon Hawk, which makes the list key load-bearing

Both melee Hunters are dual-wield, below the Beast Mastery capstone, and **now both take Lone Wolf** — so Summon Hawk is the only thing separating them, and it is also the talent the two lists actually differ by. Keyed on Lone Wolf instead, this profile would run `HUNTER_LONE_WOLF_MELEE`, never press the hawk it spends sixteen points on, and report an ordinary figure.

The key was chosen while the 16/10/25 build was the candidate, where it was one reasonable option of two. The build that shipped is the one that would have exposed the other choice.

The capstone stays first, because Beast Mastery takes Summon Hawk too and is `combatStyle: 'ranged'` — fall it into a melee list and it stands there pressing Raptor Strike.

The list is **spread from LW Melee's, not copied**, and the test asserts the relationship rather than the eight entries. The entry is gated on `hawksBelowCap` like both other lists that press it — a six-second cooldown against an eighteen-second hawk would otherwise overwrite the older of the two every time.

No `petFamily`, which is correct rather than an omission: `bringsPet` is false, so `petFor` never reaches its Cat fallback. Naming a family would be inert and would read as a pet build.

## Two fixes to `update_baseline_table.py`, both first reached by a 25th profile

- It keyed the mean sentence on the count it had just produced, so it looked for "mean across **25**" while the sentence still said 24, and failed on the one edit it exists to make. It matches any count and rewrites both numbers now.
- Its odd-row filler emitted a seven-column row against a nine-column header. Markdown accepts that silently. Every previous run had an even count.

Also refreshes the three stale DPS figures in `docs/handoff/hunter.md`, which predate the consumables, and says which share rows come from which run.

Rebased onto #211 and #213; re-measured at each base, and #213 moved no Mage figure.

2745 tests pass, typecheck clean.

body:
Stacked on #7 so CI runs the whole fix on both platforms. Once #7 is merged, GitHub retargets this to `main`.

`cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` failed on `main` with ten advisories, two rejected licences, two git sources, two wildcard dependencies and a yanked crate. All pass now.

| Advisory | Crate | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| RUSTSEC-2026-0245 (path traversal, arbitrary file write), RUSTSEC-2026-0246 (unmaintained) | sevenz-rust 0.6 | replaced by **sevenz-rust2 0.23**, its maintained fork, without the `util` feature: the `decompress_impl` helpers the advisory is about are not compiled at all. Xion's own `safe_join` still decides where every 7z entry lands. |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0187 | lopdf 0.34 | pdf-extract 0.7 to **0.12.1** (lopdf 0.42) |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0271 (FTP CRLF injection) | suppaftp 6 | **12.1.1** (optional `ftp` feature) |
| yanked spin 0.9.8 | flume via mdns-sd 0.11 | mdns-sd **0.21.5** |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0009, 0204, 0194, 0195 | time, crossbeam-epoch, quick-xml | `cargo update` |
| RUSTSEC-2025-0141 (unmaintained) | bincode via syntect 5.3 | ignored with reason: syntect only loads the dumps compiled into the binary, and has no release without bincode |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0192 (unmaintained) | ttf-parser via iced 0.14 | ignored with reason: iced's font stack, no replacement release |

Also in this PR:

- `colony-ui` moves from the `v0.1.0` git tag to **0.1.5** on crates.io, as Colony does. That removes one git source and one wildcard; `iced_term` keeps its pinned revision (still unreleased upstream) with `version = "0.8.0"` and an `allow-git` entry.
- zip 7 to **8.6**. The explicit `bzip2 0.5` dependency goes: bzip2 0.6, which zip uses, defaults to the pure-Rust backend it was there to select. `deny.toml` allows its `bzip2-1.0.6` licence and drops the unused `OpenSSL` allowance.
- `rust-version` 1.85 to **1.95**: sysinfo 0.39 already required it, and the edition 2024 resolver was holding image, ignore, encoding_rs and zbus back because of the stale value. Direct dependencies are written at their full current version (design/dependencies.md).
- With the new `rust-version`, clippy's `collapsible_if` applies to nested `if let` blocks; the second commit collapses them with `cargo clippy --fix`, no behaviour change.

Folds in Dependabot #2 (cargo-minor), #3 (colony-ui), #5 (mdns-sd) and #6 (pdf-extract).

Checked locally: `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` ok; clippy `-D warnings` on Linux and on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with `--all-features`; `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` (296 tests).

author: thebeline
body:
# Pull Request

## Description

`TextEmbeddingService` built `fastembed.TextEmbedding` without a `cache_dir` (`backend/processing/text_embedding.py`), so fastembed used its default, `$TMPDIR/fastembed_cache`. Compose gives each container a private `/tmp` that is discarded on recreate, so every image update downloaded the embedding model again, and the io and parse lanes each kept their own copy.

author: andygrove
body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

No issue. This follows up on #6441.

## Rationale for this change

#6441 makes a native Iceberg write to S3 fall back to Spark when the Hadoop configuration has an `fs.s3a.*` setting the native writer doesn't support. It already ignores Hadoop's built-in defaults and a few S3A read settings that Spark seeds into every session. Some other settings are also common in S3 deployments, and any one of them makes every native S3 write fall back:

- Since Spark 4.1, `SparkContext` sets `fs.s3a.committer.magic.enabled=true` and `fs.s3a.committer.name=magic` for every application when `spark-hadoop-cloud` is on the classpath (SPARK-47618).
- Many deployments also set `fs.s3a.committer.threads`, `fs.s3a.experimental.input.fadvise` (Hadoop's S3A docs recommend `random` for columnar formats) or `fs.s3a.bulk.delete.page.size` cluster-wide.

The fallback reason looks like this:

```
unsupported Hadoop S3A settings: fs.s3a.bulk.delete.page.size, fs.s3a.committer.magic.enabled, fs.s3a.committer.name, fs.s3a.committer.threads, fs.s3a.experimental.input.fadvise
```

None of these settings affects an Iceberg data-file write:

- The native writer doesn't go through S3A, so S3A's delete batching doesn't apply.
- `fadvise` is a read hint.
- Iceberg commits through table metadata, not through a Hadoop output committer.

## What changes are included in this PR?

The five keys are added to `IgnoredHadoopS3Keys` in `CometIcebergNativeWrite`, alongside the Spark-seeded read settings, with a comment explaining why.

## How are these changes tested?

There's a new test in `CometIcebergWriteDetectionSuite`. It checks that these settings produce no unsupported keys, and that a setting the native writer can't honor (`fs.s3a.encryption.algorithm`) is still reported next to them. The whole suite passes locally.

The pull request workflow ran two jobs: one built the configs and redeployed the twin, then a second one started its own container, checked the branch out again, and rebuilt DC1 before running ANTA, because nothing from the first job survives into it. On my last timed run that rebuild alone was 15 seconds of every pull request's check, plus the second container's startup.

This folds them into one `digital-twin` job: build, redeploy the twin, then find the twin, pin ANTA, validate, commit the report, and post the sticky comment, all against the same build. Validation still only runs if the redeploy succeeded, and the check still fails when ANTA fails. Nautobot's promote only looks at the run's overall conclusion, so the job rename doesn't affect it.

This PR has the README change. The workflow change itself is coming as a separate commit on this branch.

author: mothersphere
body:
Resolves the critical code scanning alert #6 (`rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value`, `crates/artemis-p2p/src/crypto.rs`).

## What the alert pointed at

`encrypt_for` built its nonce as `[0u8; 12]` and then filled it from `thread_rng`. The nonce itself was random, so the literal finding is a pattern match, but the code around it had real problems with where its key material came from:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Raw X25519 output used directly as the ChaCha20-Poly1305 key | HKDF-SHA256 over the shared secret, bound to a purpose label and to the sender's and recipient's public keys, in sending order |
| One key per pair of users: Alice-to-Bob equalled Bob-to-Alice, and signaling used the same key as direct messages | One key per direction and per purpose (`Purpose::DirectMessage`, `Purpose::Signaling`) |
| A low-order peer key (for example all zeros) makes X25519 return all zeros, so the "shared" key was a constant anyone could compute | Refused with `CryptoError::InvalidKey` via `SharedSecret::was_contributory`, on encrypt and decrypt |
| Nonce buffer initialised to zeros, then filled from `thread_rng` | `Nonce::try_generate()`, straight from the OS CSPRNG (getrandom) |
| Identity keys from `thread_rng` | `StaticSecret::random()`, from getrandom |
| Derived key left on the stack | `Zeroizing` buffer; the cipher wipes its own copy on drop (`zeroize` feature); decoded key bytes are wiped too |

Because the two directions use different keys, a relay can no longer bounce Alice's own message back to her as one from Bob, and a signaling ciphertext can no longer be passed off as a direct message (or the reverse). `decrypt_sent` reads back our own side of a conversation.

The HKDF labels (`artemis-p2p v1 direct message`, `artemis-p2p v1 signaling`) are public protocol constants for domain separation, documented as such in the code. They are not secrets and are meant to be identical in every client.

## Client

- A direct message that fails to decrypt is no longer shown as its raw content (the relay could have written that text under a friend's name). It shows `[This message could not be decrypted]`.
- Both receive paths (live and history) go through one `dm_text` helper. Our own messages in a history now decrypt, instead of showing base64.

## Dependencies

- `chacha20poly1305` 0.10 to 0.11.0 and `x25519-dalek` 2 to 3.0.0, plus `hkdf` 0.13.0, `sha2` 0.11.0 and `zeroize` 1.9.1, declared once in `[workspace.dependencies]` with full versions. Our crates now use one RustCrypto generation; the older `digest` 0.10 line that remains in `Cargo.lock` comes only from sqlx, axum and oauth2.

## README

The Status list gains a line saying that friends' public keys come from the relay and are not verified, so the relay operator can substitute one. That was already true and the README did not say it.

## Compatibility

Ciphertexts produced by earlier builds no longer decrypt. There has been no release, and the README already states that keys are regenerated at every sign-in, so no stored direct message was decryptable across restarts anyway.

## Tests

Five new tests: a low-order peer key is refused, two encryptions never share a nonce, the sender can read back its own message, a reflected message is refused, and a direct-message ciphertext does not decrypt as signaling. The low-order test was checked to fail without the check, and the reflection and purpose tests to fail with the old sorted, single-label derivation. All 12 crypto tests pass; clippy and fmt are clean.

**ASSA-326 box 7 has been parked on a picture nobody could take.** Every played frame in this repo holds the demo loop's own pair — a smelter and a planted drill 2.5 tiles apart on both axes, because `AssayDemoPlan.smelter_spot` starts at `(2, 2)` and `drill_spot` at `(0, 0)`. Maren priced the box as "a chain that mines for a second machine, plus a GUI run"; I said on #427 that no played frame can hold an adjacent pair. Both true of the loop — and the loop already stands two buildings up.

**THE FIXTURE IS TWO SIM COMMANDS.** `PlayerCommand::Pickup` returns a smelter to the pack with its contents, reach its only gate (`step.rs:389`), and `Place` puts it back on the drill's east tile — the one Maren's #442 measured at 95.3% of RECT and 43.5% of INK. No extra ore mined, no item invented, every command the `AssayActions` builder a button sends, and the outcome read back out of `buildings()`: a refused `Place` fails the run instead of reporting a pair nobody saw.

Seed 777042: machine 1x1 at `(74,36)`, smelter 2x2 at `(75,36)`, **SHARING AN EDGE**. Frame and key in `shared/assay/cove-assa326/`.

**TWO MISTAKES OF MINE, KEPT IN THE FILE'S OWN WORDS RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED:**

1. **The first adjacency verdict called a true pair a miss.** I compared `Building::distance_from`'s Chebyshev-to-a-rect against 0 — a measure written for a POINT against a RECT, where 0 means inside — so two rects sharing an edge come out at 1. It is per axis now, in words, because one number cannot tell an EDGE from a CORNER.
2. **The first frame carried `Place 0 · submitted` in the toast.** A cold reader asked *"how many built things are in this picture"* would have been told by the picture that something had just been placed — the panel-text leak Marlow declared himself on ASSA-273, except here I would have built it in. ASSA-294's `blind` layout separates the key from the frames and can do nothing about a sentence INSIDE the frame. The run ticks until the toast ages out, records whether it did, and says in the key when a frame is primed.

**Touches `client/tools/` only, built by Cove.** No draw call, nothing ruled: an instrument, which per Wren on #379 does not wait behind a ruling.

author: rsaryev
body:
#### Description of Change

Applications can add, detach and cycle native macOS window tabs, but cannot inspect a group's membership, tab order or selected window. This makes it difficult to restore independent tab groups after restarting an application.

Adds `BaseWindow.getTabbedWindows()`, `getSelectedTab()` and `selectTab()`, inherited by `BrowserWindow`. Adds a `tabbingMode` constructor option and property so applications can show restored windows independently before explicitly joining their tabs. Applications remain responsible for storing and restoring their sessions.

Validation on macOS arm64: Electron built successfully; the 55-test native tab suite passed twice consecutively. Coverage includes both window types, mixed groups, ordering, selection without focusing an inactive group, minimized and fullscreen windows, close cancellation, closed wrappers, and cross-process restoration after quit, close, native close and hide/quit. C++ and JS formatting/linting, documentation checks, spec typechecking and generated declaration smoke tests passed. The full test suite has not been run.

VS Code integration: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340605 — preserves native tab groups, tab order and selected tabs across sessions.

`check_model_status()` looks in `$HF_HOME/hub` and then falls back to `~/.cache/huggingface/hub`. `backend/tests/test_model_cache_detection.py` points `HF_HOME` at a temp dir but leaves `HOME` alone, so on a machine with Parakeet or Canary in its own Hugging Face cache the two "empty cache" cases find the host's copy and fail.

author: catarinagamboa
body:
Fixes #343.

The verifier assumed every return and `this` access belonged to a class, so static and default interface methods crashed before verification. Return checking now uses the nearest method and its declaring type, resolves overloads by parameter types, and keeps lambda returns separate from an enclosing method. Interface method invocations also use their registered contracts.

New passing cases cover the reported `String.length()` call, annotated static/default methods, `return this`, same-arity overloads, and lambda returns inside interface bodies. New failing cases require errors for invalid static/default returns and a bad interface method argument.

Validation: `mvn test` passed all 391 tests, and the four new fixtures produced their expected outcomes when run directly.

This change does not extend interface supertype contract inheritance.

author: prestrike00
body:
## Why

Inventory offered one flat search plus three unrelated children, so there was no way to ask for just identities, just cloud resources, or just secrets.

The cause is structural rather than cosmetic. Entity types are mostly assembled at projection time from a provider and a resource type (`provider + "." + resourceType`, `runtime.` + resourceType, `<source>.<principalType>`) rather than written as string literals. The hand-written category map could only match literals, so most records fell through to an auto-derived, auto-titled class and the sub-menu had nothing meaningful to point at.

## What changed

**Service.** A new rule-based classifier places an entity type into one of six groups: Identities, Cloud, SaaS, Code, Devices, Secrets. Rules match on exact value, prefix, or suffix, and the first matching rule wins, so narrow rules are declared ahead of the provider-prefix rules that would otherwise absorb them. Parts joined with an underscore and parts joined with a dot are compared in one normalised form, because projectors use both for the same concept.

A group id resolves against the entity kinds the catalog actually reports, so types that only exist once they are computed still land in the right group without being enumerated anywhere. A group that matches nothing returns nothing rather than falling through to an unfiltered listing.

Categories now report the group they belong to, and only when every entity type inside the category agrees.

**Console.** The inventory page became a shared workspace component. `/inventory` is the unfiltered search, and each group is the same component with a preset. The sidebar leads with Assets and lists the six groups, then the existing credential and directory pages, then Graph.

**Repairs.** Several class-map keys named entity types no projector can produce, including IAM, Google Workspace, load balancer, endpoint and DNS record entries. They now name the types that are actually emitted.

## Compatibility

- No change to the public route set, query parameters, or omitted-parameter behaviour. Group ids travel in the existing `category_id` parameter.
- `entity_type` still takes precedence over `category_id`.
- A per-class `category_id` still resolves through the class map exactly as before, and unknown ids keep the existing fallback.
- `group` and `group_label` are additive, omitted when empty.
- Surface classification is untouched. Grouping never removes a record from the asset surface; everything remains reachable from the unfiltered search.

## Tests

- Go: group classification, declaration-order overlaps, computed `runtime.*` types, underscore-joined types, ungrouped types, category/group id collisions, live-kind resolution, the empty-group guard, per-class fallback, `entity_type` precedence, and group reporting on categories.
- Web: a parity assertion that fails if the mirrored client rules drift from the service rules in content or order, plus classification, route shape, and lookup tests.
- Each new assertion was checked by reverting the behaviour it covers and confirming it fails.
- `go test ./internal/graphquery ./internal/grcinventory ./internal/bootstrap`, `make check-structural check-structural-test check-arch`, `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, and the web suite all pass. The web suite has four failures that are present on `main` and unrelated to this change. `cargo` is unavailable locally, so the Rust leg of `make openapi-check` could not run; the Go route-parity leg passes.

author: super-yojan
body: Fixes #34. TerraPhone for Android is a Kotlin/Compose shell. Estimation, the motor plant, waypoint following, occupancy integration, autonomy arbitration, and Zenoh framing stay in the shared Rust crates and cross the boundary through UniFFI Kotlin bindings, the same way the iOS app uses UniFFI Swift bindings. ## What landed - `scripts/build-android.sh` builds the host `libterra_mobile.so`, generates Kotlin bindings, and uses cargo-ndk 3.5.4 to produce release `arm64-v8a` and `x86_64` libraries. Gradle lives in `mobile/android/`. - Controller screen: simulated rover, phone IMU + ARCore VIO, velocity sliders, effort readout, and Stop. Leaving the foreground stops the controller and disconnects Zenoh with a final zero. - Waypoint: origin, goal, map tap, Johnson Center defaults, Go, and Cancel. Go steps `MobileWaypoint` and publishes that twist as `cmd_vel`. The `goal` topic stays idle so Zorvane does not run a second follower. - Occupancy from the simulated room and from a posed Zenoh depth frame. The ARCore depth path is written and not device-verified. Smoothed 16-bit depth is used; raw confidence is not applied to that image. - Zenoh is shown only on an emulator (fingerprint, not a debug flag). Default endpoint `tcp/10.0.2.2:7447`. A physical device hides Zenoh and deletes a stored endpoint and rover ID. Bluetooth is a placeholder, not a GATT client. - Autonomy chips come from `supported_autonomy_levels()`. Explore is drawn disabled. The Rust match is exhaustive, so adding `Level::Explore` (#32 / #33) fails to compile until the wire name is added. Phone-frame conversion, the velocity smoother, the ground-height latch, the simulated plant, and the room depth rays moved into `crates/terra-mobile`. iOS `PhoneController` calls those functions. That Swift change is additive and was not compiled here. ## Tests ```sh cargo test --locked --workspace ./scripts/build-android.sh cd mobile/android && ./gradlew assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest python3 scripts/check-zenoh-kotlin.py ``` `TerraCoreSmokeTest` is the Kotlin → UniFFI → Rust check (controller step, axis conversion, `MobileWaypoint`, benchmark). With `TERRA_ZENOH_SMOKE_ENDPOINT` set, the same test drives a Python Zenoh peer: `terra/rover/9/cmd_vel`, the moving payload, lease expiry to zero, the disconnect zero, and one occupied depth cell. CI job `android` installs the NDK, runs `build-android.sh`, `assembleDebug`, the unit test, and the Zenoh peer script. Zorvane on the host, for an emulator: ```sh TERRA_ROVER_COUNT=1 TERRA_ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/0.0.0.0:7447 cargo run -p zorvane ``` `10.0.2.2` is the emulator's name for the host. The default listen address `127.0.0.1` is not reachable from the guest. ## Verified on this Linux checkout - `cargo test --locked --workspace` - `./scripts/build-android.sh` for `aarch64-linux-android` and `x86_64-linux-android` - `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `testDebugUnitTest` - `python3 scripts/check-zenoh-kotlin.py` against a Python peer (31 commands, selected rover, lease zero, final zero, depth cell) - Headless Zorvane (`TERRA_HEADLESS=1`, listen `tcp/0.0.0.0:7447`) published `terra/rover/0/camera/depth` (256×192). A Zenoh client received it, and a forward `cmd_vel` moved the rover body. The host JVM `MobileZenohClient` (the same UniFFI client the app uses) connected, published a reverse target, and the sampled body pose moved backward. Depth frames on that session were sparse, so this was not a timed closed-loop run and not an emulator UI session. ## Not verified - The emulator UI. An API 35 AVD was created and QEMU started with KVM, but the process never created vCPUs and adb stayed offline. The APK was not installed. No demo was recorded. - ARCore tracking, depth, or the flat-phone mount on hardware. - Bluetooth. The GATT client is a follow-up. It should call `actuator_route`, `actuator_encode_frame`, and `actuator_fragment`. - The iOS app after the new Swift call sites. On a Mac, run `./scripts/build-ios.sh` (regenerates `mobile/ios/Generated`) and then build TerraPhone. New symbols: `deviceVectorToBody`, `yUpCameraToBodyPose`, `yUpCameraToOpticalPose`, `latchGroundOffset`, `PoseVelocityFilter`, `SimulatedPlant`, `simulatedRoomDepth`, `supportedAutonomyLevels`. iOS still sends a waypoint as an arbiter `goal` rather than stepping `MobileWaypoint`. ## Follow-ups - Bluetooth GATT client on a physical phone, using the existing Rust framing. - Wi-Fi provisioning and pairing reset once both apps share it. - ARCore on a real device. - Emulator UI against a running Zorvane process. This VM's emulator did not finish booting. - When #33 lands, add the `explore` wire name in `supported_autonomy_levels` and the chip enables itself. - Mac pass so iOS waypoint following uses `MobileWaypoint.step` the way Android does. Docs: `docs/MOBILE_ANDROID.md`.

author: vocaro
body:
`EPUBReader` now has its own identity: engine ID `org.epublib.reader` and bookmark format `epublib-cfi-v1`. Both name the library rather than a renderer, so they survive any change of how pages are drawn. The new `EPUBReader.bookmarkFormat` sits alongside `EPUBReader.identifier`, so hosts can stop hard-coding the format.

- **Clean break.** Nothing had shipped, so the WebKit reader's `org.epubreaderlib.foliate` / `epubcfi-v1` tags are not carried forward. A bookmark with those tags is refused with `incompatibleLocation`, like any other engine's.
- **Migration.** The CFI value names the same position, so a host migrates a stored bookmark by replacing its `engineID` and `format`. StudyWright stores bare CFI strings and wraps them only at restore time. When it re-pins, it replaces its literal `"epubcfi-v1"` with `EPUBReader.bookmarkFormat` (two lines in `ReaderEPUBSurface.swift`, plus its tests and device harness) and needs no data migration.
- **Docs.** Updated in `doc/architecture.md`, `doc/native-viewer.md`, `doc/integration.md`, `doc/releasing.md`, `doc/testing.md` and the release notes. The design doc also links the new fixed-layout tracking issue, #5.
- **Test.** `NativeSessionTests.testBookmarksCarryEPUBLibsIdentityAndForeignTagsAreRefused` checks that a foliate-recorded CFI restores under the new tags and that the old tags are refused.

`bash scripts/check-all.sh` passes: 281 macOS tests, 342 tests on each of iPhone 17 Pro and iPad Air 13-inch (M4), and both sample builds.

author: pikarestiv
body:
## Cart reveal

Reported from watching staff: add a product, add many more, then add the first one again — its line is scrolled out of sight, so there's no way to see the quantity changed or reach the +/− controls.

**The cart keeps its order.** It's a receipt in progress: cashiers scan it to verify what they've rung up, and customers watch that screen. A line jumping to the bottom reads as *a new item was added*, not *that one went from 2 to 3*. Reordering also means an item rung three times bounces around the list.

So only the viewport moves. After any add, if the affected line is off-screen it scrolls into view; if it's already visible, nothing happens — scrolling under a cashier who can see the line is worse than doing nothing. The line also gets a brief highlight so the quantity change is legible without anything moving. `motion-reduce` respected.

Keyed off the quantity rising rather than a tap handler, so a card tap, barcode scan, search result and suggestion chip all behave the same. The first run is skipped so a restored cart isn't treated as a fresh add.

The product grid's own reveal is unchanged and still does its separate job — showing where a scanned product sits in the grid.

## Import dialog

Was plain text and a single button. Now:

- A real **drop zone** that actually accepts drops, rather than a dashed box that only looks droppable. Hover and drag states both shown.
- A spreadsheet icon, because that's what's being imported — not a generic cloud-upload glyph.
- Wider (`sm:max-w-2xl`), which the two-column mapping step needed anyway.
- Copy rewritten: *"Bring your product list in from a spreadsheet. We'll show you how the columns matched before anything is saved."* — the em dash is gone, and the reassurance that nothing saves until you've reviewed is the thing someone importing 2,500 products actually wants to know.
- Format guidance demoted to a quiet line instead of a parenthetical caveat in the title.

Follows §6: semantic tokens throughout, `bg-white dark:bg-slate-900` for the surface, no hardcoded hex.

## Testing

`401 files / 2531 tests passing`, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Both changes are interaction and presentation, verified in the browser rather than pinned with brittle scroll-position tests.

body:
Adds the shared files of the four services to `shared/`, a pin check in `pr.yml`, a sync script and a weekly report.

What changed:
- `shared/lib/` (9 files) and `shared/test/` (7 tests and `support/contract-schema.ts`) hold the one true copy. `instrument.ts` and `logger.ts` come from catalogue: its flag fields (lab-svc-catalogue#19) are optional and write nothing when a handler reports no flags. The other three copies had drifted from catalogue.
- `xray-exporter.ts` has the fixed comment (lab-platform#56). The README of lab-platform has no section about Transaction Search, so the comment names the stack `Platform` and the section "Why Transaction Search, and who owns it" of the lab-svc-core README.
- `actions/shared-files/`: `lib.mjs` (compare, pin, sync plan, report rules), `sync.mjs` (copies the files of a commit into a service and writes `shared.lock.json`), `cli.mjs` (`pin`, `check`, `report`) and their tests.
- `pr.yml`: the job `shared` compares each shared file of the service with the file at the PINNED commit. A repository with no pin file gets a notice and passes, so nothing breaks before the services adopt it.
- `shared-files.yml`: weekly (and `workflow_dispatch`) report of the services whose pin is behind the latest commit that changed `shared/`. It keeps one issue, like the dependency audit.
- README section "Shared files": the mechanism, how to change a shared file, why no package.

Not done here: the unit tests of the shared files do not run in this repository. They need the dependencies of a service (`vitest`, OpenTelemetry, `aws-cdk-lib`). Each service runs them on its copy.

Assumptions:
- `lib/namespace.ts` and `test/namespace.test.ts` are not in the set. They differ by design between catalogue and core (service names in the stack and parameter names).
- `instrument`, `logger` and `metrics` tests are not in the set. They name the service and the route.

How verified: `node --test actions/shared-files/*.test.mjs` (79 tests), `actionlint`, and a run of sync and check against a temporary folder: 17 files equal; a changed copy fails with the file name and the sync command.

author: popeee99
body:
Avoid draining the GPU queue when guest memory is unmapped while an unrelated priority callback is pending.  Fixes #1178 (https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/issues/1178).  ### Cause and change  `RenderContext::UnmapMemory` used a global pending-priority check, so even a host-only end-of-pipe event forced `Finish()` while the guest memory-operation lock was held.  Priority operations now carry an optional guest range. Buffer and texture downloads declare their writeback ranges; flip, interrupt and suspend-point callbacks declare no guest-memory access. Omitted ranges remain conservative. The scheduler checks both queued operations and the currently executing callback under its existing mutex, retaining the active range until the callback returns. Existing cache-ownership checks and completion ordering are preserved.  Buffer downloads conservatively cover their entire source buffer, including every packed copy. This does not remove required waits for cached GPU resources, overlapping writebacks or unannotated callbacks.  ### Regression evidence  A standalone reproduction linked against unchanged upstream emulator code at `2f4b8a335d5e27a5153bdea670bd877a061e37b1` queues the existing `Sync::TriggerEopEventAtEndOfPipe` operation, then unmaps an unrelated CPU-only range. Upstream advances the submission tick from **1 to 2** and fails the no-submission assertion. With the fix, the tick is unchanged.  `SchedulerUnmapTests.cpp` uses a real Vulkan device and the production `RenderContext` and `CommandScheduler`. Its five scenarios cover host-only events, multiple queued ranges and overlap/adjacency boundaries, conservative unknown ranges, an actively executing callback, and real guest-backing writeback before unmap returns. These are state-based checks, not timing benchmarks. The focused fixture can run without the barycentric and min-LOD extensions required by the broader shader harness.  ### Validation  - Local Linux/WSL, Clang 21.1.8, Mesa llvmpipe: all five new scenarios pass. - ASan + UBSan: the test and every changed production translation unit are instrumented; all five scenarios pass without sanitizer diagnostics. Unchanged emulator translation units and third-party libraries were reused without sanitizer instrumentation. The guest test address is outside ASan's shadow reservation; no sanitizer checks are disabled. - Existing memory-tracker, page-manager, BitArray, LRU and emulator CLI CTest checks: **8/8 pass**. - Full local emulator build and the CMake regression target both succeed; CTest runs all five scenarios successfully (18.91 seconds). - Implementation-commit fork CI: [run 37852205381](https://github.com/popeee99/KytyPS5/actions/runs/37852205381) succeeds on commit `6590aabb47f2b2a272d2ad979b64d3779b687a39`: full application builds succeed on Windows, Linux and macOS; Windows CTest **12/12**, Linux **15/15** (including `scheduler_unmap`, 4.55 seconds), macOS **14/14**. All platforms build the new target; its Vulkan runtime regression runs on Linux with Mesa software Vulkan. Windows and macOS run their existing CI suites; this PR does not claim a Vulkan runtime test on those runners. - `git diff --check` passes.
- Documentation follow-up `7cbcad4a8058a6663ed17f07b42d8de4a1284659` adds function contracts only. Removing the added documentation lines reproduces the previously verified source exactly. [Cross-platform CI for this follow-up](https://github.com/popeee99/KytyPS5/actions/runs/37858261228) is in progress.  ### Related work and limits  PR #1190 changes submission ordering and merges cleanly in a three-way tree check; it was not combined for game testing. PR #702 addresses predicate waits, not unmap. It already conflicts with current main, and both changes touch the texture-download callback. Integrating both must preserve #702's pending-download bookkeeping and this PR's range argument; no combined-build claim is made.  No proprietary game files were used. Ready or Not, hardware-GPU behavior and frame-time/audio improvements were not tested. The evidence establishes removal of the unrelated submission and preservation of the tested memory-completion ordering, not a game-performance result.  ### AI assistance  OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, diff review and test execution. No human code review is claimed; human maintainer review is requested.

bbstain
body:
Before: the light attack hit almost instantly and could be spammed (one hit every 0.13 s). A counter only happened when both players attacked on the exact same frame, so taking a life was too easy. Every hit took a life. Invincibility after a hit lasted 0.55 s.

After:
- The light attack winds up for 0.1 s: the fist pulls back and a thin line shows where it will go. Then the bar shoots out and extends.
- The recharge between attacks is 0.4 s (0.8 s for the heavy).
- Getting hit while your own light attack is winding up or swinging toward the attacker counts as a counter. Nobody is touched, the counterer can attack again immediately, and the other player waits out their recharge.
- **The stun hit:** a first hit stuns (stars above the head for 2 s) without taking a life. While stunned, the next hit takes a life. To escape, you must counter or perfect-block; a normal block no longer protects. A fall still takes a life.
- **One counter gauge for the whole match** (bar at the top of the screen). Every counter, by anyone, fills it, and its phase applies to everyone:
  - Phase 2 (from 4 points): shorter recharge and more shield damage.
  - Phase 3 (from 10 points): the same, stronger.
  - Phase 4, berserk (from 18 points): speed, jump, attack speed and attack range are boosted.
  - Countering a heavy is worth 3 counters. The gauge drains after 4 s with no counter.
- Invincibility after losing a life lasts 1.2 s. In 1v1, the hit that takes a life makes the camera zoom in with a slight slow-motion.

How: `CounterGauge` (new) holds the shared gauge. `Game` creates it and hands it to every `Fighter`, and `CounterGaugeBar` (new) draws it. `Fighter.take_hit` stuns or takes a life depending on `_stun_timer`, and `recover()` clears the stun after a counter or perfect block. In `Game._resolve_hits`, a normal block no longer protects a stunned player. A hit landing on a player whose light attack is under way toward the attacker becomes a `_clash` with that player as the counterer. Online, the gauge, the 1v1 zoom and the stun are sent to guests (`ONLINE_HEADER` = 6, `_stun_timer` in `NET_VARS`). All tuning values are `const`s at the top of `scripts/fighter.gd`, `scripts/counter_gauge.gd` and `scripts/game.gd`, plus the light-attack timings in `scripts/character_stats.gd`.

Tests: section 16 of `tests/sim_test.gd` covers the wind-up, the counter during wind-up, the stun hit (second hit, timeout, normal block that doesn't protect, perfect block and counter that do), the shared gauge and its phases, berserk, the decay, invincibility, and the 1v1 zoom (none at 3 players). The older tests check "touched" (stunned or a life lost). Result: `ECHECS: 0`. An online game was tested end to end in Chromium against the local server.

author: fabriziocorbeta
body:
## Problema

Probando en vivo (teléfono real, APK firmada): mandé un mensaje, el asistente respondió correctamente (verificado directo en la DB de producción), pero la pantalla de chat se quedaba con el indicador de "escribiendo" para siempre. Solo salir y volver a entrar al chat mostraba la respuesta.

## Causa

`checkAndPoll`/`pollForAssistantResponse` decidían si seguir pollenando chequeando `it.ai_response_status == "pending"`. Pero `show.json.jbuilder` **nunca serializa** `ai_response_status` ni `ai_response_message` — campo muerto en el cliente, siempre `null`. Entonces `hasPending` era siempre `false` y el polling nunca arrancaba tras mandar un mensaje.

Al reabrir el chat sí se veía la respuesta porque `refresh()` hace un `fetchChat` directo, sin depender del polling.

## Fix

Los mensajes vuelven ordenados del más viejo al más nuevo — se puede inferir si falta respuesta sin ese campo: no llegó respuesta todavía exactamente cuando el último mensaje sigue siendo del usuario.

## Tests

El test existente de polling tenía `"ai_response_status": "pending"` en su mock — una forma que el servidor real nunca manda, por eso pasaba pese al bug real. Lo corregí para reflejar la forma real, y sigue verde con la nueva lógica.

```diff
 Member mode
   <Group screen>
     Your Group: WAM list (RSVP, join, calendar), members, transfer/leave
```

author: jeric4o
body:
Two corrections that came out of reading the previous change's own review round, rather than out of a gate.

- **The reviewing agents never said what is NOT under review.** That round spent four agent passes and a hand-applied edit on the wording of a ticket body before anyone asked whether a ticket's wording had ever been in scope. It had not: nothing gates it, nothing versions it with the code, and it is expected to lag behind what shipped. Both review contracts now carry that bound — and name the one thing that stays in scope, which is a sentence *in* the tree that puts a load-bearing rule outside it. The finding there is "this rule belongs in the repository, where something can check it", never "the external copy is wrong".
- **`/inspect` refused model invocation through a frontmatter flag** that arrived with the skill's own first commit rather than as a considered decision, and that the author did not recognise as one they had taken. Removed, and the field this repo's convention requires of a model-invocable skill put in its place — carrying its activation triggers, its skip conditions, the fact that it reads a *finished* session and is near-useless mid-task, and the cost of a pass over a whole transcript.

The patch version is bumped because this touches plugin-loaded content: the install cache is keyed by version, so without it the change reaches nobody while the update command still reports success.

author: jacobhixon47
body:
Before: familiar rewards paid 8 gold, the Moth Broker and Tinker had no familiars, and the greedy bot won about 5% of Spring runs because Masterwork was out of reach.

After: all 20 familiars from the balance tables are in the game. Four slots sit in a familiar row at the bottom right; click one to read it, sell it for half price, or move it left or right. Familiars come from the Market Square (one a day), patron picks (Mother Hollow, the Firefly Conductor), the Moth Broker, the full-moon Tinker (a Rare at a quarter off) and The Chariot. The Barn Owl shows the top three draw-pile cards above the deck.

Scoring familiars resolve after Tinctures, in slot order, so a flat bonus placed before the Will-o'-Wisp gets doubled. Every step shows in the brew breakdown.

**How:** `core/familiars.ts` holds the rules and numbers (`FAMILIAR_SCORE`, `FAMILIAR_RULES`), the codex gains a `familiars` table, and brew, payout, discard, decline and end-of-day each call the familiar hooks. New actions are `sellFamiliar` and `moveFamiliar`. The bot values familiars with a simple heuristic and sells its weakest one for a clearly better one. GDD §11 has an "In the build" note covering the open choices (Hob, Moth, Wisp, Fox, Ferret, Tortoise), and §9 and §10 are updated for the Broker, Tinker, Chariot and patron rewards.

Also in this PR:
- The sim report lists the familiars held at the end of a run.
- The debug fixture steps `{ familiar }` and `{ reward }` are added.
- `run-market` moves to seed `fx-3`, because `fx-1` no longer offers the Market on day 1, so it was snapping the errand picker.
- `art:check` now counts familiars. They use the placeholder tile until M5's sprites.

### Sims (1,000 runs each, before → after)

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Spring | 4.8% | 25.7% |
| Summer | 2.2% | 23.0% |
| Autumn | 3.9% | 29.2% |
| All unlocks | 4.5% | 29.2% |
| Random bot | 0 errors | 0 errors |

That's back in the 15-35% target band. Most losses are still the finale: in Spring, 41.2% of runs paid week-4 rent but missed the Moonless Patron (main: 24.0%), and week-3 rent failures fell from 20.9% to 11.4%. The bot ends with 2.7 familiars on average. It never buys the Barn Owl, Ferret, Raven or Frost Hare on purpose, so the sim doesn't test those.

### Fixtures and snaps

New fixtures: `run-familiars` (the row and the Barn Owl peek), `run-familiar-card` (sell and move), `run-market-familiar`, `run-familiar-gift` (Mother Hollow's pick). I reviewed these plus `run-market`, `run-market-broker-pick`, `run-market-tinker` and `run-night-gift`.

### Checks

typecheck, lint, 180 tests (22 new in `tests/familiars.test.ts`, coverage 97% on `src/core`), `art:check` and `pnpm e2e` all pass.

author: mrhinkle
body:
## Why

After #454 the sensor-health self row is green, but the `Sensor health` run on main (37857081931) still fails: `pr-review-evidence.yml` is reported FAILING / latest-non-success because its latest `pull_request_target` run ended red. It ended red by design: the sweep exits 1 whenever the event's own PR fails closed. So any PR with an unresolved identity or a carve-out turns the sensor's own workflow red, and Sensor health follows. Same fixed-point class as #454, one level over.

## What

Replace the `exit 1` on `event_fail` with a `::warning`. The verdict itself is unchanged: it is still published on the head's commit status and in the step summary. Status-write failures (`post_fail`) still exit 1, and the publish-crash stamp step (#329 / L-087) is untouched, so a broken sensor still reads as broken.

## Carve-out

This edits `.github/workflows/`, an owner carve-out: needs Mark's attestation at the exact head in addition to cross-vendor review. Authored by Claude (Agent-Vendor trailer). Refs #452, L-087, L-092.

author: abu0001-b
body:
createProject/deleteProject/getProject/renameProject interpolated the caller's projectName straight into docker exec commands, so a name such as '../..' or '.stellar' escaped the workspace and a name containing a double quote broke the quoting on the rm/mv paths. A shared isValidProjectName() now rejects anything outside ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$ (and anything containing '..') with a normal { success: false, error: 'Invalid project name' } result before any command runs, and every interpolated path/name is passed through escapeShellArg. Valid names such as 'my-contract' still create, rename and delete unchanged. Adds tests/lib/projects.test.ts covering each rejected input plus the happy path.

Fixes #65
